papers.abstract: We study a universal model for the bifurcation of asymptotic values, based on the notion of tangent-like maps and families thereof. In analogy with polynomials and polynomial-like maps, we prove that every tangent-like map can be associated to a member of the model family. In particular, the filled Julia sets of tangent-like maps are quasiconformally homeomorphic to the ones for the model family. Likewise, the bifurcation locus of a family of tangent-like maps is homeomorphic to the boundary of the {\em Tandelbrot set} $\mathcal T$, the bifurcation locus of the model. Moreover $\mathcal T$ is universal, in the sense that homeomorphic copies of it can be found densely in the activity loci of asymptotic values of any appropriate natural family of finite type meromorphic maps. When applied to the iterates of a transcendental meromorphic map, these results make it possible to build a transcendental renormalization theory, a question that has been open for the last 25 years.

papers.title: Cores and localizations of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories
papers.abstract: We consider $(\infty,d)$-categories in the limit $d\to \infty$ via the core or localization functors that forget or invert higher non-invertible arrows, respectively. We compare the two resulting $(\infty,1)$-categories of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and exhibit the localization-limit as a reflective localization of the core-limit. Furthermore, we study notions of invertibility that only emerge at $d=\infty$ and give rise to intermediate reflective localizations between the two limits. For example, we characterize coinductive completion and the maps it inverts, and reveal a new separation beyond the one of Henry--Loubaton by showing that even the stronger $ω$-completeness does not suffice to carve out the localization-limit.

papers.title: The permutation automorphism groups of irreducible cyclic codes
papers.abstract: The study of permutation automorphism groups of cyclic codes is a central topic in algebraic coding theory. A cyclic code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is called irreducible if its check polynomial is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and it is non-degenerate if it is not periodic. Such a non-degenerate code is standard if its permutation automorphism group is equal to the group generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius automorphism, and non-standard otherwise. In this paper, we give a complete classification of all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes, using the classification of finite simple groups. Our result shows that, apart from a small number of explicit exceptional families and their descendants under certain secondary constructions, every non-degenerate irreducible cyclic code is standard, and up to four explicit exceptions, every nonzero degenerate cyclic code is non-standard. This classification has several consequences. First, it yields a general description of non-standard linear recurring sequence subgroups, extending the earlier work of Brison and Nogueira; secondly, it establishes the Schmidt-White conjecture for all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes. Moreover, our results provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture of Berger and Charpin that almost all cyclic codes are standard.

papers.title: Singular spaces for computing the structured distance to singularity
papers.abstract: Finding the distance to singularity for a matrix is a ubiquitous problem in numerical linear algebra, and is elegantly solved by the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem. Its structured variant arises when one considers structured matrices and wants to preserve their structure. This problem is important for several matrix nearness problems that either entirely or partly reduce to a structured distance to singularity problem. In this work, we propose a new method for the structured distance to singularity problem based on singular spaces, that is, linear subspaces consisting of singular matrices. We study the properties of these spaces to guide the construction of the algorithm. In the Tikhonov regularized formulation, the method globally minimizes a certain objective function alternately in its arguments. We show that a restricted family of singular spaces suffices to attain the best possible improvement in a single iteration. In many of the numerical comparisons, the proposed method yields substantial reductions in running time when compared with existing methods, while the computed distances to singularity remain comparable. These gains allow larger problems to be solved within practical running times.

papers.title: Generalized $\mathbb{Z}_p$ toric codes as qudit low-density parity-check codes
papers.abstract: We study two-dimensional translation-invariant CSS stabilizer codes over prime-dimensional qudits on the square lattice under twisted boundary conditions, generalizing the Kitaev $\mathbb{Z}_p$ toric code by augmenting each stabilizer with two additional qudits. Using the Laurent-polynomial formalism, we adapt the Gröbner basis to compute the logical dimension $k$ efficiently, without explicitly constructing large parity-check matrices. We then perform a systematic search over various stabilizer realizations and lattice geometries for $p\in\{3,5,7,11\}$, identifying qudit low-density parity-check codes with the optimal finite-size performance. Representative examples include $[[242,10, \leq 22]]_3$ and $[[120,6, \leq 20]]_{11}$, both achieving $k d^{2}/n \leq 20$. Across the searched regime, the best observed $k d^{2}$ at fixed $n$ increases with $p$, with an empirical relation $k d^{2} = 0.0541 \, n^{2}\ln p + 3.84 \, n$, compatible with a Bravyi--Poulin--Terhal-type tradeoff when the interaction range grows with system size.

papers.title: Pathwise solutions of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by a multiplicative Hermite noise
papers.abstract: We study the viscous Burgers equation on the real line perturbed by a multiplicative noise $σ(u)\dot{Z}_t$, where $Z$ is a Hermite process of order $q\ge1$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$; the case $q=1$ is fractional Brownian motion and $q=2$ is the Rosenblatt process. The stochastic term is a Young integral and the equation is solved path by path. A transformation of Doss-Sussmann type reduces it to a parabolic equation with random coefficients and quadratic growth in the gradient, for which we prove a maximum principle and a gradient estimate of Bernstein type on short time windows. We obtain global existence and uniqueness, the pathwise bound $|u(t,x)|\le\|u_0\|_\infty+\|σ\|_\infty|Z_t|$, and a Wong-Zakai type result without correction term. All moments are finite and $\mathbb{E}\exp(λ\sup_x|u(t,x)|^{2/q})<\infty$ for small $λ$. For the Rosenblatt process with $σ\geσ_0>0$, $\mathbb{E}\,e^{λu(t,x)}$ is finite for small $λ$ and infinite for $λσ_0t^H\geθ_H$, an explicit spectral constant, while the left tail is sub-Gaussian. We show that the temporal Hölder exponent $H$ is optimal, identify the limits of the power variations of $t\mapsto u(t,x)$, and deduce consistent estimators of $H$ and of the noise intensity from one path observed at one spatial point. For $q=2$ we relate the pathwise solution to a Skorokhod formulation through the forward/Skorokhod correction formula of Čoupek, Duncan and Pasik-Duncan.

papers.title: Bench-MFG: A Benchmark Suite for Learning in Stationary Mean Field Games
papers.abstract: The rise of Mean Field Games (MFGs) has fostered a growing family of algorithms designed to solve large-scale multi-agent systems. However, the field currently lacks a standardized evaluation protocol, forcing researchers to rely on bespoke, isolated, and often simplistic environments. This fragmentation makes it difficult to assess the robustness, generalization, and failure modes of emerging methods. To address this gap, we propose a comprehensive benchmark suite for MFGs, focusing on the discrete-time, discrete-space, stationary setting. We introduce a taxonomy of problem classes, ranging from no-interaction and monotone games to potential and dynamics-coupled games, and provide prototypical environments for each. Furthermore, we present MF-Garnets, a method for generating random MFG instances to facilitate rigorous statistical testing. We benchmark a variety of learning algorithms across these environments, including a novel population-based approach (MF-PSO). To our knowledge, this is the first benchmark for MFGs.

papers.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
papers.abstract: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.

papers.title: Discovering hypergeometric series with harmonic numbers via Wilf-Zeilberger seeds
papers.abstract: By extracting coefficients from Wilf-Zeilberger pairs with respect to auxiliary parameters, we discover many nontrivial hypergeometric series involving harmonic numbers. In particular, we obtain a rapidly convergent series for the depth-two multiple zeta value $ζ(5,3)$, which appears to be the first result of its kind in the literature. We also investigate the Hilbert series attached to a WZ-seed and conjecture that it admits a remarkably simple form, suggesting the presence of an underlying graded-algebra structure associated with WZ-seeds.

papers.title: Induced Cycles of Many Lengths
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and let $\mathrm{cl}(G)$ be the number of distinct induced cycle lengths in $G$. We show that for $c,t\in \mathbb N$, every graph $G$ that does not contain an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t+1}$ or $K_{t,t}$ and satisfies $\mathrm{cl}(G) \le c$ has bounded treewidth. As a consequence, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a graph $G$ contains induced cycles of at least three distinct lengths.

papers.title: Size conditions and spectral conditions for generalized factor-critical (bicritical) graphs and $k$-$d$-critical graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\mbox{odd}(G)$ and $i(G)$ denote the number of nontrivial odd components and the number of isolated vertices of a graph $G$, respectively. The $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of a graph $G$ is defined as: $\mbox{def}_k(G)=\mathop{\text{max}}\limits_{S\subseteq V(G)}\{k\cdot i(G-S)-k|S|\} $ for even $k$; $\mbox{def}_k(G)=\mathop{\mbox{max}}\limits_{S\subseteq V(G)}\{\mbox{odd}(G-S)+k\cdot i(G-S)-k|S|\} $ for odd $k$. A $k$-barrier of a graph $G$ is the subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ that reaches the maximum value in the $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of $G$. A graph $G$ of odd order (resp. even order) is generalized factor-critical (resp. generalized bicritical) if $\emptyset$ is its only $k$-barrier. Denote by $E_G(v)$ the set of all edges incident to a vertex $v$ in $G$. A $k$-matching of a graph $G$ is a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow \{0,1,...,k\}$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)$ $\leq k$ for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. For $1\leq d\leq k$ and $d \equiv |V(G)|$(mod 2), if for any $ v \in V(G)$, there exists a $k$-matching $f$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)}f(e)=k-d$ and $\sum_{e\in E_G(u)}f(e)=k \text{ for any } u\in V(G)-\{v\}$. Then $G$ is $k$-$d$-critical. In this paper, we establish tight sufficient conditions in terms of size or spectral radius respectively for a graph $G$ to be generalized factor-critical, generalized bicritical, and $k$-$d$-critical. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the existence of four factors (namely, $\{K_2,\{C_t: t\geq 3\}\}$-factor, $\{K_2,\{C_{2t+1}:t\geq 1 \}\}$-factor, fractional perfect matching, perfect $k$-matching with even $k$) in a graph. Thus we also give size conditions and spectral radius conditions for a graph $G-v$ to have one of the four factors for any $v\in V(G)$.

papers.title: Stationary Mean-Field singular control of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
papers.abstract: Motivated by continuous-time optimal inventory management, we study a class of stationary mean-field control problems with singular controls. The dynamics are modeled by a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and the performance criterion is given by a quadratic long-time average expected cost functional. The mean-field dependence is through the stationary mean of the controlled process itself, which enters the ergodic cost functional. We relate optimal controls for the stationary mean-field control problem to equilibria of an associated stationary mean-field game. In particular, optimal controls induce equilibria of the associated game, while the converse holds true within the class of admissible controls satisfying an additional integrability requirement. Finally, we solve the stationary mean-field game explicitly, thereby obtaining an explicitly characterized optimal reflection policy for the stationary mean-field control problem within this restricted class.

papers.title: Regularity of Lipschitz free boundaries for weak solutions of Alt-Caffarelli type problems
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Serrin problem, we study weak solutions of the generalised Alt-Caffarelli problem $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$, $u = 0$ on $\partialΩ$, $\partial_νu = Q$ on $\partialΩ$. Our main result establishes that if $Ω$ is Lipschitz, then it is actually $C^{\infty}$ (provided that $f$ and $Q$ are smooth). This was known before only for viscosity solutions. As a corollary, we obtain an alternative solution of Serrin's problem in the case of Lipschitz domains. We also discuss the characterisation of the regularity of Lipschitz domains in terms of their Poisson kernel.

papers.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
papers.abstract: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
papers.abstract: We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available. The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.

papers.title: Efficient total facial coloring of combinatorial maps
papers.abstract: Let $1<k\in\mathbb{Z}$. A total coloring of a connected simple regular graph $G$ via color set $]k]_0=\{0,1,\ldots, k\}$ is efficient if each color yields an efficient dominating set, where efficient domination applies to each color class in $V(G)$. An efficient total coloring of $G$ via $[k]_0$ extends to an efficient total facial coloring $c$ of a map $M(G)$ of $G$ if it assigns a vertex-and-edge $k$-color set to the boundary cycle of each face, with the consequently missing color assigned to the face itself, so that the two adjacent faces along each edge are assigned different colors. Focus is set upon planar and toroidal maps. Modifications of $c$ are also treated by removing a perfect dominating set or a 1-factor from $G$.

papers.title: High-order augmented Lagrangian methods and robust multilevel inner solvers
papers.abstract: We analyze high-order augmented Lagrangian methods for convex optimization problems with linear constraints and construct robust multilevel inner solvers. For the high-order proximal point method, we derive energy error estimates under uniform convexity that distinguish the sublinear, linear, and superlinear regimes by comparing the regularization power with the uniform convexity exponent. Through duality, these estimates yield convergence results for the high-order augmented Lagrangian method. The primal subproblems become nearly semicoercive as the penalty parameter decreases. We address this difficulty using multilevel subspace correction methods whose subspaces decompose the constraint kernel. Applications to nonlinear diffusion, Darcy--Forchheimer flow, and the finite neuron method show how the multilevel design accommodates mean, divergence, and boundary constraints. Numerical experiments illustrate the outer convergence regimes and demonstrate parameter-robust behavior of the inner solvers across different meshes.

papers.title: On two conjectures in spectral hypergraph theory
papers.abstract: For a connected uniform hypergraph $H$, we prove two conjectures concerning the algebraic multiplicities of the spectral radius of its adjacency tensor and the zero eigenvalue of its Laplacian tensor. In particular, we establish that the algebraic multiplicity of each of these eigenvalues is equal to the cardinality of the corresponding projective eigenvariety.

papers.title: Global compactness results for fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy Sobolev operator on a bounded domain
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a Struwe type global compactness result for a class of nonlinear critical Hardy-Sobolev exponent problems driven by the fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy-Sobolev operator.

papers.title: Robust Parallel Machine Scheduling: A Comparison of Robustness Measures and Local Search Approaches
papers.abstract: In many real-world scheduling problems, the processing times of tasks are subject to uncertainty. This makes it essential to design schedules that are robust against disruptions. We distinguish between two types of robustness: quality-robust schedules keep a stable objective value under disruptions, while solution-robust schedules keep a stable schedule structure. We study how to generate schedules for the Stochastic Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem (SPMSP) with precedence constraints and release dates that are both quality- and solution-robust. To this end, we compare several robustness measures and local search algorithms that use these measures. We start with an extensive simulation study where we determine the correlation of 13 existing and 6 new robustness measures with both quality and solution robustness. Next, we use the measures with high robustness correlation as the objective in our local search algorithm to find the best way to generate schedules containing both job-machine assignments as well as buffer assignments. We use a new dynamic objective weight within our local search algorithms, which actively changes the objective weights in each iteration. We found that the best way to generate robust schedules is to use robustness measures that model the processing times with normal distribution approximations and to combine job placement and buffer assignment simultaneously.

papers.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
papers.abstract: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are Hölder curves or Hölder parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.

papers.title: A Benamou-Brenier Proximal Splitting Method for Constrained Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: The dynamic formulation of optimal transport, also known as the Benamou-Brenier formulation, has been extended to the unbalanced case by introducing a source term in the continuity equation. When this source term is penalized based on the Fisher-Rao metric, the resulting model is referred to as the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) setting, and allows for the comparison between any two positive measures without the need for equalized total mass. In recent work, we introduced a constrained variant of this model, in which affine integral equality constraints are imposed along the measure path. In the present paper, we propose a further generalization of this framework, which allows for constraints that apply not just to the density path but also to the momentum and source terms, and incorporates affine inequalities in addition to equality constraints. We prove, under suitable assumptions on the constraints, the well-posedness of the resulting class of convex variational problems. The paper is then primarily devoted to developing an effective numerical pipeline that tackles the corresponding constrained optimization problem based on finite difference discretizations and parallel proximal schemes. Our proposed framework encompasses standard balanced and unbalanced optimal transport, as well as a multitude of natural and practically relevant constraints, and we highlight its versatility via several synthetic and real data examples.

papers.title: Secondary Stiefel-Whitney numbers and corresponding cobordism groups
papers.abstract: For every relation $R$ between Stiefel-Whitney numbers of closed $(n+1)$-manifolds we consider an associated invariant $\varkappa_R$ of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds with a certain additional structure. For $n=2k-1$ and $R = w_{n+1}+v_k^2$ the invariant $\varkappa_R$ equals the Kervaire semi-characteristic. In addition, we construct the cobordism group $Ω_n^R$, which extends the unoriented cobordism group $Ω_n^O$. We show that $\varkappa_R$ is a complete invariant of $R$-cobordism classes of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds. We prove that our invariant $\varkappa_R$ and $R$-cobordism class of manifold are quadratic in the sense of Gusarov-Vassiliev-Podkorytov.

papers.title: Blowup for the multiplicative stochastic heat equation with superlinear drift
papers.abstract: We consider the stochastic heat equation with multiplicative white noise: $\partial_t u =\partial_x^2u + b(u) +σ(u) \dot W$, both on $[0,1]$ and $\mathbb R$. In the case of $[0,1]$ we show that the finite Osgood criterion on $b$ is a necessary and sufficient condition for finite-time blowup, under fairly general conditions on $σ$. In the case of $\mathbb R$ we show instantaneous explosion when we start with initial profile $u_0\equiv 1$. Our work introduces a novel approach that not only extends the work of [12] which dealt with bounded $σ$, but also provides an alternate route to proving such results. A key ingredient is a comparison result which shows that the solution on $\mathbb R$ stays above the corresponding solution on $[0,1]$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions.

papers.title: Absorbed Types and Derivations in Exponential o-Minimal Theories
papers.abstract: I analyze $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate and $\mathcal{O}$-residual types in an o-minimal expansion of an ordered field $\mathbb{E}$, where $\mathcal{O}$ is a convex valuation ring. The main result is a characterization of those exponential theories $T$ such that for all $(\mathbb{E}, \mathcal{O})\models T_{\mathrm{convex}}$ the image of any $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate type is given by some composition of translations, sign changes and exponential, of some \emph{possibly different} $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate type. I call these theories \emph{transserial}, and they encompass simply exponential theories such as $T_{\exp}$ and $T_{an, \exp}$. A consequence of the analysis is that there are no counterexamples to \emph{Tressl's signature-alternative} (cf [15]) in models of transserial theories admitting an Archimedean prime model. The characterization has at its core some arguments that use very few but fundamental properties of the valued differential field of germs at a cut in an o-minimal structure. These are abstracted in some conditions of compatibility between the derivation and the order or the derivation and the valuation, both ultimately stemming from the mean-value-theorem in o-minimal structures. I develop some basic theory around these notions and observe that in the case of few constants (i.e.\ when the valuation ring contains the constants) these notions specialize to notions thoroughly studied in arXiv:1509.02588

papers.title: Symmetric harmoniousness of odd-order groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every group of odd order is symmetric harmonious, i.e., there exists a permutation $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{\ell-1}$ of the elements of $G$ such that the consecutive products $g_0g_1,g_1g_2,\dots,g_{\ell-1}g_0$ also form a permutation of the elements of $G$ and $g_{\ell-i}=g_i^{-1}$ for all $1\le i\le \ell-1$, where $\ell=|G|$. Consequently, a group is symmetric harmonious if and only if it has odd order. We also characterize symmetric harmonious sequences in terms of complete mappings. As applications we obtain new examples of R*-sequenceable groups, and we show that every split extension of an odd-order group by a harmoniously matched group is both harmonious and \#-harmonious. Together with several new harmoniously matched groups ($D_{12},D_{16},D_{20},D_{24},Q_{16},Q_{24},A_4,S_4$), this yields many non-abelian groups that are both harmonious and \#-harmonious, including infinite families of dihedral and dicyclic groups and all $2$-nilpotent groups with an abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup that is neither cyclic nor elementary abelian and is central in its normalizer.

papers.title: Effective Resistance in Simplicial Complexes: Generalizations and Properties
papers.abstract: Originally introduced in circuit theory, the notion of effective resistance has been fruitfully exploited in graph theory, where each edge in a graph is understood as a resistor in an electric network. In this context, the effective resistance between two vertices quantifies the total opposition to current flow when a unit current is injected at one vertex and extracted at the other. As such, it encodes rich structural and geometric information about the underlying graph: it satisfies a minimum-energy principle termed Thomson's principle, defines a metric on the vertex set, relates to the topology of the graph through Foster's theorem, and determines the probability of appearance of an edge in a random spanning tree. Generalizations of effective resistance to simplicial complexes have been proposed in several forms, often formulated as matrix products of standard operators associated with the complex. We introduce a novel, basis-independent bilinear form, derived from an algebraic reinterpretation of circuit theory, that extends the classical effective resistance from graphs to simplicial complexes. This bilinear form acts on chains and cochains, and in particular, simplices and cosimplices in a simplicial complex. Our framework subsumes and unifies all existing matrix-based formulations of effective resistance. Moreover, we establish higher-order analogues of several fundamental properties known in the graph case: (i) we extend Thomson's principle to our basis-free framework; (ii) we establish metric properties for the effective resistance and its square root on chains and cycles, recovering the classical graph case; (iii) we provide a generalization of Foster's theorem to simplicial complexes; and (iv) we prove a matrix-tree theorem for higher-dimensional spanning trees, linking effective resistance to the probability of appearance of a simplex in random simplicial spanning trees.

papers.title: Sub-Diffusive Black--Scholes Model and Structure-Preserving Girsanov Transform
papers.abstract: We propose a sub-diffusive Black--Scholes model in which stock prices are governed by stochastic differential equations driven by sub-diffusions. The model captures the periods of low trading activity observed in bear markets, and it contains the classical Black--Scholes model as a special case. The sub-diffusive spot market is arbitrage-free but, in general, incomplete. We study the pricing of European contingent claims in this model. To this end, we establish a structure-preserving Girsanov transform for sub-diffusions. We use it to identify the minimal martingale measure of the model. This measure is the unique equivalent martingale measure under which the discounted stock prices are martingales driven by sub-diffusions with the same law as the original ones. Using this measure, we price every contingent claim in $L^p$ with $p>2$. For each such claim, we construct a replicating strategy that is mean self-financing and minimizes the local risk, and whose value process gives the price process of the claim. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the price of a European call option. We show that this price solves a partial differential equation with a fractional derivative in time, which we call the time-fractional Black--Scholes equation.

papers.title: Emerging consecutive pattern avoidance
papers.abstract: In this note we study the asymptotic popularity, that is, the limit probability to find a given consecutive pattern at a random position in a random permutation in the eighteen classes of permutations avoiding at least two length 3 consecutive patterns. We show that for ten classes, this popularity can be readily deduced from the structure of the permutations. By combining analytical and bijective approaches, we study in detail two more involved cases. The problem remains open for five classes.

papers.title: Generalized Divisors and Canonical Coarsening on Tame Deligne-Mumford Curves
papers.abstract: We study effective generalized divisors on reduced tame Deligne-Mumford curves over $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $G_1$ and $S_2$. Canonical coarsening maps divisor ideals to coarse canonical lattices. We describe its fibres by exact intervals of equivariant lattices. For flat projective finite-quotient families of geometrically reduced Gorenstein curves over locally Noetherian bases, with finite constant groups and the stated relative-duality and base-change hypotheses, we construct projective invariant-Quot schemes for fixed canonical lattices with finite flat quotients and prescribed quotient representations. A nontrivial marked deformation preserves the coarse ring, normalization, conductor and entire fixed canonical fibre, while a length-four isotypic jet detects its parameter. We compute the full normalization and conductor correction after support restriction on an explicit rank-three chart. As a module, the correction splits into one surface and two line canonical modules, with a common grading shift. The corresponding square-zero algebra extension is nonsplit. The full source-support pair is compared through second order. Exact computational certificates accompany the proofs.

papers.title: DE-Sinc approximation for unilateral rapidly decreasing functions and its computable error bound
papers.abstract: The Sinc approximation is highly effective for functions that decay rapidly at both ends of the real axis. For unilateral rapidly decreasing functions, which decay algebraically as $t\to-\infty$ and exponentially as $t\to\infty$, an appropriate variable transformation is required. Existing single-exponential transformations for this class of functions yield only root-exponential convergence, even when improved transformations are employed. This paper develops a double-exponential (DE)-Sinc approximation based on the transformation $t=2\sinh(\log(\log(1+\exp(π\sinh x))))$, which was previously introduced for numerical integration. The main contribution is a rigorous and computable error bound of order $\operatorname{O}(\exp(-cn/\log n))$ with a constant explicitly expressed in terms of the problem parameters. Under the stated assumptions, the resulting approximation achieves almost exponential convergence and is suitable for computation with guaranteed accuracy. Numerical examples satisfying these assumptions confirm the predicted convergence behavior and the validity of the derived error bound.

papers.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
papers.abstract: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-Rényi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

papers.title: Convergence of optimizers implies eigenvalues filtering at equilibrium
papers.abstract: Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard--Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic $C^2$ functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.

papers.title: The ribbon category of representations of a crossed module
papers.abstract: The theory of representations of a crossed module is a direct generalization of the theory of representations of groups. For a finite group G, the Drinfeld quantum double of the group G is a Hopf algebra that represents a special case of crossed module of finite groups. Here we study how to extend the construction of the Drinfeld quantum double for any other kind of crossed module of finite groups. This leads to a Hopf algebra D(G,H) that presents similarities with a Drinfeld double. We then study simple subalgebras of D(G,H) and give two isomorphisms for the decomposition into a product of simple subalgebras. We then study the category D(G,H)-mod^Fd of finite dimensional modules over D(G,H), which turns out to be isomorphic to the category of finite dimensional representations of finite crossed modules of groups. These categories being monoidal, we also study links between direct sums of simple objects and tensor products of simple objects and give some results for a Clebsch-Gordan formula. We, in this context, present and develop the character theory for representations of crossed modules of finite groups, and detail the proofs. We then study the category itself, which leads to some ribbon invariants.

papers.title: Noise estimation of SDE from a single data trajectory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a pathwise data-driven framework for model discovery of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) from a single trajectory, without requiring the ergodicity or stationary assumption on the underlying continuous process. By combining (stochastic) Taylor expansions with Girsanov transformations, and using the drift function's initial value as input, we construct drift estimators while simultaneously recovering the model noise. This drift is unique up to the fixed underlying Brownian sample path, in line with pathwise unique Rough-Smooth decomposition. This allows us to recover the underlying $\mathbb P$ Brownian motion increments for the observer path $ω$. Building on these estimators, we introduce the first stochastic Sparse Identification of Stochastic Differential Equation (SSISDE) algorithm, capable of identifying the governing SDE dynamics from a single observed trajectory without requiring ergodicity or stationarity. To validate the proposed approach, we conduct numerical experiments with both linear and quadratic drift-diffusion functions. Among these, the Black-Scholes SDE is included as a representative case of a system that does not satisfy ergodicity or stationarity.

papers.title: New nonabelian Hodge graphs from twisted irregular connections
papers.abstract: It is known that any meromorphic connection on the Riemann sphere determines a finite diagram (a generalised graph, possibly with negative edge multiplicities), which is invariant under the Fourier-Laplace transform. If the connection has regular singularities at finite distance and an untwisted irregular singularity at infinity, the diagram is a supernova graph, and the quiver modularity theorem of Boalch/Hiroe-Yamakawa shows that the corresponding nonabelian Hodge moduli space contains the Nakajima quiver variety of the graph as an open subset. In this note, motivated by the question of classifying these nonabelian Hodge diagrams, we obtain a necessary condition satisfied by all (core) nonabelian Hodge diagrams, involving ultrametric inequalities. We use this to investigate the class of such diagrams that are graphs (without edge-loops nor negative multiplicities), as well as certain special classes of nonabelian Hodge graphs: we show that there exist nonabelian Hodge graphs beyond the setting of the quiver modularity theorem, and obtain characterisations of fission graphs and of simply-laced nonabelian Hodge graphs.

papers.title: A posteriori existence for the Keller-Segel model via a finite volume - finite element scheme
papers.abstract: We derive two forms of conditional a posteriori error estimates for a finite volume scheme approximating the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system. The estimates control the error in the $L^\infty(0,T, L^2(Ω))$-norm and exhibit linear convergence in the mesh size, as observed in numerical experiments. Crucially, we show that, as long as the condition of the error estimate is satisfied, a weak solution exists. This means, as long as the numerical solution has good properties, we can rigorously infer existence of an exact solution.

papers.title: Dividends of the BKR Equivalence: Quantifying the Dichotomy for Skyscraper Sheaves
papers.abstract: Let $G\subset \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb C)$ be a nontrivial finite abelian subgroup and let $Ψ\colon D^b_G(\mathbb{C}^3) \xrightarrow{\sim} D^b(G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3))$ denote the Bridgeland--King--Reid equivalence. For every nontrivial character $χ$ of $G$, the transform of the corresponding skyscraper sheaf at the origin has exactly one nonzero cohomology sheaf, in degree $0$ or $-1$. We study the proportion $\mathcal B_0$ of characters for which this degree is zero. Using derived Reid's recipe, we establish the sharp bounds $1/3\leq\mathcal B_0\leq1$. For isolated quotient singularities, the lower bound sharpens to $1/2$, and we exhibit an explicit family of cyclic quotients indexed by positive integers $m$ for which $\mathcal{B}_0 \to 1$ as $m \to \infty$. We show that $\mathcal B_0=1$ precisely when the fiber over the origin has dimension at most one, and relate $\mathcal B_0$ to the Picard rank of $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ and the number of compact exceptional divisors of the resolution $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^3/G$. A theorem of Craw--Lin--Yamagishi translates these estimates into bounds for the coordinate facets of the $G$-Hilbert GIT chamber. We discuss how the proportion $\mathcal{B}_0$ adapts to non-abelian finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: From Hopf Algebras in Model Categories to Hopf Algebras in $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We show that algebra objects in model categories can be transferred to algebra objects in $\infty$-categories, without any cofibrancy or fibrancy assumptions on the algebra. We furthermore show under some mild extra assumptions that this correspondence extends to commutative bialgebras and to commutative Hopf algebras.

papers.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
papers.abstract: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Erös--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fréchet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

papers.title: Spare Strategy Analysis and Design for Mega Satellite Constellations Using Markov Chain
papers.abstract: This paper presents a Markov-chain-based method for the early-phase analysis and design of spare-management architectures for large-scale satellite constellations. To assess the long-run viability of such concepts of operations, satellite failure and replenishment processes are modeled as Markov chains and analyzed through their stationary solution. We reinvestigate an indirect spare strategy, modeled as a multi-echelon periodic-review reorder-point/order-quantity policy, in which spares are first delivered to parking orbits and then transferred to constellation planes. The stock levels in constellation and parking orbits are each modeled as independent Markov chains, and a fixed-point iteration yields a consistent joint stationary solution that describes the strategy's average behavior. This approach accurately captures the stochastic interplay within a multi-echelon model driven by orbital mechanics, avoiding the aggregation assumptions of prior works and remaining valid across a wider operating domain. Building on this fast, accurate analysis, we formulate an optimization problem and solve it via a genetic algorithm. Finally, we demonstrate the practical value of both the analysis method and the optimization framework in a real-world mega-constellation case study.

papers.title: Finite dimensional approximations for Hilbert space operators and applications in Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a unified framework for quasidiagonal and Følner-type approximations of linear operators on Hilbert spaces. These approximations (originally formulated for bounded operators and operator algebras) involve sequences of non-zero finite rank orthogonal projections that asymptotically commute with the operator -- either in norm (quasidiagonal) or in mean (Følner). Such structures guarantee spectral approximation results in terms of their finite sections. We extend this theory to unbounded, densely defined closable operators, establishing a generalization of Halmos' classical result: every closable quasidiagonal operator is a compact perturbation of a closable block-diagonal operator on the same domain. Likewise, we introduce sparse Følner sequences and establish an interplay between quasidiagonal approximations and the existence of sparse Følner sequences. The theoretical developments are illustrated with explicit examples using different types of weighted shifts and applied to quantum mechanical models, including a detailed treatment of the Weyl algebra and its Schrödinger representation.

papers.title: Generic classification of the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$
papers.abstract: In this article we show that the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$ are generically classifiable by the inverse temperature of their unique KMS state. Along the way, we show that a large class of quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_n$ are generically equivariantly $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and their corresponding dual action has the Rokhlin property generically.

papers.title: Learning from the past in an irreversible investment problem
papers.abstract: We consider an irreversible investment problem under incomplete information, where the investor decides whether and when to make investments in a project. Upon investment, the investor acquires previously hidden information from the project's past (''learning from the past''), and so the learning rate of the problem is controlled by investing. We set up this original problem as a recursively defined stopping problem with a learning-from-the-past effect. We show that, under general conditions, at each recursion step there exists a one-sided stopping boundary. We proceed to present the optimal investment strategy as a sequence of semi-explicit stopping boundaries derived from the smooth fit conditions of the corresponding free-boundary problems. Feasibility of our approach is then demonstrated by solving example boundaries numerically and by performing sensitivity analysis with respect to different model parameters.

papers.title: Thermodynamics and stability of equilibrium/non-equilibrium steady states in thermodynamically isolated/open systems -- case study for compressible heat conducting fluid
papers.abstract: We review all the calculations necessary for the construction of a Lyapunov like functional for nonlinear stability analysis of steady states in thermodynamically isolated/open systems composed of compressible heat conducting fluids.

papers.title: Cohomology and homotopy theory of Nijenhuis family algebras
papers.abstract: Nijenhuis family algebras generalize Nijenhuis associative algebras, the operator being replaced by a family of operators labelled by a semigroup $Ω$. In this paper, we introduce Nijenhuis family bimodules and show that a Nijenhuis family algebra gives rise to an associative algebra on ${A\ot\bkΩ}$. We realize Nijenhuis families and Nijenhuis family algebras as Maurer--Cartan elements of a graded Lie algebra and of an $L_\infty$-algebra. We define the cohomology of a Nijenhuis family algebra with coefficients in a bimodule via a mapping cone, obtain a long exact sequence, and show that infinitesimal deformations are classified by the second cohomology group. Finally, we show that strict homotopy Nijenhuis family algebras induce $A_\infty$-algebras on ${A\ot\bkΩ}$.

papers.title: M-estimation for Gaussian processes with time-inhomogeneous drifts from high-frequency data
papers.abstract: We study drift and covariance estimation for a stationary Gaussian process with an integrated deterministic drift, observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of an increment least-squares estimator under conditions on drift accumulation and the full covariance of the weighted increments. For directly Riemann integrable drifts, this estimator need not be consistent, as an explicit example shows. Covariance parameters can nevertheless be estimated consistently when the drift decays sufficiently fast. For smooth short-range kernels, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the centered sample variance and the normalized increment second moment, with rate $\sqrt{T_n}$. These statistics require no drift estimate and identify both parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The results clarify how drift accumulation and increment dependence affect the two estimation problems.

papers.title: Smallest gaps of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas
papers.abstract: We consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas with a general potential at the determinantal temperature, or equivalently, the eigenvalues of random normal matrices. We prove that the smallest gaps between particles are typically of order $n^{-3/4}$, and that the associated joint point process of gap locations and gap sizes, after rescaling the gaps by $n^{3/4}$, converges to a Poisson point process. As a consequence, we show that the $k$-th smallest rescaled gap has a limiting density proportional to $x^{4k-1}e^{-\frac{\mathcal{J}}{4}x^{4}}$, where $\mathcal{J}=π^{2}\int ρ(z)^{3}d^{2}z$ and $ρ$ is the density of the equilibrium measure. This generalizes a result of Shi and Jiang beyond the quadratic potential.

papers.title: Efficient Online Mirror Descent Stochastic Approximation for Multi-Stage Stochastic Programming
papers.abstract: We study the unconstrained and the minimax saddle point variants of the convex multi-stage stochastic programming problem, where consecutive decisions are coupled through the objective functions, rather than through the constraints. We approach the problems from the infinite-dimensional policy perspective, but consider an online setting where only the policies corresponding to the actual realization of the underlying stochastic process are needed. This leads to a tractable formulation, where the dimension of the output is linear in the number of stages $T$. We propose hypothetical Mirror Descent Stochastic Approximation (MDSA) for the infinite-dimensional policies using stochastic conditional gradients. By taking advantage of the decomposability of the updates across stages and realizations of the underlying stochastic process, we show that the proposed MDSA algorithms admit efficient online implementation. In the moderate-accuracy regime, where the allowed total error scales linearly with $T$, the oracle complexity is linear in $T$ and the extra space needed is independent of $T$.

papers.title: Variational Properties and KL Exponent of Square-Transformed Polyhedral Composite Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider one of the most common reparameterization techniques, the square transformation. Assuming the original objective function is the sum of a smooth function and a polyhedral function, we study the variational properties of the objective function after reparameterization. In particular, we first study the minimal norm of the subdifferential of the reparameterized objective function. Second, we compute the second subderivative of the reparameterized objective function on a linear subspace, which allows us to fully characterize the subclass of stationary points of the reparameterized objective function that correspond to stationary points of the original objective function. Finally, utilizing the representation of the minimal norm of the subdifferential, we show that the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz (KL) exponent of the reparameterized function can be deduced from that of the original function. Applications to concrete optimization models are discussed.

papers.title: The Rabin cryptosystem over number fields
papers.abstract: We extend Rabin's cryptosystem to general number fields. We show that recovery of a random plaintext from its ciphertext is as hard as the integer factorisation problem, provided the modulus in our scheme has been chosen carefully. We investigate the performance of our new cryptosystem in comparison with the classical Rabin scheme and a more recent version over the Gaussian integers.

papers.title: On steady and expanding Ricci solitons with asymptotic symmetries
papers.abstract: We establish a symmetry principle for asymptotically cylindrical steady gradient Ricci solitons and asymptotically conical expanding gradient Ricci solitons. Our symmetry principle bounds the loss of symmetry from the asymptotic link to the interior by the dimension of the weighted $L^2$ kernel of the stability operator. For homogeneous links, suitable kernel bounds imply that the soliton has an isometric action of cohomogeneity one. The results apply in particular to strictly linear stable solitons, require no curvature sign assumptions, and allow orbifold singular sets of codimension at least four. Applications include characterizations of Bryant solitons and global $U(m)$-symmetry results for solitons with quotient-Berger asymptotic links. In dimension four, we classify asymptotically $SU(2)/Γ$-cylindrical steady gradient Ricci solitons with trivial weighted kernel as finite quotients of Bryant or Appleton solitons. Under the same kernel condition, we also establish toric symmetry for asymptotically lens-cylindrical steady solitons.

papers.title: On the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius, fractional matching and factors of graphs
papers.abstract: The distance signless Laplacian matrix of a graph $G$ is define as $Q(G)=$Tr$(G)+D(G)$, where Tr$(G)$ and $D(G)$ are the diagonal matrix of vertex transmissions and the distance matrix of $G$, respectively. Denote by $E_G(v)$ the set of all edges incident to a vertex $v$ in $G$. A fractional matching of a graph $G$ is a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow [0,1]$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)\leq 1$ for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. The fractional matching number $μ_f(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the maximum value of $ \sum_{e\in E(G)} f(e)$ over all fractional matchings. Given subgraphs $H_1, H_2,...,H_k$ of $G$, a $\{H_1, H_2,...,H_k\}$-factor of $G$ is a spanning subgraph $F$ in which each connected component is isomorphic to one of $H_1, H_2,...,H_k$. In this paper, we establish a upper bound for the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius of a graph $G$ of order $n$ to guarantee that $μ_f(G)> \frac{n-k}{2}$, where $1\leq k<n$ is an integer. Besides, we also provide a sufficient condition based on distance signless Laplacian spectral radius to guarantee the existence of a $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in a graph, where $k \geq 3$ is an integer.

papers.title: Cohomological Mackey formula for quotient stacks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a restriction morphism on the critical cohomology of an equivariant Landau-Ginzburg model associated to a representation of a reductive group equipped with an invariant function. We show a compatibility formula between this restriction map and the induction map considered in earlier work in the form of a Mackey-type formula, thereby giving the critical cohomology the structure of a localized induction-restriction system. In the case of quivers, our formulas give the localized coproduct of Davison for cohomological Hall algebras of quivers with potential.

papers.title: A New Approach to Inspect Weakly Coupled Logistic Systems and their Asymptotic Behavior
papers.abstract: We consider the weakly coupled elliptic system of logistic type, \begin{equation} \begin{cases} -Δu &=μ_1u- |u|^{p-2}u+ β|u|^{\frac{p}{2}-2}u |v|{^{\frac{p}{2}}}\mbox{ in }Ω, -Δv & =μ_2 v- |v|^{p-2}v+β|u|^{\frac{p}{2}}|v|^{\frac{p}{2}-2}v \mbox{ in }Ω, \ \ u,v &\in H_0^1(Ω), \end{cases} \end{equation} where $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded connected domain with $N\geq 2$, $2< p < 2^*$, $λ_1(Ω)< μ_1\leqμ_2$, and $λ_1(Ω)$ denotes the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in $Ω$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We say the system is competitive if $β<0$ and cooperative if $β>0$, for $β\in \mathbb{R}$. We prove the existence and multiplicity of solutions to the problem \eqref{LS} in alternative variational frameworks, depending on the range of the parameter $β.$ We do not rely on bifurcation or degree theory, which have been used in the literature for logistic-type problems. Instead, the novelty is to obtain min-max type solutions by exploiting the different geometry of the functional associated with the logistic problem. In case $N\geq 2$, we establish existence and multiplicity results for different ranges of the coupling parameter, considering both the case \(2<p<4\) and the classical case \(p=4\). We also investigate the asymptotic behavior of selected solutions as \(β\to1^-\) and \(β\to-\infty\).} \textsc{Key words: Logistic System, Ground State Solution, Linking structure, Seminodal Solution.}{\small} \textsc{MSC 2020: } {\small 35J15 35J20, 35J60, 62J12.}

papers.title: Adaptive refinement in defeaturing problems via an equilibrated flux a posteriori error estimator
papers.abstract: An adaptive refinement strategy, based on an equilibrated flux a posteriori error estimator, is proposed in the context of defeaturing problems. Defeaturing consists of removing features from complex domains to simplify mesh generation and reduce the computational cost of simulations. It is a common procedure, for example, in computer aided design for simulation-based manufacturing. However, depending on the problem at hand, geometrical simplification may significantly deteriorate the accuracy of the solution. The proposed adaptive strategy is hence twofold: starting from a defeatured geometry, it iteratively performs both standard mesh refinement and geometrical refinement by selecting, at each step, which features must be reintroduced to significantly improve accuracy. Similar adaptive strategies have been previously developed using residual-based error estimators within an IGA framework. Here, instead, we extend a previously developed equilibrated flux a posteriori error analysis, designed for standard finite element discretizations, to make it fully applicable within the adaptive procedure. In particular, we address the assembly of the equilibrated flux estimator in presence of elements trimmed by the boundary of included features, adopting an unfitted finite element strategy to handle feature inclusion. The resulting estimator allows us to bound both the defeaturing and the numerical sources of error, with additional contributions accounting for the weak imposition of boundary conditions.

papers.title: Finite element form-valued forms: Construction
papers.abstract: We provide a finite element discretization of $\ell$-form-valued $k$-forms on triangulation in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ for general $k$, $\ell$ and $n$ and any polynomial degree. The construction generalizes finite element Whitney forms for the de~Rham complex and their higher-order and distributional versions, the Regge finite elements and the Christiansen--Regge elasticity complex, the TDNNS element for symmetric stress tensors, the MCS element for traceless matrix fields, the Hellan--Herrmann--Johnson (HHJ) elements for biharmonic equations, and discrete divdiv and Hessian complexes in [Hu, Lin, and Zhang, 2025]. The construction discretizes the Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) diagrams. Applications of the construction include discretization of strain and stress tensors in continuum mechanics and metric and curvature tensors in differential geometry in any dimension.

papers.title: Continuous-time mean field games: a primal-dual characterization
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a primal-dual formulation for continuous-time mean field games (MFGs) and provides a complete analytical characterization of the set of all mean field equilibria (MFEs). We reformulate the representative player's control problem as a linear program over occupation measures and derive its dual formulation over smooth subsolutions of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation. This primal-dual formulation yields a verification theorem for MFEs under measurable coefficients and provides necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing all MFEs under a strong duality condition. We establish this strong duality for nondegenerate diffusions with Hölder continuous coefficients through a new global $C^{2,α}$ regularity result for fully nonlinear parabolic HJB equations. A key insight is that the dual variable need only coincide with the HJB solution on the support of the mean field flow. Compared with existing approaches, our characterization requires neither convexity of the Hamiltonian nor uniqueness of its optimizer, accommodates relaxed equilibria, and remains applicable when the HJB equation lacks classical solutions.

papers.title: Navigating Demand Uncertainty in Container Shipping: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Enabling Adaptive and Feasible Master Stowage Planning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has successfully solved various deterministic and stochastic planning problems. However, conventional RL struggles with complex real-world constraints, particularly when feasibility is explicit and depends on the current state or trajectory. In this work, we address stochastic sequential decision-making with state-dependent constraints through a real-world case study of the master stowage planning problem in container shipping, which aims to optimize revenue and costs under demand uncertainty and operational constraints. We propose a deep RL framework with an encoder-decoder model that integrates problem instance, solution, and uncertainty information to guide planning. We introduce differentiable projection layers that enforce convex polyhedral constraints, while Jacobian corrections offset the projections to yield unbiased policy gradient estimates. Experiments show that our model efficiently finds adaptive, feasible solutions that generalize across distribution shifts and scale to longer planning horizons, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in constrained RL and stochastic programming. As such, our policies enable adaptive, uncertainty-aware planning that can support resilient and sustainable supply chains.

papers.title: Finite convergence and minimizer extraction in moment relaxations with correlative sparsity
papers.abstract: We identify a new sufficient condition for the finite convergence of moment relaxations of polynomial optimization problems with correlative sparsity. This condition, which follows from a solution to a correlatively sparse version of the classical truncated moment problem, requires that certain moment matrices admit a flat extension and that the variable cliques underpinning the relaxation satisfy a "running intersection" property. We also describe an algorithm that, when these conditions are met, extracts at least as many minimizers for the original polynomial optimization problem as the largest rank of the moment matrices in its relaxation. Our results, along with the necessity of the running intersection property, are illustrated with examples.

papers.title: Graded String Diagrams with Applications in Probabilistic Reasoning
papers.abstract: We introduce string diagrams for graded symmetric monoidal categories. Our approach includes a definition of graded monoidal theory and the corresponding freely generated syntactic category. The para construction on monoidal actegories is a motivating example for our framework, and we show how an axiomatic presentation of the resulting category $\mathbf{Para}(\mathbb{G},\mathbf{C})$ may be modularly obtained from presentations for $\mathbb{G}$ and $\mathbf{C}$. We demonstrate three different applications of our diagrammatic language under the same theme: probabilistic reasoning. First, we show how to axiomatise a variant of the graded category $\mathbf{ImP}$, recently introduced by Liell-Cock and Staton to model imprecise probability. This culminates in a representation, as string diagrams with grading wires, of programs with primitives for nondeterministic and probabilistic choices and conditioning. Second, we exploit our modular presentation result to provide a new proof for a presentation of $\mathbf{Gauss}$, the category of Gaussian stochastic maps. Third, we use grading wires to represent causal interventions on Bayesian networks.

papers.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over quartic number fields with rational $j$-invariant
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve defined over a quartic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with $j(E)\in\mathbb{Q}$. We classify the possible group structures of $E(K)_{\mathrm{tors}}$, concluding that the only additional possibilities, besides those occuring over quartic fields by base change from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, are $\mathbb{Z}/17\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/21\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Geometry of multidimensional Farey summation algorithm and frieze patterns
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a new geometric approach to subtractive continued fraction algorithms in high dimensions. We adapt a version of Farey summation to the geometric techniques proposed by F. Klein in 1895. More specifically we introduce Farey polyhedra and their sails that generalise respectively Klein polyhedra and their sails, and show similar duality properties of the Farey sail integer invariants. The construction of Farey sails is based on the multidimensional generalisation of the Farey tessellation provided by a modification of the continued fraction algorithm introduced by R. W. J. Meester. We classify Farey polyhedra in the combinatorial terms of prismatic diagrams. Prismatic diagrams extend boat polygons introduced by S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko in the two-dimensional case. As one of the applications of the new theory we get a multidimensional version of Conway-Coxeter frieze patterns. We show that multidimensional frieze patterns satisfy generalised Ptolemy relations.

papers.title: On the Stokes conjecture for compressible gravity waves of extreme form
papers.abstract: In 1880, G. G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol.I] examined an extreme two-dimensional irrotational periodic traveling water wave under the influence of gravity and conjectured a symmetric corner of \(120^\circ\) at the crest. The conjecture was first proved rigorously by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. In the early 2010s, Varvarua and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] revisited the conjecture by introducing a novel geometric method, which provided an affirmative answer to the conjecture without requiring the structural assumptions used in earlier works, such as the isolation of the stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the free surface. The main purpose of this paper is to establish the validity of the Stokes conjecture in the context of compressible gravity water waves. More precisely, we prove that, at each stagnation point of a compressible gravity water wave, a sharp crest with an included angle of \(120^\circ\) forms, which gives the first rigorous confirmation of the compressible counterpart of the classical Stokes conjecture of 1880. The central aspect of our approach is the discovery of a new monotonicity formula and a modified version of it for quasilinear free boundary problems of Bernoulli type. Another key ingredient is a new nonlinear frequency formula, which we combine with the concentration-cancellation theory of Evans and Muller [J. Amer. Math. Soc. 7 (1994)]. These newly developed monotonicity formulas are valid for nonlinear problems and enable us to carry out a blow-up analysis at each stagnation point and to provide a complete classification of the blow-up limits near each stagnation point.

papers.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
papers.abstract: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.

papers.title: Some invariants of totally disconnected locally compact groups: cohomology and combinatorics
papers.abstract: The paper investigates two invariants for totally disconnected locally compact (t.d.l.c.) groups: the number of ends and the rational discrete cohomological dimension. Firstly, for a compactly generated t.d.l.c. group $G$, it is shown that its number of ends can be expressed in terms of the low-dimensional rational discrete cohomology of $G$, generalising a notable theorem by E. Specker to the t.d.l.c. setting. Secondly, we focus on a t.d.l.c. group $G$ acting under suitable conditions on a building $Δ$, showing that both the number of ends and the rational cohomological dimension of $G$ are related to those of the Weyl group associated to $Δ$. In special cases, we compare the rational discrete cohomological dimension of $G$ to its flat-rank, and in the appendix we provide examples for which these two invariants coincide. Finally, for t.d.l.c. groups with rational discrete cohomological dimension one that act properly and chamber-transitively on locally finite buildings, we explicitly construct a proper cocompact action on a tree out of the action on the building. All the results of independent interest in Coxeter theory have been included in the appendix.

papers.title: A phase transition for the cokernels of random band matrices over the p-adic integers
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}_n$ be an $n\times n$ Haar-uniform band matrix over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with band width $w_n$. We prove that $\text{cok}(\mathbf{B}_n)$ has Cohen-Lenstra limiting distribution if and only if \[\lim_{n\to\infty} \left(w_n-\log_p(n)\right)=+\infty.\]

papers.title: Existence of two-dimensional deep capillary solitary water waves with constant vorticity
papers.abstract: We consider two-dimensional capillary water waves with nonzero constant vorticity in infinite depth. We first derive the Babenko equation that describes the profile of the solitary wave. When the velocity $c$ is close to a critical velocity, the Babenko equation can be reduced to the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation plus perturbative error. This gives the existence of small-amplitude solitary wave solutions for the water wave system with constant vorticity whose profiles are close to solutions of the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation.

papers.title: Semihomogenous vector bundles, $\mathbb Q$-twisted sheaves, duality, and linear systems on abelian varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we point out the natural relation between $\mathbb Q$-twisted objects of the derived category of abelian varieties, cohomological rank functions, and semihomogeneous vector bundles. We apply this to two basic classes of objects, corresponding to each other via the Fourier-Mukai-Poincaré transform: positive twists of the ideal sheaf of one point and of the evaluation complexes of ample simple semihomogeneous vector bundles. This naturally leads to the introduction of $\mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$- graded section modules associated to line bundles on abelian varieties built by means of semihomogeneous vector bundles (containing the usual section rings). We prove a duality relation between such modules associated to dual polarizations, which is not visible at the level of the usual section rings. Other applications include formulas relating the thresholds of relevant cohomological rank functions appearing in this context. As a consequence we show a lower bound for the base point free threshold of a polarization in function of its type, and some obstructions to surjectivity of multiplication maps of global sections of certain line bundles.

papers.title: A Non-Markovian Approach to a Stochastic Rumor Dynamics with Cognitive Deliberation
papers.abstract: We introduce a non-Markovian rumor model on a complete graph of $n$ vertices, integrating the classical interactional framework of Daley and Kendall (1964) with modern cognitive insights into misinformation. Unlike traditional Markovian models, our approach incorporates a deliberation delay -- a decision-making window where individuals evaluate information before committing to dissemination or refutation. We establish a Functional Law of Large Numbers (FLLN) and a Functional Central Limit Theorem (FCLT) to characterize the asymptotic behavior and diffusion-scaled fluctuations of the process.

papers.title: Inventory Control and Storage Design via an $L^{\infty}$-control approach
papers.abstract: Inventory control traditionally focuses on pricing and production rates, while physical storage capacity is typically fixed at the initial design stage. This paper addresses this relatively unexplored aspect by formulating a non-standard optimal control problem. The objective combines the classical integral term, capturing inventory-related costs, with an L^\infty-term, representing the maximum inventory level over the planning horizon. We first establish a relationship between the optimal pricing and production-rate policies, reducing the problem's dimensionality. Building on our earlier framework, we establish the existence of an optimal relaxed control and obtain an ε-optimal pure control for the reduced problem through smooth approximation. Numerical solutions of the resulting approximate problem demonstrate a substantial reduction in required storage capacity, with a negligible loss in net revenue (less than 6%), after accounting for shortage, holding, and production costs. We also observe that increasing the weight of the L^\infty-component reduces fluctuations in the inventory trajectory. These findings are particularly relevant when future demand information is incomplete or unavailable. In such settings, dynamically adjusting pricing and production policies to keep inventory levels close to zero can substantially reduce storage requirements with only a negligible loss in net revenue. Our results highlight the potential of incorporating inventory-level considerations directly into operational decision-making, particularly when physical storage capacity can be designed flexibly.

papers.title: Bounding Shortest Closed Geodesics with Diameter on compact 2-dimensional Orbifolds Homeomorphic to $S^2$
papers.abstract: Length-bounded sweepouts provide a method for bounding the length of the shortest closed geodesic of a closed manifold. In this paper, we generalize this approach to the case of compact 2-dimensional orbifolds homeomorphic to S^2 as well as compact 2-dimensional orbifolds with finite orbifold fundamental groups. We establish an inequality for the length of the shortest closed orbifold geodesic in terms of the diameter.

papers.title: Subgroup Separability of Artin Groups II
papers.abstract: In this short note, we establish a more concrete characterization of subgroup separable (LERF) Artin groups, building on a previously known criterion. Specifically, we prove an Artin group is LERF if and only if its underlying graph does not contain certain induced subgraphs, thus providing a more direct generalization of the Metaftsis-Raptis criterion for RAAGs. Consequently, we prove every LERF Artin group is coherent and obtain a graph condition for coherent Artin groups to be LERF.

papers.title: The multiples of a numerical semigroup
papers.abstract: Given two numerical semigroups $S$ and $T$ we say that $T$ is a multiple of $S$ if there exists an integer $d \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$ such that $S = \{x \in \mathbb{N} \mid d x \in T\}$. In this paper we study the family of multiples of a (fixed) numerical semigroup. We also address the open problem of finding numerical semigroups of embedding dimension $e$ without any quotient of embedding dimension less than $e$, and provide new families with this property.

papers.title: Arithmetic varieties of numerical semigroups
papers.abstract: In this paper we present the notion of arithmetic variety for numerical semigroups. We study various aspects related to these varieties such as the smallest arithmetic that contains a set of numerical semigroups and we exhibit the root three associated with an arithmetic variety. This tree is not locally finite; however, if the Frobenius number is fixed, the tree has finitely many nodes and algorithms can be developed. All algorithms provided in this article include their (non-debugged) implementation in GAP.

papers.title: Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics
papers.abstract: We derive the heat equation for the thermal energy under diffusive space-time scaling for a purely deterministic microscopic dynamics satisfying Newton equations perturbed by an external chaotic force acting like a magnetic field.

papers.title: Data-proximal null-space networks for inverse problems
papers.abstract: Inverse problems with incomplete data are severely ill-posed and require regularization. Learned reconstructions incorporate prior information effectively, but their regularization properties are less well understood than those of classical variational methods. We propose data-proximal null-space networks, which post-process an initial reconstruction obtained by a classical regularization method and extend null-space networks by allowing learned corrections that are not restricted to the null space, while bounding their effect on the measured data by a prescribed tolerance. Combined with a convergent, possibly nonlinear regularization method, these networks yield convergent regularization methods with convergence rates and data-proximity bounds. A calmness-based analysis covers fixed networks with radial clipping even when the operator range is not closed; their correction outside the null space vanishes in the limit, so that they differ from null-space networks only at positive noise levels. For the limited-angle Radon transform, exact data consistency preserves the visible singularities of the initial reconstruction, whereas data proximity controls the visible error in a weak Sobolev norm proportional to the data norm, but not its singularities. For compactly supported objects, null-space networks act trivially, whereas data-proximal networks can still correct nearly invisible components. In limited-angle computed tomography, data-proximal networks substantially improve on null-space networks and, unlike residual networks, guarantee a prescribed bound on the data change.

papers.title: Calligraphs and sphere realizations
papers.abstract: We introduce a recursive procedure for computing the number of realizations of a minimally rigid graph on the sphere up to rotations. We accomplish this by combining two ingredients. The first is a framework that allows us to think of such realizations as of elements of a moduli space of stable rational curves with marked points. The second is the idea of splitting a minimally rigid graph into two subgraphs, called calligraphs, that admit one degree of freedom and that share only a single edge and a further vertex. This idea has been recently employed for realizations of graphs in the plane up to isometries. The key result is that we can associate to a calligraph a triple of natural numbers with a special property: whenever a minimally rigid graph is split into two calligraphs, the number of realizations of the former equals the product of the two triples of the latter, where this product is specified by a fixed quadratic form.
