The conjecture states that every Boolean function in an even number of variables $n$ of algebraic degree at most $n/2$ can be written as the sum of two bent functions. We show that for every $n=2^k\geq 8$, the symmetric function $F_n=1+σ_2+σ_4+σ_6+\cdots+σ_{n/2}$ has degree $n/2$ and cannot be written as a sum of at most two bent functions. Here $σ_j$ is the elementary symmetric Boolean polynomial of degree $j$. Furthermore, we show that the eight-variable member of this family can be represented as the sum of exactly three bent functions. Using the connection between bent-sum decompositions and derivatives of bent functions, we also obtain an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions that cannot be derivatives of bent functions.

papers.title: Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one
papers.abstract: We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.

papers.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
papers.abstract: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. Its remaining life expectancy has no known closed form, and numerical evaluation alone does not reveal how the immaturity hazard enters it. We show that the remaining-lifetime distribution at age $x$ is Gompertz--Makeham with a Poisson-distributed Makeham term. Successive Makeham terms differ by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines, and the Poisson mean is the cumulative immaturity hazard remaining after age $x$. In a latent-clock construction, individuals carry a Poisson number of constant-rate clocks, and selection removes those carrying more clocks first. Integrating the mixture yields an exact series for remaining life expectancy with a closed-form truncation bound. The life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality is close to the probability of carrying a clock times life expectancy with that hazard removed, with a closed-form error bound. In annual fits to Swedish female mortality, this loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, a decline equal to 15\% of the gain in life expectancy at birth, and the approximation was always within 0.06 years.

papers.title: The Convergence Rate of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods with General Inertial Term for Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, where each objective is a smooth convex term plus a proper closed convex term and the proximal subproblem keeps a separate offset for each objective. For a two-parameter root momentum rule with trajectory-dependent coefficients, we construct a new energy function and establish an energy identity. This yields sharper convergence guarantees: boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of $o(k^{-2})$, and displacement decay of $o(k^{-1})$ whenever the first parameter converges to a value in $(0,1)$; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. At the critical value $α=3$, we obtain $u_0(x^N)\le \frac{2\ell R}{N(N+3)},$ together with $O(1/N)$ displacement decay, square summability, and weak Pareto convergence. The remaining little-$o$ question at $α=3$ is reduced to the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy. For $1<α<3$, we prove the rate $O(N^{-(α-1)})$, and for every $α>0$ we obtain $u_0(x^k)\to0$, $F_i(x^k)\to c_i$, and $\sum_k D_k/k<\infty$. A JOS1 experiment numerically validates the predicted little-$o$ separation and the rate behavior.

papers.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: We construct canonical projective birational models of normal proper integral algebraic spaces over arbitrary fields. The construction preserves the intrinsic quasi-projective core and is natural under semilinear isomorphisms. For smooth proper integral input in characteristic zero, we combine an intrinsic choice of ideals with Włodarczyk's principalization to obtain a canonical tower of blowups in smooth centers ending in a smooth projective variety. Consequently, every compact connected Moishezon manifold admits a smooth projective bimeromorphic model to which all automorphisms lift compatibly. The main ingredient is a family-sum argument yielding an intrinsic finite selection of maximal tuples of boundary ideal germs; successive modifications strictly decrease the boundary-image dimension. We also construct canonical quasi-projective models for nonproper normal input and a greatest schematizing ideal for separated finite-type algebraic spaces over noetherian bases. Oda's threefold illustrates the construction.

papers.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of angles whose dynamical rays land on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials, and understanding when ray connections between the trees first appear when moving along veins of the Mandelbrot set. If one of the mating parameters is fixed, we prove that first ray connections are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins. We also prove that the locus of parameter pairs in two given veins for which there are no ray connections between the trees is open. Additionally, we show that there are no ray connections between small Julia sets in matings of locally connected rabbit tunings.

papers.title: A Note on the Finite-Exceedance Dependence Principle for Sum--Maximum Asymptotic Independence
papers.abstract: Asymptotic independence between sum-type and maximum-type statistics arises repeatedly across many areas of probability and statistics, particularly in high-dimensional testing and random matrix theory. Motivated by the shared structure underlying existing proofs, which is obscured by their model-specific formulations, this note isolates a common intermediate principle. We introduce a finite-exceedance dependence principle: if the finite-exceedance dependence error vanishes at every fixed order and high-order exceedances are mildly controlled, then a finite-order Bonferroni argument yields asymptotic independence between the sum and the maximum. We further give an independent-proxy criterion for verifying this: for each finite set of exceedances, it suffices to construct an exactly independent proxy for the sum-type statistic whose approximation error is negligible in aggregate. Local deletion under dependency graphs and Gaussian regression and residualization are two examples. The framework gives modular derivations of existing sum--max independence results.

papers.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
papers.abstract: We prove the Díaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yalç$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
papers.abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.

papers.title: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet \(L\)-functions over \(\Q\) with conductors coprime to \(3\), with a main term of order \(Q\) and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order \(Q^{\frac{5}{6}}\) in the same family, with error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)\). We explicitly evaluate the secondary coefficient and prove that it is strictly negative. We also prove unconditionally that the secondary polynomial in the squarefree second moment of the natural cubic Hecke \(L\)-functions over \(\Q(\sqrt{-3})\) has degree one and strictly positive leading coefficient, which we evaluate explicitly.

papers.title: Higher-order derivatives and their applications to diffeomorphism groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the diffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher-order $μ$-discreteness for subgroups $Γ< {\rm Diff}(M)$, and show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher-order $μ$-discreteness. Finally, we give examples showing that higher-order $μ$-discreteness encompasses a strictly larger class of subgroups of $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$ than its lower-order counterpart.

papers.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
papers.abstract: We prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for Brownian interpolant Euler sampling from the true source under arbitrary Borel couplings, even with nonintegrable endpoints. At fixed stopping time and noise level, a fourth displacement moment yields an $O(N^{-1})$ discretization term. A second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence with grid refinement and vanishing drift error. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, the original and comparison paths have KL of orders one and $1/\log N$ relative to the exact-drift Euler path. On the same geometric grid, terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling has an $O((M_2+d)/N)$ discretization term. We prove expected stopped-output KL consistency for a learner trained on iid endpoint pairs with fresh true-source initialization. In a spatial image control, iterative sampling has worse fair energy scores than direct prediction with resampled residuals. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.

papers.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group as defined by Barnet-Lamb et al. in [2]. In this article, we determine explicit modular local Serre weights for mod $p$ Galois representations $\barρ_h$ associated to eigenforms $h$ of $G$, with arbitrary weights and small slopes. As a consequence, we also determine modular global Serre weights in certain cases. We show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms corresponding to totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$--modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.

papers.title: Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data
papers.abstract: We extend the Bakry--Émery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{\max\{λ,μ\}}\] when $μ>2$ and $k\ge3λ^2/μ$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(λ+4)$ to a logarithmic bound. We also address several related conjectures. In their monograph \emph{Distance-Regular Graphs}, Brouwer, Cohen, and Neumaier conjectured that every amply regular graph with $μ>1$, except the icosahedron, satisfies ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le2k/(λ+2)$. We confirm this bound when $μ>λ+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $μ=λ$. For amply regular graphs with $μ\geλ$ and $μ>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/μ+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture. In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when ``$s>2$, $c>2$, $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$'' and when ``$s=2$, $c>7$''. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $μ>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.

papers.title: A nonstandard selfinjective algebra of Euclidean type
papers.abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$. We realize the four-dimensional selfinjective algebra $Ω(1)$ as an admissible infinite cyclic orbit algebra of the repetitive Kronecker category. Thus an algebra long stated to be nonstandard is of Euclidean type in the orbit-algebra sense. We also identify a gap in an earlier proof of its nonstandardness and give an independent proof by determining all connected Galois covering sources of $Ω(1)$. Together, these results disprove the implication from Euclidean type to standardness in the equivalence explicitly stated by Bocian--Holm--Skowroński (2004) and Bocian--Skowroński (2005). They also contradict the standardness conclusion of the Proposition in \S2.1 of Skowroński (1989); its main theorem in \S1.5 assumes standardness and is not contradicted by this example.

papers.title: Minimax Regret for Sobolev Kernel-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We study the minimax regret rate for episodic kernel-based reinforcement learning, where the expected reward and transition density belong to a Sobolev reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), with continuous state and action spaces, and adversarial initial states. For Sobolev smoothness parameter $ν>0$, state dimension $d_S$, and action dimension $d_A$, we prove that the minimax expected regret over $T$ episodes is $\widetildeΘ(T^{\max\{e_A,e_B\}})$, where $e_A=\frac{ν+d_A}{2ν+d_A}$, $e_B=\frac{ν+d_A+3d_S/2}{2ν+d_A+2d_S}$ with the other model parameters fixed. The two exponents reflect the distinct difficulties of action selection and learning across states. We introduce Sobolev Optimal Value Iteration (\texttt{SOVI}), which attains this rate from observed rewards and transitions. For fixed smoothness and reference-kernel lengthscale, its regret bound has a prefactor polynomial in the state-action dimension $d=d_S+d_A$, horizon $H$, reward and transition RKHS norm bounds $B_r,B_p$, and the norm-comparison factor $Λ$, up to logarithmic factors; $Λ=1$ for normalized Matérn kernels. The algorithm separates initial action selection from continuation-value estimation and combines local polynomial approximation with the shared RKHS structure of the approximation errors. Our matching upper and lower bounds determine the optimal dependence on the number of episodes for Sobolev kernel-based reinforcement learning regret minimization. Thus, we partially address the open problem in Vakili(2024) under Sobolev kernel RL.

papers.title: Swapping Compatible Words
papers.abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality if and only if $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. Carrigan et.~ al.~ ask in if there is a ``natural'' bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a ``natural'' bijection $Φ$ from the set of all finite words to itself that swaps $p$ and $q$ in each word $Ω$, meaning that $Ω$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $Φ(Ω)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $Ω$ into $Φ(Ω)$.

papers.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation compatible with all its corners: for every $k\ge1$, each connected component of the $k$-corners maps onto the image of a subcomplex, and every open simplex lies in the set of points of a single depth. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

papers.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
papers.abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.

papers.title: A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a uniform lower bound for the length of a planar distance set under a bound on the concentration of mass. For each $0<η<1$, we obtain $b(η)>0$ such that every compact $F\subset\overline{B}(0,1)$ carrying a Borel probability $ν$ with $ν(B(z,r))\le2r^{1+η}$ for all $z\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $0<r\le1$ satisfies $|ΔF|\ge b(η)$. For a compact planar set $E$ of diameter $D>0$ carrying a probability with $μ(B(z,r))\le A(r/D)^{1+\varepsilon}$ for all centers and $0<r\le D$, where $A\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, localization gives $|ΔE|\ge c_{\varepsilon,p}DA^{-p}$ for each fixed $p>1/\varepsilon$, with $c_{\varepsilon,p}>0$ depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $p$. In particular, every compact planar set of Hausdorff dimension greater than one has a distance set of positive length. The proof uses scale-dependent cutoffs to construct approximants to a fixed positive distance measure. The same approximants have summable total-variation errors and summable integrals of the squared modulus of their Fourier transforms over the corresponding dyadic bands. We develop the multiscale method of OpenAI's release on October 6, 2026 in the plane and prove the estimates with constants uniform over the normalized family. This paper is for expository purpose only and is not intended for publication.

papers.title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
papers.abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $2.06970$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a good-set energy estimate derived from a convex entropy identity. The constant is sharp for the abstract combination of these two estimates; no optimality is claimed for the operator norm. Local elliptic regularity is used to justify the passage to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

papers.title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

papers.title: Square-difference factorization: ring structure, torsion splitting, and ideal classes
papers.abstract: We introduce and study commutative rings whose regular ideals, or all ideals, factor into square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We establish permanence under finite products, suitable localizations and quotients, and coefficient descent for monoid algebras. For an SP-domain, the regular factorization property is equivalent to the localization obtained by inverting $2$ being zero or Dedekind; equivalently, the maximal ideals avoiding $2$ are invertible and form a discrete subspace in the inverse topology. Over an arbitrary domain, we characterize unique functorial splitting of localization on all torsion modules by a condition excluding nonzero prime chains across the vanishing set of the localized element. Complementary localizations of one-dimensional Prüfer domains give a decomposition of invertible ideal groups and an exact Picard-group sequence. For an SP-domain whose Picard group has finite exponent $m$, every irreducible element has local valuation at most $m$. We also give regular-ideal criteria for arbitrary idealizations and a complete strong-factorization criterion over von Neumann regular bases. The zero ideal is treated separately throughout, and explicit examples show why unrestricted quotient and localization assertions fail.

papers.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-Kähler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.

papers.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
papers.abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.

papers.title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collision part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.

papers.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
papers.abstract: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.

papers.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is linearly stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.

papers.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
papers.abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Grünbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Grünbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gröbner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

papers.title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
papers.abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N\geq4$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta--Iovita--Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard--Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao--Liu. When $p$ has a unique prime of $F$ above it, we remove this hypothesis and obtain unconditional properness, by establishing base-change compatibility for spaces of overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and analyzing the associated spectral variety over certain closed subspaces of the weight space.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
papers.abstract: We establish a criterion for the irreducibility of Verma modules over symmetrizable Kac--Moody superalgebras. Our main tool is the Weyl-Kac denominator identity.

papers.title: Path-Space Optimal Transport with Interactions: Kinetic Equations and Eikonal Structure
papers.abstract: We study a dynamical optimal transport problem on path-space with kinetic cost and nonlocal interaction. For a Gaussian interaction kernel, cyclical monotonicity and the regularity of the effective endpoint cost yield a conservative vector field associated with the initial momentum of the optimal trajectories. Separately, the Gaussian interaction potential $W_{π_0}$ satisfies a uniform gradient estimate and, under a quantitative condition on the interaction strength, is a classical and hence viscosity subsolution of an eikonal equation. We also derive the Euler--Lagrange dynamics directly from path-space optimality by means of endpoint-preserving perturbations of the optimal path measure. The associated phase-space marginals satisfy a measure-valued Liouville-type, or nonlocal kinetic, equation driven by the smooth Gaussian self-consistent force. Conversely, a superposition principle lifts suitable measure-valued solutions of the phase-space continuity equation to measures on phase-space trajectories. Thus path-space optimal transport provides a variational connection between endpoint geometry, eikonal behavior of the Gaussian interaction potential, and kinetic mean-field dynamics.

papers.title: On pointwise convergence of singular integrals of Christ-Journé type
papers.abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to establish the pointwise almost everywhere convergence of the singular integrals of Christ-Journé type. To this end, we prove the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the corresponding maximal operator defined as \[ T^*[a] f(x):= \sup_{r>0}\left|\int_{|x-y| > r} K(x-y) \int_0^1 a(tx + (1-t)y)\, dt f(y)\, dy\right|, \] where $K$ is a Calderón--Zygmund kernel and $a\in L^\infty$. This result resolves a problem posed by Seeger (Rev. Mat. Iberoam., 2014).

papers.title: The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labordère
papers.abstract: We determine the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with $β\in(0,1)$ absorbed at zero, for every correlation $ρ$: the probability $P(k)$ that the forward ends above $f_0e^k$ satisfies $-k^{-2}\ln P(k)\to(1-β)^2/(2ν^2T(1-(ρ\wedge0)^2))$. The implied volatility therefore tends to $ν\sqrt{1-(ρ\wedge0)^2}/(1-β)$. Henry-Labordère's conjectured limit $ν/(1-β)$, which Hagan's leading-order formula also gives, holds for $ρ\ge0$ and fails for $ρ<0$, where survival keeps the noise orthogonal to volatility above a moving square-root barrier. The Gaussian estimate behind his second conjecture does not hold for $ρ<0$; the rate is instead given by the intrinsic distance within the survival domain.

papers.title: On wall-crossing invariant combinations of Welschinger numbers for rational surfaces with a conic bundle
papers.abstract: We refine the real enumerative invariants insensitive to changes in the real structure introduced in our previous paper on del Pezzo surfaces, and extend these refined invariants to arbitrary rational surfaces. The construction involves a choice of an auxiliary conic bundle together with a Pin-structure. We prove that the resulting invariants are independent of these auxiliary choices and establish recursive relations for their computation.

papers.title: Cohomological non-rigidity of toric manifolds
papers.abstract: For every integer $d\geq4$, we construct pairs of projective toric manifolds of complex dimension $d$ that are not homotopy equivalent but have isomorphic integral cohomology rings and homotopy equivalent 5-fold suspensions. We also construct pairs of quasitoric manifolds over the $d$-dimensional cube with these properties. Our construction starts with a closed, oriented smooth manifold $B$ of real dimension $6$ whose integral cohomology ring is generated by $H^2(B)$. For a class $u\in H^2(B)$, let $L_u$ denote the complex line bundle with first Chern class $u$, and set $P_u=\mathbb P_B(L_0\oplus L_u)$. We show that if $u,v\in H^2(B)$ satisfy $uv=0$, then, for every finite product $N$ of complex projective spaces, the manifolds $P_{u+v}\times N$ and $P_{u-v}\times N$ have isomorphic integral cohomology rings and homotopy equivalent 5-fold suspensions. To distinguish their homotopy types, we introduce the sets of strong zero-product pairs $\mathrm{SZ}^{n,m}(X)\subseteq H^n(X)\times H^m(X)$, which are preserved by homotopy equivalences. Using these sets, we give explicit conditions on $u$ and $v$ ensuring that these manifolds are not homotopy equivalent, and exhibit toric and quasitoric examples satisfying these conditions.

papers.title: Adaptive Inference for Functionals of M-Estimands
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning and contextual bandit algorithms have become increasingly common in sequential decision-making applications. When these methods are deployed in high-stakes domains, there is growing interest not only in learning effective policies, but also in conducting statistical inference for quantities learned under adaptive data collection. However, classical procedures applied naively in these settings can fail: even when estimators are unbiased, their variance becomes path-dependent and as a result may not be asymptotically normal. A growing literature has emerged to ameliorate this problem, but solutions tend to be problem specific and often rely on correct specification of a working model. In this work, we develop a unified framework for constructing asymptotically valid confidence intervals to cover smooth functionals of nonparametric M-estimands under adaptive sampling. Under Neyman orthogonality, we provide two novel methods for performing inference: (1) a self-normalized statistic based on the realized quadratic variation of the influence function and (2) a statistic using a plug-in estimate of the conditional variance based on reweighted influence function increments. Our results allow for flexible nonparametric estimation of nuisance parameters and remain valid under model misspecification. Our theory is supported by a simulation study for a dynamic pricing application which demonstrates that this method can produce asymptotically valid confidence intervals where standard methods fail.

papers.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the Kähler Property
papers.abstract: We prove that the Kählerness of a finitely presented, residually finite group is not determined by its profinite completion, which answers a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober. In the proof, we give explicit constructions to characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions.

papers.title: Beyond Empirical Support: Structured Outlier Generation via Sinkhorn Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Outliers are essential for evaluating and improving the robustness of machine learning systems, especially when future distributions may differ significantly from historical training data. In high-stakes applications, robustness often depends on rare cases that finite datasets fail to capture, making simple resampling or perturbation insufficient for stress scenario generation. Existing outlier synthesis methods typically rely on sparse neighborhoods, low support latent regions, or classifier boundary crossings, which can be heuristic, unstable, and tied to specific modalities or architectures. We therefore propose Sinkhorn Boundary Outlier Generation (SBOG), a structured framework for latent-space outlier generation that couples Sinkhorn optimal transport geometry with distributionally robust boundary modeling. The resulting Sinkhorn-induced support cost guides the sampler toward weakly supported boundary regions, while semantic constraints prevent uncontrolled drift from the intended context, yielding controlled deviations from the in-distribution reference measure rather than arbitrary sparse-region samples. Experiments on time series anomaly generation and image outlier synthesis show that our framework produces informative, semantically controlled outliers and improves downstream robustness evaluation across modalities, providing a foundation for stress scenario generation beyond empirical support.

papers.title: $σ$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-networks, $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizability, and local HCP-finiteness
papers.abstract: For every admissible ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, we prove that every regular space with a $σ$-hereditarily closure-preserving (HCP) $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-metrizable, answering Problem~5.2 of Zhou--Liu--Liu--Lin. The proof combines existing characterizations with a local countability bound. If $y_n\to_{\mathcal{I}} x$ in a space $X$ and $\{n:y_n\ne x\}\in\mathcal{I}^{+}$, then every point-discrete family of $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is countable. If no such sequence exists at $x$, then $\{x\}$ itself is an $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhood. These alternatives imply that every space with a $σ$-point-discrete $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal{I}$-$snf$-countable. We say that $\mathcal{I}$ has local HCP-finiteness if, in every $T_1$ space, the convergence and support assumptions above imply that each HCP family of $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is finite. A countable Rudin--Keisler antichain of free ultrafilters gives an admissible ideal without this property, so the countability bound cannot in general be strengthened to finiteness. Every $P^{-}$ ideal has local HCP-finiteness. We give sufficient conditions for Fubini products, heterogeneous Fubini sums, and increasing unions to preserve this property. These results establish local HCP-finiteness for the finite Fubini powers of $\mathrm{Fin}$, Katětov's first limit-stage ideal $\mathrm{Fin}^ω$ and its finite successors, the tree-derived rank-$ω$ ideal $\mathcal H_{<ω}$, and the inductive-limit ideal $\mathrm{Fin}_ω$. All these examples except $\mathrm{Fin}$ fail $P^{-}$.

papers.title: Quantitative QSD convergence in 1-Wasserstein distance via the Föllmer drift
papers.abstract: We develop a novel pathwise approach to study the convergence of the law of killed diffusion processes conditioned on non-absorption, towards a quasi-stationary distribution (QSD) as time goes to infinity. We start from the general observation that the dynamics of an absorbed Markov process conditioned upon survival up to time $T>0$ is the minimizer of the pathwise relative entropy with respect to its unconditioned dynamics, under a simple distributional constraint at that time; in other words, a Föllmer process. We then show how this result applies to a Brownian diffusion process softly-killed at a state-dependent regular rate, and characterize the minimizer and its drift change. In the case when the diffusion process is moreover reversible, we leverage these ideas and recent results on the propagation of weak log-concavity of HJB semigroups to prove that, under strict asymptotic convexity of the potential, the conditioned dynamics satisfies a contractivity property in $1$-Wasserstein distance, uniformly in $T>0$. We then establish the existence of a QSD with a large domain of attraction and deduce the exponentially fast convergence to it of the conditioned semigroup in the $1$-Wasserstein distance as $T$ goes to infinity. Finally, we deduce the exponentially fast convergence, also in $1$-Wasserstein distance, of the law of the corresponding Q-process towards its equilibrium.

papers.title: Applications of a Commutation Formula II
papers.abstract: The principal {\it commutation formula} underlying the paper by Deift [24], is of the type \[ - z (AB - z I)^{-1} + A (BA - z I)^{-1} B = I, \quad z \in [ρ(AB) \cap ρ(BA)]\backslash\{0\}, \] where, temporarily, and for simplicity only, $A,B$ represent bounded operators in a Banach space. A fundamental consequence of this commutation formula is the fact that $AB$ and $BA$ are {\it essentially isospecral} in the sense that \[ σ(AB) \backslash \{0\} = σ(BA) \backslash \{0\}. \] Moreover, under appropriate trace class hypotheses, this implies the fundamental identity for (Fredholm) determinants \[ \det(I - AB) = \det(I - BA), \] which extends to modified (or regularized) Fredholm determinants. In this paper we briefly recall some of the applications of these commutation formulas to isospectrality, integrable systems, regularization of PDEs, and estimates in Statistical Mechanics and Quantum Field Theory discussed in [24]. Subsequently, we review some of the ramifications of commutation formulas that were established over the past fifty years, including determinants and dimension reduction, random matrix theory and dimension expansion, integrable operators, Poncelet's porism, interpolation, eigenvalue computation, KPZ, Pfaffians, the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation, one-dimensional scattering theory, Floquet theory, and the Miura transformation connecting the KdV and mKdV hierarchies.

papers.title: Polyhedral Methods for Cooperative Games: Small Lifts and Hard Faces
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of fundamental algorithmic problems -- membership testing, separation, valid-inequality testing, and linear optimization -- over polytopes and cones arising from cooperative games (also known as pseudo-Boolean functions). A central obstacle in the study of such problems is that a general cooperative game on $n$ players requires $2^n$ values, so the input size is $2^n$ for a game with $n$ players, making these computational tasks theoretically trivial. Restricting to $k$-additive games reduces the input size to $O(n^k)$, making such games a natural target for meaningful questions about the existence of efficient algorithms. On the positive side, we give an explicit extended formulation of size $O(n^k)$ for the core of $k$-additive $k$-monotone games, allowing all four problems to be solved by a single polynomial-size linear program -- in particular, circumventing the ellipsoid method that is needed when building from earlier tractability results of Deng and Papadimitriou, or of Edmonds. For the cone of $k$-additive $(k{-}1)$-monotone games, we give a complete characterization of its extreme rays and derive the same $O(n^k)$ bound on extension complexity, yielding a geometry-based proof and generalization of a result of Billionnet and Minoux. On the negative side, we show that for $l \leq k-2$ the cone of $k$-additive $l$-monotone games is computationally intractable: membership testing is not in NP (unless NP\,=\,coNP), valid-inequality testing is NP-complete, and extension complexity is at least $1.5^n$. Our hardness results yield, as a special case, a result of Crama and of Gallo and Simone. Furthermore, our hardness results also explain the lack of any good characterization of the extreme rays of the cone of $k$-additive $(k{-}2)$-monotone games.
authors: Michel Grabisch and. Hans Raj Tiwary

papers.title: The flip symmetry on Khovanov-Rozansky homology
papers.abstract: The flip symmetry on link diagrams induces an involution on Khovanov-Rozansky ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ homology. We prove that this involution is the identity over the integers, generalizing a previous result of Chen and the author. The key ingredients of the proof are (1) a homotopy perturbation argument from a detailed study of the fork twist, which allows us to reduce the computation to planar ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ webs, and (2) the computation of the flip map for planar ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ webs via diagrammatics of Soergel bimodules. The latter computation can also be interpreted as a naturality result for the half twist action on type $A$ Soergel bimodules, which might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Weighted averages and applications to sets of multiple recurrence
papers.abstract: We introduce new techniques for determining combinatorial properties of sets of multiple recurrence by considering weighted averages with quickly growing weights. Our main result is a far-reaching generalization of Szemerédi's Theorem which additionally confirms a conjecture of Bergelson-Moreira-Richter and contains as special cases both a variant of the Polynomial Szemerédi Theorem due to Bergelson-Leibman-Lesigne and the fact that if $f$ belongs to a broad class of smooth functions and satisfies $x^{d-1}\prec f(x)\prec x^d$ for some $d\in \mathbb{N}$ then for any $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, any invertible measure preserving system $(X,\mathscr{B},μ,T)$, and any $A\in \mathscr{B}$ with $μ(A)>0$, the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}: μ(A\cap T^{-[f(n)]}A\cap T^{-2[f(n)]}A\cap \cdots\cap T^{-\ell[f(n)]}A )>0\}$ is thick, meaning that it contains arbitrarily long intervals of natural numbers. Additionally, we formulate and prove a generalization to weighted averages of Boshernitzan's criterion for uniform distribution which we use in the proof of our main result.

papers.title: Sharp iterated-logarithmic thresholds for quantitative measure and orbit equivalence between integer lattices
papers.abstract: We identify the sharp iterated-logarithmic thresholds at the critical exponent for quantitative measure equivalence and orbit equivalence between integer lattices. To be more precise, let $n>m$ be two positive integers, $α$ be a positive number and $( β_j)_{j \geqslant 1}$ be a finitely supported sequence of non-negative numbers. We show that there is a quantitatively $t^α\cdot \prod_{j \geqslant 1} ( \log^{(j)}{t} )^{-β_j} $-integrable measure equivalence from $\mathbb{Z}^n$ to $\mathbb{Z}^m$ if and only if either $α<m/n$ or $α=m/n$ and there is $j_* \geqslant 1$ such that $β_j= 1$ for all $1 \leqslant j < j_*$ and $β_{j_*} > 1$. Here $\log^{(j)}$ is the $j$-fold iterated logarithm. The same characterization holds for quantitative orbit equivalence. This characterization greatly strengthens the previous best-known result, due to the work of Delabie, Koivisto, Le Maître and Tessera (2022) and the work of Correia (2025), which asserts that there is a $t^α$-integrable ($α>0$) measure equivalence (or orbit equivalence) from $\mathbb{Z}^n$ to $\mathbb{Z}^m$ if and only if $α<m/n$. In particular, our result solves, in much stronger forms, two open problems posed respectively by Delabie, Koivisto, Le Maître and Tessera, and by Naryshkin and Petrakos.

papers.title: A New Approach to Universal Measurability
papers.abstract: V. Fedorchuk, A. Chigogidze and T. Banakh in 2003 and V. Bogachev in 2024 posed the following questions: (i) is it true that $P_τ(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_σ(X)$; (ii) is it true that $P_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_R(βX)$ if and only if $X$ is pseudocompact, where $P_σ$, $P_τ$ and $P_R$ are the functors of probability measures on the space $X$ that are, respectively, $σ$-additive on the Baire $σ$-algebra, $τ$-additive, and Radon? The answers to these questions are negative. In this paper the questions are put into a general framework: for spaces of measures $Q_p(X)\subset Q_q(X)$ of various types we study when $Q_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $Q_q(X)$. It is proved that for spaces of alternating measures $M_p(X)\subset M_q(X)$ the $C$-embeddedness, the $C^*$-embeddedness and the $G_δ$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and a criterion in terms of sequences of continuous functions is given. The question of $C$-embedding of measure spaces is an extension of the question of coincidence of measure spaces, which is a development of the classical concepts of universally measurable and universal measure zero sets. Note (corrected version): incorrect statements of the previous versions are marked or removed; see the last section of the paper.

papers.title: Abundance of typical horseshoes for the random standard map
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of typical horseshoe, consisting of a pair of rectangles admitting Markov returns at times of positive lower density, with controlled hyperbolic geometry and orbits that shadow typical trajectories. We prove the abundance of typical horseshoes for the random standard map and establish several statistical properties of the system, including exponential mixing and large deviation estimates for the associated projective and two-point processes.

papers.title: Universality transitions in the logarithmic law of random determinants beyond the fourth moment
papers.abstract: For real random matrices $A_n=(a_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ with independent centered entries of unit variance, \citet{BaoPanZhou2015} established the classical logarithmic law under a uniform fourth-moment condition: \[ \frac{\log|\det A_n|-\frac12\log(n-1)!} {\sqrt{\frac12\log n}} \Rightarrow \mathcal N(0,1). \] We find that this Gaussian universality can be extended beyond the fourth-moment condition, with two distinct transitions in the center and fluctuation scale as the moment condition gradually weaken. The first critical condition is the uniform integrability of the family $\{|a_{ij}|^4/\sqrt{\log(e+|a_{ij}|)}\}_{n,i,j}$. The classical law remains valid under this weaker condition, with no change in center or scale. As the moment condition is weakened further, the classical center can fail. Replacing the classical center $\frac12\log(n-1)!$ by the actual mean $\mathbb E\log|\det A_n|$ preserves the standard Gaussian limit at the original scale and allows the moment condition to be relaxed to a second critical condition: uniform integrability of $\{|a_{ij}|^4/\log(e+|a_{ij}|)\}_{n,i,j}$. Under still weaker moment conditions, the classical scale $\sqrt{\frac12\log n}$ can also fail. Replacing this scale in turn by the actual standard deviation $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\log|\det A_n|)}$ yields a standard Gaussian limit whenever the expectations of $|a_{ij}|^4/\{\log(e+|a_{ij}|)\}^α$ are uniformly bounded over $n,i,j$, for any fixed $α\ge0$. The results using the actual mean or standard deviation additionally assume uniformly bounded entry densities. We establish the sharpness of the first two critical conditions via counterexamples. We further obtain Berry--Esseen bounds for all three normalizations, with optimal rates under a uniform fourth-moment bound.

papers.title: Representation Varieties of Stacks and Trace Maps
papers.abstract: We define a derived stack $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ which generalizes the assignment $A\leadsto \operatorname{Rep}_n(A)$ to an algebra of its derived $GL_n$-representation variety of arXiv:1112.1449 from algebras $A$ to perfect stacks $X$ over characteristic 0 fields. In the case of a quasi-projective classical scheme $X$, we show that $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ admits a subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)\subset \mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$, which is in fact represented by a derived scheme almost of finite type. We further construct a Fourier-Mukai integral transform between the derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ which induces a trace map at the level of Hochschild homology generalizing the trace morphism constructed in arXiv:1112.1449 (for finitely presented commutative algebras). We show that the subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ is a derived enhancement of the framed locus of the Quot scheme of points and that this derived scheme is a $GL_n$-torsor over the stack of coherent length $n$ torsion sheaves. Hence, this stack is an analog of the derived character stack for quasi-projective schemes, and we show that for smooth, Calabi-Yau $X$, it inherits a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of arXiv:1111.3209 from the one constructed in arXiv:1812.11913 on the moduli stack of perfect complexes with proper support. This structure is shown to give a generalization of the classical symplectic structure on character varieties of surfaces of genus 1 constructed by Goldman \cite{gold}.

papers.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
papers.abstract: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through the effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.

papers.title: PAC-Bayesian Bounds for Learning Partially Observed Stochastic Linear Time-Invariant State-Space Systems with Inputs and Sub-Gaussian Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper we derive a Probably Approximately Correct (PAC)-Bayesian error bound for partially observed linear time-invariant (LTI) stochastic dynamical systems in state-space form with inputs and sub-Gaussian noise. Such bounds are widespread in machine learning, and they are useful for characterizing the predictive power of models learned from finitely many data points. The bound derived in this paper relates the expectation of prediction errors with the prediction error generated by the model on the data used for learning. In addition, we show that it can also be used to derive bounds for the parameter estimation error. In turn, this allows us to provide finite-sample error bounds for the prediction error and parameter estimation error for a wide class of system identification algorithms. Furthermore, as LTI systems are a sub-class of recurrent neural networks (RNNs), these error bounds could be a first step towards PAC-Bayesian bounds for RNNs.

papers.title: Schwartz-Class Gabor Windows and the Balian-Low Classification
papers.abstract: A lattice Gabor frame consists of a window function and its time-frequency shifts along a lattice. We classify the lattices that admit Schwartz-class and, equivalently, Feichtinger frame windows. Except for symplectically irrational lattices of critical covolume 1, we determine the lattice-dependent achievable window smoothness and decay using the scale of modulation spaces. For symplectically rational lattices, including the rational lattices typically used in digital applications, the classification is governed by an integer lattice parameter introduced herein, the symplectic index gap. Our results extend the classical and amalgam Balian-Low theorems. The companion paper "Tilings, Packings, and Smooth and Compactly Supported Gabor Windows" develops the associated tiling-packing theorem and compact-support constructions.

papers.title: Self-similar structure of non-isothermal variable-density mushy Stefan problems and an improved low-Mach enthalpy method
papers.abstract: The enthalpy method was introduced in the late 1970s to simulate phase-change problems on fixed grids without explicitly tracking the moving phase-change front. It remains one of the most widely used approaches in academic and commercial software for the simulation of industrial melting and solidification processes. For pure phase-change materials (PCMs) that melt or solidify at a single temperature, the enthalpy method introduces an artificial mushy region bounded by the solidus temperature, $T^{\rm sol}$, and the liquidus temperature, $T^{\rm liq}$. As the numerical parameter $ΔT=T^{\rm liq}- T^{\rm sol}$ approaches zero, the solution obtained with the enthalpy method is generally assumed to converge to that of the classical Stefan problem, in which the phase-change front is infinitesimally thin. This assumption is largely based on benchmark studies performed under the simplifying assumption of equal solid and liquid densities. In this work, we systematically investigate the accuracy and spatio-temporal convergence properties of the enthalpy method for both low- and high-density-ratio phase-change problems. Because the limiting behavior $ΔT\rightarrow0$ is difficult to realize numerically, owing to the diminishing thickness of the mushy region, we formulate and analyze the finite-$ΔT$ mushy Stefan problem solved by the enthalpy method. We show that this problem possesses a self-similar structure that reduces the governing equations to a boundary-value problem involving two unknown parameters. The theoretical analysis also enables improvements to our previously developed low-Mach enthalpy method, enhancing its stability and accuracy as the density ratio between the two phases increases from $\mathcal{O}(1)$ to $\mathcal{O}(3)$.

papers.title: Beyond ICA: Identifiability by Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: We prove the population-level identifiability of deep generative models (DGMs) with piecewise-affine (PWA) decoders and Gaussian mixture model (GMM) priors, in a purely unsupervised setting. We introduce three algebraic contrast principles for symmetry breaking: *domain contrast*, which trivializes the mixture symmetry group, a label-free counterpart of the sufficient-variability assumption of nonlinear ICA; *mechanism contrast*, which ensures every decoder branch gets an observational boundary across which it toggles alone; and *interaction contrast*, which forbids parameter conspiracies between latent components and decoder branches. Together they exploit the interplay between the discrete combinatorics of the PWA map and the continuous symmetry structure of the latent GMM. Continuity is replaced by algebraic symmetry conditions; injectivity is decoupled from structural identification and required only for pointwise inversion. Our results form a hierarchy: from *law identifiability* (LID; latent distribution up to a global affine map) through *map identifiability* (MID; decoder up to the same map) to *posterior* and *pointwise identifiability*. The ICA-form ambiguity emerges under conditions on diagonal component covariances. The interaction contrast is the only one of our contrasts required on the estimator side. To our knowledge this is the first to develop algebraic symmetry-breaking into an identifiability engine for a concrete nonlinear model class, the first to admit discontinuous decoders, and the first to handle fully non-injective decoders, where every observation admits multiple latent codes.

papers.title: Beyond Mock Modularity: Elliptic Corrections for Higher Dyson Ranks
papers.abstract: When $m = 1$, the Dyson rank generating function is a classical bridge between partition theory, Ramanujan's mock theta functions, and the theory of harmonic Maass forms and nonholomorphic Jacobi forms. The rank is a statistic on partitions, and the higher Dyson systems, for $m \geq 2$, are a natural multivariable refinement of it, combining $m$ graded rank contributions. Unlike the classical case, these higher systems are not expected to fit the mock-modular framework, which raises the question of what analytic structure governs them. We show that their root-of-unity specializations carry a hidden elliptic structure. For $m\ge2$, the primitive $(2m+1)$st-root specialization of their generating function leads to a product deformation whose associated seed satisfies a finite $q$-difference recurrence with an explicit polynomial defect. Using bilateral periodization we construct a meromorphic lift satisfying a twisted index-$m$ elliptic transformation law, with at most simple poles on a prescribed lattice orbit. The poles can be removed by subtracting an explicit multiple of an Appell--Lerch kernel and a specified translation removes the twist. The resulting holomorphic finite parts admit a finite theta decomposition. These results grew out of a human--AI collaboration, and the key new formulas were formalized and machine-verified in Lean/Mathlib by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Deep Gaussian Processes on Directed Acyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: Many real-world processes can be represented as compositions of functions along a directed acyclic graph (DAG). In causal modelling, these correspond to the underlying mechanisms; in engineering, to multiple fidelity levels; and in gene-regulatory networks, to transcription factors. These functions are partially observed across the DAG, with noisy and heterogeneously sampled measurements, posing significant challenges for reconstruction, uncertainty propagation, and inference. To tackle these challenges, we place priors over functions and naturally arrive at Deep Gaussian Processes over DAGs. We theoretically study their prior-collapse behaviour and the effect of graph topology and intermediate observations on the preservation of information. We obtain almost-sure lower bounds on the asymptotic frequency of depths at which the distinction between inputs is preserved, identify broad kernel classes for which these hold, and prove an observation by \citep{dunlop2018} on the role of input connections. We offer a structured variational approximation that retains graph dependencies, preserves compositional uncertainty, and captures the explaining-away behaviour of colliders. Finally, we empirically validate our theory and methodology at scale and under DAG misspecification. We then model a latent-collider DAG, a protein signalling network, and a multi-fidelity \mbox{heavy-ion} collision emulation task, attaining state-of-the-art performance while recovering low-fidelity contributions and yielding interpretability over the simulator hierarchy.

papers.title: On the Chow ring of very general abelian varieties and a question of Pirola
papers.abstract: We prove that for a very general abelian variety of dimension $\geq 4$, a divisor $D\in {\rm CH}^1(A)$ that satisfies $D^2=0$ in ${\rm CH}^2(A)$ is of torsion. The same result is also established for a very general Jacobian in genus $4$. We use then the second statement in order to prove a conjecture of Pirola, which states that any rational section of the Kummer fibration $K=J/\pm {\rm Id}\rightarrow \mathcal{M}_4$, where $J\rightarrow \mathcal{M}_4 $ is the Jacobian fibration, must be a multiple of the Griffiths-Pirola section given by the difference of the two trigonal divisors.

papers.title: Causal Inference for All: Marginal Estimands for Outcomes Truncated by Death
papers.abstract: In longitudinal studies, outcomes of interest are often truncated by death, meaning that they are only observed or well-defined conditional on intercurrent events such as survival. Existing strategies face a trade-off: causally interpretable estimands, such as survivor average causal effects, target a latent subgroup, whereas while-alive and composite summaries apply to the full population but are difficult to interpret as causal effects on the non-mortality outcome. We address these challenges by introducing methodology for a new set of estimands that (i) concern the entire population, (ii) remain causally interpretable, and (iii) leverage the longitudinal data commonly available in studies with outcomes truncated by death. The set of estimands includes single-world marginal separable effects that generalize conditional separable effects to full-population summaries. We develop identification and estimation results for these estimands and apply the methodology in a reanalysis of a prostate cancer trial, highlighting how different estimands can yield different treatment conclusions.

papers.title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
papers.abstract: The independence number $α$ of a finite simple graph lies between the polynomial-time computable Havel-Hakimi residue $R$ and annihilation number $a$. The Caro-Wei sum $W$ gives another lower bound and the known upper bound $α\le(Δ+1)W/2$ for maximum degree $Δ\ge1$. This upper bound does not by itself control the larger quantity $a$. This note proves $a\le(Δ+1)W/2$ for $Δ\ge1$, with equality attained, for example, by regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Together with $R\ge W$, this bound shows that the interval from $R$ to $a$ improves or matches both Caro-Wei endpoints. Its sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains $(Δ+1)/2$, even among connected graphs. For maximum degree at least three, the bound also proves the inequality $α\ge(a+R)/Δ$ conjectured by TxGraffiti, an automated conjecturing program. A direct calculation handles connected graphs of maximum degree two. Together these cases resolve the conjecture for every connected graph with at least three vertices. The single edge is the only nontrivial connected exception. Equality holds for exactly eight connected graphs up to isomorphism. For maximum degree at least three, the conjectured lower bound never exceeds the residue, so it gives no stronger independence estimate.

papers.title: Lyapunov-Based Sample Complexity Analysis for Weakly-Coupled MDPs
papers.abstract: We study the sample complexity of learning in average-reward weakly-coupled Markov decision processes (WCMDPs) and Restless Bandits (RBs) under a generative model. Naive reduction to a tabular MDP leads to high complexity bounds as the state-action space is exponentially large in the number of arms $N$. By exploiting the weakly coupled structure, we show that near-optimal policies can be learned with sample and computational complexities that are polynomial in $N$. Specifically, we analyze the plug-in approach, which applies an efficient planning algorithm to an empirical model estimated from data. For fully heterogeneous WCMDPs, we establish the first finite-sample PAC guarantee with polynomial complexity and an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap. For homogeneous RBs, we further prove that a smaller optimality gap is achievable under mild structural assumptions. A primary technical contribution is a novel Lyapunov-based analysis framework. Unlike classical approaches that rely on the difficult-to-control bias function, our framework uses an explicitly constructed Lyapunov function along with a drift transfer technique between the true and empirical models. A key step of independent interest in our framework is a fine-grained perturbation analysis for the underlying linear programming (LP) relaxation, which provides a general tool for analyzing LP-based policies and weakly-coupled systems.

papers.title: More Residually Solvable One-Relator Groups
papers.abstract: We say a word in a free group is ``partially positive'' if there is at least one generator which appears in the word, but does not appear with negative exponent. We show that one-relator groups with a partially positive relator are residually solvable. This extends a theorem of Baumslag showing one-relator groups with positive relators are residually solvable.

papers.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
papers.abstract: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by training learnable components through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size when the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection is numerically unstable under repeated eigenvalues. We address the first with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that reduces memory from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n + \mathrm{nnz}(A))$, and the second with a stable backward rule based on the Dalečkii--Krein representation of the Fréchet derivative. Together, these enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm starts for COSMO. On standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs, ranging from max-cut and Lovász $\vartheta$ to robust estimation and control, the learned policies outperform tuned COSMO on every problem class, reducing iterations to tolerance by up to 60$\times$, and transfer without retraining to instances up to 10$\times$ larger in the size parameter while retaining 2--5$\times$ speedups. Our matrix-free solver implementation also batches naturally on the GPU, solving 64 Lovász $\vartheta$ SDPs 14$\times$ faster than sequential COSMO.jl. When embedded in sequential convex programming for nonlinear covariance steering, our learned optimizers outperform the interior-point solver Clarabel in terms of both success rate and solve time.

papers.title: A criterion for weighted uniform distribution along functions from a Hardy field
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Boshernitzan states that if $f$ is a function which belongs to a Hardy field and which satisfies $|f(x)|\prec x^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, then the sequence $(f(n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly distributed modulo 1 if and only if $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{|f(x)-p(x)|}{\log(x)} = \infty$ for all $p(x)\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. We provide a new proof of this result using methods from summability theory and we extend Boshernitzan's criterion by obtaining necessary and sufficient conditions for $f$ to be uniformly distributed modulo 1 with respect to a broad class of weighted averages. As an application of our results, we show that for the function $f(x) = x^{3/2}$ and for any $(a,b)\subset [0,1]$, and all sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an $n\in [N-N^{\frac{1}{4}},N]$ such that $f(n)\mod 1\in (a,b)$.

papers.title: Measuring multivariate maximal tail dependence
papers.abstract: The classical tail dependence coefficient (TDC) may fail to capture non-exchangeable features of bivariate tail dependence since it evaluates the underlying copula only along the diagonal. To address this limitation, several measures of strongest manifestation of tail dependence have been proposed in the bivariate case, including a measure based on the tail copula of the underlying bivariate copula. This paper introduces and investigates the multivariate maximal tail concordance measure (MTCM), which extends the bivariate measure to the multivariate case. The MTCM quantifies the largest tail mass over lower hyperrectangles of common unit volume, while the associated maximizer identifies the direction of maximal tail probability. We establish fundamental properties of the MTCM in the multivariate case, including existence of an optimal direction. We also derive analytical representations for several important model classes. Closed-form expressions are further obtained for survival Marshall-Olkin copulas, Archimax and nested Archimedean copulas with regularly varying Archimedean generators. An application to trivariate annual sea-level maxima in England reveals off-diagonal stress directions and differences in extremal dependence that are not summarized by likelihood values or the TDC alone. A basis-risk analysis of a parametric insurance further shows that the fitted model with relatively low values of TDC and MTCM can nevertheless yield the most conservative risk assessment due to its non-exchangeability in the tail.

papers.title: Cesàro means of firmly nonexpansive iterates need not converge strongly
papers.abstract: Firmly nonexpansive operators arise naturally as resolvents of monotone operators and as generalizations of projections and proximal mappings in convex optimization and fixed point theory. While their iterates are known to converge weakly to a fixed point, strong convergence is not guaranteed (Genel and Lindenstrauss, 1975). Strong convergence of Cesàro means of iterates is also known to fail for general nonlinear nonexpansive mappings (Krengel and Lin, 1987). In this paper, we show that this failure persists in the much smaller class of firmly nonexpansive mappings. Using suitable meshes, we construct a new explicit family of counterexamples in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with the origin as the unique fixed point. In the harmonic case, the Cesàro means of the iterates remain bounded away from the origin. Another variant yields Cesàro means that converge strongly to the origin. A third variant presents Cesàro means whose norms oscillate in the sense that their liminf is zero while their limsup is positive. Thus the strong convergence conclusion in von Neumann's linear mean ergodic theorem does not extend to Baillon's nonlinear mean ergodic theorem, even for firmly nonexpansive mappings.

papers.title: Tropical Degrees and Stable Intersections
papers.abstract: We study finite set-theoretic intersections of tropical curves with tropical hypersurfaces. An elementary divisor argument bounds their cardinality by the weighted sum of the Newton support function over the unbounded directions of the curve, without a transversality hypothesis. For tropical lines the bound is $h_Δ(1,\dots,1)+\sum_i h_Δ(-e_i)=n!\,\MV(Δ,Σ,\dots,Σ)$. Explicit examples show that neither the $\ell^1$-diameter nor the support cardinality minus one gives a corresponding bound for tropical lines. We also record width refinements of the classical-line estimate of Lang, Shapiro and Shustin. A self-contained account of the standard transverse multiplicity formulas explains the role of saturated normal lattices and mixed-cell volumes. Finally, applying the tropical Bernstein theorem to locally independent subsystems gives a mixed-volume bound for the regular transverse locus of a redundant system. An example shows why a fixed subsystem need not compute the count on the whole redundant intersection.

papers.title: The $L^p$ spectrum of the Stokes operator on hyperbolic 3-space and exponential decay for the Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We determine the $L^p$ spectrum, $1<p<\infty$, of the Stokes operator $A=-\PP\LD$ on divergence-free vector fields of hyperbolic 3-space of curvature $-a^2$, where $\LD=Δ_B+\Ric$ is the Ebin-Marsden deformation Laplacian and $\PP$ is the Leray projector. The spectrum is the parabolic region $a^2\{4+z^2:\ z\in\C,\ |\im z|\le|1-2/p|\}$. For $p>2$ every interior point is an eigenvalue, realized by an explicit family of divergence-free swirl fields which leave $L^p$ exactly at the boundary of the region. It follows that the Stokes semigroup on $\Lp$ has exponential type exactly $-μ_p$ with $μ_p=a^2\bigl(4-(1-2/p)^2\bigr)$. At $p=3$ this is $35a^2/9$, which lies strictly above the rates $26a^2/9$ and $10a^2/3$ that follow from pointwise domination by the scalar heat semigroup and from interpolation, and strictly below the $L^2$ gap $4a^2$. For the Navier-Stokes equations with small data in $L^3$, whose global solvability on $\HH^3$ is due to Pierfelice, the solutions decay in $L^3$ and in $L^6$ at every rate below $μ\cdot35a^2/9$, where $μ$ is the viscosity, and no faster rate holds for the linearized flow. The exponent $3$ is the usual scaling threshold. Curvature fixes the time scale of the decay and introduces no new threshold.

papers.title: Fast and Stable Gradient Approximation for Quadratic Forms of Hermitian Matrix Functions
