papers.abstract: Let $f:M^n\to\Sn^{n+q}(1)$ be a minimal immersion of a closed connected manifold with $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$, and let $S$ be the squared length of its second fundamental form. We prove an integral inequality that gives $\max_M S\ge n$ if the immersion is not totally geodesic. If $n\ne4$ or $q=2$, equality $\max_M S=n$ holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface; if $n=4$ and $q\ge3$, equality holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface or the standard minimal embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ in $\Sn^7(1)$. Both classifications are understood up to an ambient isometry, a totally geodesic inclusion, and a finite covering. We construct the integral inequalities using polynomial weights and divergence identities. The required algebraic estimates are proved by sums of squared tensor norms.

papers.title: A Note on the Cut-Locus-Corrected Fréchet Mean Central Limit Theorem
papers.abstract: We record two observations concerning \cite{HLW24}. First, the proof of its Theorem~1 yields the population linearization (13)--(14) at \textit{any critical point} of the Fréchet function $F_μ$, under its remaining geometric and measure-theoretic assumptions; neither \textit{isolation} nor a \textit{nonsingular} Hessian of $F_μ$ is needed. Second, its Theorem~2 is given a shorter proof by applying the M-estimator theorem \cite[Theorem~5.23, pp.~53--54]{vdV98} to negative squared distance in normal coordinates, as opposed to the Donsker argument used there. We verify the pointwise differentiability, local square-integrable Lipschitz bound, second order expansion of population loss, consistency, and empirical maximization hypotheses. The resulting covariance retains the cut-locus correction. The same argument applies to a measurable selection of \textit{local} sample Fréchet minima when the population Hessian is positive definite.

papers.title: Feynman-Kac Representation and the Asymptotic Speed of the Fisher-KPP Equation with Finite-Activity Jump Noise
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher--KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump Lévy noise, i.e.\ a compensated Poisson random measure of finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jumps and jumps multiplicatively at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman--Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. The representation converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, allowing a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation, we derive sharp upper and lower bounds for the propagation of the front: for every speed $c>2\sqrt{1+a}$ the solution decays exponentially along the ray $x=ct$, while for every speed $c<2\sqrt{1+a}$ it does not. The two together identify the asymptotic speed in the critical-speed sense: the threshold between exponentially decaying and non-decaying fronts equals $2\sqrt{1+a}$ almost surely, an identity proved without any a priori existence of the limit $R_δ(t)/t$. The complementary bounds $2\sqrt{\underlineγ}\le c\le2\sqrt{\overlineγ}$ also hold, with $\overlineγ,\underlineγ$ explicit in $ε$ and $μ$. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which underlie the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, and numerical simulations illustrate the informativeness of the speed bounds.

papers.title: The fixed-point proportion of Lattès maps
papers.abstract: How often does an element of the geometric iterated Galois group of a Lattès map fix a vertex of the tree? Let A/K be an abelian variety over a separably closed field of characteristic 0, G <= Aut(A,0) finite, and alpha an isogeny of degree at least 2 normalising G. The Lattès map on X=A/G has a preimage tree governed by alpha-power torsion; we determine the fixed-point proportion in every dimension. For zeta in G the weight is the reciprocal of the number of fixed points of zeta in alpha-power torsion (zero if infinite); equivalently, it is a product of p-adic absolute values of determinants on the alpha-active subspaces; for scalar alpha=m the proportion is (1/|G|) times the sum over 1 != zeta in G of the product over p dividing m of the p-adic absolute value of det(1 - zeta | H_1(A,Z)). We deduce positivity and vanishing criteria, prove the groups G_infinity are martingale groups, determine the limit law, and reduce groups with translations to the fixed-origin case. In dimension one we determine ten values for scalar multipliers and nontrivial G <= Aut(E,0), and for the eight quadratic Lattès classes the proportions are 1/8, 1/4 and 5/16. Bridy-Jones-Kelsey-Lodge exclude the Lattès case from their main theorem; their Theorem 2.5 periodic-point bound is attained, via reductions modulo split primes p = 1 (mod 4), for the map (x^2+a)/(x^2-a), a^2 = -1, and we settle the exceptional case of the Fariña-Asategui-Radi conjecture.

papers.title: Holomorphic calculus on $L^p(\ell^q)$ with optimal angle
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic Hörmander calculus on $L^p(X;\ell^q)$ at the optimal angle $\max\{\arcsin|1-2/p|,\arcsin|1-2/q|\}$, with boundary Sobolev order $s>3$.

papers.title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}, \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of fermion condensation to construct a continuous family of planar superalgebras, which we call the Clifford BMW supercategories. The tower of endomorphism algebras, $CW_n(σ, ε)$ is a combination of Birman Wenzl Murakami algebras and Clifford algebras, much in the spirit of the Hecke Clifford algebras. This tower of algebras appears to be new, and already yields some exciting combinatorics.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global Hölder regularity
papers.abstract: Let $ C_ω$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $ω\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_ω$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $β^+>0>β^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $β^\pm$. As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/β^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-Δ_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_ω$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$. The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global Hölder regularity for $(-Δ_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible Hölder exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.

papers.title: Validity of the Behrens--Fisher solution
papers.abstract: The Behrens--Fisher fiducial interval for the difference of two normal means is known from the numerical work of Robinson (1976) to be conservative, but a proof has been lacking. The results here prove that the fiducial interval for any linear combination of $k$ normal means has coverage probability at least its nominal level for all values of the unknown variances. Taraldsen (2026) explains this in more detail using the original data of Behrens (1926). The proof presented in the following rests on a novel plug-in inequality: if a threshold function controls a scaled sum of pivots pointwise in the scale vector, then it also controls the sum with the observed scales plugged in, provided the location errors satisfy a concentration condition formulated through a weighted geometric mean. Independent normal errors satisfy the condition.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.

papers.title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutions in 5+1 dimensions
papers.abstract: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically in [1] that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $λ=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction.

papers.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
papers.abstract: For every fixed odd $d\ge5$, we prove that the circular flow number of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph is asymptotically almost surely less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ for an explicit constant $\varepsilon_d>0$. At degree five the upper bound is $3-1/24006$. At degree seven it is $21/8$, answering a question of Li and Li. For every fixed $p\ge1$, we also obtain a strongly connected Jaeger orientation at degree $4p+1$, with outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$. At large degrees we count dense bisections together with sets that violate their cut inequalities. This gives flow intervals of length $O(d^{-2})$ above the maximum-bisection lower bound of Li and Li. The finite-degree estimates, together with the large-degree transfer, also prove the conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis that the threshold for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the corresponding bisection threshold by at most one.

papers.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_σ\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $σ\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

papers.title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
papers.abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every non-contractive bijection $F$ is asymptotically an isometry along its backward orbits: for all $a$ and $\varepsilon>0$, $0\le d(Fx,Fy)-d(x,y)<\varepsilon$ for $x$ far in the past of $a$ and all $y$. Zavarzina asked whether every such bijection of a precompact space is an isometry; the author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) answered no. Each such $F$ has a register, a quasi-pseudo-metric $λ^-\le d$ for which $F$ is an isometry, with round-trip distances totally bounded on orbits; after completion, $F$ acts on each orbit as a rotation of a compact monothetic group, its rigid shadow. The defect $d-λ^-$ from $x$ to $y$ is at most the fee of $x$ (the supremum of its defects to earlier iterates) and at least the excess of $x$'s fee over $y$'s now or at any earlier time, less their round-trip register distance; the fee never decreases forward along orbits and tends to zero backward. In this sense, every such $F$ is a toll over its rigid shadow. The fees bound the defect but do not determine it: three spirals show it can depend on $y$, vanish at a distant $y$ even when $x$ has a positive fee, and be positive toward later iterates of $x$. The toll-spiral paper asked whether every such map is conjugate to a tolled extension, a fixed toll zone over an isometric shadow, possibly with infinitely many zones. If only descents are charged, the answer is no, even up to bi-Lipschitz conjugacy; on each infinite orbit, a map is such an extension over its register exactly when its ascents carry no defect. Fees may vanish at any rate, but for zone tolls (two-valued, shift-monotone, subadditive along their routes) they reach zero at a finite depth. The general results hold on quasi-pseudo-metric spaces where every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; all but the statements listed at the end are machine-checked in Lean.

papers.title: Haagerup symmetries of the $E_8$ theory and conformal nets at central charge eight
papers.abstract: A Haagerup algebra is a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight with $\mathrm{Rep}(U)$ braided equivalent to the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category. We prove that $U$ has exactly three holomorphic extensions, each isomorphic to $V_{E_8}$, and that the corresponding Lagrangian algebras have module categories $\cal H_1$, $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$. The extensions attached to $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ are the two lattice extensions of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$. We prove a recognition theorem for $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ among unitary fusion categories of rank six with three invertible objects, a noncommutative Grothendieck ring and trivial pointed associator. For simple regular unitary vertex operator algebras with bounded localized vertex operators, we construct the transport module of two ordinary unitary modules when the second integrates in Tener's annular sense. For a unitary conformal Haagerup subalgebra of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, these results give a completely rational net with representation category $Z(\cal H_3)$, a realization of the Haagerup subfactor and the generalized orbifold of Bischoff. In particular, they apply to the strongly local explicit algebra $S$ of levels $(3,13)$, whose Haagerup property is established in [ArhIII, Theorem 6.1]. In [ArhIII], the net of $S$ is recognized from strong rationality and lattice branching, and a diagonal extension of the net is then used to identify $\mathrm{Rep}(S)$. Here an exact construction of the compatible unitary structure on the diagonal lattice algebra $V_{E_8 \oplus E_8}$, followed by passage to the twin algebra, proves complete unitarity and Condition I+ for every Haagerup algebra. This also gives the VOA--net comparison through smeared vertex operators for unitary conformal embeddings in $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$.

papers.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.title: Another Application of the Alternating Map: Time-and-Band Limiting
papers.abstract: Castillo's dual equations for the alternating map reduce polynomial time-and-band limiting to two scalar problems. We determine the concentration multiplicities at a single cutoff, with sharp finite support and moment requirements. When the scalar problems admit irreducible tridiagonal commutants, we classify every real symmetric pentadiagonal commutant of the simple concentration matrix and construct one with simple spectrum. Its half-bandwidth is minimal for $N\ge3$ in polynomial degree order. Laguerre, Jacobi and Meixner input give applications; the constructions of Castro and Grünbaum follow by specialization. We give spectral-gap and rounding bounds, and certify small concentration values and deficits for noninteger Jacobi parameters.

papers.title: Perfect 1-factorisations of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group
papers.abstract: A perfect 1-factorisation (P1F) of $K_{2n}$ is a partition of its edges into $2n-1$ perfect matchings, any two of which form a Hamiltonian cycle. Exhaustive classification is known only up to $K_{16}$. We present a method for the exhaustive generation, up to isomorphism, of perfect 1-factorisations with a non-trivial automorphism group, which reduces the search tree far enough to make $K_{18}$ and beyond feasible. It combines two ideas. For automorphism groups of order greater than 2, classical results of Ihrig on the automorphisms of P1Fs are used as tools that reject almost all prescribed cycle types without search. For the order-2 case, which dominates, candidates are recalculated from inherited compatibility lists, in the spirit of Gill and Wanless, with an outer loop over two further rows that keeps those lists small, and Ihrig's results restrict the first factor. As the numerical proof of the method we compute all 10,710 P1Fs of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group; before, only six were known.

papers.title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. Our main contribution is the development of an easy-to-implement observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. Furthermore, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of the same dispersive water-wave models.

papers.title: Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight
papers.abstract:
Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules. For the levels $(3,13)$, $U_2$ is one of four Galois conjugate subspaces. Together with $U_1$ it generates the unitary $C_2$-cofinite algebra $S$, which is isomorphic to the algebra constructed by Jiao. For the levels $(1,39)$, $U$ contains the explicit algebra of Riesen. The associated lattice of $U$ is that of the form $x^2+xy+10y^2$, resp.\ $3x^2+3xy+4y^2$, the two classes of the principal genus of discriminant $-39$. Exchanging them in the decomposition of $U$ over its Heisenberg commutant gives a Haagerup algebra $U^
atural$ of the other levels, and $U \mapsto U^
atural$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of the two cases. The classification gives exactly two isomorphism classes, forming a single hyperbolic genus, as soon as either explicit candidate is known to be a Haagerup algebra. This property is proved for $S$ in [ArhIII], where the twin $S^
atural$ is also identified, with the algebra of Huang and Riesen, using the results of Dong, Jiao and Xu [DJX26]. The explicit algebras of Jiao and Riesen have rational forms. The proofs combine exact trace relations given by vector-valued modular forms, exact computations in a model of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, and genera of vertex operator algebras.

papers.title: A study for well-filtered spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we focus on well-filtered spaces. By using the Rudin sets and WD sets, we obtain the following results: (1) The product of arbitrarily many Scott well-filtered dcpos is still well-filtered with respect to the Scott topology. Thus we give positive answers for two questions proposed by Xu and Zhao; (2) Let $P$ be a dcpo with $ΣK(P)$ being well-filtered and $Q$ an RB-domain. Then $ΣK(P\times Q)$ is well-filtered if $K(P\times Q)$ is a dcpo; (3) An intrinsic characterization of the $WD$ sets is given in terms of Scott open filters.

papers.title: Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
papers.abstract: We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors with alternating small differences lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for norm-sigma-compact DSS families and uniform nuclear tails on each compact piece. For norm-compact families we also obtain common Hilbert-space factors and uniformly small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. We present the main argument as a candidate proof over the real field.

papers.title: Representability of Graphical Symplectic Matroids
papers.abstract: Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.

papers.title: Sharp digirth bounds for C(k,k)-subdivisions in digraphs
papers.abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. We extend a problem of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud [European J. Combin. 122 (2024)] on subdivisions of $C(k,k)$ to digraphs with several vertices of out-degree one. Following the sharp result of Chen et al. [arXiv:2610.38574v1 (2026)] for at most one such vertex, we determine the exact digirth threshold when at most $r\ge4$ such vertices are permitted. Specifically, for all integers $k\ge2$ and $r\ge4$, every digraph of minimum out-degree at least one, with at most $r$ vertices of out-degree one and digirth at least $r(k-1)+1$, contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$.

papers.title: Coarse comparison of Bessel families
papers.abstract: A Bessel family is a collection of vectors of a Hilbert space whose coefficients are square summable; orthonormal bases and frames are examples. We compare two such families by asking when the size of the coefficients of one is controlled, up to constants, by that of the other after a change of variables taken from a fixed class $\mathcal O$ of operators. Each class (bounded, injective, bounded below, invertible, Fredholm, and others) gives an equivalence relation that ignores redundancy and treats frames and nonframes on the same footing. For every relation we determine the classes by explicit spectral data: the singular numbers of the analysis operator, its kernel, the closedness of its range, and the multiplicities of its spectrum at each dyadic scale. We also characterize the families equivalent to an orthonormal basis, compute an operator Banach--Mazur distance, and prove a Paley--Wiener stability result that needs no frame assumption. These relations are instances of the comparison categories of a companion article.

papers.title: On the Hodge Extension of Local Kähler Forms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Stein manifold, and let $K=\{h\le0\}$ be a compact sublevel set of a strictly plurisubharmonic function $h$ defined near $K$. It is known that $K$ is meromorphically convex in $X$ if and only if $dd^ch$ extends to a Hodge form on $X$. We show that if $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the direct sum of a free abelian group and a torsion group, for example if it is finitely generated or if $X$ is a Stein surface, then any extension of $dd^ch$ to a Kähler form on $X$ can be modified, after replacing $h$ by a positive multiple, into a Hodge form. Thus, meromorphic convexity of $K$ is equivalent to the extendability of $dd^ch$ as a Kähler form. We also show that the topological assumption cannot be dropped: we construct a Stein manifold $X$ of dimension $6$ with $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Q$, a sublevel set $K$ as above that is not meromorphically convex although $dd^ch$ extends to a Kähler form, and a totally real torus in $K$ that is isotropic for a Kähler form but is not meromorphically convex. This shows that the Hodge condition in Guedj's characterization of meromorphically convex totally real submanifolds cannot be weakened to a Kähler condition, and gives counterexamples to two criteria stated by Cieliebak and Eliashberg.

papers.title: No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces
papers.abstract: Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.

papers.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
papers.abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

papers.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
papers.abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and linearized polynomials connect field extensions, normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Cyclotomic cosets link additive symmetries and local phase data with polynomial composition, factorization, and compatible lifting. Low-degree subfield representations and relative traces lead to root-block recovery, while return maps on root fibers organize constructions of irreducible polynomials. Coding applications include duality, distance bounds, Fourier support, and syndrome decoding. Character sums yield trace-norm distributions, the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field sums and curve point counts. The final chapter constructs finite fields as residue fields of unramified p-adic extensions and relates Teichmuller representatives and Hensel lifting to cyclotomic orbits, periodic digit expansions, Witt carries, coefficient valuations, and Newton slopes. The emphasis throughout is on explicit proofs and reusable connections between field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

papers.title: An upper bound of 60 for the Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3)
papers.abstract: We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 60. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers.

papers.title: Classification of reduced free products of nuclear C*-algebras
papers.abstract: Consider the countably infinite reduced free product $D$ of copies of $(\mathrm C([0,1]),λ)$, where $λ$ is Lebesgue measure. It is proved that finite and countable reduced free products of unital separable nuclear UCT $\mathrm C^*$-algebras with respect to a chosen family of faithful traces are classified, after adjoining $D$, by the Elliott invariant. In other words, an isomorphism between the naive K-theory invariants of two such algebras is induced by an isomorphism between the algebras.

papers.title: Motivic $C_p$-power operations in $\mathrm{MGL}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of the Hopkins-Morel-Hoyois theorem for fields $k$ of characteristic unequal to $p$ containing all primitive $p$-power roots of unity for a fixed prime $p$. This new proof follows Quillen's proof for the structure of the homotopy groups of $\mathrm{MU}$ which utilizes topological power operations. To this end we define a motivic analog of the Steenrod power operations, using the theory of normed motivic spectra as developed by Bachmann--Hoyois and their application for the definition of motivic colimits as developed by Bachmann-Elmanto-Heller.

papers.title: Modular Existential Closedness
papers.abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(τ_1, \ldots, τ_n, j(τ_1), \ldots, j(τ_n)) \in V$ with $τ_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouché's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

papers.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The main result states that, under the assumption of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Based on this result, we also establish multilinear extrapolation of boundedness on rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and multilinear extrapolation of compactness on general Banach function spaces. Beyond that, we give characterizations of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on both general Banach function spaces and certain specific function spaces. All results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

papers.title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
papers.abstract: A central limitation of modern machine learning systems is the lack of formal certificates guaranteeing their behavior beyond empirical, sample-based evaluation. Sum-of-squares (SOS) methods provide such guarantees by certifying polynomial inequalities over continuous domains via semidefinite programming (SDP). While prior work has introduced SDP layers as differentiable components in neural networks, repeated learning calls can lose the computational benefit of the forward program's sparse representation. We propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve. Under a fixed template and learned objective coefficients, each layer avoids building dense certificates and reuses its sparse structure across training steps. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves up to 2.7 times speedup in total warm-call time, with nearly 100 times lower memory usage (1.7 vs. 160 GiB) for relatively large problem sizes for the tested dense parameterization. Experiments cover sparse polynomial certification, pendulum control, combinatorial relaxations, robotics projection, oscillator chains, and pose graph synchronization. A design study achieves zero certified violations across unseen problem instances and sizes, while requiring roughly 7 times fewer optimization solves than estimating gradients by perturbing the objective coefficients and re-solving the problem (finite differences). These results show that sparse certificate values can be effectively integrated into learning pipelines when the backward pass respects the verifier's structure.

papers.title: Weakly Unitary Zeon Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, zeon matrix groups are discussed for the first time. Extending the concept of unitary complex matrices (i.e., matrices $A$ such that $A^\dagger A=\mI$) to matrices having entries in the complex zeon algebra $\CZ$, a ``zeon dagger'' operator $\zdag$ is defined and used to declare a zeon matrix $Ξ$ to be {\em unitary} if $Ξ^\zdagΞ=\mI$. The unitary zeon matrices of order $n$ form a subgroup $\U_n$ of all invertible order-$n$ zeon matrices. A more interesting notion is that of ``weak unitarity'' of a zeon matrix. In particular, a zeon matrix $Ξ$ will be said to be {\em weakly unitary} if $Ξ^\zdagΞ=\mI+Γ$, where $Γ$ is a diagonal nilpotent zeon matrix. The weakly unitary matrices of order $n$ form a group $\W_n$, of which $\U_n$ is a subgroup. It is further shown that the exponential of a graph's nilpotent adjacency matrix has a natural orthogonal decomposition into the sum of a weakly unitary zeon matrix and a nilpotent zeon matrix. Eigenvalues of the weakly unitary zeon matrix reveal information about the graph's cycles and paths.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
papers.abstract: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $α$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($α= 0)$ and the SQG equation $(α= 1)$. We prove that, for every $α\in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$. The proof has been formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: SAT Solving by Multiplication in and Addition out of Clauses
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described in the two earlier articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a conjunction of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations by inverting the problem: we multiply letters (literals) in the transferred clauses and use a binary iterated composition based on adding polynomials for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value T=0. With reversed literal repetition, we get the CNF as the sum of the transformed clauses. In fact, we can always reduce to multiplication in and addition out of clauses, as we do not look for the entire kernel of PBE for a YES instance for SAT.

papers.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.

papers.title: Mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim beyond the polylog quotient
papers.abstract: We develop an algorithmic approach to mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim theory for the full unipotent fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \smallsetminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, beyond the polylogarithmic quotient used in previous work. The key step is computing the cocycle evaluation map in the presence of a nontrivial motivic Galois action, using relations among motivic multiple zeta values. This yields explicit Kim functions involving multiple polylogarithms, as well as an algorithm for solving the $S$-unit equation whose halting is implied by certain natural conjectures. As an application, we prove new instances of Kim's Conjecture, including the first examples with $\#S = 2$.

papers.title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
papers.abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean. By referring to an additional announced uniform zero-free half-plane for general Dedekind zeta functions, we also establish the corresponding result for certain explicit new families of non-Galois cubic, quartic and quintic fields of unit rank one or two.

papers.title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for the Minimal Input/Output Node Cardinality Disturbance Decoupling Problem over Networks via Output Feedback
papers.abstract: For networked systems, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm for solving the minimal input/output node cardinality disturbance decoupling problem via output feedback. The algorithm computes an optimal solution, namely, a pair of minimum-cardinality sets of control input and measurement output nodes that achieve disturbance decoupling, by solving a min-cut/max-flow problem on an extended network.

papers.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework leveraging knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix up to a linear transformation. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

papers.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic. The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest. Concurrently, another counterexample (of a very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.

papers.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
papers.abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

papers.title: Reduced Embry characterizations of quasinormal operators
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any two integers $2\le m<n$, a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfying \[ A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k, \qquad k\in\{m,n\}, \] is quasinormal. More generally, we show that the inequalities \[ A^{*m}A^m\ge(A^*A)^m \quad \text{and} \quad A^{*n}A^n\le(A^*A)^n \] already imply quasinormality. Together with the known single-exponent counterexamples, this completely resolves the reduced Embry problem for bounded operators: the identities $A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k$, $k\in S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots\}$, characterize quasinormality if and only if $S$ contains at least two distinct integers greater than one. We also resolve the flatness problem for operators of class $\mathcal A$: equality between two consecutive normalized moments $(A^{*n}A^n)^{1/n}$ and $(A^{*(n+1)}A^{n+1})^{1/(n+1)}$, with $n\ge2$, implies quasinormality. Both results rely on an interpolation estimate obtained either from Hansen's inequality or from the transformer inequality for weighted operator geometric means. The solution to the reduced Embry problem additionally uses an extremal argument for optimal power bounds.

papers.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
papers.abstract: On a totally bounded metric space, every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces this fails. Here quasi-metrics are $T_1$: $d(x,y)=0$ implies $x=y$. Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether rigidity holds at least for bijections. The author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) shows that it does not. We prove that compactness restores it: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity is needed, even on a compact, hereditarily precompact space. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps, we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is also Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. Such maps are then surjective. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$, $d(x,y)=0$ implies $d(y,x)=0$, if hereditary precompactness is taken to mean that every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; surjectivity then holds up to points at distance 0 both ways. The weaker $T_0$ axiom is not enough: there is a $T_0$ space, compact in both topologies and satisfying all the other hypotheses of both theorems, with a bijective non-contractive non-isometry. Finally, for an asymmetric norm in finite dimension, the classical theorem makes the symmetric unit ball and sphere rigid for all non-contractive self-maps, and the forward ones if the norm is $T_1$. In infinite dimension, the symmetric ball and sphere need not be plastic, and for the forward ones we pose the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler. The two theorems and the counterexamples of Section 6 are machine-checked in Lean, except the steps listed at the end.

papers.title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
papers.abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We show that it need not be, even when the space is hereditarily precompact. On the integers, take the distance of an irrational rotation and add a fixed toll $c>0$ to every step from a nonnegative integer down to a smaller one. The resulting space, the toll spiral, is a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, and the shift $n\mapsto n+1$ is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction works over any metric space $Y$: for every bijective isometry $σ$ of $Y$ and every point whose $σ$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, adding the same toll along the orbit gives such a counterexample, for instance over the $p$-adic odometer. The conjugate of the toll spiral is not even precompact, so the hypothesis on the conjugate in Zavarzina's positive result cannot be dropped, even for bijections. The toll spiral is also not expand-contract plastic, since the inverse shift is a non-expansive bijection that is not an isometry. For an arbitrary bijective non-contractive map $F$, the distance from $F^kx$ to $F^ky$ has a limit as $k\to-\infty$; $F$ is an isometry for this limit, and the excess $D_0$ of the distance over it is the defect. On a hereditarily precompact space, we prove a monochromy theorem: if a pair $(a,b)$ has positive defect $η$, then there are natural numbers $t_1<t_2<\cdots$ such that either $D_0(a,F^{-Δ}a)>η/4$ for every difference $Δ=t_j-t_i$ with $i<j$, or $D_0(F^{-Δ}b,b)>η/4$ for every such $Δ$. Three boundary results delimit the remaining question; the open case, that of separated spaces compact in one of their topologies, has since been settled by the author (arXiv:2610.14301). The construction, in general and for the circle, is machine-checked in Lean 4 using Mathlib, with no unproved steps.

papers.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction across Smoothness and Noise Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study adaptive stochastic non-convex optimization under unknown smoothness and noise conditions. Our algorithms require no smoothness constant, noise bound, initial function gap, or oracle-regime label. We first propose a fixed-budget method that combines normalized momentum, recursive variance reduction, and a fresh gradient stage, followed by fresh validation of the candidates. We prove that the same output has expected gradient norm $O(T^{-1/4})$ under objective smoothness and bounded noise variance, $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ for noiseless gradients, where $T$ counts individual gradient evaluations. We then develop an anytime algorithm whose three optimization paths preserve their endpoints across reporting and budget-extension boundaries. The same three rates hold at every deterministic query budget, although the algorithm receives no information about the budget $T$. The analysis combines a scale potential, a uniform second-moment bound, and accounting for candidates retained through unfinished blocks. An optional sample-mean selector further reduces cumulative validation work from $O(T)$ to $O(T^{2/3})$ while preserving these rates.

papers.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
papers.abstract: Given an integer $k \geq 2$, there are integers $M_k$ and $P_k$ so that for all $A \subseteq \mathbb F^n_p$ does not contain a restricted polynomial progression of the form \begin{align*} x, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^2 \\ y_2^2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n^2 \end{pmatrix}, \ldots, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^{k-1} \\ y_2^{k-1} \\ \vdots \\ y_n^{k-1} \end{pmatrix}, \end{align*} where $x \in \mathbb F^n_p$, with $p>P_k$, and $y \in \{0,2, 3, \ldots, M_k\}^n \backslash \{\vec{0} \}$, for some fixed $M_k$, then $A$ must have density bounded above by $\frac{C}{(\log^{(k^{O(k)})} n)^c}$, where $C, c>0$ only depend on $k$ and $p$. For $k\geq 4$, the best previously known bound came from the density Hales--Jewett theorem and was of inverse Ackermann type. The proof uses a recent inverse theorem for noise stability of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer, which arose in the study of constraint satisfaction problems. The main new ingredient is a proof that the underlying distribution counting restricted polynomial progressions does not admit a nontrivial abelian embedding, by way of an involved algebraic argument. Reasonable bounds are provided for $P_k$ and $M_k$.

papers.title: Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: The linear arrangement of a simple graph $G = (V,E)$ is a bijective labeling $π$ of the vertices of $G$ to the set $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The maximum linear arrangement ($\texttt{maxLA}$) problem is to determine whether $G$ has a labeling such that the sum of labels across $G$'s edges, $\sum_{uv \in E} |π(u) - π(v)|$, is at least a given value $k$. Minimum linear arrangement ($\texttt{minLA}$) is defined analogously. Both $\texttt{maxLA}$ and $\texttt{minLA}$ are known to be NP complete for general graphs. $\texttt{minLA}$ has shown to be NP complete for bipartite graphs by Evans and Shiloah in 1975. It has been an open problem whether the same holds for $\texttt{maxLA}$. In this paper we prove that $\texttt{maxLA}$ is NP complete for bipartite graphs.

papers.title: Local Characterizations of Oka Manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that strong dominability, the LAP, and the Oka property are equivalent for complex manifolds. The proof turns approximation across an attached disc in one complex variable, uniformly in holomorphic parameters, into convex approximation in arbitrary dimension. We also characterize Oka manifolds by the LEP, formulated in terms of centered holomorphic families of discs. In dimension $n\geq1$, LEP propagates across sets of zero $(2n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The Oka property is local in the Euclidean topology, and it descends under surjective holomorphic maps between connected complex manifolds. Deformations of very free rational curves give the Oka property for every smooth connected complex projective rationally connected manifold $X$, and for $X\setminus A$ whenever $A\subset X$ is a closed algebraic subset of codimension at least two. Compact Kähler manifolds admitting a Kähler metric with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature, or having nef tangent bundle, are also Oka. For $n\geq1$, the complement of a smooth hypersurface $D\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ is Oka if and only if $d\leq n+1$.

papers.title: The consistency strength of the failure of amenable C-sequences
papers.abstract: We determine the consistency strength of the existence of a regular uncountable cardinal carrying no amenable $C$-sequence. It is equiconsistent with the existence of an inaccessible cardinal $κ$ which is $Π^1_ξ$-indescribable for every $ξ<κ^+$ in the transfinite second-order hierarchy of indescribability. For the lower bound, we prove that the failure of amenability at $κ$ implies that $L$ contains such a cardinal at or below $κ$, using constructible guessing sequences, correct constructible levels, and a transfinite induction. For the upper bound, we prepare the cardinal so that every proper initial segment of a full Hechler iteration of length $κ^+$ preserves weak compactness. Each final $C$-sequence appears at a bounded stage and is captured at the next stage on a stationary set; the remaining closed iteration preserves that capture.

papers.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
papers.abstract: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an $(m,n)$ Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers $m,n$.

papers.title: Logarithmic upper bounds and axial front selection for spatially periodic lattice Fisher--KPP equations
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=Δ_{\Z^d}u+F(x,u)$ on $\Z^d$ ($d\geq2$) with a spatially periodic Fisher--KPP reaction $F$ and a nonzero, finitely supported initial datum $u_0:\Z^d\to[0,1]$. We establish a logarithmic upper bound on the front position that holds uniformly in the observation direction, with a logarithmic delay coefficient governed by the outward normal to the asymptotic spreading body. When the linearized growth rate $F_s(x,0)$ is independent of the longitudinal coordinate, we prove the matching axial Bramson correction and show that the solution converges uniformly on fixed-width half-tubes to a critical pulsating front up to a bounded, slowly varying phase shift. For critical pulsating profiles $Φ(s,x)$ satisfying $Φ(s,x)\leq C(1+s)\ee^{-λs}$ for $s\geq0$ and $x\in\Z^d$, where $λ>0$ is the critical spatial decay rate, we derive the precise leading-edge asymptotic expansion and prove uniqueness up to translation. As a consequence, in the axial regime we obtain sharp asymptotics for the arrival times $T_θ(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:u(t,x)\geqθ\}$ ($0<θ<1$), including the asymptotic time lag between distinct level sets at a remote site and the period-to-period passage time along the axis. For general periodic linearized growth rates, we introduce a nonlinear subsolution built from a positive quotient of linear Dirichlet evolutions on a retreating domain and formulate sufficient kernel estimates for a matching directional lower bound.

papers.title: Amortized Score-Hamiltonian Policy Iteration: A Grid-Free Scheme for Relaxed Stochastic Control Problems
papers.abstract: We develop an amortized, grid-free implementation of continuous Langevin dynamics based policy-value iteration for entropy-regularized, infinite-horizon relaxed stochastic control problems. The improvement rate of the exact iteration is a discounted aggregate of relative Fisher information between the policy and the Gibbs law of its Hamiltonian. The associated score residual is the velocity with which the control's Langevin dynamics transport its law. We project this velocity onto a conditional sampler shared across states, instead of one Langevin dynamics per state, and the value dynamics onto a parametric critic, estimating both projections at sampled states to obtain coupled actor--critic flows. The score loss measures the actor's agreement with the current critic, while the policy-evaluation residual measures the critic's agreement with the actor. We also derive gradient and Hessian residuals, including a Feynman--Kac representation for the gradient equation, to control errors not detected by the projected value iteration. An exact decomposition of the HJB residual combines these errors into a policy-suboptimality bound under verification and logarithmic Sobolev assumptions. In the linear-quadratic class, both projections are exact and recover the pointwise iteration, and we provide numerical experiments on general models to demonstrate the coupled actor--critic learning in high-dimensions.

papers.title: A Dubnov-Ivanov-Nagata-Higman Theorem for NIP nilrings
papers.abstract: We prove that NIP nilrings of bounded nilexponent are nilpotent. We also deduce that NIP $ω$-categorical $n$-Engel Lie algebras of characteristic $p>n$ are nilpotent, yielding a case of the Lie algebra analogous of Wilson conjecture for $ω$-categorical groups.

papers.title: Betti Numbers of Odd Biisotropic Symplectic Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We compute the singular cohomology groups of odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ by presenting an explicit dimension-preserving combinatorial bijection between the Bialynicki-Birula cells in $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ and the Schubert cells in $\operatorname{Gr}(k, 2n+2-k)$.

papers.title: Cubic arithmetic-geometric mean and isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves
papers.abstract: We construct degree-three isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic different from three, which correspond to a step of the cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. As an application, we describe the Serre-Tate canonical lift of an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic three by the 3-adic cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. We also discuss the relations of the Hesse curves with complex and finite hypergeometric functions.

papers.title: Boundary-layer separation beyond the square-root law
papers.abstract: We construct solutions to the two-dimensional stationary Prandtl system under a constant adverse pressure gradient exhibiting a family of distinct separation laws. More precisely, for every integer $\ell\ge1$, we construct smooth initial data for which separation occurs at a finite location $x=x^\ast$, with \[ \partial_y u(x,0) =\mathbf C_\ell(x^\ast-x)^{\ell/2}\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr), \qquad x\uparrow x^\ast, \] where $\mathbf C_\ell>0$ depends on the initial data. We determine the local asymptotic structure of the solution near separation through matched inner and outer expansions based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. This description addresses Open Problem~5 proposed by Oleinik and Samokhin~\cite{OleinikSamok-book-99}. We prove the nonlinear stability of the square-root separation law ($\ell=1$) under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.

papers.title: Aigner's majorization conjecture in quantitative group testing: counterexamples and eventual sufficiency for star forests
papers.abstract: We refute Aigner's majorization conjecture for star forests in adaptive quantitative group testing with two defective items. Each test counts the defectives in a chosen subset; the possible defective pairs form the edges of a star forest. Aigner's necessary majorization condition is sufficient through five tests but is not sufficient at any budget from six onward. Nevertheless, for every fixed number of stars, it becomes sufficient once the test budget is large enough. We prove that majorization is sufficient for all forests with at most twenty-nine stars, and that this bound is sharp. We also construct counterexamples that pass arbitrarily many successive compatibility checks based on majorization. The five-test converse, counterexamples, eventual sufficiency theorem and unbounded-delay construction have analytic proofs. The sharp finite support bounds also use exact integer-inequality certificates.

papers.title: Structure of derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings
papers.abstract: In this article, we study derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings regarded as discrete rings. We compare each such algebra with the degreewise inverse limit of the derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in finite rings and with its subalgebra consisting of elements with uniformly finite double-coset support. Under cohomological comparison hypotheses, the natural map to this subalgebra has image given by its degree-zero part and its positive-degree torsion. We describe the kernel in terms of continuous cohomology and prove that it is a divisible square-zero ideal annihilated by every positive-degree element. These comparisons are compatible with Yoneda products, and the action on torsion Ext classes factors through the image. We compute the resulting algebras for the additive group $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and determine the underlying graded abelian groups for $(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p),\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_p))$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p>3$. The examples exhibit distinct effects of the coefficient topology and the support condition.

papers.title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) is commonly approached through specialized acquisition functions or scalarization schemes designed to explicitly account for trade-offs among non-preferential objectives. In this work, we show that such complexity might be unnecessary. We propose a framework that extends standard single-objective acquisition functions directly to the multi-objective setting through a hypervolume-based methodology. We further extend hedge strategies for acquisition functions, which are typically used only in single-objective optimization, to the multi-objective regime. Our approach requires minimal modification to existing Bayesian optimization pipelines and avoids the need for bespoke multi-objective formulations. We demonstrate how a broad class of commonly used single-objective acquisition functions and hedge strategies can be adapted in a principled manner to handle multiple objectives, while preserving their intuitive interpretation and computational efficiency. Empirically, we evaluate the proposed methods across a range of synthetic and real-world multi-objective benchmarks. Despite their simplicity, our extensions consistently match or outperform more complex state-of-the-art MOBO methods in terms of optimization performance and sample efficiency. These results suggest that effective multi-objective Bayesian optimization can be achieved by reusing and carefully extending well-established single-objective acquisition strategies, offering a simpler and more flexible alternative to existing approaches.

papers.title: Multiplicity-Weighted Moments of a Two-Monomial Harmonic Map Beyond the Caustic
papers.abstract: While the Jacobian of a planar harmonic mapping keeps a constant sign, the signed and the unsigned area elements agree up to that sign, and the two natural moment hierarchies coincide. Once the Jacobian changes sign the critical circle acquires a caustic as its image, part of the plane is covered several times with opposite orientations, and the hierarchies part company: integrating a radial weight against $J_F$ lets overlapping sheets cancel, giving the degree-weighted moments $J_n$, while integrating against $|J_F|$ lets every sheet count positively, giving the multiplicity-weighted moments $J_n^{\pm}$. These are the classical degree and area formulas for the same map, the second weighted by the multiplicity function (Banach indicatrix). It is the second family, the one the caustic threatens, for which a closed form is no longer automatic. For the two-monomial map $F(w)=w+iC\bar w^{k}$ on an annulus we show that it has one anyway: $J_n^{\pm}$ is the total variation of the very same explicit primitive whose endpoint difference gives $J_n$. Crossing the caustic therefore costs exactly one extra evaluation point, the critical radius $r_*=(k|C|)^{-1/(k-1)}$, and it is the same point for every order $n$: the weight $|F|^{2n}$ is nonnegative and so contributes no sign change of its own. On the degree-weighted side $J_n$ has a boundary-only closed form for every $n\ge0$, the zeroth being the signed area of the image counted with degree, and the complex-weighted moments vanish unless $(k+1)\mid(m-\ell)$. Neither weighted integral is a new object, and the caustic of this family has been located before in the literature on harmonic trinomials; what is new is the closed evaluation of the multiplicity-weighted hierarchy across it.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $α$ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_α^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.

papers.title: Geometric Detection and Finiteness of Log Crystalline Local Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a geometric detection theorem for log crystalline local systems in the smooth proper setting with a normal crossings boundary. The associated special-fiber log $F$-isocrystal detects geometric absolute irreducibility and, modulo constant rank-one twists, determines the pullback to the geometric generic fiber. The main ingredient is a determinant argument combining a finite-order rank-one reduction, logarithmic period comparison, and the Plücker embedding. As an application, using Abe--Esnault's finiteness theorem and finiteness of stable lattices, we prove finiteness, up to geometrically constant rank-one twists, of geometrically absolutely irreducible log crystalline local systems of fixed rank. Coefficients may lie in any fixed finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and no bound on the Hodge--Tate weights is imposed.

papers.title: When is the twist of a Leavitt path algebra again a Leavitt path algebra?
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Zhang twist of Leavitt path algebra $L_K(E)$ using a graded automorphism $σ$ induced by a graph automorphism such that the twisted algebra is a Leavitt path algebra over another graph $E_σ$ which is a twisted graph obtained from the original graph $E$. We also show that the hypothesis that $σ$ be induced by a graph automorphism cannot be dropped as we construct a graded automorphism of the Leavitt path algebra of an infinite graph whose Zhang twist is not isomorphic to any Leavitt path algebra. We also define the notion of noncommutative projective scheme for $\mathbb Z$-graded algebras that coincides with the notion of noncommutative projective scheme for connected $\mathbb N$-graded algebras defined by Artin and Zhang and study it in the context of twists of Leavitt path algebras. We establish combinatorial connection between the graphs $E$ and $E_σ$ and as a consequence, we show that many ring-theoretic properties are invariant for Leavitt path algebras under the twist by $σ$. In particular, we show that the invariant basis number property is preserved under Zhang twists considered here for finite graphs, whereas the module type is not preserved.

papers.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
papers.abstract: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.

papers.title: Projective Rigidity of $U(k)$-Radial Ricci-Flat Kähler Metrics
papers.abstract: We study Kähler immersions of Ricci-flat metrics into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space. Let $L^{\otimes k}\simeq K_X$ over a real-analytic Kähler manifold $X$. Let $φ$ be a base potential and $s$ the canonical squared fibre norm on $L^{\oplus k}$. Consider Ricci-flat potentials $φ+h(s)$ near the zero section, with $h$ independent of the base point. We prove that local projective inducibility forces the base to be Ricci-flat and the metric to split locally as $X\times\mathbb C^k$. In that case projective inducibility is equivalent to that of the base. The proof combines Calabi's criterion, positivity of the homogeneous fibre-degree blocks, and the singularities of the radial profile. A related obstruction along holomorphic curves excludes every positive multiple of the Taub--NUT metric and Calabi's hyperkähler metrics on $T^{*1,0}\mathbb{CP}^n$. Applications also include the resolved conifold, canonical-bundle metrics in non-Einstein classes, and Cifarelli's rank-two Type-2 metric.

papers.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
papers.abstract: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

papers.title: Dynamic Centrality Measures for Water Distribution Network Hydraulics
papers.abstract: Water distribution networks (WDNs) are susceptible to various failures, including but not limited to human errors, cyber-attacks, and network modifications, necessitating the vulnerability analysis of WDNs. Graph-theoretic centrality measures---as a main class of centrality measures---aim to rank the network components solely based on their influence (i.e., criticality) on the WDN topology in the case of input changes, while overlooking the WDN dynamics.
