To overcome such a limitation, this paper uses a control-theoretic centrality measure to identify the network's most and least influential pipes in WDNs, by simultaneously incorporating the dynamics and topology of the WDN. First, given a WDN modeled by nonlinear differential-algebraic equations (NDAEs) consisting of transient flow dynamics as differential equation (DE) and conservation of water mass as algebraic equation (AE) and considering the pipe flow rates as states of the state-space (SS) representation, we extract a linearized system modeled by linear ordinary differential equations (LODEs) around the equilibrium (i.e., steady) flow rate vector. Second, treating pipe flow rates as SS nodes (states), we introduce a node centrality-based measure, namely \textit{vulnerability vector (VV)}, to rank the network pipes based on their influence on the dynamics and topology of the WDN in the case of input changes. In particular, the network's most and least influential pipes can be identified through such a centrality-based approach. This enables water engineers to understand the WDN's vulnerability better and effectively prioritize the maintenance and operational efforts on the most influential pipes within the WDN.

papers.title: Vertex interpolation by bivariate $C^1$ cubic splines: counterexamples, geometric stability, and indecomposable defects
papers.abstract: We study vertex evaluation on the full space of continuously differentiable piecewise cubic polynomials on a fixed planar triangulation. A complete dual description turns failure of interpolation into balanced edge weights with nonzero vertex loading. It leads to exact counterexamples with 17, 25, 31 and 41 vertices, each with one relation and the classical lower-bound dimension. The 31- and 41-vertex examples have interior graphs that are trees. We give a geometric construction criterion for a sector-completion family and a certified implicit construction outside that family. With all boundary vertices fixed, the nearby bad configurations form a four-dimensional smooth locus in the 17-vertex case, two intersecting components of dimensions six and five in the 25-vertex case, and isolated transverse points in the two tree examples. A common Schur-complement estimate explains their different interpolation costs. We first realize arbitrary defect by decomposable chains of the 41-vertex example. We then construct obstructions from individually interpolatory blocks, prove that the capacity of one complete edge is exactly five, and build a fixed-square family with arbitrarily large strongly indecomposable defect. The latter excludes two triangle-disjoint connected normal bad submeshes even when those submeshes may have holes.

papers.title: Resolvent Estimates for the Stokes Operator in a Three-Dimensional Lipschitz Domain
papers.abstract: By refining the approach developed in \cite{AGH-2015, GS2026a}, we establish resolvent estimates in $L^p_σ(Ω)$ for the Stokes operator in a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$ in $\R^3$ for $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$, where $\e>0$ depends on $Ω$. As a consequence, the Stokes operator generates a uniformly bounded analytic semigroup in $L^p_σ(Ω)$. The range for $p$ is sharp. The results are particularly surprising, as it is long believed that the $L^p$ resolvent estimates in three-dimensional Lipschitz domains may fail for large $p$. In the appendices we prove an interpolation theorem between $L^2_σ(Ω)$ and $L^\infty_σ(Ω)$. We also show that for $1< p< \infty$ and a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$ in $\R^d, d\ge 2$, the resolvent estimate in $L^p(Ω; \C^d)$ can hold only if the Helmholtz projection is bounded on this space. This explains the counter-example constructed in \cite{Deuring-2001}. Finally, we prove that the resolvent estimate may fail in $L^p_σ(Ω)$ for $1< p< (3/2)$ and $d\ge 3$ as a consequence of failure of the Helmholtz decomposition of $L^p(Ω; \C^d)$.

papers.title: Multiple ergodic averages for commuting multiplicative actions
papers.abstract: We study the convergence of multiple ergodic averages involving several commuting multiplicative actions. We prove that for finitely generated systems, the averages $$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N S_{1,n}F_1\cdot\ldots\cdot S_{\ell,n}F_\ell$$ converge in norm, settling a conjecture of Frantzikinakis. Our proofs feature tools from ergodic theory and probabilistic number theory. We exploit some stability properties of additive functions to establish a novel variant of \Katai's orthogonality criterion, which leads to box seminorm control for our averages. Using the theory of magic extensions introduced by Host and a delicate complexity reduction argument, we eventually reduce our problem to known convergence results.

papers.title: Robust Model Order Selection via Dithered Differential Step-Down Thresholding
papers.abstract: We propose a dithered differential step-down thresholding (DSDT) algorithm for robust model order selection in stationary noise. Evaluating only exceedance counts over a decreasing threshold grid, the proposed algorithm stops when detecting noise extrema value clustering. We prove that deterministic threshold grids are inconsistent under lowered floor detection thresholds due to threshold grid misalignment error. We bound this error using randomized grid dithering. For arbitrary deterministic shifts, any joint noise distribution, and data-dependent thresholds, we obtain non-asymptotic bounds on the estimation risk and family-wise error rate, establishing DSDT as a universal false alarm suppressor for any single-threshold algorithm. When the scale sequence tends to zero or extremes cluster along the search grid, DSDT achieves asymptotic exact order recovery of separated deterministic components exceeding the noise maximum plus the grid step, even below the minimax threshold or without a detection threshold. Using multiple independent dithers reduces error bounds. We provide convergence and consistency analysis for an arbitrary number of dithers. This analysis establishes asymptotic bounds under extreme value laws and non-asymptotic bounds under nondecreasing hazard rates. The results extend to unseparated deterministic shifts, random shifts, unknown noise scales, and multi-dimensional search grids. We show that DSDT is robust to data quantization.

papers.title: Asymptotic Bounds for Online Ramsey Numbers of Stars versus Long Paths and Cycles
papers.abstract: The online Ramsey game for graphs $G$ and $H$ is played on the infinite complete graph $K_\mathbb{N}$. In each round, Builder chooses an edge, and Painter colors it red or blue. The online Ramsey number $\tilde{r}(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $t$ for which Builder has a strategy guaranteeing a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ within $t$ rounds. For every fixed integer $k\ge4$, the best-known asymptotic lower bounds for $\tilde{r}(K_{1,k},P_n)$ and $\tilde{r}(K_{1,k},C_n)$ are $\left(\frac{k+3}{4}+o(1)\right)n$ as $n\to\infty$. We improve the corresponding asymptotic upper bounds from $\left(k+o(1)\right)n$ to $\left(\frac{k+3}{3}+o(1)\right)n$ as $n\to\infty$.

papers.title: Selfless Reduced Crossed Product $C^{*}$-Algebras Arising from Almost Periodic Actions
papers.abstract: We prove that the reduced crossed product arising from an almost periodic action of an infinite countable discrete group on a unital, separable $C^*$-algebra is selfless whenever the crossed product is simple and monotracial and the group admits a topologically free extreme boundary action. We also give an alternative proof of a special case of a result of Gao, Junge, Kunnawalkam Elayavalli, Patchell, and Robert: the direct product of an exact $C^*$-simple group and a $C^*$-selfless group is $C^*$-selfless.

papers.title: Robust High-Order Projector-Splitting Integrators
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze an increment-based $K$-$L$ integrator for dynamical low-rank approximation. This formulation eliminates the separate backward $S$-step and is algebraically equivalent to the fixed-increment projector-splitting integrator of Lubich and Oseledets. We establish a relaxed-exactness estimate that bounds the error in the low-rank approximation in terms of the prescribed increment error, with constants independent of small singular values. This estimate provides a framework for achieving robust high-order convergence through sufficiently accurate increments. We then construct low-rank Runge--Kutta methods in which both the stage and final approximations are computed using the $K$-$L$ integrator, without basis augmentation or rank truncation. Since classical Runge--Kutta order conditions alone do not guarantee robust high-order convergence for this construction, we derive sufficient conditions on the coefficients that ensure the required stage accuracy and establish robust convergence of order $p$. We identify explicit Runge--Kutta schemes of orders $p=2,3,4$ satisfying these conditions, and numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

papers.title: Spanning $H$-subdivisions with Prescribed Path Lengths
papers.abstract: We study spanning $H$-subdivisions in dense graphs where the length of every subdivision path is prescribed in advance. This problem is motivated in part by a question of Pavez-Signé [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128], who asked whether the subdivision paths in a spanning $H$-subdivision can be required to have similar lengths. Let $h\ge3$ be an integer and let $0<β\llα\ll1/h$. We prove that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $δ(G)\ge n/2+\lfloor h/3\rfloor$ has the following property. For every graph $H$ with $h$ edges and no isolated vertices, write $E(H)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_h\}$, and every choice of integers $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_h\ge4$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^h\ell_i=n-|V(H)|+h$ and $\sum_{\ell_i<αn}\ell_i\leβn$, the graph $G$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision in which the $i$th edge of $H$ is replaced by a path of length exactly $\ell_i$. We also give a family of examples showing that a linear additive term in $h$ is necessary in general.

papers.title: Nearly balanced spanning subdivisions in dense digraphs
papers.abstract: Pavez-Signé [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128] conjectured a Dirac-type condition for spanning $H$-subdivisions and asked whether the subdivision paths can additionally be required to have similar lengths. Lee [European J. Combin. 124 (2025), 104059] resolved the existence conjecture in the stronger setting of digraphs. We answer the length-control question in this stronger directed setting: for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $C_0>0$ such that, for every digraph $H$ with $h$ arcs and no isolated vertices, every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ with $n\ge C_0h$ and $δ^0(D)\ge(1/2+\varepsilon)n$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision whose subdivision paths have lengths differing by at most one.

papers.title: Equi-dependence implying independence
papers.abstract: It is shown that, if an event $A$ has the same conditional probability in each trial in an infinite sequence of Bernoulli trials, then $A$ is independent of each trial. More general results are actually established.

papers.title: Schwarzian Residue of the Samuelson Obstruction in Tangent Lagrangian 2-Webs
papers.abstract:
The Samuelson condition, a classical area-ratio condition for planar Lagrangian $2$-webs, is equivalent in local web coordinates $(u,v)$ to $\partial_u\partial_v\log|J_F(u,v)|=0$, where $F$ is the inverse web-coordinate map and $J_F$ is its Jacobian. For the tangent-line family $L_t: y=tx+h(t)$, with $h$ smooth on an open interval, let $Ψ(u,v)$, for $u
eq v$, be the intersection map of $L_u$ and $L_v$, write $J_Ψ$ for its Jacobian, and set $S_h(u,v) := \partial_u\partial_v\log|J_Ψ(u,v)|$ where $J_Ψ(u,v)
eq0$. Near each diagonal point $(t_0,t_0)$ with $h''(t_0)
eq0$, the obstruction admits the decomposition $S_h(u,v) =  rac{1}{(v-u)^2} + R_h(u,v)$, where $R_h$ extends smoothly across the diagonal near $(t_0,t_0)$. The universal pole yields $S_h(u,v)>0$ off the diagonal in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $(t_0,t_0)$, so the tangent web does not satisfy the Samuelson condition there. We call $R_h(t,t)$ the Schwarzian residue and show that $R_h(t,t) =  rac{1}{2}\{σ,t\} = -κ_{\mathrm{aff}}(σ) \left( rac{dσ}{dt}ight)^2$. Here $σ$ is the equi-affine arclength parameter of the envelope $γ(t)=(-h'(t),h(t)-t h'(t))$, and $\{σ,t\}$ denotes the Schwarzian derivative of $σ$ with respect to $t$. The equi-affine curvature $κ_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is defined by $γ_{σσσ}+κ_{\mathrm{aff}}γ_σ=0$. We also derive the transformation law of the residue under reparametrization of the tangent-line family.

papers.title: The maximum volume polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the sphere
papers.abstract: A classical problem in convex and discrete geometry asks for the convex polyhedron of greatest volume whose vertices are chosen from the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$. For a prescribed number $N$ of vertices, the problem is known only in a small number of cases, namely $4\leq N\leq 8$ and $N=12$. In the case $N=9$, Wimmer showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the volume maximizer must be combinatorially equivalent to a triaugmented triangular prism. In this note, we complete the proof by determining the volume maximizer among all inscribed polytopes which are combinatorially equivalent to a triaugmented triangular prism. Consequently, every convex polyhedron with at most nine vertices on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has volume at most $3\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}-3}$, with equality, up to rotation, precisely for the ``symmetric'' triaugmented triangular prism whose vertex coordinates we compute exactly.

papers.title: Optimal Oracle Complexity for Weakly Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the oracle complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $ρ$-weakly convex and $G$-Lipschitz functions, where stationarity is measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope. We consider an exact first-order oracle that returns both the function value and the full subdifferential at every query point. In the principal parameter regime, we prove that every first-order algorithm, including randomized algorithms, requires $Ω(\tfrac{ρG^2Δ}{ε^4})$ oracle queries to succeed with any fixed positive probability, where $f(0)-\inf f\leΔ$. This lower bound matches the best known deterministic and stochastic first-order upper bounds, up to universal constants, and establishes the optimal randomized first-order oracle complexity. The result separates smooth nonconvex and weakly convex optimization: the additional $ε^{-2}$ factor is intrinsic to nonsmooth geometry rather than stochastic oracle noise.

papers.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
papers.abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkané to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}

papers.title: Contact Surgery Numbers of the 3-torus
papers.abstract: We study contact surgery numbers for contact structures on the 3-torus. We show that all contact structures obtained via contact surgery along a Legendrian Borromean ring are overtwisted, and that this construction yields infinitely many pairwise non-contactomorphic contact structures on $\mathbb{T}^3$. We prove an obstruction on the maximal Thurston-Bennequin invariant of 3-component links to produce $\mathbb{T}^3$ by Dehn surgery. We also compare Legendrian surgery presentations of the Stein-fillable contact structure on $\mathbb{T}^3$. In this setting, we exhibit a non-destabilizable Legendrian knot with no graded normal ruling whose associated Stein filling has nonzero full symplectic homology.

papers.title: Incidence algebras and beyond: brick-continuity and generic bricks
papers.abstract: We will show that the twelve families of minimally representation-infinite incidence algebras are brick-continuous and admit a generic brick, which will be explicitly constructed. After that, reversing the reduction process between posets, we will show that any representation-infinite incidence algebra is brick-continuous and admits a generic brick, which can be explicitly computed using what will be called ''extension functors''. Lastly, a method to apply these results to a broader class of algebras is given.

papers.title: Topological Rigidity of Contractible 3-Manifolds and Handlebody Interiors under Nonnegative Scalar Curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that a contractible $3$-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to $\R^3$. We also prove that, if the interior of a compact handlebody of genus $γ$ admits such a metric, then $γ\leq1$. This answers two open questions posed by Wang and Gromov, respectively.

papers.title: Relative stability, relative categoricity and internal covers
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a countable complete theory with a distinguished unary predicate $P$, and let $T^{P}$ be the theory of the $P$-parts of models of $T$ with the induced structure. $T$ is said to be relatively categorical or categorical over $P$ if any isomorphism between the $P$-parts of two models of $T$ lifts to an isomorphism of the models in question. We study the special case of relative categoricity where $T$ is internal to $T^{P}$ (that is, every model $M$ of $T$ is in the definable closure of $P(M)$ together with additional parameters from $M$). We first give a structure theory for such $T$: after passing to $T^{eq}$ and naming a parameter, $T$ is the same thing as a "pure torsor cover" of $T^{P}$, namely simply adjoining to $T^{P}$ a new sort for a torsor $S$ for a $\emptyset$-definable group $G$ in $T^{P}$, with no additional structure. We discuss relative stability, or stability over $P$, and give a characterization of relative stability, superstability, and $ω$-stability of $T$ in terms of $H$ having the stable chain condition, superstable chain condition, and $ω$-stable chain condition, respectively.

papers.title: Mersenne Representation, the Conolly Sequence, and Soliton Profiles over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We study the canonical skew-binary representation of nonnegative integers, whose positional weights are the Mersenne numbers \(2^{k}-1\), and its decomposition into the binary and nonbinary sides. The nonbinary values, arranged in increasing order, form the OEIS sequence A055938, and their successor structure gives a direct proof of the relation with the OEIS sequence A080578 that is recorded as conjectural in the OEIS entry for A080578. The resulting formulas show that the Conolly sequence describes both sides of the decomposition: a shifted Conolly sequence is the counting function of the binary side, while the same sequence gives the increasing enumeration of the nonbinary side. We then develop the parent map, truncation blocks, truncation remainders, and the Mersenne tau function associated with this representation. The parent map is conjugate to deletion of the lowest digit. Differences of the Mersenne tau rows recover the parent iterates and the counting function, and they give formulas for digit reconstruction and for a diagonal tau defect. Finally, we revisit a known finite-depth one-soliton family of the finite-field BBS. The Mersenne combinatorics is used directly to reconstruct a global integer-valued traveling-wave profile and to prove an integer window-counting theorem. Reduction modulo \(3\) yields the corresponding finite-field traveling-wave solutions. We also construct an integer-valued traveling-wave tau function whose front values are given by the Mersenne tau rows. The resulting construction shows how the combinatorics of a number representation can enter directly into the reconstruction of solutions of an integrable system.

papers.title: Divisor moments of polynomials in Fourier coefficients of modular forms
papers.abstract: We study higher moments of the divisor function evaluated at polynomial expressions in the Fourier coefficients of a non-CM newform. The logarithmic exponent appearing in our estimates depends only on the number of irreducible factors of the polynomial and remains unchanged under a Sato--Tate restriction. The proof combines an effective Chebotarev theorem, or an effective Chebotarev--Sato--Tate theorem, with the arithmetic of joint cycle types and a mean value estimation for multivariable multiplicative functions with Frobenian support.

papers.title: A Continual Validation, Updating, and Decision-Making Framework for Self-Adaptive Digital Twins: A Case Study in Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Digital Twins support real-time decision-making through predictive models of physical systems, yet their reliability can deteriorate as operating conditions evolve. Maintaining predictive fidelity under such changes is challenging, particularly when model adaptation relies on limited streaming data, and updated models must be evaluated before deployment. Here, we present an online adaptation framework that integrates gradient-based drift detection, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and statistical model validation within model predictive control. Changes in prediction-loss gradients trigger batch-wise model updates using Low-Rank Adaptation, while a paired moving-block bootstrap test evaluates predictive improvement before deploying the updated model. The framework is evaluated using a stochastic dynamical system with abrupt changes and a simulated directed energy deposition process with gradual changes in material properties. Results show improvements in predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation during the evaluated post-adaptation intervals, alongside improved reference tracking and reduced constraint violations in the manufacturing case study compared with the investigated baselines. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating continual validation with model adaptation while acknowledging the trade-off between responsiveness and predictive reliability in evolving Digital Twins.

papers.title: On Lagrangians of Oakley-Usher type
papers.abstract: The main theme of this paper is to study symplectic (un-)knottedness of Lagrangian submanifolds which are not tori. Our construction of such Lagrangians is inspired by the generalized Polterovich Lagrangians of Oakley--Usher and relies on an adaptation of symplectic reduction methods going back to Chekanov--Schlenk and McDuff's probes to the case of non-abelian group actions. We compare Oakley--Usher Lagrangians to their (un-)knotted cousins to find that, depending on the situation, they are: (1) not diffeomorphic, (2) diffeomorphic, but not Lagrangian isotopic, (3) Lagrangian isotopic, but not Hamiltonian isotopic, (4) Hamiltonian isotopic. This relationship between them frequently changes when the ambient space is compactified by a symplectic cut. In the companion paper "Lagrangian tori in the three-dimensional quadric and mirror symmetry", we focus on monotone tori in the three-dimensional quadric and compute their enumerative invariants and study their relationship to mirror symmetry.

papers.title: On Congruences modulo powers of 3 for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partitions in $k$-Colors
papers.abstract: In 2017, Keith defined and studied a multi-restricted partition function $RD^{l,t}(n)$, the number of integer partitions of n into parts that are simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct if none of the parts is divisible by $l$ and parts appear fewer than $t$ times. Thereafter, in a series of papers Buragohain et al. and Nadji et al. examined combinatorial and arithmetic properties of $RD^{l,t}(n)$. In this article, we focus on simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct partitions in 3-colors, $RD^{l,t}_3(n)$ and establish infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 for specific values of $(l,t)$. For instance, for positive integers $n$ and $k$, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}RD_3^{3,3}\left(3^kn+\frac{3^k+1}{2}\right)q^n\equiv0 \pmod{3^{k+1}}. \end{align*} Our approach involves Hirschhorn's H operator technique.

papers.title: Fuss-free cumulative universes: theory and practice
papers.abstract: Universes are central to dependent type theory, and they are notoriously difficult to handle in a way that is both correct and usable. We propose a new "fuss-free" generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes that dispenses with the intricate theory of coherent universe coercions in favour of a simpler formulation, which we prove equivalent by means of a normalisation theorem for the former. We study the fuss-free formulation by means of (1) an abstract specification of its bidirectional elaboration algorithm, and (2) a concrete implementation in Haskell. We also describe and implement an extension of the fuss-free universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description from which prior notions of cumulative inductive type may be derived.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of the Boltzmann equation via bilinear estimates
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness of the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for small initial data in the critical Besov space $B_{1,1}^{d-1}L_v^1$ and in the critical Sobolev space $W^{d-1,1}L_v^1$. The proof is based on new bilinear estimates for the nonlinear collision operator, which rely on transversality considerations.

papers.title: Transformation theorem and monotonicity of the numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls
papers.abstract: In \cite{HH}, H. Huang-X.Huang introduced the generalized Reifenberg condition which describes the non-increasing property of numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls and gave a transformation theorem under this condition. In this note, we study how almost Euclidean factors of concentric geodesic balls interact with harmonic splitting maps under a lower Ricci curvature bound and prove a dimension gap for harmonic functions of almost linear growth and then derive a transformation theorem under a non-decreasing property compared with the non-increasing property above. We also construct complete manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose balls are uniformly almost $1$-Euclidean at every scale, but for which no single harmonic function can be transformed into a splitting function at all smaller scales which give a negative answer to the existence question for all-scale splitting functions in \cite{HH}.

papers.title: Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis
papers.abstract: We study binary classification when the two classes are elliptical with a shared radial generator $g$. The log-likelihood ratio is then an additive function of the two squared Mahalanobis radii, with radial link $\varphi=\log g$. For Gaussian classes $\varphi$ is affine and the rule reduces to quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA); otherwise the Bayes link is not the identity. Instead of fitting this link with a spline smoother, we derive its family from the within-class law of the radius and estimate a finite fractional-power projection. We prove that the link is identifiable from the radius law, that the plug-in estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal under finite-moment conditions, and that the induced classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal in an iterated sieve limit. For $d\ge2$ and non-nested class parameters, the identity link suffices only for affine (Gaussian) generators. The bridge, GAM membership and the affine direction of this dichotomy are verified in Lean 4. We compare against the global Mahalanobis-GAM of Ghosh et al. (2025), re-implemented with mgcv REML splines at equal input budget. On two UCI benchmarks the derived link ties with the fitted GAM. On six financial series from three asset classes, with validation that respects temporal dependence, it is never significantly worse than the fitted GAM: better on CAD/USD and tied on the other five. It beats QDA on the three heaviest-tailed series (oil $[+0.023,+0.069]$, S&P 500 $[+0.039,+0.125]$, JPY/USD $[+0.009,+0.047]$) and ties elsewhere. A rate simulation with a closed-form ground truth reproduces the $\sqrt{n}$ rate and, under covariance heterogeneity, QDA's risk floor against the derived link's vanishing excess risk. The derived link thus matches a tuned GAM without smoothing-parameter selection and improves on QDA where the generator departs from the Gaussian.

papers.title: The Quantum Pendulum of Turbulent Flow: Decaying turbulence as a thermal state of an integrable system
papers.abstract: We present a theory of decaying turbulence in which the statistics of a classical flow becomes quantum mechanics in loop space. The loop functional, the average of $e^{\mathrm{i}Γ/ν}$ for the circulation $Γ$ around a loop, is the wave function, and the Navier-Stokes equation becomes the linear loop equation. An exact operator identity represents the functional as the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/ν$, with the loop parameter as time and viscosity as Planck's constant. The turbulent state is the equal-weight density matrix on a decaying trajectory, a quantum form of the ergodic hypothesis. As in quantum field theory, turbulence at infinite Reynolds number is defined by regularization and renormalization; the loop equation regularized on $N$-sided polygons has an exact manifold of decaying solutions, the Euler ensemble, labeled by rational angles and spins. As a fermionic trace, its partition function and conditional vorticity correlations become, in the local limit, Gibbs averages of two Mathieu quantum pendulums, an integrable system. The energy spectrum, given by explicit quadratures, falls as $k^{-1}\log(1/kL)$ at small $k$ and as $k^{-7/2}$ at large $k$, with $L=\sqrt{\tildeν(t+t_0)}$ and turbulent viscosity $\tildeν$. At $kL=\sqrt2$ its slope diverges as a double logarithm: the decay at fixed $k$ is singular at a finite time, and the vorticity correlation oscillates with period $\sqrt2\,πL$. The reduction to the pendulums, with the continuum and grand canonical limits at every nonzero separation, is formally verified in Lean 4 in forthcoming work by Y. Jiang, A. Migdal et al. The theory rests on stated physical hypotheses, as statistical mechanics rests on the Gibbs distribution; its comparison with simulations and experiment is so far qualitative.

papers.title: Effective Horizons for Prophet Inequalities with Discounted I.I.D. Rewards
papers.abstract: We study prophet inequalities for $n$ i.i.d. base rewards subject to multiplicative discounts across $S$ phases. For equal-length phases and a common discount factor $\widetildeγ$, we characterize the optimal competitive ratio of single-quantile policies as $n\to\infty$ with $S$ and $\widetildeγ$ fixed. The resulting sharp guarantee describes the dependence on the phase parameters: it recovers $1-1/e$ without discounting and approaches $1/2$ in the worst-case regime. We also establish a distribution-free comparison that bounds the discounted prophet by a fractional i.i.d. maximum with effective horizon $B$, the sum of the discount weights across all observations. The comparison yields acceptance probability $1/B$, determined only by the phase profile. This calibration attains the canonical optimum even among single-quantile policies that may choose their acceptance probability using the known base distribution. The comparison also gives guarantees for heterogeneous discounts and unequal phase lengths. A complementary optimal-stopping upper bound establishes the same limiting optimum of $1/2$ for arbitrary stopping rules in the canonical model. Finally, the same effective-horizon calibration sets acceptance probability $1-\widetildeγ$ under infinite-horizon geometric discounting. This explicit quantile rule attains Boshuizen's (1994) known optimal worst-case ratio $1/(1+\widetildeγ)$ without solving a Bellman equation.

papers.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
papers.abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.

papers.title: Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths
papers.abstract: We study finite expected-signature information for mixed-fBm paths with Hurst indices above $1/4$. Up to level three, the only parameter-dependent expected features are the variance transform $q_θ$ and the time-ordered transform $R_θ$. We prove the scale tradeoff $2K$ level-two scales versus $K$ selected level-two/three scales, together with separation and local inverse bounds.

papers.title: A calculus of types in Isbell nuclei
papers.abstract: We identify two constructions from different mathematical traditions. In linear logic and realisability, logical types are generated rather than fixed in advance: one begins with a universe of realisers equipped with execution, uses orthogonality to test their interactions, and takes types to be the biorthogonally closed subsets. In enriched Isbell duality, a quantitative relation induces an adjunction whose fixed points form a category, its nucleus. These constructions proceed by different means; we show that, in the present setting, they produce the same objects. The shared datum is minimal: an associative product, called execution, and a real-valued measurement, with no compatibility assumed between them. The failure of the measurement to be additive is at once the relation defining orthogonality and the quantitative relation whose Isbell nucleus we form, and the types cut out by orthogonality are exactly the fixed points of the associated adjunction. The identification pays off in both directions. The most natural product of types fails to be associative; repairing this failure forces a different notion of type, sensitive to both sides of a composite, on which the induced product is associative and, when execution has units, carries two residuals. What emerges is a noncommutative Lambek calculus, derived directly from execution and orthogonality rather than imposed. In the reverse direction, each such type, read on the categorical side, generates a quantitative relation of its own, and with it a derived adjunction and a further generation of types; these derived types are again types of the original situation, computed by the residuals of the Lambek calculus. We also prove a coherence theorem for the threefold arrangements of this construction and, in the finite-dimensional case, give explicit formulas for the product.

papers.title: Multipoint Characterization of Higher-Order Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: In the paper, we prove a rather general characterization of higher-order Sobolev spaces. We show that the $k\mathrm{th}$-order regularity, where $k \in \mathbb{N}$, is captured via inequalities involving $2^k$-tuples of points. In fact, in full generality, the obtained results characterize higher-order Sobolev spaces based on Banach function spaces. Moreover, we show an analogous characterization of higher-order Hölder spaces. Finally, we propose a way to use the obtained results to define higher-order Sobolev and Hölder spaces on metric measure spaces.

papers.title: Weighted Conformal Clustering
papers.abstract: Clustering is a central tool for discovering latent structure in unlabeled data; yet modern clustering pipelines often end with a hard assignment of each observation to a cluster without rigorous measures of assignment uncertainty. We propose a novel weighted conformal approach for constructing valid confidence sets for cluster labels. The key difficulty is that the labels available for calibration are not observed ground-truth labels, but synthetic labels produced by a data-dependent clustering algorithm. Our method develops a conformal inference algorithm that corrects the resulting mismatch with the latent target labels through weights by formulating conformal clustering as a conditional label-distribution shift problem. We first derive an oracle procedure that attains finite-sample marginal coverage and then develop a computationally tractable and implementable version using estimated conditional label probabilities and novel augmented calibration. We show that the coverage of the estimated-weight procedure depends on the estimator, giving an explicit bound on the loss relative to the nominal level. Empirical studies demonstrate that the proposed weighted approach offers improvements over the recently proposed split conformal clustering procedure in terms of informative confidence set size, especially in nonlinear and high-dimensional clustering applications.

papers.title: Orbital Networks in the Three-Body Problem
papers.abstract: Orbital transfers in multi-body systems are often studied as isolated trajectory design problems, making it difficult to identify the larger transport structure connecting families of periodic orbits, including which families act as hubs, gateways, relays, or persistently difficult-to-access regions. This work introduces a reachable-set-based framework for constructing orbital networks in the circular restricted three-body problem. Finite-$ΔV$ and finite-time-of-flight reachable-set overlaps are used to infer accessibility relationships between representative periodic orbit families on a common Jacobi energy manifold and to assemble these relationships into a weighted orbital network. Applied to the Earth-Moon system, the resulting network reveals distinct accessibility regimes in which direct reachability, graph connectedness, and feasible multileg closure emerge separately. The analysis identifies multi-orbiter cycler orbits as the dominant hub, gateway, and relay families, with the (3,2)-cycler dominating across much of the sampled budget plane and the short-period (1,1)-cycler dominating in the low-time-of-flight regime, while the stable 2:1 resonant orbit remains persistently difficult to access. Although the maximum-budget network is nearly complete in a binary sense, its weighted accessibility remains strongly non-uniform. Selected proxy-supported connections are refined into concrete trajectories through differential correction, with corrected transfer costs remaining below the proxy estimates in all tested cases. Together, the results demonstrate how reachable-set overlap geometry can expose large-scale transport structure in nonlinear gravitational systems without requiring exhaustive pairwise trajectory optimization.

papers.title: The Bogomolov property for $p$-supercuspidal eigenforms
papers.abstract: We prove a lower bound on the Weil height, the so-called Bogomolov property, for the algebraic extensions of $\mathbb Q$ cut out by the adelic Galois representations attached to certain eigenforms whose local component at a prime $p$ is supercuspidal. To this end, we give a method for constructing metric inequalities over $p$-adic Lie extensions of fields over $\mathbb Q$ that are finitely ramified at $p$.

papers.title: Robust Ensemble Kalman Filtering Under Observation Noise Misspecification
papers.abstract: We address observation noise misspecification in Bayesian filtering of dynamical systems via generalised Bayesian inference. Mismatch in tail decay between the true data generating process and an assumed observation model, often indicated via outliers, can strongly impact Bayesian updates in Kalman filters and their ensemble approximations. Adjusting information processing in the analysis step by employing diffusion score matching achieves robustness while maintaining closed-form Gaussian updates and good uncertainty quantification. We provide theoretical properties of this novel Kalman filter in linear Gaussian state space systems covering conjugacy of the analysis step, robustness, covariance stability, and tuning. We extend the approach to non-linear signal dynamics by adapting ensemble Kalman filter variants. Simulation studies on 2D target tracking and the Lorenz-63 and 40D Lorenz-96 systems highlight a critical trade-off between robustness and stability in filtering.

papers.title: An Exact Marginal Likelihood for Inference under Careless Responding
papers.abstract: Careless or insufficient-effort responding threatens the validity of self-report measurement. Mixture models for careless responding specify its form, and screening rules and robust methods depend on a threshold or tuning constant with no direct meaning in terms of careless responses. We propose ExHuber, a Bayesian method for inference on the engaged population under Huber's contamination model, in which an unknown proportion of responses comes from a contaminating distribution of unspecified form instead of the structural model. With a finite support of responses, such as the values of a scale score, a Dirichlet prior and a Beta prior on the contaminating distribution and its proportion yield a closed-form exact marginal likelihood of the structural parameters. Under a prior favoring a contaminating distribution on a few values, we show that the posterior of the structural parameters is consistent when careless responses occupy few values of the support, without knowing which values. Dynamic programming evaluates the marginal likelihood and its gradient at a cost quadratic in the sample size, which enables gradient-based sampling. Simulations from graded response models show accurate inference under straightlining and repeated response patterns, and an application to Big Five scales estimates the engaged mean of each scale.

papers.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
papers.abstract: Evaluating large language models increasingly relies on LLM-as-a-judge protocols, but such evaluations remain costly: different judges have different prices and reliabilities, and the difficulty of each prompt-response pair can vary substantially. This raises a basic allocation question: under a fixed budget, how should one distribute evaluation queries across heterogeneous judges and instances to obtain the most accurate score estimates? We formalize this question as budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation under independent, unbiased score observations. Given $K$ prompt-response pairs and $J$ judges with known costs but unknown query-judge variances, our goal is to estimate the bounded score vector while minimizing an $\ell_p$-error. Our first contribution is to analyze the inverse-variance weighted estimator (IVWE) and to derive the oracle allocation that minimizes its leading error bound. Since this allocation depends on the unknown variances, we then address the unknown-variance setting by proposing EST-IVWE, an adaptive algorithm that constructs and uses optimistic variance estimates to stabilize the empirical allocation. We prove that EST-IVWE matches the oracle IVWE rate up to lower-order terms in the budget. Our second and central theoretical contribution is a local minimax lower bound matching the leading allocation-dependent rate, establishing asymptotic instance-optimality up to logarithmic factors. An Assouad-type construction based on local, variance-preserving perturbations yields this bound both in expectation and with constant probability. A complementary Fano-type change-of-measure argument captures the logarithmic dependence on the confidence level with a different (suboptimal) allocation geometry. Finally, we numerically validate our approach on synthetic data and resampled HelpSteer2 evaluations, demonstrating improvements over naïve uniform allocation.

papers.title: Topological symmetric and braid homologies
papers.abstract: We identify topological symmetric homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra and topological braid homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_2$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra. In this way, topological symmetric homology and topological braid homology can be regarded as variants of $1$-dimensional representation homology. In order to identify topological braid homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_2$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra, we prove that the $\mathbb{E}_2$-monoidal envelope of the associative operad can be identified with the braided crossed simplicial group. Using this, we also compute the topological braid homology of grouplike $\mathbb{E}_1$-spaces. Further, we develop computational tools for topological symmetric and braid homologies. These tools allow us to perform low-degree computations of topological symmetric homology and prove that it is not Morita invariant. We also compute the topological $Δ\mathbf{G}$-homology of Thom spectra in general and produce explicit formulas in the case of topological symmetric and braid homologies.

papers.title: Generalized Fermat equation over cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_l$-extensions of totally real fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a totally real field of odd degree $m$ in which $2$ is inert. Let $l\geq5$ be a prime totally ramified in $K$ with $\gcd(m,l(l-1)/2)=1$ and $2^{l-1}\not\equiv1\pmod{l^2}$. We prove the asymptotic Fermat's Last Theorem over every layer $K_{n,l}$, $n\geq1$, of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_l$-extension of $K$. Using $S$-unit bounds, we also give criteria for the generalized Fermat equation $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ to have no asymptotic solutions in $K_{n,l}^3$ when the coefficients $A,B,C$ are supported at the primes above $2$ or $2d$, with $d$ an odd prime. In particular, for every fixed integer $r\geq2$ other than $4$, the equation $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no asymptotic solutions in $K_{n,l}^3$ for each fixed $n\geq1$. Thorne's modularity theorem makes the resulting bounds effective in each layer $\mathbb{Q}_{n,l}$ to which our criteria apply.

papers.title: Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
papers.abstract: Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.

papers.title: Implementation-Based Incentive Design for Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand and Transit Systems
papers.abstract: Achieving a socially desirable operating point for a multimodal transportation system is challenging when Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand (AMoD) and Public Transit (PT) operators pursue selfish objectives alongside endogenous passenger choices. Existing equilibrium-based regulation models typically search over municipal policies to predict the induced operator equilibrium, creating strong behavioral assumptions, equilibrium-selection issues, and difficult bilevel optimization problems. This paper proposes an implementation-based alternative. Rather than asking which municipal action induces the best equilibrium, we ask: given a target operating profile, what minimum realized transfer makes unilateral deviation unattractive for each operator? Using k-implementation theory, this payment decomposes into two unilateral deviation gains: one for the AMoD operator and one for PT. Calculating this payment requires computing three distinct objects: the social target, the AMoD best response, and the PT best response. This is nontrivial because each represents a large-scale network optimization problem complicated by endogenous mode choice and congestion. To address this, we develop tailored mathematical formulations and algorithms for each oracle. For the social target, we derive a decomposition and entropy-regularized mixed-integer convex formulation balancing social optimality and implementability. For the AMoD oracle, we derive an exact reformulation, a convex relaxation providing a global upper bound, and a sequential convex approximation for feasible lower bounds. For the PT oracle, we develop a mixed-integer convex relaxation and characterize its exactness condition. A NYC case study shows the framework computes tight implementation-payment bounds and reveals how the dominant source of incentive misalignment shifts with congestion.

papers.title: Cover-free families on graphs
papers.abstract: A family of subsets of a $t$-set is a \emph{$d$-cover-free family} or $d$-CFF if no subset in the family is contained in the union of any $d$ other subsets. Let $t(d, n)$ denote the minimum $t$ for which there exists a $d$-CFF on a $t$-set with $n$ subsets. Since a $1$-CFF is the same as a Sperner family, using Sperner's theorem, we get $t(1, n) \sim \log_{2}(n)$ as $n$ grows. Erdös, Frankl, and Füredi (JCTA, 1982) proved that $3.106\log_{2}(n) < t(2,n) < 5.512\log_{2}(n)$. This paper focuses on generalizing $1$-CFF and $2$-CFF using a graph $G$ where vertices correspond to subsets in the set system. A $G$-Sperner$(t, n)$ is a family of subsets of a $t$-set such that each edge of $G$ specifies a pair of subsets not contained in each other, where as a $G$-CFF$(t, n)$ is a family of subsets of a $t$-set such that it is $G$-Sperner and the union of a pair of subsets corresponding to each edge of $G$ does not contain any other subset in the family. Let $t_s(G)$ and $t(G)$ denote the minimum $t$ for which there exist a $G$-Sperner$(t, n)$ and a $G$-CFF$(t, n)$, respectively. In this way, $t_s(K_n) = t(1, n)$ and $t(K_n) = t(2, n)$. Firstly, we prove $t_s(G) = t(1, χ(G))$ for any simple graph $G$ and provide various upper and lower bounds for $t(G)$. The \emph{trivial bound}, $t(1, n) \leq t(G) \leq t(2, n)$ holds for any simple graph $G$ with no isolated vertex, with the lower bound tight for an infinite family of star graphs and the upper bound tight for complete graphs. We study when these bounds can be improved and give better constructive upper bounds for families of graphs such as stars, paths, cycles, wheels, and windmill graphs. In particular, a construction based on mixed-radix Gray codes yields $\log_{2}(n) \leq t(P_n) \leq t(C_n) \leq 1.893\log_{2}(n) + \mathcal{O}(1)$ where $P_n$ and $C_n$ are paths and cycles with $n$ vertices.

papers.title: Quotient-Categorical Representations for Bellman-Compatible Average-Reward Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Average-reward reinforcement learning requires estimating the gain and a state-dependent bias, which solves the Poisson equation only up to an additive constant. Distributional analogues of the bias inherit this same ambiguity. We introduce a quotient-space formulation in which state-indexed laws are identified up to a common translation, together with a categorical parameterization that respects this symmetry. On this space, we define a projected average-reward distributional operator and show that it is well-defined, non-expansive in a coordinate Cramér metric, and admits fixed points. We interpret the projected fixed points through geometrically-stopped differential returns, whose categorical operators are contractive and whose fixed points converge in the Abel sense to a canonical fixed point of the projected undiscounted operator. We show that the means of the projected fixed points match the scalar bias up to an error caused by endpoint clipping of the categorical projections, and we bound this error. Finally, we establish almost-sure convergence and finite-iteration residual bounds for temporal-difference recursions with gain-centered rewards under i.i.d. and Markovian sampling. When the gain is unknown, we couple the recursion with an online gain estimator and prove the same guarantees under Markovian sampling, with a bound on the gain error.

papers.title: Measuring and Decomposing Mode Separation via the Canonical Diffusion
papers.abstract: Mode separation, namely how sharply a distribution fragments into barrier-separated clusters, is a fundamental geometric property of densities, difficult to quantify in high dimensions. Modes are often the meaningful alternatives in the data, such as the conformations of a molecule or the distinct semantic types among a generative model's outputs. Mode separation is distinct from dispersion, which is what standard label-free tools capture: differential entropy rises with spread regardless of fragmentation, and PCA orders directions by variance regardless of barriers. Mutual information does capture it, but only given the latent component labels, which are usually unavailable. We measure mode separation through a single stochastic process intrinsic to the density, namely the unique reversible diffusion with $f$ as its stationary distribution and a constant scalar diffusion coefficient. From its autocovariance matrix we extract two readouts. The first, SSA (Sum of Squared Autocorrelations), is a scalar barrier-sensitive measure. The second, DA (Dominant Autocorrelation directions), gives linear projections ordered by metastability rather than variance. Under an isotropic-Gaussian null, we derive the limiting spectrum of the empirical autocovariance in closed form, generalizing the Marchenko--Pastur law. Its upper edge gives a noise floor that separates metastable directions from sampling noise. Both readouts use only samples and a score function, scaling to high dimensions through pretrained score-based generative models via Tweedie's identity. We apply our framework to three settings: (i) synthetic Gaussian mixtures, where SSA tracks mutual information; (ii) SDXL text-to-image generations, where SSA and DA capture structure that entropy and PCA miss; and (iii) molecular dynamics of alanine dipeptide, where DA recovers the known slow backbone dihedrals from static samples alone.

papers.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on Cayley graphs over dihedral groups
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of Cayley graphs over dihedral groups that exhibit perfect state transfer between distinct vertex states in Grover walks. For $n\ge 3$, let $D_n:=\langle a,b : a^n=b^2=1,\ bab=a^{-1}\rangle$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$, and let $S\subseteq D_n\setminus\{1\}$ satisfying $S=S^{-1}$ and $\langle S\rangle =D_n$. We show that the Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(D_n,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $(D_n,S)$ is equivalent to one of the following pairs: $(D_n,\{b,ba\})$; $(D_n,\{a,a^{-1},ba,ba^{-1}\})$, where $4$ does not divide $n$; or $(D_{2m},\{b,ba^{m},ba,ba^{m+1}\})$, where $m$ is odd. Our proof combines the representation theory of $D_n$ with tools from algebraic number theory.

papers.title: A Measure-Theoretic Formulation of Behavioral Systems
papers.abstract: Ensemble control specifies probability laws on admissible trajectories, including their temporal dependence. Starting from an arbitrary closed behavior, we organize its laws into a framework that connects standard probability-measure geometry, occupation-measure control, and data-driven trajectory parametrization. Classical convexity and extreme-point properties describe the feasible laws, while classical Bellman duality governs additive control objectives. On compact state and input spaces, full-path constrained duality for continuous trajectory functions gives primal attainment and zero gap whenever feasible. For controllable linear time-invariant systems, the noise-free Fundamental Lemma yields an equivalent law-level Hankel factorization, with a canonical pseudoinverse lift. The factorization transfers trajectory-law constraints exactly to coefficient space and connects them to covariance control. Explicit noisy-Hankel bounds quantify subspace approximation for second-moment-bounded laws under known rank and Gaussian output measurement noise. Numerical studies include a nonlinear reset problem whose nonadjacent correlation constraint requires temporal memory, covariance-constrained optimization, and noisy-data policy evaluation. Known transition kernels provide a further structural perspective through history-conditional consistency.

papers.title: Data-Driven Continuous-Time LQR: Linking Reinforcement Learning and Behavioral System Theory
papers.abstract: Behavioral system theory and reinforcement learning (RL) have independently developed data-driven approaches to the continuous-time LQR problem, yet their respective methods have largely evolved in separation. We connect these two adjacent lines of work by studying their data-driven parameterizations, namely a closed-loop (CL) parameterization from behavioral system theory and an integral RL (IRL) parameterization. The CL parameterization characterizes the closed-loop system via a matrix that satisfies equality constraints. While this parameterization has been extensively studied for discrete-time systems, we adapt key results to the continuous-time setting and develop a policy iteration (PI) scheme, derive an algebraic Riccati equation, and introduce an alternative convex program. The IRL parameterization utilizes off-policy data to perform policy evaluation, which is used for PI or value iteration. Within the IRL framework, we derive a policy gradient flow and propose convex programs for the LQR problem. Finally, we provide a unified treatment of these parameterizations that enables a systematic understanding of existing approaches, and clarifies their structural relationships.

papers.title: A High Dimensional Wild Bootstrap Max-Test for Detecting the Presence of Significant Predictors
papers.abstract: We construct a block bootstrap max-test for detecting the presence of significant predictors in a high dimensional setting, allowing for weakly dependent and heterogeneous (possibly non-stationary) data. The number of covariates to be screened may be large $p$ $>>$ $n$, and growing at an exponential rate, provided $\ln (p)$ $=$ $o(n^{a})$ for some $a$ $>$ $0$ that depends on memory decay and the growth of higher moments. We study the problem of correlation screening in a high dimensional marginal regression setting, assuming so-called \textit{physical dependence} in a time series setting. We entirely sidestep covariance matrix estimation and adaptive re-sampling by working with a max-statistic over the many computed parameters. Thus we do not need endogenous selection of the most relevant predictor index yielding non-uniform asymptotics, nor do we need a post-estimation Bonferroni correction. The sequence of non-standard approximating distributions arising from the maximum of an increasing number of estimators is easily approximated by a multiplier (wild) block bootstrap. The max-test controls for size well, performs well against various deviations from the null, including very slight deviations with a weak or sparse signal. A numerical experiment is performed and an empirical example with the VIX volatility index is provided.

papers.title: A generalisation of the Gagliardo--Nirenberg Inequality with applications to mass-critical and mass-subcritical elliptic equations
papers.abstract: Via a new inequality à la Gagliardo--Nirenberg, we prove the existence and nonexistence of solutions to \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} (-Δ)^s u + \fracμ{|y|^{2s}} u + λu = f(u), \quad \mathbb{R}^N \ni x = (y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^K \times \mathbb{R}^{N-K}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} u^2 \, \mathrm{d}x = ρ\end{cases} \end{equation*} in the mass-critical and mass-subcritical regimes, where $s>0$, $N \ge K \ge 2$, $μ\in \mathbb{R}$ belongs to a specific range, $ρ>0$ is given a priori, and $λ\in \mathbb{R}$ is unknown. Additionally, we obtain similar results for the problem above with $μ=0$ and $N \ge 1$ as well as a related curl-curl equation. Finally, we provide a thorough insight into the threshold for $ρ$ that divides the scenarios of negative and zero least energy.

papers.title: A structure-preserving semi-implicit finite volume scheme on vertex-staggered unstructured meshes
papers.abstract: We present a structure-preserving semi-implicit finite volume method on vertex-based staggered meshes for the compatible discretization of first-order systems of time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs). The method preserves divergence-free and curl-free vector fields exactly thanks to the compatible vertex-staggered discretization of the state variables on unstructured grids consisting of primal Delaunay triangles and their dual polygons. For the weakly compressible Euler equations, the scheme is asymptotic preserving, yielding a consistent discretization of the incompressible limit as the Mach number goes to zero. The scheme applies to a broad spectrum of PDEs, including the weakly compressible and incompressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system, and the incompressible version of the first-order hyperbolic Godunov-Peshkov-Romenski (GPR) model for continuum mechanics. The computational domain is covered by a primal triangular mesh and a dual tessellation made of star polygons. Scalar quantities (pressure, density, viscous stress) are defined at nodes, with pressure updated implicitly in a continuous finite element fashion, yielding a symmetric and positive definite pressure system. Instead, vector fields (velocity, momentum, magnetic and distortion fields) are stored at triangle barycenters and evolved explicitly using a compatible finite volume scheme. With the semi-implicit discretization, the CFL restriction is independent of the sound speed, allowing simulations at low Mach numbers. The compatible formulation ensures an exactly divergence-free velocity field in the incompressible limit, an exactly divergence-free magnetic field for MHD, and an exactly curl-free inverse deformation gradient in solid mechanics. The scheme has been extended to second-order accuracy. The method is validated through a set of test cases.

papers.title: Adaptive refinement based on local approximation power of hierarchical spline spaces
papers.abstract: We propose an adaptive refinement strategy for hierarchical B-splines that increases the approximation power of every marked cell by at least one. Here, the approximation power of a cell is the finest level $\ell$ such that all the B-splines of level $\ell$ that do not vanish on the cell belong to the hierarchical space. This increase can be achieved with the standard refinement of hierarchical meshes, in which each cell is subdivided at most once per step, provided that the regions formed at each level by the cells with this property are nested. We call the hierarchical meshes with this nesting property \emph{weakly admissible}, characterize them, and prove that the proposed refinement preserves weak admissibility. We also prove a complexity estimate: the number of cells created along the adaptive process is bounded by a constant times the total number of marked cells. Moreover, we extend known local $L^q$ estimates for a multilevel quasi-interpolant on these meshes to Sobolev norms, showing that the local error bound on each active cell is governed by its approximation power, which supports using this quantity to drive the refinement. Numerical experiments illustrate the local gain of resolution produced by the proposed strategy, as well as its robustness with respect to the marking criterion and the marking parameter.

papers.title: Sparse Network Inference under Imperfect Detection and its Application to Ecological Networks
papers.abstract: Recovering latent structure from count data has received considerable attention in network inference, particularly when one seeks both cross-group interactions and within-group similarity patterns in bipartite networks, which are widely used in ecology research. Such networks are often sparse and prone to imperfect detection. Existing models mainly focus on interaction recovery, while the induced similarity graphs are much less studied. Moreover, existing models for under-counted data place sparsity, if at all, on the detection model rather than on these graphs. To address these issues, we propose a nonnegative low-rank factorization framework that jointly estimates detection probabilities and promotes sparse within- and cross-group graphs through $\ell_{1/2}$ regularization. For the resulting nonconvex, nonsmooth problem, we develop an ADMM-based algorithm with adaptive penalization, and establish asymptotic feasibility and KKT stationarity of cluster points under stated assumptions. We also give sufficient conditions for exact recovery of within- and cross-group graphs. On synthetic data with up to 20% missing entries, the method recovers the graphs and detection probabilities with competitive accuracy. Across three ecological datasets, it matches the baseline held-out predictions while estimating detection probabilities and within- and cross-group graphs.

papers.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
papers.abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

papers.title: Logarithmically Coupled p-Laplacian Systems: From Discrete Ground States to Rigidity and Critical Continuous Limits
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of logarithmically coupled \(p\)-Laplacian systems on locally finite graphs and in the critical case \(p=N>4\). The coupling poses two challenges: the energy functional is ill-defined on the natural Sobolev space, and loss of the \(L^\infty\)-embedding prevents standard control of logarithmic terms. To resolve this non-separable logarithmic singularity, we develop an \textbf{exponent calibration technique} that converts logarithmic terms into strictly lower-order power estimates. The technique plays an essential role in two critical steps: the existence proof for the regularised problem and the uniform boundedness of regularised ground states that restores compactness. Thus, we prove solvability of the original ill-posed continuous critical equation. In the discrete setting, we identify five new intrinsic structures, including an exact constrained Hessian factorisation and a scalar rigidity index. We complete a discrete--continuous double loop, providing a unified variational framework for logarithmically coupled systems.

papers.title: Inversion monotonicity in subclasses of the 1324-avoiders
papers.abstract: We prove injectively that the pattern-avoiding permutation classes $\mathrm{Av}(1324, 231)$ and $\mathrm{Av}(1324, 2314, 3214, 4213)$ are inversion monotone: for every $k$, the number of length-$n$ permutations with $k$ inversions in either class is weakly increasing in $n$. These are the first known nontrivial examples of the phenomenon. The latter is a special case of a general construction. We also characterize the finitely based permutation classes in which the number of length-$n$ members with a fixed number of inversions stabilizes as $n$ grows, and determine the limiting values for all classes $\mathrm{Av}(1324, p)$ with $p \in S_4$. Connections to several nice families of integer partitions are revealed. Lastly, we show that for asymptotically almost every pattern $p \in \mathrm{Av}(1324)$, the class $\mathrm{Av}(1324, p)$ is inversion monotone in the region $n \geq \frac{k+7}{2}$, expanding on the work of Linusson and Verkama. This work is motivated by the conjectures of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson that $\mathrm{Av}(1324)$, and more generally $\mathrm{Av}(p)$ for every nonidentity pattern $p$, is inversion monotone.

papers.title: Automatic feature identification in least-squares policy iteration using the Koopman operator framework
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a Koopman autoencoder-based least-squares policy iteration (KAE-LSPI) algorithm for reinforcement learning (RL). The KAE-LSPI algorithm is based on reformulating the so-called least-squares fixed-point approximation method in terms of extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD), thereby enabling automatic feature learning via the Koopman autoencoder (KAE) framework. The approach is motivated by the lack of a systematic procedure for selecting features or kernels in linear RL techniques. Unlike previous approaches, no features or kernels need to be fixed a priori in our method. We discuss the theoretical convergence of KAE-LSPI under suitable assumptions, similar to kernel-based least-squares policy iteration (KLSPI). We empirically compare our method with two existing algorithms: least-squares policy iteration (LSPI) and KLSPI. In particular, for the chainwalk problem, the resulting policies are either optimal or nearly optimal for both three approaches. For the cart-pole system, KAE-LSPI outperforms the other two approaches in terms of policy performance.

papers.title: Discrete hypocoercive estimates for discontinuous Galerkin methods: application to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a class of structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin schemes for the nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck model, reformulated as a hyperbolic system through a Hermite expansion in the velocity variable. We discretize the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with the discontinuous Galerkin method, while the Poisson equation is approximated with either a discontinuous Galerkin method or a Raviart-Thomas mixed finite element method. We prove the exponential relaxation to equilibrium for suitable initial data, uniformly with respect to the discretization parameters thanks to discrete hypocoercivity arguments. Moreover, we check that the resulting semi-discrete schemes preserve the physical invariants along with the L 2 variational structure of the linearized model. Numerical simulations verify the accuracy and the long-time behavior of the scheme.

papers.title: Biregular bipartite multigraphs and matchings in tensor products of bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We answer a question of P. Higgins on permutations and involutions in binary arrays, arising in the study of regular finite semigroups. For a binary rectangular matrix M, we prove that if there is a permutation pi(x, y) = (f(x, y), g(x, y)) of its cells satisfying M(x, g(x,y)) = 1 for every cell, then there is an involution with the same property. The elementary proof places coins in the nonzero cells, reduces their support to a forest, and assigns consecutive integer weights to the coins incident to each row and column. We also prove a multiplicativity formula for bipartite expansion and a perfect matching theorem for tensor products of supports of matrices with prescribed margins. We study a stronger conjecture of F. Petrov on disjoint swaps in biregular bipartite multigraphs. We prove this conjecture for k = mn + eps, |eps| <= 2, and for n = 6, k = 6m + 3, and give a group-theoretic reformulation.

papers.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Discounted Infinite-Time Mean Field Games
papers.abstract: In [18], we introduced discounted infinite-time mean field games. Subsequently, in [19], we studied the connection between infinite-time mean field FBSDEs and elliptic master equations. In this paper, we further investigate the regularity of the representative player's value function $V(x,μ)$. We first establish strong well-posedness and uniqueness in law for an extended class of infinite-time FBSDEs. In the weighted $L_r^2$ framework, we construct directional variations and obtain a bounded continuous representation of the Lions-derivative of $\partial_xV$. Under additional smoothness and quantitative stability assumptions, $L_r^p$ estimates for scalar linear FBSDEs allow us to establish the existence of higher-order derivatives of $\partial_xV$. Consequently, $\partial_xV$ is a classical solution of the elliptic master equation for the value function's derivative.

papers.title: A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.

papers.title: Topological insights into Monoids and Module systems
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a monoid and let $G$ denote its quotient groupoid. We introduce the Riemann-Zariski space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ associated with $H$ and prove that it is a spectral space. We then show that, if $H$ is an $s$-Prüfer monoid, the space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ is homeomorphic to the prime $s$-spectrum of $H$ endowed with the Zariski topology. Next, given a finitary ideal system $r$ on $H$, we prove that the space of $r$-ideals $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$, endowed with the Zariski topology, is spectral, and that the prime $r$-spectrum of $H$ is proconstructible in $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$. We also introduce a new topology on the set $\mathcal{X}$ of all generalized $H$-module systems and study its properties. In particular, we show that $\mathcal{X}$ and its subspace $\mathcal{X}_{\textup{fin}}$ of finitary generalized $H$-module systems are spectral spaces. Finally, we provide a characterization of those subsets of the set of overmonoids of $H$ that are quasi-compact.

papers.title: Novel technique based on Léja Points Approximation for Log-determinant Estimation of Large matrices
papers.abstract: The computation of the Log-determinant of large, sparse, symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices is essential in many scientific computational fields such as numerical linear algebra and machine learning. In low dimensions, Cholesky is preferred, but in high dimensions, its computation may be prohibitive due to memory limitation. To circumvent this, Krylov subspace techniques have proven to be efficient but may be computationally expensive due to the required orthogonalization processes. In this paper, we introduce a Newton-Léja interpolation based approach for estimating log-determinants, where the implementation is only based on matrix multiplications and a rough estimation of eigenvalue bounds of the matrix. The method employs an adaptive stopping criterion to select the degree of interpolation according to the data and introduces a centered, scaled-based formulation for computing the logarithmic divided differences. By combining Newton-Léja interpolation with a randomized algorithm called Hutch++, we obtain a matrix-free log-determinant estimation framework that avoids explicit matrix factorization and Krylov basis orthogonalization. We establish approximation error bounds for the Newton-Léja interpolation and derive an inexact oracle error bound that separates stochastic trace estimation from the approximation errors in the projected and residual components. Numerical experiments on both large sparse synthetic matrices (Gaussian Markov Random fields) and large-scale real-world matrices demonstrate that our method substantially reduces computational time while retaining competitive accuracy, thereby confirming its effectiveness, scalability, and favorable accuracy-cost trade-off for large-scale log-determinant estimation compared with stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ) and related stochastic trace-estimation methods.

papers.title: Revisiting the Algebraic and Analytic Descriptions of Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: The Wintner-Wielandt theorem exposes a fundamental incompatibility between the canonical commutation relation (CCR) and the Hilbert-space formulation of quantum mechanics. While the conventional approach preserves the CCR by extending the Hilbert-space framework to a rigged Hilbert space, this work develops the complementary alternative. Retaining the Hilbert space, the unavoidable trace obstruction requires a boundary modification of the CCR, consistently realizable only in a space of finite, albeit arbitrarily large, dimension. In this setting, the eigenvalue problems of position and momentum admit explicit solutions within the Hilbert space.
