They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting, where non-Markovian corrections appear in higher moments. For finite-mean sojourn times, the framework recovers the known stationary distribution through a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem, with transition rates replaced by pseudo-rates. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short graph-theoretic proof of the previously established constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to extend established results on weak ergodicity breaking for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks, allowing for generally heterogeneous, transition-dependent waiting-time distributions.

papers.title: Characteristic cycles and Gevrey irregularity in hypergeometric families
papers.abstract: We show that the characteristic cycle multiplicities of $A$-hypergeometric systems are upper semicontinuous in the parameter for every rational projective weight, thereby proving a conjecture of Schulze and Walther [Duke Math. J. 142 (2008), 465--509]. The proof uses a specialization formula for filtered families satisfying a fixed product support condition, expressing the difference between the special and generic characteristic cycles as the characteristic cycle of the first Tor module. Combined with the Gevrey index theorem, this yields upper semicontinuity of generic Gevrey irregularity and of each of its graded dimensions. We also construct non-Cohen--Macaulay semigroup rings whose Gevrey dimensions are constant in the parameter despite the presence of a genuine irregular slope, showing that the Gevrey jump locus need not coincide with the full exceptional arrangement defined by Ext.

papers.title: Irrationality exponents of logarithms of positive rational numbers
papers.abstract: We study rational approximation to logarithms of positive rational numbers and give a separated-weight determinant argument for $μ(\log r)=2$ whenever $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\setminus\{1\}$. The geometric input is an interpolation theorem for logarithmic jets at points with distinct multiplicative coordinates. Its successive weight thresholds are independent of the interpolation centres; the eventual degree threshold may depend on them. A local intersection-length bound and a curve inequality lead to surjectivity through a blow-up and Serre vanishing. For a fixed rational argument, this produces a nonzero rational determinant. Clearing denominators gives an arithmetic lower bound, while an exact row translation and repeated Taylor indices yield a contradictory analytic upper bound. The consequences include nonzero rational linear combinations of such logarithms, rational affine changes, and logarithms of positive numbers with a rational positive integer power. We also give a bounded-fibre interpolation extension, an explicit bound for the final analytic degree, and a counterexample to interpolation under the volume condition alone.

papers.title: A secondary index map on relative K-homology
papers.abstract: We introduce a secondary index map from relative K-homology to the K-theory of a relative structure algebra. We prove an algebraic Mayer-Vietoris sequence for the relative structure algebra, and prove compatibility of the secondary index map with the Mayer-Vietoris boundary map. As an application, we compute the secondary index of the Dirac operator on an even-dimensional spin manifold with collared metric having uniformly positive scalar curvature on the boundary. This computation leads to a refinement of the delocalized APS-index theorem.

papers.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
papers.abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.

papers.title: Random Cayley sum hypergraphs and $k$-fold sumsets
papers.abstract: We denote by $f_k(Γ)$ the largest integer with the property that every subset of a finite abelian group $Γ$ of size at least $|Γ| - f_k(Γ)$ is a $k$-fold sumset. Extending a recent result of Alon and Pham, we prove that $$ f_k(Γ) \leq \widetilde{O} \left(n^{(2k-1)/(4k-3)}\right) $$ holds for all finite abelian groups $Γ$ and integers $k \geq 2$, where $n = |Γ|$. Additionally, we also show that the lower bound $f_k(Γ) \geq \widetildeΩ \left(n^{1/k}\right)$ holds if $Γ$ has no nontrivial element of order dividing $k$. Our upper bound improves a previous result of Balogh, Liu, and Sharifzadeh, and recovers the bound of Alon and Pham in the case $k = 2$. The proof relies on a new upper bound for the independence number of random Cayley sum hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: A two-stage approach to satellite constellation optimization: classical and QUBO formulations
papers.abstract: The design of satellite constellations for Earth observation requires balancing spatial coverage, revisit time, cost, and operational complexity. This paper considers the problem of designing the orbits of a given number of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) or Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) satellites to maximize the spatial and temporal resolution achieved over a prescribed set of ground targets. This kind of problem is inherently nonconvex and possibly combinatorial, making its solution computationally demanding for large constellations and target sets. To address this challenge, we propose a two-stage optimization strategy that separates spatial-coverage design from temporal-resolution optimization, thereby reducing the complexity of the overall problem. Two variants of the method are developed. The first employs continuous decision variables during the spatial-optimization stage, whereas the second discretizes these variables and reformulates the problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. The latter formulation enables the use of efficient classical QUBO solvers and is directly compatible with quantum-annealing hardware. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach to the design of heterogeneous LEO and VLEO Earth-observation constellations and establishes a pathway for exploiting emerging quantum-optimization technologies in satellite mission design. Preliminary simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the strategy.

papers.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
papers.abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.

papers.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

papers.title: High-dimensional Gaussian Graphical Model Testing for Long-Memory Time Series
papers.abstract: Many real-world high-dimensional time series exhibit long-memory, but Gaussian graphical model testing in this regime remains understudied. We develop a direct, data-adaptive test statistic for assessing conditional independence in the graph structure of stationary Gaussian time series. We establish a finite-sample, Berry--Esseen type Gaussian approximation bound for the statistic, which applies to both short-memory and long-memory time series. The testing procedure uses a block bootstrap method, on which we provide a finite-sample validity result including in the ultra-high-dimensional scenario, and can be extended to comparing graphical structures in two-sample tests. We also develop a consistency-empowered correction to the statistic and show that such tests attain asymptotic consistency in both size and power. Our proposed method is applied to real-world fMRI data to understand functional connectivities within brain in different periods.

papers.title: A diagrammatic presentation for every pivotal pointed fusion category
papers.abstract: We provide a generators and relations presentation of pivotal pointed fusion categories, $Vec(G,ω,π)$. Unlike the well-known skeletal model, our presentation is strict and allows multiple isomorphic objects. Our main tool is skein theory, which allows us to apply topological tools to understand the relations of morphisms in the category. This expository paper provides details of skein-theoretic work in the setup that allows multiple isomorphic labels in the generators, which didn't previously exist in the literature.

papers.title: Reduction of Zieve's Conjecture on the Hurwitz problem to Three Branch Points
papers.abstract: M. E. Zieve conjectured that a candidate datum over the sphere is realizable whenever the gcd of the parts of every branch partition is one and it satisfies the lcm condition. We prove that this conjecture reduces to its three-branch-point case. More precisely, if every Zieve-admissible triple is realizable, then every Zieve-admissible datum with at least four branch points is realizable. As already noted by Petronio, Zieve's conjecture would imply the prime-degree conjecture of Edmonds, Kulkarni, and Stong. Song, Wen, and Zhang proved the latter conjecture in a preprint posted on arXiv in September.

papers.title: The proper geometric dimension of the mapping class groups of non-orientable surfaces with punctures
papers.abstract: We study the proper geometric dimension of {\it full} mapping class groups of non-orientable surfaces with punctures. Building on the computation for closed non-orientable surfaces, we prove that the proper geometric dimension agrees with the virtual cohomological dimension in all but a finite collection of low-complexity cases, for which we obtain explicit bounds. Our results provide the non-orientable counterpart of the corresponding computations for mapping class groups of closed and punctured orientable surfaces.

papers.title: Directed partial orders on the complex number field
papers.abstract: We construct a class of positive cones that make $\mathbb{C}$ into a directed partially ordered ring. The positive cones are defined using integral closures of local rings, associated with a transcendence basis and a chosen real generator. A localization criterion also yields such orders on every transcendental extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For a fixed coefficient field, we prove that two real generators define the same cone if and only if they differ by an affine map with positive real-algebraic slope and translation algebraic over that field. The nonzero positive elements are closed under inversion.

papers.title: Non-simple blow-up for the Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: The existence and structure of non-simple blow-up are fundamental questions for the self-dual Chern--Simons--Higgs equation. Physically, this phenomenon describes magnetic-flux concentration in several cores whose mutual distances are much larger than their widths, although all cores approach the same vortex point. Despite substantial progress for singular Liouville equations, the existence of non-simple blow-up solutions to the full Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on closed surfaces has remained open in both the Chern--Simons (CS) and mean-field regimes. We prove that the cores of every non-simple cluster have equal limiting masses, share a common profile type, and form an asymptotically regular polygon. These identities yield an explicit finite list of admissible cluster masses and a four-unit mass-gap criterion. We also construct non-simple blow-up solutions on closed Riemannian surfaces in both regimes. Together, these results establish a sharp arithmetic criterion for single-point non-simple CS blow-up on each fixed flat torus when a suitable exterior divisor may be chosen, and show that vortex blow-up need not be simple, answering Li--Liu's question in the negative.

papers.title: Homogeneous linearly ordered spaces
papers.abstract: Every compact subspace $K$ of a homogeneous generalized ordered (GO) space $X$ satisfies $χ(K)\leqω_1$ and $|K|\leq 2^{ω_1}$. If $χ(K)>ω$ for some such $K$, then $χ(X)=ω_1$ and $πχ(X)=ω$. We construct a homogeneous $σ$-compact linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) $\mathbf{H}$ with a compact subspace $K$ such that $χ(x,K)=ω_1$ for every $x\in K$ and $c(K)=w(K)=|K|=2^{ω_1}$, where $c(K)$ denotes cellularity. Thus both bounds are attained by the same compact space. Every semitopological group that is a GO space is hereditarily paracompact and has metrizable compact subspaces. If it is not a $P$-space, it is also first countable and submetrizable. A semitopological group that is a LOTS, or a topological group that is a GO space, is either metrizable or is a $P$-space. We also show that in an order-homogeneous LOTS every compact subset is first countable.

papers.title: Moment Lagrangians, unobstructedness and symplectic groupoids
papers.abstract: Moment Lagrangian $L_μ$ is a Lagrangian in $T^*G^- \times Y^- \times Y$ associated to a Hamiltonian $G$-space $Y$ with a moment map $μ$. In this paper, we prove that $L_μ$ is tautologically unobstructed under mild assumptions on $Y$. As a key ingredient in the proof, we constructed a new symplectic groupoid structure on $T^*G^- \times Y^- \times Y$ over $G\times Y$ for which $L_μ$ is simultaneously the unit and the fixed locus of the inversion, which might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Fixed-Perimeter Franklin Statistics and an Eventual Inequality
papers.abstract: Gray, Payne, Swisher, and Watson conjectured that, for fixed integers $j \geq 0$ and $k \geq 2$, the number $FD_{j,k}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ having exactly $j$ part sizes of multiplicity at least $k$ is eventually at least the number $FO_{j,k}(n)$ having exactly $j$ distinct occurring part sizes divisible by $k$. We derive bivariate generating functions for both statistics using the profile-word encoding of a partition. For $k \geq 3$, coefficient extraction shows that fixing $j$ changes the order of the dominant pole but not its location. The corresponding dominant singularities are positive real numbers $ρ_k$ and $σ_k$, where $ρ_k$ satisfies $ρ_k+ρ_k^2+\cdots+ρ_k^k=1$ and $σ_k$ satisfies $σ_k^k=(1-σ_k)^{k-1}$. We prove that $ρ_k<σ_k$ for every $k \geq 3$. Consequently, $FD_{j,k}(n)/FO_{j,k}(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, proving the conjecture and yielding a strict eventual inequality for $k \geq 3$. The case $k=2$ recovers the known exact identity.

papers.title: Stable and Gaussian Fluctuation Limit of a Lévy-Driven Slow-Fast System
papers.abstract: We study fluctuation limit of a slow-fast system driven by $α$-stable Lévy noise with $1<α<2.$ The slow component is generated by an odd polynomial function $f(y):=y^q,$ while in the fast component, the drift is $g(y):=-|y|^p\operatorname{sgn}(y)$ for some $p>0.$ Although the noise is given, the fluctuation limit is either a stable process or a Brownian motion, depending on both $p$ and $α.$ The critical line between stable limit and Brownian limit is $q+1-p=α/2.$

papers.title: Networked Admissibility-Preserving Control for Directed Safe Coordination
papers.abstract: This paper addresses safe coordination of scalar agents with constrained input dynamics over fixed rooted digraphs. We propose a networked Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) architecture for a common moving output corridor under heterogeneous asymmetric input bounds, wherein the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the physical inputs. In logarithmic barrier coordinates, the closed-loop dynamics form an exact cascade of exponentially decaying realization errors and directed consensus dynamics. We derive direction-specific compatibility conditions that guarantee uniform corridor and input margins, bounded commands, unique complete solutions, and exponential consensus for compact initial sets. The closed-form expression for the agreement value quantifies the effect of the initial APIR mismatch. Under the corresponding compatibility conditions, partial pinning guarantees safe reference tracking whenever the root component contains at least one informed agent. Simulations illustrate the coordination guarantees.

papers.title: Exponential Consensus and Flocking in Multi-Agent Systems with Infinite Fading Memory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the emergent collective dynamics of multi-agent systems driven by infinite distributed fading memory of Volterra type. We establish a unified theoretical framework covering both first-order opinion consensus dynamics and second-order velocity alignment flocking kinematics. By introducing Dafermos past-history transformations, the governing integro-differential systems are reformulated into dynamical systems on extended product Hilbert spaces. For first-order dynamics, we prove that fading memory inherently provides a hidden dissipative mechanism, guaranteeing unconditional global exponential consensus with or without instantaneous communication forces. For second-order dynamics, by developing a unified energy-multiplier framework that seamlessly couples instantaneous communication with memory dissipation, we establish unconditional global exponential flocking for both the pure fading memory system and the mixed interaction system, completely independent of the spatial dispersion or the communication tail.

papers.title: Inverse Semiclassical Scattering at Fixed Energy
papers.abstract: We investigate inverse scattering at a fixed energy for semiclassical Schrödinger operators with smooth potentials. For compactly supported potentials satisfying a natural virial condition, we prove that, under the sharp condition, $\liminf_{h\to0}\|S_1(λ,h)-S_2(λ,h)\|<2$ implies $V_1=V_2$, provided the fixed energy $λ$ lies above both potentials. We then consider radial short-range repulsive potentials. Under a monotonicity assumption on the radial force, we show that the semiclassical differential cross section at a fixed energy, up to $o(1)$ as $h\to0$, determines the potential in the classically accessible region. Finally, we obtain an analogous rigidity result for nontrapping compactly supported perturbations of the Euclidean metric under a strict convexity assumption.

papers.title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Refinement
papers.abstract: We introduce the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial F_Γ(G;x,y) = \sum_{H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}P_{Γ/h}(x,y), which aggregates the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials associated with all subgroups of a finite group acting on a graph. We derive the equivalent element-wise representation F_Γ(G;x,y) = \sum_{g\in G}c_G(g)P_{Γ/g}(x,y), where c_G(g) = \sum_{\langle g\rangle\leq H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}. The coefficient function depends only on the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and is constant on conjugacy classes. This yields decompositions by cyclic subgroups and conjugacy classes and an interpretation in terms of the incidence algebra of the subgroup lattice. After normalization, the coefficients define a probability distribution obtained by choosing a subgroup uniformly and then an element uniformly from that subgroup. We also establish diagonal multiplicativity for disjoint unions and a weighted cycle-index expression for edgeless graphs. A further contribution concerns the distinguishing power of the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial. We answer a question of Dohmen and Lange-Geisler affirmatively by exhibiting two non-isomorphic graphs, P_3 and K_2 \mathbin{\dot\cup} K_1 under C_2-actions, with identical orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. The two actions nevertheless have different multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. Thus the multiorbital polynomial is not determined by the orbital bivariate polynomial, whereas the converse question remains open.

papers.title: Quantitative Tiling Stability From Quadratic Discrepancy In Hamming Spaces
papers.abstract: Quadratic ball discrepancy measures how uniformly a code meets Hamming balls over all centers and radii. Perfect codes minimize this quantity among codes of the same cardinality. We prove a quantitative refinement: at the parameters of every perfect code other than a one-word code or the full space, the discrepancy excess over the minimum is at least an explicit positive multiple of the discrepancy at the packing radius. The latter equals the tiling defect divided by the square of the code cardinality. This defect is the total squared deviation of the covering multiplicity from one. The comparison applies to all codes of that cardinality. For one-error perfect codes, the coefficient is at least one, and no larger constant holds for all such codes; explicit coefficients depending on the parameters can be much larger. The tiling defect also measures the failure of uniform ball noise to smooth a code distribution. Consequently, the same discrepancy excess gives explicit bounds on holes, overlaps, and divergence from the uniform distribution.

papers.title: Sieve dimension and search depth for the Erdős-Straus conjecture, $n \equiv 1 \pmod{24}$
papers.abstract: For primes $n\equiv1\pmod{24}$, we study the depth of explicit, factorization-free searches for a decomposition of $4/n$ into three positive unit fractions. Let $E_2(N;J)$ be the set of such primes $n\le N$ for which no coprime pair $1\le u,a\le J$ admits a divisor $s\mid an+u$ with $s\equiv-1\pmod{4ua}$. For every fixed $J$, we prove $|E_2(N;J)|\ll_J N/(\log N)^{1+A(J)/2}$, where $A(J)$ counts the coprime pairs in $[1,J]^2$. The proof uses a fixed-point-free involution and identifies the exact dimension of the covering. We also establish a dual Type I divisor criterion and an unconditional obstruction: at the fixed shift $c=7$, both branches of the cofactor criterion fail for $\asymp N/(\log N)^{3/2}$ primes. At growing depth, an exact reciprocal-totient asymptotic with leading constant $9/(2π^2)$ improves the explicit large-sieve bounds to $O(N\exp(-0.0942(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^5$, and to $O_\varepsilon(N\exp(-(0.1093-\varepsilon)(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^{4+\varepsilon}$ for fixed sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Finally, combining a truncated Type I pass with a sparse residual search yields a complete, factorization-free batch decision procedure for all primes in $[N,2N]$, using $O(N^2(\log N)^2\exp(-c_0(\log N)^{2/3}))=o(N^2)$ arithmetic operations for some $c_0>0$. The conjecture itself remains open.

papers.title: Estimating Treatment Effects Through Intermediate-Event Pathways with Multi-State Data
papers.abstract: During clinical trials evaluating a drug's effect on a survival endpoint, intermediate events often occur before the primary event. The treatment can affect the primary event through multiple pathways via intermediate events. With multiple intermediate events, each is a treatment-induced confounder of transitions out of the others, so we cannot identify natural or separable effects. We instead consider stochastic interventions that assign each transition the identifiable observed-history hazard of either arm. Contrasts between the resulting counterfactual cumulative incidences define transition-, event-, and path-targeted effects, identifiable without cross-world or isolation assumptions. Based on the efficient influence functions for the counterfactual cumulative incidences under hypothetical interventions, we construct multiply robust and semiparametrically efficient estimators for these targeted treatment effects. Our proposed framework quantifies treatment effects through each transition, on each event, and along each path. By analyzing data from the LEADER trial, we find that liraglutide significantly reduces the risk of cardiovascular and microvascular events. The reduction in all-cause mortality is primarily mediated by its effects on expanded major adverse cardiovascular events.

papers.title: A fully discrete LBRFD-IPDG method for linear fourth-order parabolic equations
papers.abstract: We propose a fully discrete method for linear fourth-order parabolic equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions, combining an implicit LBRFD multistep scheme in time with a mixed interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method in space. The temporal discretization employs equispaced linear barycentric rational interpolants and incorporates a startup procedure. To facilitate the spatial discretization, the original problem is reformulated through an auxiliary variable. For certain parameter pairs $(n,d)$, the LBRFD method is shown to be $A(α)$-stable and to possess a wider stability angle than the corresponding BDF$p$ method of the same order. Stability and a priori error estimates are established via a $G$-energy technique and the discrete Grönwall lemma. The theoretical analysis yields a total $L^2$ error estimate of order $h^{k-1}+τ^p$, where $p=d$ if $n-d$ is even and $p=d+1$ if $n-d$ is odd. The reduced spatial convergence rate is attributed to boundary contributions on $\partialΩ$. Despite this theoretical prediction, numerical experiments confirm the stability and demonstrate optimal convergence of order $h^{k+1}+τ^p$.

papers.title: Finite-coefficient K-theory of henselian valued fields and Gersten injectivity
papers.abstract: Let $W$ be a henselian valuation ring with fraction field $L$, residue field $k$, and value group $Γ_W$. Let $N=\ell^ν$ be invertible in $W$. Choose an ordered $\mathbf Z/N$-basis $B$ of $Γ_W/NΓ_W$. Products of suitable classes define an equivalence of complete filtered spectra $$ \bigoplus_{\substack{J\subseteq B\\J\text{ finite}}} Σ^{|J|}\operatorname{Fil}_{\mathrm{mot}}^{\bullet-|J|} K(k;\mathbf Z/N) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Fil}_{\mathrm{mot}}^{\bullet} K(L;\mathbf Z/N) $$ The summand indexed by $\varnothing$ is the generic restriction map, after the rigidity equivalence $K(W;\mathbf Z/N)\simeq K(k;\mathbf Z/N)$, and is therefore split injective. Independently of this splitting, excision yields a lifting theorem for regular henselian pairs. In particular, this yields finite-coefficient Gersten injectivity for noetherian henselian regular local rings. Applications to completions along regular primes give relative and sometimes nonhenselian examples. More generally, if $P$ is a Prüfer ring and $R$ is a henselian local ind-smooth $P$-algebra, then $R$ is a domain and $K_n(R;\mathbf Z/N)\to K_n(\operatorname{Frac}(R);\mathbf Z/N)$ is injective for every $n$, provided $N\in R^\times$. These injectivity consequences extend from prime-power to arbitrary finite invertible coefficients by primary decomposition.

papers.title: Static Equilibria of Perturbed Spheres: A Single-Harmonic Class Map, a Parity Obstruction, and a Certified Counter for the Mono-Monostatic Regime
papers.abstract: Varkonyi and Domokos proved that homogeneous convex bodies with any prescribed numbers $S\ge1$ of stable and $U\ge1$ of unstable static equilibria exist, the case $S=U=1$ being the mono-monostatic Gomboc. We give a complete constructive answer for the simplest nondegenerate shapes: a homogeneous body whose boundary is the unit sphere perturbed radially by a single real spherical harmonic $Y_\ell^m$ of degree $\ell\ge2$ and order $1\le m\le\ell$ has exactly $S=U=m(\ell-m+1)$ stable and unstable equilibria, for every amplitude in the convex range when $m\ge2$, and for small amplitude when $m=1$. The reduction to the critical points of the perturbing harmonic is an identity when $m\ge2$: the symmetry of a single tesseral harmonic pins the centroid at the origin exactly, so the centroid-to-surface distance is a strictly increasing function of the harmonic. We count the critical points of $Y_\ell^m$ from its separable structure and verify the Poincare-Hopf balance in index form. Three consequences follow. (i) A single harmonic populates only the diagonal $S=U$ of the equilibrium-class lattice; no single harmonic of degree $\ge2$ is mono-monostatic. (ii) Any centrally symmetric (even-degree) perturbation has even $S$ and $U$ and cannot be mono-monostatic, a parity obstruction. (iii) Mono-monostaticity is therefore intrinsically multi-harmonic. A predict-then-confirm numerical study on eight single-harmonic bodies matches the formula exactly. For the multi-harmonic regime we give a certified equilibrium counter (interval arithmetic with Krawczyk uniqueness and Hessian classification) that, given the centroid, provably neither under- nor over-counts. It certifies that a member of a known analytic family, at an amplitude of our own choosing inside the strictly convex sub-regime, is mono-monostatic. For that body the centroid is exactly the origin, so its certificate is unconditional.

papers.title: U-centering as subset ANOVA: edge regression and higher-order theory
papers.abstract: Unbiased squared distance covariance and the Hilbert-Schmidt independence criterion (HSIC) are fourth-order U-statistics, yet U-centering evaluates them from pairwise arrays in $O(n^2)$ operations. We show that U-centering is exactly least-squares residualization after fitting additive endpoint effects. This analysis of variance (ANOVA) interpretation explains the zero row sums and the normalization through residual degrees of freedom. The same geometry gives regression representations of dependence and two-sample statistics, exact permutation variances, and relations among pooled and regression mean squares. For arrays indexed by $r$-element subsets and $n\ge2r$, higher-order U-centering removes all lower-order subset effects and projects onto a space of dimension $\binom{n}{r}-\binom{n}{r-1}$. For fixed symmetric square-integrable kernels evaluated on independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) paired observations, we derive the residual covariance matrix, exact mean-squared errors for estimating the highest-order Hoeffding components, unbiased positive semidefinite (PSD) covariance estimates, and moment formulas under independence and permutation. The normalized residual inner product equals a direct unbiased estimator involving up to $2r$ observations, but can be evaluated in $O(n^r)$ operations for fixed $r$. For four-argument matching kernels, three matrix products yield exactly unbiased estimators of a fourth spectral moment of kernel cross-covariance in $O(n^3)$ arithmetic and $O(n^2)$ storage. A numerical illustration distinguishes dependence structures with equal HSIC and different spectral concentration.

papers.title: Perfect Codes As Exact Minimizers Of Quadratic Discrepancy In q-ary Hamming Spaces
papers.abstract: Total quadratic ball discrepancy measures the deviation of codeword counts from uniformity over all Hamming balls. We prove that, whenever a Hamming space and cardinality admit a perfect code, the discrepancy minimizers among all subsets of that cardinality are precisely the perfect codes. This extends Barg's binary minimizing result and characterizes equality over arbitrary finite alphabets. At parameter sets that satisfy the sphere-packing condition and Lloyd's integral-root condition for correcting one or two errors, we give an explicit lower bound whose attainment is equivalent to perfect tiling: the discrepancy that a perfect code with these parameters would have. For one error, these include parameters at which the existence of a perfect code is open. For alphabets of size at least four, the discrepancy is an affine function of an energy with a strictly completely monotonic potential; for these alphabets, known universal energy bounds also give these lower bounds, and, when a perfect code exists, known universal optimality results also give the characterization of the minimizers. Over the ternary alphabet, complete monotonicity fails, and we prove the ternary bounds directly at all Hamming parameters and at the Golay parameters, the only nontrivial ternary cases.

papers.title: Rankin-Selberg duality via gluing
papers.abstract: We use a gluing procedure introduced by Ginzburg to describe the relative Langlands dual of the hyperspherical Hamiltonian $(\mathrm{GL}_n \times \mathrm{GL}_m)$-variety $T^*(\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{C}^m,\mathbb{C}^n))$, and in particular the Rankin-Selberg case $m=n$. We show that the dual is isomorphic to the triangle part of Cherkis-Nakajima-Takayama bow varieties, recovering a result of Nakajima. Using this result, we give a new proof of a theorem of Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima describing the regular perverse sheaf in type $A$. Following a suggestion of Ginzburg, we explain how to modify the gluing so that the dual Hamiltonian variety of $T^*\mathbf{N}$, for any gluable finite-dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a complex reductive group $G$, is naturally equipped with an anti-symplectic involution, and give an explicit formula for this involution in the Rankin-Selberg case.

papers.title: Adjacency-degree algebras and spectral determination of graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with adjacency matrix $A$ and degree matrix $D$. Applying $A$ and $D$ repeatedly to the all-ones vector produces a space $M_G$ of functions on the vertices, and these functions are constant on the orbits of the automorphism group. We call $G$ AD-observable if $M_G$ contains the indicator vector of every orbit, and AD-separable if the functions in $M_G$ separate the orbits. Forests are AD-observable, by McKay's leaf-pruning argument. Our main result is that for every cograph, $M_G$ is spanned by the indicator vectors of the cells of the stable partition of color refinement. Hence a cograph is AD-observable, or equivalently AD-separable, exactly when color refinement finds its orbits, and we describe these cographs by their cotrees. We also show that two cographs with the same number of vertices and the same homomorphism counts from all caterpillars have the same counts from all trees. The main result does not extend to distance-hereditary graphs: we give two such graphs on nine vertices that are AD-separable but not AD-observable.

papers.title: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem in operator algebras
papers.abstract: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem up to similarity in operator algebras asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$. We construct block-diagonal compact operators for which this implication fails. For von Neumann algebras with separable predual, we prove that this cancellation property is equivalent to subhomogeneity. Moreover, we obtain a cancellation law for finite ampliations in unital Banach algebras when the commutant of one element is finite dimensional modulo its Jacobson radical.

papers.title: Regularity and Decay for Navier-Slip Fluid-Structure Interaction in Exterior Domains
papers.abstract: We study the linearized motion of a spherical rigid body immersed in an incompressible viscous fluid occupying the whole space, under Navier slip boundary conditions with friction. While semigroup regularity and decay estimates are well understood for the no-slip case, such results have been limited to bounded domains in the slip setting. By exploiting the geometric regularity of the sphere, we establish strong $L^q$-regularity, bounded analyticity, and sharp $ L^q-L^r$ estimates for the corresponding fluid-structure operator. These results would provide a foundation for constructing strong $W^{2,1}_q$ solutions and Kato-type solutions to the corresponding nonlinear system.

papers.title: Tautological classes on KSBA spaces
papers.abstract: We extend the definitions of kappa, psi and lambda classes from the case of moduli spaces of stable curves to the higher-dimensional case of KSBA spaces, and prove a number of their basic properties.

papers.title: Curvature-Dependent Path Concentration in Stochastic Fast-Slow Systems with Noise on the Slow Variable
papers.abstract: We study stochastic fast-slow systems with noise acting exclusively on the slow variable near uniformly attracting, normally hyperbolic critical manifolds $x=X^\ast(y)$. The deviation equation contains transmitted diffusion and an Itô curvature forcing of order $O(σ^2\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert)$. Using a parameter-dependent Lyapunov function and stopped martingale estimates, we obtain geometry-dependent concentration bounds under the sufficient noise restriction $σ\le C_0\min(\sqrt{\varepsilon},\varepsilon^{1/4}L_{\mathrm{geom}}/\sqrt{λ_0})$, where $λ_0$ is the uniform spectral gap and $L_{\mathrm{geom}}=\sqrt{λ_0/(\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert\lVert h\rVert^2)}$. For fixed geometry and any fixed $p>0$, the confidence radius on $[0,T/\varepsilon]$ is $O(\varepsilon+σ^2+σ\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)})$, with stopped fast-variable failure probability at most $\varepsilon^p$; slow-variable exit is controlled separately. We also establish an adiabatic error bound of order $O(\varepsilon+σ\sqrt{\varepsilon}+σ^2\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert)$, with explicit failure probabilities. These estimates quantify the curvature dependence of fast-variable concentration and its $O(\varepsilon)$ contribution to the slow-error upper bound for fixed geometry.

papers.title: HJ numbers revisited
papers.abstract: Hales-Jewett theorem is well known. We prove a primitive recursive bound, in fact an $\clE^5$ one, for the density version. In preparation we deal with what was the main induction step in the old proof of Hales-Jewett as a result in its own right with better bounds. Also in improving our bounds.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Transitive permutation groups with trivial four point stabilizers"
papers.abstract: This article revisits earlier work by the last author together with Kay Magaard. We correct mistakes in results about the Sylow 2- and 3-structure of groups that act with fixity 3 and one result about possible components, we improve some results and we add details.

papers.title: Symplectic Hamiltonian Direct Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Wave Propagation
papers.abstract: This paper presents a symplectic Hamiltonian direct discontinuous Galerkin (DDG) method for approximating wave propagation problems, including the linear and semilinear wave equations. Within an auxiliary-variable-free DG framework, we prove that the symmetry of the numerical flux bilinear form is equivalent to the existence of a discrete Hamiltonian structure. It follows that methods such as the symmetric interior penalty, BR2, and symmetric DDG (SDDG) methods admit a discrete Hamiltonian structure, whereas the Baumann--Oden and DDG methods do not possess this property. Exploiting this structure, we construct fully discrete symplectic schemes by combining the SDDG spatial discretization with symplectic time integrators. We also develop a unified treatment of periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin boundary conditions that preserves the discrete Hamiltonian structure of the SDDG scheme. We further derive error estimates for the SDDG method applied to semilinear wave equations under these boundary conditions, showing the optimal convergence rate for the displacement and the suboptimal convergence rate for the velocity. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate that the symplectic Hamiltonian DDG method achieves superior long-time energy conservation and accuracy.

papers.title: Algebra of the Infrared with Elliptic Curve-Valued Potential
papers.abstract: We study an extension of the algebra of the infrared to curve--valued potentials, focusing on the elliptic curve case. Given a finite configuration of points on an elliptic curve, we construct associated \(L_\infty\)-algebra. Adding an extra point produces a directed \(A_\infty\)-algebra and an \(L_\infty\)-morphism to their directed Hochschild deformation complexes. Maurer--Cartan elements of the \(L_\infty\)-algebra determine \(A_\infty\)-deformations of the directed algebra. We formulate a conjectural comparison between Maurer--Cartan deformations of the directed algebra and the directed Fukaya--Seidel category associated to compatible finite collections of thimbles.

papers.title: A Topological Formula for Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations
papers.abstract: We exhibit a formula relating the correlation between Wilson loop variables in Potts lattice gauge theory to a topological quantity in the plaquette random cluster model. As applications we prove exponential decay of correlations between slowly growing Wilson loop variables for Ising lattice gauge theory on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ at all but the critical temperature, we demonstrate that the correlation length is finite at sufficiently high or low temperatures in any dimension, and we show that the correlation length of the model on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ with free boundary conditions equals that of the dual model with constant boundary conditions when $q$ is prime.

papers.title: Foliated and Mather-Jacobian discrepancies via tangential arcs
papers.abstract: We express the log discrepancies of co-rank one foliations on normal varieties in terms of arc codimensions and differential orders. On smooth threefolds, if a foliation has simple singularities and its separatrices form an algebraic simple normal crossings divisor, we identify its foliated discrepancies with those of an ordinary pair for every divisor centred on the separatrices. This gives adjunction and log canonical threshold formulae. For algebraic images of the separatrices, we estimate changes in boundary orders caused by failure of ideal generation and by descent through the conductor. For locally complete intersection images, comparison on a common resolution yields criteria for equality of discrepancies and bounds on log canonical thresholds.

papers.title: Geodesic Divergence on Riemannian Planes with Bounded Geometry
papers.abstract: In this article, we study Riemannian planes $(M,g)$ which satisfies a bounded geometry condition ( bounded sectional curvature and a non-vanishing injectivity radius of $(M,g)$). We show that such a Riemannian plane is always quasi-isometric to a radially symmetric plane which also satisfies the aforesaid bounded geometry condition. Using that, we study the quasi-redirecting boundary of Riemannian planes with bounded geometry and show that it is either a single point or $\mathbb{S}^1$. We contrast the quasi-redirecting boundary with the Martin boundary and construct Riemannian planes with bounded geometry for which the We also characterise quasi-redirection in Riemannian planes with bounded geometry via their asymptotic cones and their cut points. Lastly, we characterise $\mathbb{E}^2$ and $\mathbb{H}^2$ upto quasi-isometry by their asymptotic cones.

papers.title: Absolute Continuity of Monotone Aggregations under Positive Regression Dependence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide sufficient conditions for the absolute continuity of one-dimensional push-forwards of dependent random vectors. Suppose that $X$ has an absolutely continuous distribution and that the conditional distribution of an $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued random vector $Y$ given $X=x$ is nondecreasing in $x\in \mathbb{R}$ in the usual stochastic order. For Borel maps $g\colon \mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying a coordinatewise monotonicity condition in $Y$ and a uniform lower-increment condition in $X$, we prove that $g(X,Y)$ has an absolutely continuous distribution. The result requires neither independence nor a joint density, and allows the marginal law of $Y$ to be completely arbitrary. Moreover, the result remains valid if $\mathbb{R}^d$ is replaced by an arbitrary measurable space endowed with a reflexive binary relation. We discuss consequences for monotone risk aggregation and extensions of the familiar regularization by convolution beyond independent random variables.

papers.title: Thermodynamic formalism for non-compact systems with expansivity and specification
papers.abstract: We develop a new theory of thermodynamic formalism for non-compact flows, providing criteria for existence and uniqueness of equilibrium states, as well as ergodicity and a Gibbs property. These criteria include new versions of the expansivity and specification properties that hold for geodesic flows on non-compact negatively curved manifolds. Previous results on thermodynamic formalism for these geodesic flows were restricted by a pinched curvature condition, which we remove, allowing curvature to approach both $0$ and $-\infty$. Our results also apply to geodesic flows beyond the smooth setting, including locally CAT(-1) spaces.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean balanced metrics and their application to totally degenerate abelian varieties
papers.abstract: For a polarized complex manifold with discrete automorphism group, it is known that if the first Chern class admits a cscK metric, then the balanced metrics, which are characterized in terms of the algebro-geometric notion of Chow stability, approximate this cscK metric. In this paper, we study a non-Archimedean analogue of this phenomenon. In particular, we prove that such an analogue holds for polarized totally degenerate abelian varieties. As an application, we also show that, for a totally degenerating family of polarized abelian varieties, the validity of this non-Archimedean analogue yields a uniform estimate for the Calabi--Yau metrics on fibers sufficiently close to the degenerate fiber.

papers.title: A non-trivial index difference on surfaces of genus at least $3$
papers.abstract: For every closed surface of genus at least $3$, equipped with any bounding spin structure, we show that the index difference, viewed as a map from the fundamental group of the space of Dirac-invertible Riemannian metrics to $\KO^{-4}(*)$, is non-trivial. If the genus is at least $5$, we also show that the aforementioned index difference is surjective. For products of two closed surfaces of genus at least $3$, equipped with any spin structure, we prove that the corresponding space of Dirac-invertible Riemannian metrics is not contractible. We discuss the relationship of this result to the existence of metrics with harmonic spinors in dimension~$4$.

papers.title: The inradius law for the cavities of planar Brownian motion, with applications to the Wiener sausage
papers.abstract: Let $K_1=B[0,1]$ be the trace of a planar Brownian motion, and let $N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)$ count the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K_1$ with inradius greater than $η$. As $η\downarrow0$, we prove that $η^2(\log(1/η))^2N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)\to c_{\mathrm{in}}=(π/2)\int G^2d\mathcal{L}\in(0,1/2]$ almost surely and in $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,2]$, where $G$ is the inradius divided by the square root of the area and $\mathcal{L}$ is Werner's limiting shape law. Inradius determines survival under thickening: a cavity contains a hole of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ if and only if its inradius exceeds $r$. Brownian scaling shows that, for fixed $r>0$ as $T\to\infty$, the number of cavities of $B[0,T]$ with inradius greater than $r$ is asymptotic to $4c_{\mathrm{in}}T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ in probability and in $L^p$, $p\in[1,2]$. It also gives lower bounds for the sausage's hole count, the Betti curve of its degree-one persistent homology, and its radius integrals, with constant $4c_{\mathrm{in}}$ in expectation and any smaller constant with probability tending to one. A matching upper bound cannot follow from general bounds in terms of perimeter, area, diameter or length. We prove that it is equivalent to a first-moment estimate for near-critical pockets: holes at level $η$ on which the distance to the trace is at most $2η$. Equivalently, it suffices to control residual pockets beyond one per cavity with inradius in $(η,2η]$. This estimate is proved in a companion paper, yielding the exact order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ for the expected number of holes.

papers.title: Domination in Johnson graphs J(n, 3) for odd n
papers.abstract: In 2025 Cornet, Dravec, and Torres determined the domination number $γ(J(n,3))$ of the Johnson graph for every even $n \ge 6$, expressing it as a closed form $φ_n$ in terms of Fort-Hedlund covering numbers, and conjectured the same value for odd $n$. We prove this conjecture: $γ(J(n,3)) = φ_n$ for every odd $n \ge 7$. A dominating set of $J(n,3)$ is the same as a lotto design $\mathrm{LD}(n,3,3,2)$, and the lotto numbers $L(n,3,3,2)$, and hence $γ(J(n,3))$, were already determined for every $n$ by Bate (1978) and by Brouwer (1981); a short degree argument of Füredi, Székely, and Zubor (1996) gives the same lower bound for all $n \not\equiv 9, 10 \pmod{12}$. The contribution of this paper is therefore a new proof of the odd case, carried out within the bijective framework of Cornet, Dravec, and Torres.

papers.title: On statistical inference for non-linear dynamical systems evolving in their global attractor
papers.abstract: We consider a periodic scalar reaction-diffusion system over a two-dimensional domain under natural conditions on the reaction function and with initial condition $θ$. We show that on the global attractor $\mathcal A$ of the resulting dynamical system $(u_θ(t):t>0)$, a reverse Poincaré inequality holds true, and that as a consequence the map $θ\mapsto u_θ(t)$ satisfies an $L^2(\Om)$-Lipschitz stability estimate on $\mathcal A$ for any $t>0$ fixed. We then show that statistical recovery of an initial condition $θ$ in the attractor $\mathcal A$, as well as prediction of the states $u_θ$, is possible from discrete measurements of the system at parametric $1/\sqrt N$ convergence rates.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Decentralized Stochastic Convex Optimization over Networks
papers.abstract: We study decentralized stochastic smooth convex optimization, where $M$ workers minimize an average objective using local stochastic gradients and neighbor-only communication over a fixed gossip network. A central question in this setting is to determine the largest number of workers that can be used under a total budget of $N$ gradient samples while still preserving the centralized $O(1/\sqrt N)$ statistical rate. We introduce an accelerated decentralized method that preserves this rate for up to $\smash{M\lesssim \sqrtρ\,N^{3/4}}$ workers, where $ρ$ is the spectral gap of the gossip network, improving the best prior maximal scaling of $\smash{M\lesssim ρ\sqrt N}$. The method is based on a one-step-delayed stochastic acceleration scheme that enables workers to interleave minibatching with accelerated gossip while controlling residual disagreement, and its guarantee depends only logarithmically on the optimum-local heterogeneity. We also establish a matching lower bound for linear-span decentralized first-order methods, showing that the method is optimal up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: On the First Caustic of Elliptical Billiards
papers.abstract: A point source of light is placed inside a billiard with a smooth, convex, closed boundary. For any integer $n$, the $n$-th caustic by reflection, denoted by $Γ_n$, is the envelope of light rays that have undergone $n$ reflections in such a billiard after emanating from the source. It has been conjectured by Gil Bor and Serge Tabachnikov that for an elliptical billiard, $Γ_n$ has exactly four ordinary cusps; this problem is a billiard variation of Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement, which concerns the number of cusps in the conjugate locus of a point on an ellipsoid. Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, and Serge Tabachnikov have proven that $Γ_n$ has at least four ordinary cusps. In this paper, we present a proof that $Γ_1$ has exactly four ordinary cusps, using billiards in complex spaces.

papers.title: Second-order PACF asymptotics and discrimination between fractional Gaussian noise and $\FARIMA(0,d,0)$
papers.abstract: Fractional Gaussian noise and $\FARIMA(0,d,0)$ have the same long-memory pole $|θ|^{-2d}$ and hence the same leading PACF law $α(n)\sim d/n$. We show that this agreement breaks at the first non-universal order. For $0<d<1/2$, the pure fGn PACF satisfies $$ α_{\fGn}(n)=\frac d n+\frac{C_{\fGn}(d)}{n^2}+o(n^{-2}), \qquad C_{\fGn}(d)<d^2, $$ The proof uses the Bingham--Inoue--Kasahara representation, a phase-coefficient expansion for fGn, and a Hankel-operator perturbation argument. Thus the fGn spectral envelope is invisible at first order but visible in second-order finite prediction, explaining why short-memory order selection can differ when fGn data are fitted by FARIMA-type models.

papers.title: Undecidability in Relevant Logic
papers.abstract: We prove undecidability for every positive relevant logic extending the system axiomatized by hypothetical syllogism, prefixing, and suffixing and contained in the logic of the semilattice frame $(P_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb{N}), \cup, \varnothing)$. This settles the longstanding decision problem for the semilattice relevant logic S in the negative, contrary to prevailing expectations of decidability. It also provides a new proof of Urquhart's (1984) undecidability theorem for R, E, and T, now by reduction from the Wang tiling problem for arbitrarily large finite isosceles right triangular regions of the plane.

papers.title: Morse flow categories as exit path categories
papers.abstract: We prove that the topological flow category $\mathcal{M}$ arising from a Morse-Smale pair $(f,ξ)$ on a smooth closed manifold $X$ is equivalent, as an $\infty$-category, to Lurie's $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sing}_A(X)$ of exit paths in $X$ with respect to the stratification by the stable manifolds of $ξ$. The objects of $\mathcal{M}$ are the critical points of $f$, and for every pair of critical points, the space of morphisms of $\mathcal{M}$ between these is the space of possibly broken trajectories of $ξ$ connecting them; it can be identified up to homotopy with the space of unbroken ones. The latter maps naturally to the space of exit paths connecting these critical points; we prove this map to be a weak homotopy equivalence. Then, we combine these ingredients with several others to construct a zigzag of equivalences between the homotopy coherent nerve of $\mathcal{M}$, denoted $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$, and $\mathrm{Sing}_A(X)$. The $n$-simplices of $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$ are homotopy coherent diagrams of $n$ composable morphisms of $\mathcal{M}$; we introduce the notion of unbroken diagram, yielding an $\infty$-subcategory of $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$, which we refer to as the flow coherent nerve of $\mathcal{M}$. The simplices of the latter give rise to stratified maps out of a family of stratified cubes, into $X$. We organize this family into a functor from the category of finite ordered sequences of critical points, to the category of $A$-stratified topological spaces, and we prove a comparison result with the usual stratified geometric realization functor. We finally use a theorem of Tanaka that associates a functor to a semi-simplicial map between $\infty$-categories that satisfies certain conditions. Our theorem has implications regarding constructible sheaves and the description of homotopy types in terms of flow categories.

papers.title: Whittaker groups and hyperelliptic curves
papers.abstract: Let K be a complete, non-archimedean valued field with a residue field of characteristic different from 2. A Whittaker group G is a discontinuous subgroup of PGL(2,K), freely generated by elements s_0,...,s_g of order two, each defined by a pair of fixed points {a_0,b_0},...,{a_g,b_g}. These fixed points are called ``in good position''. A subgroup W in G of index 2 is a Schottky group and produces a hyperelliptic Mumford curve Omega/W --> Omega/G = P^1, called `Whittaker curve', of genus g and with branch locus B in P^1(K). An explicit parametrization of Whittaker curves in terms of theta functions for W and G and the data of the fixed points, is developed. In particular, this allows one to express the branched points (and other data such as p-adic periods and p-adic heights) in terms of values of theta functions. A central theme of this paper is the relation between the fixed points and the branch locus. For a given configuration (P,m) of $g+1$ pairs of points in P^1, one defines a rigid space Fix_{P,m} of fixed points in good position with that configuration and a rigid space of branched points $ Branch_{P,m} in that configuration. A main result is that the natural morphism FB: Fix_{P,m} --> Branch_{P,m} is a rigid etale covering with Galois group {\pm 1}^{d-1} for some d>0. For all cases of genus g=2,3 (and for some more), an approximation of FB is computed which confirms the main result. Classification of Whittaker groups and analytic reductions of Whittaker curves is another important issue of this paper. The background material in this paper complements the work of L.~Gerritzen, G.~Van Steen, F.~Herrlich and others. It involves re-examination of some proofs, the derivation of properties of semi-stable analytic reductions and studying good position of fixed points.

papers.title: Self-Distillation is Optimal Among Spectral Shrinkage Estimators
papers.abstract: Self-distillation has emerged as a promising technique for improving model performance in modern machine learning systems. We develop the statistical foundations of self-distillation in high-dimensional linear regression by introducing and analyzing a broad class of estimators, namely spectral shrinkage estimators. We consider both spiked and general covariance matrices. For the former, we establish that when the covariance has $s$ distinct spikes, $s$-step self-distillation achieves optimal prediction among spectral shrinkage estimators, outperforming well-known estimators in statistics and machine learning. Moreover, we show that $s$ steps are necessary for optimality: any $(s-k)$-step distilled estimator is strictly suboptimal for $1 \leq k \leq s$. For general covariance matrices, we show that self-distillation approaches the optimal limiting prediction risk among continuous spectral shrinkage estimators as the number of distillation steps increases. We further develop a generalized cross-validation procedure for selecting the distillation parameters from data and establish an asymptotic oracle guarantee for the resulting estimator. We also study a federated approach where multiple data centers share spectral shrinkage estimators and a common server seeks to aggregate them to achieve optimal performance. In this case, we find that the best local rule again takes the form of self-distillation, though it differs from the optimal rule when data are hosted centrally on a single server. Together, our results explain why self-distillation improves predictive performance and provide a broader statistical framework that connects it to classical shrinkage-based methods.

papers.title: Keisler Measures and Generically Stable Random Types
papers.abstract: We introduce the notions of $rgs$ and $irgs$ for Keisler measures, motivated by the study of generically stable random types and their associated Morley sequences. We obtain characterizations of these notions in terms of averages of classical first-order formulas over suitable probabilistic partitions (Theorems 3.2 and 3.3). We compare these notions with $fim$, $fam$, and self-averaging, and show that for types the notions $fim$, $irgs$, and $rgs$ coincide. We prove that if a definable global Keisler measure$μ$ is not dependent, then every Morley sequence in its canonical random extension $r_μ$ is divergent (Theorem 4.7). Consequently, every $irgs$ measure is dependent (Corollary 4.8) and hence symmetric (Corollary 4.13). Furthermore, we show that for $irgs$ measures the model-theoretic instability events $\mathbf{O}^\varphi$, $\mathbf{I}^\varphi$, and $\mathbf{L}^\varphi$ have $\mathbb{P}_μ$-measure zero (Theorem 5.4). In view of the equivalence of $fim$ and $irgs$ subsequently established in [6], this provides an alternative proof of the corresponding result for $fim$ measures in [9].

papers.title: Higher-Order Neyman Orthogonality in Moment-Condition Models
papers.abstract: We construct moment functions that are Neyman-orthogonal to a chosen order in moment-condition models that involve finite-dimensional nuisance parameters. These moment functions reduce sensitivity to estimation error in the nuisance parameters and, as such, offer a unified and tractable route to higher-order debiasing in a wide range of econometric models. The number of additional nuisance parameters required by our construction, beyond those already present in the original moment conditions, is independent of the order of orthogonalization and can be reduced to a single scalar if desired.

papers.title: On the existence of optimizers for nonlinear time-frequency concentration problems: the Born-Jordan distribution
papers.abstract: We study the $L^p$ concentration problem for the Born-Jordan distribution in dimension $d>1$, thus extending the one-dimensional analysis in [Stra-Svela-Trapasso, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)]. We show that the existence of concentration optimizers depends on the exponent $p$ with a critical threshold at $p_*(d)= \frac{2d}{d-2}$ for $d\geq2$ (with the understanding that $p_*(2)=\infty$). In particular, for subcritical exponents $1\leq p<p_*(d)$ we prove that the supremum is finite and is attained, whereas for supercritical exponents $p>p_*(d)$ we show that the functional is unbounded. We also provide the complete solution in the (significantly more) challenging critical regime in dimension $d=2$. For the critical case in dimension $d=2$ and the supercritical case in dimension $d>2$ we also show that $L^2$ functions whose Born-Jordan distribution does not belong to $L^p$ are generic in the Baire sense. For the critical exponent in dimension $d>2$, for which Wang has recently shown that the supremum is finite, we prove that the functional is not sequentially weakly upper semicontinuous, showing that the still open question of attainment is nontrivial.

papers.title: Minimal Filling Architectures for Polynomial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Minimal filling architectures describe the smallest hidden-layer widths for which the neurovariety of a polynomial neural network fills its ambient function space. It was conjectured that every such architecture has unimodal hidden widths. We construct counterexamples to this conjecture using a frontier search and certify the main example through finite-field Jacobian computations and recursive dimension bounds. In the opposite direction, we prove that every minimal filling architecture of depth at most three is unimodal. A nonunimodal minimal filling architecture of depth four shows that the depth bound is sharp.

papers.title: Scaling Symmetries and Conformal Relative Equilibria on Poisson Manifolds, with Applications to Lie-Poisson Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate conformal relative equilibria for Hamiltonian systems on exact Poisson manifolds equipped with scaling symmetries. By introducing conformally Poisson actions and conformal momentum maps, we characterize these equilibria through an augmented Hamiltonian formulation; in the nondegenerate case, this recovers the conditions recently developed for the exact symplectic case. Specializing to the Lie-Poisson manifold $\mathfrak g^*$ associated with an arbitrary finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, we show that its natural scaling action makes $\mathfrak g^*$ an exact Poisson manifold. We then establish a purely algebraic existence criterion: there exists a homogeneous Hamiltonian on $\mathfrak g^*$ admitting a nontrivial conformal relative equilibrium if and only if $\mathfrak g$ contains an element whose adjoint operator has a nonzero real eigenvalue. Applying this criterion to the Bianchi classification, we identify exactly the real three-dimensional Lie algebras for which there exists a homogeneous Hamiltonian admitting a nontrivial conformal relative equilibrium. As a prominent application, we show that nontrivial conformal relative equilibria exist for a rigid body on $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)^*$, whereas the classical free rigid body on $\mathfrak{so}(3)^*$ admits no nontrivial conformal relative equilibria.

papers.title: Grokking or Glitching? How Low-Precision Drives Slingshot Loss Spikes
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks exhibit periodic loss spikes during unregularized long-term training, a phenomenon known as the "Slingshot Mechanism." Existing work usually attributes this to intrinsic optimization dynamics, but its triggering mechanism remains unclear. This paper proves that this phenomenon is a result of floating-point arithmetic precision limits. As training enters a high-confidence stage, the difference between the correct-class logit and the other logits may exceed the absorption-error threshold. Then during backpropagation, the gradient of the correct class is rounded exactly to zero, while the gradients of the incorrect classes remain nonzero. This breaks the zero-sum constraint of gradients across classes and introduces a systematic drift in the parameter update of the classifier layer. We prove that this drift forms a positive feedback loop with the feature, causing the global classifier mean and the global feature mean to grow exponentially. We call this mechanism Numerical Feature Inflation (NFI). This mechanism explains the rapid norm growth before a Slingshot spike, the subsequent reappearance of gradients, and the resulting loss spike. We further show that NFI is not equivalent to an observed loss spike: in more practical tasks, partial absorption may not produce visible spikes, but it can still break the zero-sum constraint and drive rapid growth of parameter norms. Our results reinterpret Slingshot as a numerical dynamic of finite-precision training, and provide a testable explanation for abnormal parameter growth and logit divergence in late-stage training.

papers.title: Ropelength-Filtered Reidemeister Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove relative smoothing with uniform reach control for one-parameter families of positive-reach $C^{1,1}$ knots and combine it with relative multijet transversality to obtain projection-generic regularization inside strict ropelength sublevels. Passing to a lifted Reidemeister multigraph reconstructs the admissible $π_0$ of every strict projection-framed ropelength sublevel, and the right-relaxed diagrammatic merge scale equals the geometric one. The normalised projection-framed sublevels are compact, so connected merge levels are attained. These degree-zero results are organized by a fibre cosheaf: a filtered relational cellular cosheaf of sets on the planar Reidemeister multigraph, whose stalks are strict fibre components and whose costalks are the relations realized by Reidemeister movies. The lifted multigraph is its Grothendieck construction, reconstruction is a descent statement, and the diagram image is its support. The diagram image computes merges exactly when no stalk is persistently separated, and a canonical flat coarsening is the coarsest diagram-indexed model that computes components. For amphichiral knots the spherical diagram image cannot detect mirror barriers, whereas the planar image can; no planar type of the standard diagrams of $4_1$ and $6_3$ is fixed by crossing switch. Symmetric hubs and finite certificates give upper bounds for mirror merges, and sign separators give lower bounds. For finite recognition we distinguish full rooted-ball occurrence, visibility in the monotone diagram-image filtration, and saturation. Every finite Reidemeister submultigraph becomes visible at a finite ropelength level, a visible saturated Barbensi-Celoria characteristic certificate determines the knot type up to mirroring, and a universal computable crossing-complexity bound controls visibility.

papers.title: Hyper Input Convex Neural Networks for Shape Constrained Learning and Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: We introduce Hyper Input Convex Neural Networks (HyCNNs), a novel neural network architecture designed for learning convex functions. HyCNNs combine the principles of Maxout networks with input convex neural networks (ICNNs) to create a neural network that is always convex in the input, theoretically capable of leveraging depth, and performs reliably when trained at scale compared to ICNNs. Concretely, we prove that HyCNNs require exponentially fewer parameters than ICNNs to approximate quadratic functions up to a given precision. Throughout a series of synthetic experiments, we demonstrate that HyCNNs outperform existing ICNNs and MLPs in terms of predictive performance for convex regression and interpolation tasks. We further apply HyCNNs to learn high-dimensional optimal transport maps for synthetic examples and for single-cell data, where they oftentimes outperform ICNN-based neural optimal transport methods and other baselines across a wide range of setting.

papers.title: Metastability Landscapes in Nonlinear Ghost-Normal Scalar Fields
papers.abstract: We investigate finite time dynamics in nonlinear classical scalar field systems containing one ghost and one normal kinetic sector. Using a spacetime finite element formulation, we study the dependence of threshold crossing and numerical continuation times on initial amplitude, characteristic wavenumber, spectral tilt, phase structure, and spatial localization. In the quartic model, larger amplitudes generally lead to earlier growth, while higher wavenumbers and ultraviolet-biased spectra favor longer resolved bounded evolution. Smooth compact initial data exhibit a broad region with no observed growth threshold crossing over the simulated interval. A direct comparison of two Gaussian evolutions shows that enhanced low-wavenumber power can precede rapid field growth, although this observation does not establish a universal spectral-transfer mechanism. We also compare the quartic interaction with a lifted $φ^6$ potential. The latter gives a markedly different continuation landscape, with a broad long-converged region followed by shorter accessible terminal times at larger amplitudes. Localization diagnostics do not identify a persistent oscillon core in the selected cases. By distinguishing amplitude growth, spectral reorganization, solver-limited termination, and finite-time censoring, our results characterize a nontrivial metastability landscape without implying global or quantum stability.

papers.title: A theory of generalized Lamé curves
papers.abstract: We study the generalized Lam'e equation (GLE) on an elliptic curve $E$ with multiple regular singularities $\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i = 1}^r$ of weights $\mathbf{n} = (n_i)_{i = 1}^r$. By analyzing the locus admitting quasi-periodic solutions, we construct two fundamental algebraic curves: (i) The generalized Lam'e curve (GLC), $\mathcal{Y}_{\mathbf{n}, \mathbf{p}}$, which lies in an affine bundle over $\operatorname{Sym}^n E$ for total weight $n:=\sum n_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ and parametrizes generalized Hermite--Halphen ansatz solutions. (ii) The log-free curve, $V_{\mathbf{n}, \mathbf{p}}$, a non-complete intersection variety arising when all $n_i \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{N}$, which we prove is a reduced curve, confirming a conjecture of Wang. We analyze the GLC as an algebraic family over the pole configuration space. By studying the addition map$$σ\colon \operatorname{Sym}^n E \longrightarrow E,$$where we establish a generically finite, universal degree formula, we show that the geometry of boundary degenerations under pole collisions perfectly mirrors the tensor algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{C})$-modules within the BGG category $\mathcal{O}$. This provides the local structural limits needed to establish the global flatness of the GLC. Furthermore, we develop a framework of twisted isomonodromic deformations and construct $(\mathbf{n}, \mathbf{p})$-deformed pre-modular forms parameterized by twisted monodromy data $(t,s)$. Their vanishing solves the underlying monodromy problem and factorizes along boundary strata, allowing an arbitrary configuration to be continuously deformed down to the classical Lam'e equation. Finally, using an asymptotic scaling technique, we give a complete extension of Treibich's generic counting for $r=2$ symmetric pairs to all smooth elliptic curves.

papers.title: Spherical Cap $L_2$ Discrepancy -- Blessing of Dimensionality and a Distance-Kernel Variant
papers.abstract: We prove a dimension-explicit upper bound for the information-complexity (also called the inverse of the discrepancy) of the classical spherical cap $L_2$ discrepancy on the $d$-dimensional sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$. For every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, this bound implies that a single point suffices in all sufficiently large dimensions, which shows a ``blessing of dimensionality'' for the associated numerical integration problem. We then introduce a one-parameter family of distance reproducing kernels for the Sobolev space $H^{(d+1)/2}(\mathbb{S}^d)$. For the balanced kernel $K(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})=1-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\|\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{y}\|$, a lower bound together with a random-point upper bound shows that the normalized information-complexity is $Θ_\varepsilon(d)$ for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. Thus its dependence on $d$ is determined up to constants depending only on $\varepsilon$. Finally, we study the one-sided spherical cap discrepancy obtained by restricting the height parameter to $[0,1]$. We derive its kernel and Stolarsky's invariance principle explicitly. A sharp mean-distance inequality, attained by regular simplices, determines its normalized information-complexity exactly in all sufficiently large dimensions and proves strong polynomial tractability with optimal $\varepsilon$-exponent two.

papers.title: DeepRitzSplit: A Variational Neural Operator Framework for Gradient Flows with Application to Dendritic Growth
papers.abstract: Phase-field models are widely used to simulate microstructure evolution but their numerical solution remains computationally demanding. Neural operator surrogates provide a promising alternative, yet existing approaches are data-driven, requiring large datasets and exhibiting limited robustness when extrapolating to unseen configurations. We introduce DeepRitzSplit, an unsupervised neural operator framework for gradient-flow systems based on a variational formulation of energy-stable splitting schemes. It learns the time evolution semigroup associated with a convex-concave free-energy decomposition by minimizing the underlying variational problem at each time step. It is designed to inherit the dissipative structure of the underlying gradient flow without requiring trajectory datasets. We further introduce a Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture motivated by splitting schemes, with separate reaction and diffusion components to improve training efficiency and interpretability. We assess the approach on the Allen-Cahn equation and apply it to a phase-field model of anisotropic dendritic growth during solidification. In the Allen-Cahn benchmark, DeepRitzSplit shows better generalization than the supervised baseline on the out-of-distribution configurations tested, using 180 training configurations. In dendritic growth, the method captures the overall phase morphology and dendrite tip velocity well, while the tip radius is more sensitive to the training strategy. Refinement based on the residual of the splitting scheme markedly improves this second-order morphological quantity. The trained operators retain good predictive capabilities on configurations substantially different from the training set. These results demonstrate the potential of variationally trained neural operators as physically informed surrogates for accelerated microstructure simulations.

papers.title: Semistable Reduction Theorem for Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
papers.abstract: We prove the semistable reduction theorem for $\mathcal{E}^†_K$-valued and $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over $k((t))$-varieties which were introduced by Lazda and Pál. As an application, we prove the finite dimensionality of $\mathcal{E}^†_K$-valued rigid cohomology with compact support.

papers.title: Exotic Hopf maps, weight shifting and applications to vector bundles
papers.abstract: Using motivic homotopy theory we produce several explicit polynomial representatives of the suspension of the Hopf map defined over the integers. We derive from this computation an explicit rank 2 vector bundle on the Jouanolou device of the projective space of dimension 3 over the integers.

papers.title: Convergence and Stability of a Catching-Up Algorithm for Differential Inclusions with Maximally Monotone Operators
papers.abstract: We study a catching-up algorithm with approximate projections for finite-dimensional differential inclusions governed by a maximally monotone operator and a continuous perturbation. Through the canonical decomposition of the operator into a regular part and the normal cone to the closure of its domain, the problem becomes a sweeping process, discretized by an explicit predictor step and a feasible approximate projection. For variable time steps, the approximations converge, up to a subsequence, to a solution on every finite horizon when the mesh size and the accumulated projection-error budget vanish and the nodes stay in a common compact convex set. This set comes from linear growth on finite horizons and, without any growth condition, by dissipativity of the projected field at a feasible center, which confines the nodes to a fixed ball uniformly in time for small steps and small projection errors.
