We also construct a subtree of $G$ with critical site percolation probability $\sqrt{2}-1$. We prove a general stability theorem for infinite connected locally finite graphs $G\subseteq H$ on the same vertex set. Suppose that, at parameter $a\in(0,1)$, the probability that a deterministic finite set meets an infinite open cluster in $G$ tends uniformly to one as its size grows. Then, for each fixed $b\in(a,1]$, under the standard monotone coupling, almost surely every infinite open cluster in $H$ at parameter $b$ contains an infinite open cluster in $G$ at parameter $a$. No planarity, transitivity, or uniform degree bound is required. Finally, we obtain a lower bound on two-point connectivity under uniqueness for arbitrary infinite locally finite graphs, yielding a general criterion for nonuniqueness.

papers.title: The Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function
papers.abstract: We use an elementary arithmetic argument, going back to Blom and Fr{ö}berg, to obtain upper and lower bounds for the denumerant function of Sylvester for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$. The bounds hold along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$, share the leading term of the denumerant, and yield its asymptotic behaviour with an explicit error term; for large $n$ and under a mild condition, a polynomial refinement of the lower bound improves on the lower bound of Agnarsson.

papers.title: Embeddings of $k$-complexes in $2k$-manifolds and minimum rank of partial symmetric matrices
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a $k$-dimensional simplicial complex having $n$ faces of dimension $k$, and $M$ a closed $(k-1)$-connected PL $2k$-dimensional manifold. We prove that for $k\ge3$ odd $K$ embeds into $M$ if and only if there are $\bullet$ a skew-symmetric $n\times n$-matrix $A$ with integer entries, whose rank over $\mathbb Q$ does not exceed $rk H_k(M;\mathbb Z)$, $\bullet$ a general position PL map $f:K\to\mathbb R^{2k}$, and $\bullet$ orientations on $k$-faces of $K$ \newline such that for any nonadjacent $k$-faces $σ,τ$ of $K$ the entry $A_{σ,τ}$ equals to the algebraic intersection of $fσ$ and $fτ$. We prove some analogues of this result (for any parity of $k$), including those for $\mathbb Z_2$- and $\mathbb Z$-embeddability. Our results generalize the Bikeev-Fulek-Kyn\v cl criteria for the $\mathbb Z_2$- and $\mathbb Z$-embeddability of graphs to surfaces, and are related to the Harris-Krushkal-Johnson-Paták-Tancer criteria for the embeddability of $k$-complexes into $2k$-manifolds. The main novelty of this paper is passing from the cohomology condition of Paták-Tancer to the simpler extendability of some intersection function to a low-rank matrix (defined in the paper using the idea of Fulek-Kyn\v cl).

papers.title: Uniqueness of the critical and supercritical Liouville quantum gravity metrics
papers.abstract: We show that for each ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$, there is a unique metric associated with Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) with matter central charge ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M}$. An earlier series of works by Ding-Dubédat-Dunlap-Falconet, Gwynne-Miller, and others showed that such a metric exists and is unique in the subcritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$, which corresponds to coupling constant $γ\in (0,2)$. The critical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} = 1$ corresponds to $γ=2$ and the supercritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (1,25)$ corresponds to $γ\in \mathbb C$ with $|γ| = 2$. Our metric is constructed as the limit of an approximation procedure called Liouville first passage percolation, which was previously shown to be tight for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$ by Ding and Gwynne (2020). In this paper, we show that the subsequential limit is uniquely characterized by a natural list of axioms. This extends the characterization of the LQG metric proven by Gwynne and Miller (2019) for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$ to the full parameter range $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,25)$. Our argument is substantially different from the proof of the characterization of the LQG metric for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$. In particular, the core part of the argument is simpler and does not use confluence of geodesics.

papers.title: Characterization of Fréchet Spaces and Application to Hausdorff MNC
papers.abstract: We study the Hausdorff measure of noncompactness associated with compatible metrics on Fréchet spaces, with the aim of extending its Banach-space properties. After recalling the characterization by complete translation-invariant metrics with convex balls, we calculate the scalar Hausdorff measure for a standard weighted fractional metric. For bounded nonprecompact sets its value is the unique root of an equation involving a finite seminorm gauge determined by the covering radius. This yields an actual Hausdorff-condensing criterion for compact perturbations of maps having separate contraction constants at the seminorm levels. On countable products of Banach spaces we obtain an exact coordinate formula and a sharp scalar contraction bound on bounded domains, without requiring a uniform gap between the coordinate constants and one for strict condensation. For closed subspaces, an exact finite-projection formula retains the compatibility constraints on covering centers. Explicit examples show why separately computed seminorm measures cannot generally be substituted into the metric formula. Applications to spaces of real sequence-valued continuous functions give an explicit oscillation formula and exhibit the compatibility obstruction on an unbounded interval. Classical fixed-point consequences are recorded briefly.

papers.title: Some ordering properties of highest and lowest order statistics with exponentiated Gumble type-II distributed components
papers.abstract: This paper studies stochastic comparisons of the highest and lowest order statistics arising from independent Exponentiated Gumbel Type-II distributed random variables. First, using vector majorization, we establish a comprehensive set of stochastic orderings for the lowest and highest order statistics with respect to the outer and inner shape parameters. In particular, for the lowest order statistic, we derive results on the usual stochastic order and likelihood ratio order, which further imply failure rate, mean residual life, and increasing convex orderings. Second, we show that the lowest order statistics satisfy a proportional failure rate structure. In addition, we also establish star and dispersive orderings. For the highest order statistic, we obtain results in the reversed failure rate order, and we show that, in general, a proportional failure rate structure does not hold. Moreover, unlike several classical exponentiated models, the highest order statistics are not necessarily comparable in the usual stochastic order under heterogeneity of the inner shape parameters. Finally, we extend the analysis using multivariate chain majorization to study the effect of simultaneous variation in scale and outer shape parameters. Under this framework, we establish usual stochastic ordering results for both the lowest and highest order statistics. It provides more general reliability comparisons under joint parameter heterogeneity.

papers.title: Scl in graphs of groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a group acting on a tree with cyclic edge and vertex stabilizers. Then stable commutator length (scl) is rational in G. Furthermore, scl varies predictably and converges to rational limits in so-called "surgery" families. This is a homological analog of the phenomenon of geometric convergence in hyperbolic Dehn surgery.

papers.title: Dense semigroups of triangular matrices
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ be the semigroup of $n\times n$ lower triangular matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$. We show that $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ has dense subsemigroups generated by $n+1$ matrices, and that $n+1$ is the least possible number of generators; the same holds for dense subgroups of the group of invertible lower triangular matrices. The generators can be written down explicitly: $n$ of them are diagonal and one is a diagonal matrix plus a nilpotent perturbation. More precisely, let $D_0,\dots,D_m$ be diagonal matrices generating a dense subsemigroup of the diagonal matrices, where the diagonal entries of $D_0$ have strictly monotone moduli, and let $A$ be a lower triangular matrix with the same diagonal as $D_0$. We prove that the semigroup generated by $A,D_1,\dots,D_m$ is dense in $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ if and only if every subdiagonal entry of $A$ is nonzero.

papers.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
papers.abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.

papers.title: Maximally transitive semigroups of $n\times n$ matrices (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that for every $n\ge 1$ there is a pair of $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$ that generates a dense subsemigroup of the space $M_n(\mathbb{K})$ of all $n\times n$ matrices. Since the powers of a single matrix are never dense, two generators is optimal. Equivalently, there is a $2$-generator semigroup of linear maps whose action on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^n$ is topologically transitive, whereas no semigroup of linear maps acts topologically transitively on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^{n+1}$. In fact, for such a semigroup every orbit closure in $(\mathbb{K}^n)^k$, for every $k\ge1$, is as large as linear algebra allows. Along the way we give a short self-contained proof of the density of explicit $2$-generator subsemigroups of $GL_2^+(\mathbb{R})$ and of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$, based on a simple criterion for closed subsemigroups of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$.

papers.title: Dense 2-generator subsemigroups of $2\times 2$ matrices (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: We show that the semigroup of real linear fractional transformations of a proper subinterval of the real line does not contain a dense subsemigroup generated by two elements, while it does contain dense subsemigroups generated by three elements. For the semigroup generated by the two maps $x\mapsto 1+a/x$ and $x\mapsto x/b$ (the only pair not excluded by elementary arguments) we compute the closure exactly, and we describe all of its orbit closures in the plane. Consequently the semigroup of $2\times2$ matrices with nonnegative entries has no dense $2$-generator subsemigroup but has dense $3$-generator ones. In contrast, we prove a general density criterion for subsemigroups of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ generated by three explicit matrices, and use a word identity of length seven to produce, for both $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$, uncountable families of pairs of matrices that generate dense subsemigroups; a fully explicit rational example is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1/2\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\0&-8/3\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus the minimal number of generators of a dense subsemigroup is $3$ for the nonnegative cone and $2$ for $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: A Collatz-type conjecture on the set of rational numbers (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: Let $θ(x)=(x-1)/3$ if $x\ge1$ and $θ(x)=2x/(1-x)$ if $0\le x<1$. We conjecture that the $θ$-orbit of every nonnegative rational number ends in $0$. A weaker conjecture asserts that no map in the semigroup generated by $3x+1$ and $x/(x+2)$, other than the generators' powers, has a positive rational fixed point; equivalently, the only matrices in the semigroup generated by $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}3&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with an integer eigenvalue are their pure powers. We prove sharp two-sided bounds for the smallest eigenvalue of every word in the more general semigroups attached to the maps $\varphi_{a,b}$, which explain why the pair $\{2,3\}$ is distinguished: it is the only pair with $(a-1)(b-1)=2$. Combining these bounds with congruences for the trace, we determine the possible integer eigenvalues of words, and we prove that $θ$ has no rational $1$-circuits, no rational $2$-circuits and no even rational circuits. We show that, for each $k$, a random $k$-syllable word with exponents at most $M$ has an integer eigenvalue with probability at most $2k(k+\log_2 2k)/M$. Finally, we verify by computer that $θ$ has no positive rational cycle of length at most $36$.

papers.title: Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits (revised version)
papers.abstract: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every $n\ge 1$ we construct two $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the orbit of every vector $p\in\mathbb{K}^n$ with $p_1\ne 0$ under the semigroup generated by $A$ and $B$ is dense in $\mathbb{K}^n$; the remaining vectors lie in an invariant hyperplane, so the set of vectors with dense orbit is exactly the complement of a hyperplane. Thus two generators always suffice for a hypercyclic semigroup of matrices, in contrast with the commutative case, where $n+1$ generators are needed on $\mathbb{C}^n$. We give a transparent reformulation of the hypotheses, a criterion for the density of $\{a^mb^n\}$ that makes them checkable, and explicit examples with complete proofs. As applications we obtain affine pairs on $\mathbb{K}^n$ all of whose orbits are dense, and, for every $n$, a pair of real matrices with an orbit that is somewhere dense but not dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Constructive algebraic methods for bisymmetric means
papers.abstract: We prove continuity for reflexive, bisymmetric binary operations that are strictly increasing in each variable, under certain algebraic conditions. In fact, for some algebraic weights we construct a weighted quasi-arithmetic representation of such functions without assuming continuity. An elementary construction gives the case $r=2/3$. More generally, a word equality whose polynomial difference has a unique simple zero $r\in(0,1)$ forces the representation with weight $r$; every algebraic $r$ with no other conjugate in $(0,1)$ arises this way. The proof uses an affine embedding and a dense-domain extension argument.

papers.title: Nonconstant Congruence Speeds of Integer Tetration in Non-Squarefree Radices
papers.abstract: We further develop the theory of congruence speed for integer tetration in non-squarefree numeral systems, building on Appendix B of [M. Ripà and G. Di Pietro (2026), A compact notation for peculiar properties characterizing integer tetration, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics, 32(3), 477-496]. For bases coprime to the radix, we establish an eventual floor-difference representation and determine the exact spectrum of attainable least periods. We construct explicit arithmetic progressions containing infinitely many prime bases with nonconstant congruence speed for every non-squarefree radix, thereby proving the coprime-infinitude conjecture posed in Appendix B. We also derive a uniform quadratic bound for the least coprime base with nonconstant congruence speed and establish exact natural densities of nonstabilizing bases, both among integers coprime to the radix and among those not divisible by its radical, together with the corresponding relative density among primes. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the perfect-power congruence-speed identity (Equation (2.12) of the cited paper) to hold in arbitrary radices, determine the exact least eventual period when stabilization fails, and establish a separate criterion for the boundary case of the original parameter restriction.

papers.title: Excluding 54 of the 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
papers.abstract: Let $P_{a,b,u}(t)$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$12$ third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over $\mathbb{Q}$. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by $t\mapsto-t$. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over $\mathbb{Q}_2$, using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from $\mathbb{Q}_2(i)$. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly $22$ of the $76$ nontrivial partitions of $12$, thereby excluding $54$ complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, $37$ follow from evenness alone and $17$ from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.

papers.title: Topological and measurewise amenability for locally compact groupoids
papers.abstract: We prove the equivalence of topological and measurewise amenability for $σ$-compact locally compact groupoids with a Hausdorff unit space and a continuous Haar system. This in particular includes the second countable locally compact Hausdorff case. Our proof averages arbitrary Radon probability measures along strictly positive densities to obtain quasi-invariant measures. We overcome the lack of absolute continuity of the original measure with respect to its quasi-invariant substitute by also averaging the Reiter functions along the same density.

papers.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension six
papers.abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of six-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Instead of solving the overdetermined Jacobi system of 120 quadratic equations on 90 structure constants modulo $\mathrm{GL}(6,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses the Levi--Malcev decomposition, Mostow's nilradical constraints, and the Skjelbred--Sund cohomological central extension technique. In the semisimple sector, the four real forms of $A_1\oplus A_1$ are classified by Killing signature invariants, with explicit matrix representatives for $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})_{\mathbb{R}}\cong\mathfrak{so}(3,1)$. For non-solvable algebras with three-dimensional radical, representation-theoretic rigidity shows that $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ cannot couple indecomposably with non-abelian radicals, yielding exactly three indecomposable classes governed by $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$. In the solvable category, Mostow's theorem restricts the nilradical dimension to $\{3,4,5,6\}$. The nilpotent sector in dimension six has twenty-four indecomposable isomorphism classes plus decomposable counterparts. Solvable non-nilpotent algebras are classified by nilradical codimension, with explicit real Jordan matrix representations for codimension one and two that resolve continuous moduli under gauge actions. The work also computes the minimal faithful representation dimension $μ(\mathfrak{g})$ under Ado's theorem, relates the classification to invariant complex structures on nilmanifolds, and provides a deterministic, page-breakable identification algorithm.

papers.title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
papers.abstract: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. Consequently these maps are independent of the handle decomposition and of the Heegaard data, and form a functor isomorphic to framed instanton homology; where both are defined, our isomorphisms agree with those of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy modulo two. The proof rests on two analytic results for the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation: an adiabatic limit in which a compression body collapses next to a holomorphic strip and becomes the Lagrangian boundary condition of its flat connections, and an excision theorem along a torus.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction. We also prove NP-completeness on chordal bipartite graphs for every fixed palette size $k\ge4$. For strongly chordal graphs, reverse simple elimination gives a constructive upper bound of one more than the clique number. We obtain exact polynomial-time algorithms under several conditions on the maximum cliques, including when they induce a connected subtree of a clique tree. For strictly chordal graphs we characterize the optimum and construct an optimal coloring in $O(n+m)$ time, where $n$ and $m$ count the vertices and edges. For strongly chordal graphs with clique-tree separators of size at most $s$, we give an exact algorithm in $n^{2^{O(s+1)}}$ time, with no bound on the clique number.

papers.title: Local cohomology over Steenrod algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q = p^s$ elements. Let $S = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} S_n$ be a non-negatively graded commutative, Noetherian $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra. Assume $S$ has a structure of an unstable Steenrod algebra. Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded unstable $S$-module. Let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal in $S$. We prove that for $i \geq 0$ the local cohomology modules $H^i_I(M)$ has a structure of a Cartan $S$-module. As application we give a direct and considerably simpler proof of D. Bourguiba and S. Zarati's generalization of Landweber-Stong conjecture. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for $S$ to have $S_r$-property of Serre in terms of Dickson polynomials.

papers.title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
papers.abstract: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero. In the two minimal nonempty cases, we show an embedding of an exterior algebra into the cohomology ring, and prove containment of the binary octahedral and binary icosahedral groups, respectively, in its fundamental group.

papers.title: $s$-quasi-transitive weakly distance-regular digraphs
papers.abstract: A digraph is $s$-quasi-transitive if, for every path $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of length $s$, either $(x_0,x_s)\in AΓ$ or $(x_s,x_0)\in AΓ$ (or both). In this paper, we give a characterization of $s$-quasi-transitive commutative weakly distance-regular digraphs, where $s=4$, or $s\geq 5$ and the cycle polar diameter is at least $s$.

papers.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
papers.abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4π^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

papers.title: Exact penalties for maximum-edge bicliques in bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Given a bipartite graph $G$, we denote by $g(G)$ the largest product $|A||B|$ over pairs of vertex sets $A$ and $B$, one on each side, with no edge between them. These pairs are the bicliques of the bipartite complement of $G$; hence, computing $g(G)$ is the maximum-edge biclique problem, which is NP-hard, as shown by Peeters in 2003. Gillis and Glineur characterized it by a continuous quadratic program, in which a large enough penalty on the edges of $G$ makes the global maximizers correspond to the maximum pairs and the local maximizers to the maximal ones. We propose a new threshold for the penalty, which depends only on $g(G)$. For any penalty at or above it, the global maximizers correspond exactly to the maximum pairs, and every local maximizer with positive value corresponds to a maximal pair. This threshold is never larger than theirs and is sharp up to an additive $1/2$. Spectral and semidefinite bounds give computable penalties; in experiments, a simple local ascent succeeds far more often with the semidefinite one than with the earlier thresholds, although on our graphs that bound already reveals $g(G)$. The penalty formulation, whose optimal value is $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, is also a copositive formulation of $g(G)$. Strengthening a semidefinite bound of Laurent, Polak and Vargas with the completely positive cone gives exactly $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, while the doubly nonnegative strengthening is already inexact on six vertices. Finally, Pólya's linear programming approximations of the copositive cone become finite at an explicit level and converge to $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$ without ever being exact.

papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by García-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

papers.title: Extending a property of vector spaces to abelian groups
papers.abstract: In this note, we determine the finite abelian groups $G$ such that for every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exists an automorphism $f\in{\rm Aut}(G)$ with ${\rm Fix}(f)=H$. This provides a partial answer to a problem posed by Deaconescu and Walls. Two generalizations of this problem are also proposed.

papers.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
papers.abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates among observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a data-driven threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule allows lower thresholds to retain more observations for testing while limiting size distortions, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

papers.title: A Complete Equational Theory for Quantum Circuits with Generalized Control
papers.abstract: Controlled subcircuits are commonplace in quantum algorithms as they represent the quantum analogue of branching statements (if then). We introduce a generalization of controlled subcircuits in the form of a binary operation which sends pairs of unitary quantum circuits to a generalized controlled operation, whose semantics are based on matrix exponentials and logarithms. The family of quantum circuits with generalized controlled operations and circuit exponentiation is denoted HQC for Hierarchical Quantum Circuits. We formalize HQC as a modified prop category using a novel category-theoretic construction, and provide a sound and complete equational theory for diagrammatic reasoning in HQC.

papers.title: On Packed Passenger Permutations
papers.abstract: An occupied seat in a binary row is called packed if both of its immediate neighbors are occupied. We give a self-contained combinatorial account of this statistic, equivalently the number of overlapping occurrences of 111. An occupied-block decomposition yields a coefficient formula at fixed occupancy and a direct proof of the sharp minimum max{0,3m-2n-2} for m passengers in n seats, including arrangements attaining the bound. The same decomposition gives a rational generating function, recurrences, expectations, and avoidance asymptotics. Full rows, in which every empty seat would become packed upon being filled, are related to independent sets of a path. A neighborhood-union expansion also gives exact counts on rectangular grids. The emphasis is a unified elementary presentation and explicit extremal constructions, rather than a new general enumeration method.

papers.title: Local Homological Mirror Symmetry
papers.abstract: Local mirror symmetry, originated from the work of Chiang-Klemm-Yau-Zaslow arXiv:9903053, indicated a potential relation between mirrors to a vector bundle and mirrors to its zero section. In this paper, we constructed a homological mirror to these local varieties and proved the corresponding Homological Mirror Symmetry statement. As an application, we constructed infinite families of exotic Weinstein sectors as mirrors to Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: Multiplicity and least energy sign-changing normalized solutions for a Kirchhoff equation on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sign-changing normalized solutions of the Kirchhoff problem \[ \begin{cases} -\left(a+b\displaystyle\int_Ω|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)Δu =|u|^{p-2}u+μu &\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0 &\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \] subject to the constraint \[ \int_Ω|u|^2\,dx=c, \] where $a,b>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth bounded connected domain, $1\le N\le3$, $c>0$ is prescribed, and $μ\in\mathbb R$ is a Lagrange multiplier. We assume $2<p<\infty$ for $N=1,2$ and $2<p\le6$ for $N=3$. For every integer $k\ge1$, we obtain at least $k$ distinct pairs of sign-changing normalized solutions for sufficiently small $c>0$. We determine the small mass asymptotics of their energies, Lagrange multipliers, and rescaled profiles in terms of the distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues and their eigenspaces. When $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$, we obtain infinitely many such pairs for every prescribed mass $c>0$, with energies tending to $+\infty$. At $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$, this conclusion holds for every sufficiently small fixed mass. We also establish the existence of a least energy sign-changing normalized solution on general bounded domains for every prescribed mass when $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$. For sufficiently small mass, such a solution exists on general bounded domains when $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$ and on star-shaped domains when $p>2+\frac{8}{N}$. For any family of such least energy solutions, the rescaled profiles approach the $L^2$-unit sphere of the second Dirichlet eigenspace in $H_0^1(Ω)$ as $c\to0^+$. The finite multiplicity and least energy results include the Sobolev critical case $N=3$, $p=6$. The proofs combine a localized symmetric minimax construction, energy comparisons with one-signed critical points, and compactness arguments that preserve the sign-changing property.

papers.title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
papers.abstract: In the random Lorentz gas, a point tracer moves through spherical obstacles of (reduced) density $Φ$ centered on a Poisson point process in $d$-dimensional space, $\mathbb{R}^d$, and becomes localized once the vacant space stops percolating, at $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$. The dimensional scaling of this void percolation threshold has remained elusive. Prior bounds, conjectural ones included, ranged from $Ω(1)$ to $O(d\ln d)$, leaving even the scaling undetermined. We here prove that $Φ_{\rm p}(d)=Θ(d)$, and in particular that $\tfrac12\,d \le Φ_{\rm p}(d) \le 5\,d$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The upper bound counts hierarchical families of escape waypoints called tree embeddings; the lower bound is via a weighted second-moment estimate on an explicit ensemble of ballistic escape routes. A linear scaling of $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$ excludes the $d\ln d$ growth suggested by analogy with other systems in the random first-order transition universality class and is consistent with the numerical estimate $Φ_{\rm p}/d \to 3.40(5)$. Because the mean-field dynamical transition is likewise linear, $Φ_{\rm d}\simeq 2.40\,d$, our result fixes the activated window $[Φ_{\rm d},Φ_{\rm p}]$ as a bounded---rather than diverging---correction to mean-field dynamical arrest in sufficiently high $d$.

papers.title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
papers.abstract: We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<α<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $σ\partial_xF\ge0$, $σQ\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α/2}$. In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-α/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-α/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of Bénilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α})$. This bound takes the place of the Oleĭnik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-α/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.

papers.title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
papers.abstract: Stopping games are the multiplayer generalization of optimal stopping problems, in which each player independently chooses when to stop, and the payoff depends on who stops first and when. While the existence of $\varepsilon$-equilibria in two-player stopping games with integrable payoffs is known, the multiplayer case has remained open. We prove that every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium for every $\varepsilon > 0$, provided the filtration is conditionally atomless. This condition is satisfied, in particular, when the underlying probability space is $\{0,1\}^{\dN}$ endowed with the uniform measure and its natural filtration. Our method also shows that every three-player stopping game, without the restriction to conditionally atomless filtration, admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, for every $\varepsilon > 0$. The proof combines techniques developed for two-player stopping games and for multiplayer quitting games, with a key new insight: the richness encoded in a conditionally atomless filtration can substitute for an external public randomization device, allowing players to coordinate without an explicit coordination signal.

papers.title: On Amoebas and the Arithmetic Rigidity of the Mahler Measure
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric rigidity theory for Mahler measure based on the global structure of Ronkin functions and amoebas. Our starting point is the theorem of Ronkin describing the affine linearity of the Ronkin function on the complement of the amoeba and the identification of its gradients with lattice points of the Newton polytope. Combining this deep analytic input with convex duality and toric geometry, we show that the vanishing of the Mahler measure is an extremal phenomenon: it occurs if and only if the Ronkin function collapses to the piecewise linear support function of the Newton polytope. This collapse forces a degeneration of the amoeba onto the $(n\!-\!1)$-skeleton of a toric fan and implies that the zero locus of the polynomial is contained in a translate of a codimension-one subtorus. As a first application of this rigidity principle, we recover the generalized Kronecker theorem characterizing Laurent polynomials of vanishing Mahler measure. Our approach bypasses the classical Boyd--Lawton limit formulas and replaces analytic projection arguments by a global convex-geometric and potential-theoretic mechanism rooted in the geometry of amoebas.

papers.title: On a Dual Heterotic Kodaira-Spencer Theory
papers.abstract: We consider a dual version of heterotic Kodaira-Spencer theory on a Calabi-Yau three-fold $X$ with background fluxes, related to the type I BCOV theory of Costello-Li. We implement the Green-Schwarz mechanism of Costello-Li, where the Beltrami differential plays the role of the Green-Schwarz field. On a compact Calabi-Yau three-fold with background gauge fluxes $F$, where $\mathrm{tr}(F^2)$ is trivial in cohomology, retaining gauge anomalies only and leaving gravitational anomalies to future work, we incorporate the Costello-Li Green-Schwarz mechanism into the classical deformation complex. This gives a theory governed by a nilpotent operator $\bar D$ on $Q=T^{1,0}X\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)\oplus T^{*1,0}X$, whose extension maps carry holomorphic derivatives, so that $(Q,\bar D)$ is not a holomorphic bundle. Using diagonal $\bar\partial^\dagger$-gauge, the one-loop gauge anomaly cancels, assuming that the extension maps of $\bar D$ do not modify it, which we argue is plausible. Introducing an auxiliary $(0,2)$-form, we construct a cubic interacting theory whose gauge symmetries are governed by an $L_3$ algebra. On compact Calabi-Yau three-folds, and for sufficiently small fields, we show that the equation of motion is equivalent to the Maurer-Cartan equation, together with a divergence-free constraint on the Beltrami differential. Finally we trivialise $\bar D$ locally to the Dolbeault operator. The (non-tensorial) transition maps glue into a quasi-holomorphic extension sheaf $\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}}$, for which we prove a Dolbeault theorem, $H^{0,q}_{\bar D}(Q)\cong\check H^q(\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}})$.

papers.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers II. Rational Maps
papers.abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked which analytic functions map the set $\mathscr L$ of Liouville numbers into itself. In the first paper of this series, we proved that every real-analytic solution on an open interval is the restriction of a real rational function. We now identify a canonical subfield $\mathbb L$ of $\mathbb R$ such that, for every nonconstant $R\in\mathbb R(X)$ and every nonempty open interval $I$ in its domain, $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathscr L$ if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$ and $R^{-1}(\mathbb Q)\cap I\cap\mathscr L=\varnothing$. The weaker inclusion $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathbb Q\cup\mathscr L$ holds if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$. If $R$ is not defined over $\mathbb L$, every such interval contains a Cantor set of Liouville numbers whose images under $R$ are irrational and have irrationality exponents bounded by a constant depending only on $R$. We also construct continuum many positive strong Liouville numbers $σ$ for which $σX^m$ preserves $\mathscr L$ for every $m\geq2$, with all nonzero rational fibers consisting of $U_m$-numbers.

papers.title: Noncommutative weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity over locally compact quantum groups
papers.abstract: We study weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity for Hopf-von Neumann algebras and locally compact quantum groups. For a Hopf-von Neumann algebra $(M,Γ)$, we introduce the space ${\rm WAP}_{{\rm Bessel},π_u}(M_*)$ through norm convergence conditions on rows and columns of slices associated with Bessel families in the universal representation. We prove that this space is the largest $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm WAP}(M_*)$ when separately continuous lift of the co-multiplication is multiplicative, and that the two spaces coincide when $M$ is commutative. Furthermore, the algebra $\{x\in C_b(\mathbb{G}): Γ(x)\in M(C_0(\mathbb{G})\otimes C_b(\mathbb{G}))\}$ is characterized as the greatest left introverted $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ satisfying a left Bessel condition on $L^2(\mathbb{G})$. We also show that ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ is a $C^*$-algebra whenever the center of $C_0(\mathbb{G})$ contains an element on which the bounded counit is non-zero.

papers.title: Orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We study the inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+Δu+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\R\times\R^N,\quad N\ge2. \] For every initial datum in $H^1(\R^N)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. We also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated Nehari minimization problem. For $ω\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{N-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+ω})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+ω})|x|}, \] whereas for $ω<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. Finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $ω>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<ω<-1+(N-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.

papers.title: Distributed Geometric Optimization and Control of Rigid Differential-Drive Formations from Relative-Position Measurements
papers.abstract: Distance based formation control fixes the shape of a robot team but leaves its position and orientation unconstrained. We regulate all three for differential drive robots that have only one absolute position anchor, absolute headings, body frame relative position measurements, and communication with their neighbors. We derive a two layer estimation control scheme directly from optimization. The first half of the result is a set of graph-proximal estimators that reconstruct the centroid, the anchor vector, and the centered coordinates. Exact proximal updates reach consensus in finitely many steps, and a finite number of primal dual iterations leaves a bounded reconstruction error. The controller combines proximal centroid and orientation steps with distance gradient shape regulation, and a finite rotation removes the orientation drift caused by the shape step. A discrete Lyapunov analysis gives local exponential convergence once the estimators have converged. We validate the method in ROS 2 Gazebo and in experiments with five physical robots.

papers.title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters
papers.abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. Classical approaches fail along three distinct axes: Kalman-based methods assume Gaussian posteriors and produce biased estimates under nonlinear observation operators; particle-based methods represent distributions with weighted samples and collapse in high dimensions due to the curse of dimensionality; and kernel-based methods move beyond discrete particle representations but cannot maintain their density approximation affordably as dimension grows. The Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) avoids all three constraints by encoding the filtering density in a score function and approximating that score with a training-free Monte Carlo estimator, enabling stable filtering in high-dimensional, chaotic systems. This survey traces EnSF's mathematical foundations, establishes it as the state of the art for non-Gaussian, high-dimensional filtering, and examines fourteen extensions that expand its operational reach. Twelve of the fourteen extensions preserve this training-free Monte Carlo estimator at the core of the update, with only two departing from it to achieve planetary-scale deployment.

papers.title: A Christov Integrating Factor Method for Approximating Rational PDE Solutions
papers.abstract: Rational solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) are notoriously difficult to approximate via spectral Fourier methods due to their algebraically slow decay rate. In this work we discuss approximating rational PDE solutions in a basis of orthogonal functions known as the Christov functions, allowing for the computation of its spectrum via the fast Fourier transform. An explicit fourth-order integrating factor method is derived. The effectiveness of the method is tested on several nonlinear PDEs. Relative to a straightforward pseudo-spectral approximation, the integrating factor method supports larger regions of stability resulting in a more efficient scheme.

papers.title: On Submanifolds with constant Möbius Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: In the Möbius geometry of submanifolds there exists an important Möbius invariant tensor called the Möbius metric which together with the Möbius second fundamental form, the Blaschke tensor and the Möbius form constitute a complete system of conformal invariants for umbilic-free submanifolds when the dimension $n \geq 3$. An umbilic-free immersion $f:M^{n}\to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is said to have constant Möbius Ricci curvature if its Möbius metric has constant Ricci curvature. In this paper, we classify umbilic-free immersions $f:M^{n}\to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ with constant Möbius Ricci curvature, flat normal bundle and two distinct principal normal vector fields. We prove that a submanifold with constant Möbius Ricci curvature and flat normal bundle has closed Möbius form, and then we classify such submanifolds provided the Möbius form vanishes identically on $M^{n}$.

papers.title: Isospectral Deformations of Diagonal Matrices by Symmetric Matrices in Dimension Four
papers.abstract: For a diagonal matrix $D$ with distinct diagonal entries in an algebraically closed field $K$ we study the symmetric matrices $Q$ with entries in $K$ such that the affine line $D+tQ$ has the same eigenvalues in $K$ as $D$. We study the equality of characteristic polynomials, $χ_{D+tQ}(x)=χ_D(x) \text{ for all }\: t\in K$ and examine the resulting system of equations. For generic diagonal matrices of size at most $4$ we show that only the trivial symmetric matrix $Q=0$ satisfies this isospectral condition. We use this result to compute the degree of a field extension that appears in the invariant theory of quadratic forms under congruence action.

papers.title: An improved bound for the intersection of two longest cycles in $k$-connected graphs
papers.abstract: A conjecture attributed to Smith states that in every $k$-connected graph, every pair of longest cycles intersects in at least $k$ vertices. We prove that every two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph on $n$ vertices intersect in at least $\min\{k,10k-n-30\}$ vertices. Consequently, Smith's conjecture holds whenever $k\ge \frac{n+30}{9}$. This improves the previous bound of $\frac{n+16}{7}$ for $n>33$ and also implies a bound of $\frac{n+22}{9}$ for paths instead of cycles.

papers.title: Metallic Circles: Concyclic Tangency Points of Ford Circles over $k$-Fibonacci Quotients
papers.abstract: Extending a result of Kocik, we show that the tangency points of the Ford circles built over quotients of $k$-Fibonacci numbers are concyclic: they lie on a circle centred on the horizontal axis, of radius $\sqrt{k^2+4}/2$, meeting it at the reciprocal of the metallic ratio $σ_k$ and at $-σ_k$. Concyclicity turns out to be a quadratic identity of the sequence read in coordinates. In the Poincaré half-plane, this circle is a geodesic along which the tangency points advance with constant step $2\lnσ_k$.

papers.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $Λ$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $Λ$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

papers.title: Improving the accuracy of the momentum-exchange method in lattice Boltzmann methods
papers.abstract: In the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), the momentum-exchange method (MEM) is widely used to evaluate hydrodynamic forces at fluid-solid interfaces due to its computational efficiency and geometric flexibility. However, when mapping complex geometries onto structured Cartesian grids, the physical boundary rarely intersects the lattice links exactly at their midpoints. This discrepancy violates an implicit assumption inherent to the conventional momentum-exchange (CME) formulation. In this study, we systematically analyze this geometric deficiency and demonstrate that it induces significant force inaccuracies, even in elementary flows where the solid boundary deviates from the midway position. To resolve this, we propose a modified momentum-exchange (MME) method that explicitly accounts for the exact boundary location along the lattice links, demonstrating enhanced accuracy for both flat and curved geometries. Furthermore, we address another critical issue with the interpolation-supplemented bounce-back (ISBB) schemes, and that is their inherent violation of local mass conservation. This mass leakage induces unphysical pressure buildup in the system, which compromises the accuracy and stability of the LBM. We propose a mass-conservative remedy for ISBB schemes that eliminates this leakage. Through a series of benchmark simulations of increasing complexity, we demonstrate that combining the proposed MME with the mass-corrected ISBB scheme drastically improves the fidelity of hydrodynamic force evaluations, establishing a robust framework essential for moving boundary problems and fluid-structure interactions.

papers.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
papers.abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $ζ(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $Δ_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $κ_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $κ_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-χr$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $χ$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $κ$.

papers.title: Perfect Partitions of Regular Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $I_{n,n}$ be a fixed perfect matching of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, and let $L_{n,1}=K_{n,n}-I_{n,n}$. A perfect set of $L_{n,1}$ is a $1$-factorization of $L_{n,1}$, that is, a set of $n-1$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings whose union is $E(L_{n,1})$; a perfect partition of $L_{n,1}$ is a partition of the set of all perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ into perfect sets. Brualdi, Chiang, and Li (2005) asked whether $L_{n,1}$ admits a perfect partition. Identifying both sides of the bipartition with $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots ,n\}$, the perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ are exactly the derangements of $[n]$, the perfect sets correspond bijectively to the reduced Latin squares of order $n$, and the perfect partitions are exactly the perfect matchings of the $(n-1)$-uniform hypergraph whose vertices are the derangements of $[n]$ and whose edges are the perfect sets. We first give, for every $n$, a constructive lower bound on the maximum number of pairwise disjoint perfect sets of $L_{n,1}$. We then show that $L_{5,1}$ has exactly $42$ distinct perfect partitions and that $L_{6,1}$ has at least $82$ distinct perfect partitions; these are the first examples demonstrating that perfect partitions need not be unique. Finally, we exhibit two distinct perfect partitions of $L_{7,1}$, resolving the $n=7$ open problem raised by Brualdi et al.

papers.title: An improved lower bound for maximal partial Room squares
papers.abstract: We establish a new asymptotic lower bound for the volume of a maximal partial Room square of even order $n$. We prove that its volume is at least $\frac{2\sqrt{66}-6}{57}n^2-O(n)$, improving the leading coefficient $1/8$ in the lower bound obtained by Meszka and Rosa. The proof combines two counting arguments, one based on a transversal of empty cells and the other on the graph of occurring symbol pairs.

papers.title: Practical Semialgebraic Optimization via Sparse Sample-Based Sum-of-Squares Programming
papers.abstract: As the importance of semialgebraic optimization grows in engineering, so does the need for scalable sum-of-squares (SOS) methods. Their convex relaxations can guide mixed-integer search and often deliver certified global optima outright. Scaling traditional SOS typically requires hand-crafted bases and redundant constraints, whereas sample-based SOS numerically exploits feasible set geometry to reduce bases and build smaller, often tighter relaxations from black-box evaluations. However, discrete variables can require exponentially many samples, and each sampled equation couples all cliques, destroying correlative sparsity. In this work, we avoid enumeration and slack variables by sampling a tractable variety that contains the feasible set, with multipliers only for the omitted constraints. To recover sparsity, we introduce "separator" polynomials that split the sampled equations into local systems coupled only on clique overlaps. This yields a novel, convergent hierarchy of semidefinite programs (SDPs) with block sizes and sample requirements governed by local interactions rather than total problem size. Lastly, we show how to verify sample sufficiency and prune redundant equations numerically before solving. In robust estimation and motion planning, we obtain certifiably small optimality gaps at scales far beyond those reported for traditional sparse SOS. For example, we solve a truncated least-squares 3D registration problem with 1600 candidate correspondences in under 49 seconds using an off-the-shelf SDP solver on a laptop CPU.

papers.title: A physics-based adaptive low-rank method for 6D Vlasov simulations
papers.abstract: The numerical simulation of kinetic plasma models in six-dimensional phase space poses significant computational and memory challenges, particularly when considering modern high-performance computing architectures. In this work, we propose an adaptive dynamical low-rank approach for the efficient solution of the 6D Vlasov--Poisson system. Our strategy is an extension of the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator. The algorithm changes the rank based on physical observables (e.g., the electric field and energy) as opposed to controlling the error in the distribution function. Our approach is memory efficient in the sense that only rank $r$ objects are required to implement the scheme. This makes the algorithm suitable for performing high-dimensional computations on graphic processing units. Comparisons with rank adaptive Basis-Update & Galerkin integrators exhibit both significant memory savings and reduction in run time. We show, by presenting a variety of 6D benchmark experiments implemented in the C++/CUDA low-rank framework Ensign, that our technique allows us to run simulations with a significantly smaller rank, while still preserving the physical fidelity. Thus, the approach substantially reduces memory footprint and computational cost and enables simulations that are prohibitively expensive for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.

papers.title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
papers.abstract: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution. Instead, it reduces the spectral lower bound to a central limit theorem for the trace of the transition matrix at powers much larger than the logarithmic scale, a range that previous results failed to reach. Both the general strategy and the central limit theorem might be of independent interest.

papers.title: An axiom of unique reflection
papers.abstract: We characterize neutral planes by three metric conditions: existence of geodesics, side-side-side congruence, and uniqueness of reflection.

papers.title: Non-Kähler Hyperbolicity: Surfaces and Codimension One
papers.abstract: We study hyperbolicity notions for compact complex manifolds defined by special Hermitian metrics and by holomorphic maps from $\mathbb C^{n-1}$ (divisorial hyperbolicity). For surfaces we show that divisorial and Brody hyperbolicity coincide and that Hermitian-symplectic and Kähler hyperbolicity coincide when $h^{2,0}=0$. In any dimension we prove obstructions to Gauduchon hyperbolicity, show that projective spaces are not divisorially hyperbolic, and give divisorially hyperbolic manifolds that are not balanced hyperbolic.

papers.title: Higher theta lifts via BGG resolutions
papers.abstract: We compute higher theta lifts of ladder representations of general linear groups over division algebras over non-archimedean local fields. We achieve this by constructing BGG-type coresolutions and proving that their terms are acyclic for the covariant theta functor. We then compute the resulting complex explicitly, determining the higher theta lifts and the degrees in which they are nonzero.

papers.title: The square function estimates for cones in arbitrary dimensions and elliptic quadrics
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the square function estimate for the light cone in $\R^d$, $d\ge3$, at the exponent $p=2(d-1)/(d-2)$, with loss $[\log(2R)]^{5/p}$ can be deduced from local-smoothing and auxiliary-energy statements in the October 25, 2026 OpenAI manuscript. Exact affine sections preserve these logarithmic bounds and give corresponding estimates for spheres, ellipsoids, elliptic paraboloids, and compact patches of two-sheet elliptic hyperboloids in $\R^{d-1}$.

papers.title: Seeking the dense half in $K_4$-free graphs
papers.abstract: We show that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a balanced bipartition such that neither part contains more than $0.0671n^2 + o(n^2)$ edges. This improves the previous best bound of $0.074n^2$ by Xu and Zhang. We also formulate a conjecture that the tight bound for this problem is $\frac{425}{6498}n^2 \approx 0.0654n^2$, and present a construction showing that it would be best possible.

papers.title: Ramification of Weighted Central Paths and Super-linear Interior-Point Methods for Semi-definite Optimization
papers.abstract: The local convergence of primal-dual interior-point methods for semi-definite optimization is closely tied to the regularity of the central path at its limiting point. Without strict complementarity, the central path can exhibit fractional power asymptotics and need not be differentiable in the ordinary barrier parameter. We show that this obstruction can be removed simultaneously for a family of weighted \AHO~central paths. More precisely, there exists a common ramification exponent $N$ such that all weighted paths in a fixed neighborhood of the identity become analytic at the limiting point after the reparametrization $μ\mapstoμ^N$. Using higher-order derivatives of these reparametrized paths, we construct a feasible $p$th-order predictor-corrector interior-point method. Under a uniform predictor regularity condition, and without assuming strict complementarity, we prove that the normalized complementarity gaps converge with $Q$-order at least $(p+1)/ρ$, where $ρ$ is the reparametrization exponent used by the method. We also establish super-linear convergence of the simultaneously vanishing primal-dual blocks, derive an explicit quantitative reduction bound throughout the predictor regularity region, and obtain a doubly logarithmic outer iteration bound once the iterates enter the local super-linear regime. Finally, we illustrate the predicted higher-order behavior on a collection of degenerate and non-degenerate semi-definite optimization problems.

papers.title: The odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$
papers.abstract: We introduce a class of interesting algebraic varieties --- odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k,2n+1)$ and study them with an emphasis on the case of the submaximal odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(n,2n+1)$, which we call catalecticant varieties. The main result of the paper is a construction of a full exceptional collection in the derived category of the catalecticant sixfold $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$.

papers.title: An Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom law for a kinematic model of turbulence
papers.abstract: We prove an Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom-type law for passive scalars advected by a family of random $C^α$ velocity field proposed in \cite{JDEMS} as a kinematic model of turbulent fluids. Up to a technical assumption on one parameter, the expectation of the squared $L^2_t H^γ_x$ norm of solutions to the passive scalar equation is bounded by the squared $L^2$ norm of the deterministic initial datum, uniformly in the viscosity, whenever $α+ 2γ< 1$. The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.

papers.title: Compatible Hamel Topologies, Real Valued Isomorphisms and Rational Scalar Continuity
papers.abstract: We study Hamel character topologies on the real line in two parts. Part I treats the full real-orbit (TVG) and the rational-parameter (TVGQ) dual pairs. A divisibility-chain criterion decides compatibility on the rationals and on Q/Z. Compatible subsets of one chain have a compatible join, but two different chains need not: an explicit Chinese remainder construction gives two compatible topologies with an incompatible join. This answers the compact-union question negatively, disproves the Greatest Compatible TVG Conjecture for every nonzero rational-valued Hamel functional, and shows that the corresponding rational and real dual pairs admit no Mackey topology. We classify additive homomorphisms and isomorphisms of the real-valued observation spaces and their automorphism groups, prove that both prime square-denominator topologies are non-nuclear, classify sequences converging for every coefficient functional, and show that the real parameters of continuous characters of the integers with the mixed-prime metric form a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Part II studies real vector spaces whose Hausdorff additive group topology makes every fixed rational scalar multiplication continuous (TVGQ). A rational-valued Hamel functional and a rational parameter space S generate precompact, modular and real-valued observation topologies whose exact scalar ring is the multiplier ring of S. We compute their completions and character groups, classify the precompact TVGQ topologies, characterize universal separating sequences, show that local compactness and sigma-compactness force the scalar ring to be a field, classify isomorphisms within each modular family (exactly 2^c types), identify greatest-compatible existence with the unrestricted Mackey problem, and prove that all compatible topologies for the rational Hamel pair are non-Baire.

papers.title: Tangle Invariants Valued in Derived Categories of Sheaves and the Rouquier Complex
papers.abstract: We develop effective calculation tools for constructing categorified invariants of tangles and knots, following the work of Cautis and Kamnitzer. These invariants, originally constructed by means of Fourier-Mukai transform functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on certain iterated flag varieties, can be given an alternative algebraic description by using tilting bundles. We use this method and provide several examples of its application, in the hope of showing its utility to explicit pen-and-paper computations. This tilting-bundle method also allows us to lift the construction from derived to homotopy categories of complexes of modules, reducing the calculation of tangle invariants to a type of categorified matrix algebra, where the matrices in question have maps between their elements and calculations get turbocharged with chain homotopy.

papers.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
papers.abstract: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism. If $M$ is null-bordant, $Z(M)$ is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of $Z(S^d)$ which is fixed to be $Z(S^d)^{χ(M)/2}$ for even $d$ and can be removed for odd $d$. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In $d=4$ the obstruction is the signature: $Z(M)/Z(S^4)^{χ(M)/2}$ can be extracted if and only if $σ(M)=0$. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class $p_1$ has a local expression and thus $e^{iθσ(M)}=e^{\frac{i}{3}θ\int_M p_1}$ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the $4+1$-dimensional invertible phase with partition function $(-1)^{\int w_2w_3}$ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and $\mathbb{CP}^2\times S^1$, give opposite signs.

papers.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
papers.abstract: We prove a lower bound of $Ω_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusnády's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors.

papers.title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data
papers.abstract: Data arising in scientific applications often exhibits complex nonlinear structure. Identifying and parameterizing said nonlinearities can enable better modeling, enhance predictive analysis, data interpolation, denoising, and anomaly detection. In this paper, we develop theoretical and computational methods to detect and parametrize Euclidean point cloud data lying near a wedge sum of tori. Specifically, we use persistent cohomology and cup products to identify the distinct toroidal components, and on each component, we optimize over low-energy multivariate trigonometric polynomials for best data fit. The ensuing optimization problem reduces to generalized ridge regression, which can be solved efficiently via standard techniques. We demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in both synthetic and real datasets, including interpolation of low frame-rate recurrent videos, attractor recovery in quasiperiodic dynamical systems, and the parametrization of gene-space cycle data for parasites and humans.

papers.title: Efficient counting of 2 x 4 LEGO brick buildings
papers.abstract: We outline the algorithmic advances behind our recent computation of the number 8364925094730088313 of ways to combine eleven 2 x 4 LEGO bricks.

papers.title: Every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph with $r\geq 17$ contains a second Hamilton cycle
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Sheehan states that every Hamiltonian $4$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle. A natural problem is to find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every Hamiltonian $r$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle when $r\geq k$. Thomassen proved that $k\leq 300$. Improving Thomassen's result, Haxell, Seamone, and Verstra{ë}te proved that $k\leq 23$. We improve this bound by proving that every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph contains a second Hamilton cycle whenever $r\geq 17$. Our new idea is to establish a transversal theorem for set systems on a cycle using Harris's results on the Moser--Tardos algorithm for Local Lemma. We then apply Thomassen's theorem on independent dominating sets to obtain a second Hamilton cycle. For $r\ge 18$, we also give some algorithms to find such a transversal.

papers.title: Classification and $C_2$-cofiniteness of rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights
papers.abstract: We obtain classification results for rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights. More precisely, we prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of OZ type strongly generated by its conformal weight two subspace $V_2$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of Virasoro minimal models. We also prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type generated as a vertex algebra by its conformal weight one subspace $V_1$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of simple affine vertex operator algebras associated with finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras at positive integral levels. Consequently, Zhu's conjecture that rationality implies $C_2$-cofiniteness holds for both classes, and every such rational vertex operator algebra is regular.

papers.title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
papers.abstract: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of $\mathcal{C}$-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most $2$, which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most $2$; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.

papers.title: Regularity Theory for the Equation $\det(D^2u) = f(u)$ in Two Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the interior regularity of convex solutions to $$\det D^2u = f(u)$$ in planar domains, with no regularity or monotonicity assumptions on $f$. In particular, when $f$ is bounded between positive constants, we show that $u$ is locally $C^{1,\,1}$, and that its level sets near a critical point are asymptotically ellipses. Our analysis relies on a new monotone quantity for a second-order flow satisfied by the support functions of the level sets of $u$. As a byproduct of our methods, we obtain Liouville theorems that generalize a classical result of Jörgens, and include a complete classification of global solutions in 2D to an obstacle problem studied by Jin-Tu-Xiong. As another application, we obtain regularity and rigidity results for rotating-wave solutions of the semigeostrophic equations from meteorology.

papers.title: Explicit bounds for the number of solutions to Roth-type inequalities over adelic curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an upper bound on the number of a special system of Roth-type Diophantine inequalities over proper adelic curves. By refining the technique from previous work, we successfully eliminate the large-height restriction on the solutions. Furthermore, the constraints on the parameters within the inequality are further relaxed.
