papers.title: Dual-Mode Extremum Seeking for Diffusion Systems with Boundary-Cost Feedback
papers.abstract: Thermally tuned devices pose a basic control problem. A heater on one edge of a thin plate must hold a small element at an unknown optimal temperature, and the only signal available is the device's own performance. Boundary measurements of {such} an unknown performance objective can be used to tune a diffusion process without reconstructing its spatial state. This paper studies a dual-mode extremum-seeking controller for this setting, modeled as a semilinear diffusion equation on a square with nonuniform boundary actuation. The implementation contains two scalar states and exploits the leading attenuation and \rev{$π/4$} phase \rev{lag} of the diffusion response, a property shared by every periodically heated surface. It requires neither numerical plant coefficients nor the sign of the input gain. An energy estimate first establishes exponential stability of a coupled linear diffusion and controller model. A local bound on the remaining reaction and cost nonlinearities then yields stability and disturbance estimates for the averaged system. Complete kernel and boundary-trace arguments justify a change of coordinates that compares the implemented and averaged trajectories for all time. The resulting practical stability guarantee concerns the field, input bias, and sensitivity estimate, and is unaffected by a constant cost offset under corresponding filter initialization. At fixed dither amplitude, the residual state bound decreases with the inverse square root of frequency, while the ultimate cost bound decreases with its inverse. A thermal optical-filter example illustrates the predicted trends and the conservatism of the sufficient conditions.

papers.title: On Jordan nilpotency of index n in group rings
papers.abstract: Let $RG$ be the group ring of an arbitrary group $G$ over an associative and commutative ring $R$ with identity. In this paper, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for $RG$ to be Jordan nilpotent of index $n \geq 2$. In particular, we establish a connection between the study of Jordan nilpotency in group rings and the study of Lie nilpotency in these algebras. We also classify the Jordan nilpotency of $RG$, over rings of arbitrary characteristic, up to the index $6$.

papers.title: A characterization of a family of integral Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. In our earlier work, we proved that the quasi-strongly regular Cayley graph $Γ_H(G)$ is integral whenever $H$ is normal in $G$, and raised the question of whether the converse also holds. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively. We prove that if $Γ_H(G)$ is integral, then $H$ must be a normal subgroup of $G$. Consequently, $Γ_H(G)$ is integral if and only if $H\lhd G$. Our proof uses the irreducible representations of $G$ and the dimensions of their $H$-fixed subspaces. For a non-normal subgroup $H$, we construct a two-dimensional invariant subspace of a suitable representation operator and show that the corresponding eigenvalues are irrational.

papers.title: Improved deterministic integer factorization by quadratic-image sieving
papers.abstract: Let $N=pq$ be a semiprime and let $\ell\nmid N$ be an odd prime. For $a\ne0$ modulo $\ell$, put $H_a(N;\ell)=\{ax+Nx^{-1}:x\in\F_\ell^*\}$. For a primitive root $γ$, the size of $H_γ(N;\ell)\cup H_{γ^2}(N;\ell)$ is determined by the Frobenius trace of $Y^2=(X^2-1)(X^2-γ)$. We study the resulting trace-selection problem through finite certificates, a congruence modulo $8$, and a GRH-conditional positive-density family from the CM specialization $γ=2$. Independently of this conditional result, we obtain a deterministic factorization algorithm from the residue-known coefficient lattice of Harvey and Hittmeir (\emph{Math. Comp.}, 2022). The actual babystep index is a nondegenerate quadratic image modulo each selected prime divisor of the auxiliary modulus. After a computable translation, every such image avoids a fixed set of $(\ell-χ(-1))/4$ residues. This forbidden set is optimal among translated sets that must handle both square classes of the leading coefficient. Gauss reduction, a nearby lattice-vector selection, arbitrary-point multipoint evaluation, and the unrestricted large-order algorithm of Harvey and Hittmeir (arXiv, 2026) give the bit-complexity bound $N^{1/5}\exp(-(\log(4/3)/50+o(1))\log N/\log\log N)$. Its secondary factor is asymptotically smaller than every fixed negative power of $\log N$, improving the general bound of Harvey and Hittmeir (\emph{Math. Comp.}, 2022) and the balanced-semiprime bound of Gao et al.\ (arXiv, 2025).

papers.title: Dual Banach spaces with AP but without BAP
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to the AP-to-BAP and BAP-to-MAP questions for dual Banach spaces. More precisely, there is a separable Banach space $V$ with the metric approximation property (MAP) such that $V^*$ has the approximation property (AP) but no bounded approximation property (BAP). There is also a separable MAP space $X$, isomorphic to $\ell_1$, whose dual has BAP but no MAP. This resolves a longstanding open question explicitly stated in \cite{Oja2010}. The constructions rely on a finitely generated group without Property A and a quantitative estimate for optimal bounded approximation constants of projective tensor products.

papers.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

papers.title: Robust Multigrid on Adaptive Meshes for the Integral Fractional Laplacian
papers.abstract: We analyze a geometric multigrid method on locally refined mesh hierarchies for non-local variational problems, focusing on the integral fractional Laplacian. For newest-vertex-bisection-generated hierarchies, we prove uniform contraction of the multigrid iteration independently of the refinement level, the smallest local mesh size, and the polynomial degree in the finite element discretization. The proof is based on an abstract Hilbert-space framework, a strengthened Cauchy--Schwarz estimate obtained from a near-/far-field decomposition of the non-local bilinear form, and a multilevel stable decomposition independent of the discretization parameters. Numerical experiments underline the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Floer theory on based loops and fundamental groups of Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}^n$
papers.abstract: We obtain new constraints on the topology of Lagrangian submanifolds in the standard symplectic vector space $\mathbb{C}^n$ using Floer theory on the based loop space, generalizing a theorem of Fukaya-Irie. In particular, we show that non-trivial connected sums of closed, spin, aspherical manifolds of even dimensions do not admit Lagrangian embeddings into $\mathbb{C}^n$. A feature of the proof is that the obstructedness of the Floer theory is used to constrain the fundamental group of the Lagrangian.

papers.title: Ideals of 2-minors of nearly determinantal matrices
papers.abstract: We introduce nearly determinantal matrices and study their ideals of $2$-minors. We classify nearly determinantal matrices whose ideals of $2$-minors are prime. Furthermore, we characterize those nearly determinantal matrices whose ideals of $2$-minors are prime and Cohen--Macaulay with linear resolutions.

papers.title: A comparison of three models of a whirling string as it becomes chaotic
papers.abstract: A stretched wire driven near its fundamental frequency can leave the plane of the driving force and whirl. At larger amplitudes the whirl becomes modulated, reverses its direction, and becomes chaotic. Three models of this motion are in common use: the geometrically exact string equations; a two-mode model -- the Kirchhoff-Carrier equation with one transverse mode in each plane; and the averaged equations for the slow amplitudes of those two modes. We integrate all three under similar conditions and compare them along the route to chaos, which starts with a Hopf bifurcation of the steady whirl and passes through period doublings to chaotic attractors organized by a Shil'nikov homoclinic orbit. The small parameter of the averaging, the ratio $\varepsilon = c/ω_1$ of the modulation rate to the fundamental frequency, runs from 0.005 to 0.02. Qualitatively the three models agree in the sequence of bifurcations, the coexisting attractors, the return maps and the Lyapunov exponents. Quantitatively, averaging places each local bifurcation $0.7\varepsilon$ to $1.2\varepsilon$ higher in the scaled detuning. The geometrically exact and two-mode models agree with each other to within 0.002 at the local bifurcations for $\varepsilon \le 0.01$. The Shil'nikov ratio, which decides whether chaos accompanies the homoclinic orbit, agrees among the three models to within 1.5% for $\varepsilon \le 0.01$, yet the homoclinic bifurcation itself moves by about $\varepsilon$ at the lower damping and by 6 to 9 times $\varepsilon$ at the higher; the difference is set by how quickly the return of the homoclinic loop changes with detuning.

papers.title: Natural Expansiveness and Equilibrium States for Semiflows
papers.abstract: We introduce natural expansiveness, a notion of expansiveness for non-invertible dynamical systems which is defined by using the natural extension. We show that every expansive homeomorphism or flow, every positive expansive endomorphism and every positive expansive semiflow without end points is naturally expansive. Moreover, we prove that the suspension of a naturally expansive endomorphism is naturally expansive. This gives examples of naturally expansive semiflows which are neither positive expansive nor restrictions of expansive flows. Then we extend natural expansiveness and the topological pressure to semiflows which are not necessarily continuous, by using a pseudosemimetric $d_ρ$. We introduce the notion of $d_ρ$-conjugacy, and we prove that every regular impulsive semiflow is $d_ρ$-conjugate to a continuous semiflow. As an application, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of equilibrium states for regular impulsive semiflows.

papers.title: Two-sided estimates for two-point local time tails of branching random walks: a Green function criterion
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the joint tails of local times at two distinct sites for branching random walks (BRWs). Our principle results establish a general Green-function criterion for two-sided exponential tail bounds with a common spatial factor given by a three-point Green function convolution, and further identify a strict inequality that must be satisfied by the corresponding exponential constants. In particular, we verify this criterion for subcritical BRWs on finitely generated groups, for critical BRWs on non-elementary hyperbolic groups, and for critical BRWs on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d\geq 5$. As applications, we revisit the growth rate of visited sites on spheres in hyperbolic groups obtained by Sidoravicius et al. [Commun. Pure Appl. Math. 2023], and also establish lower bounds for the probabilities of visiting finite sets in Euclidean lattices.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of generic Riemann solutions to one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the time-asymptotic stability of the one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, assuming that the corresponding quasi-neutral Euler equations admit a generic Riemann solution consisting of a shock, a contact discontinuity, and a rarefaction wave. It is proved that there exists a unique global-in-time solution, which converges in $L^\infty$ norm, as time goes to infinity, to the ansatz composed of a viscous shock with a time-dependent shift, a viscous contact wave, and an inviscid rarefaction wave. The main difficulty arises from the non-conservative lower-order source terms induced by the electric potential in the momentum and energy equations, which significantly complicates the proof of the existence of individual waves (especially the viscous shock) and the derivation of the relative entropy estimates. To overcome this, we make full use of the Poisson equation satisfied by the electric potential, and combine the weighted relative entropy method with the $a$-contraction method with shifts to close the estimates within the $H^2$-perturbation framework.

papers.title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
papers.abstract: We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schrödinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.

papers.title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
papers.abstract: Quantum-inspired numerical methods for partial differential equations represent discretized fields and operators as quantics tensor trains (QTT), so that their cost depends on how compressible the problem is rather than on the number of unknowns. Global spectral formulations in this setting have so far relied on Fourier bases, restricted to periodic problems, or on collocation, which does not preserve the variational structure exploited by tensor-network solvers. We introduce a QTT Chebyshev-Galerkin method that assembles and solves global spectral systems directly in compressed form, without forming the underlying arrays. Starting from the weak formulation, the method handles coupled elliptic systems with variable coefficients, smoothly mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet-Robin boundary conditions, and yields symmetric positive-definite systems suited to variational tensor-network solvers. Parameters and random inputs enter as additional coordinates, so the same construction returns the solution over an entire parameter space in a single solve. In linear elasticity, the method retains spectral convergence and reaches errors below $10^{-8}$ on a three-dimensional benchmark, beyond those attained by QTT finite differences and Q2/Q4 FEniCSx finite elements over the tested range. A six-parameter cantilever design study covering $1.7\times10^{7}$ designs is solved in a single 92s run, and a stochastic problem with ten random coordinates is represented with $2.4\times10^{6}$ times less memory than its full coefficient array.

papers.title: An ambient metric framework for sharp compactness of the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature problem
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric method for studying $C^{2N}$-compactness of positive solutions to the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature equation on closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds, for every integer $N\ge1$ and every dimension $n>2N$. Assuming the GJMS operator is invertible, its Green function is positive, and the positive mass condition holds, we establish sharp dimension ranges for the compactness of the set of all positive solutions with prescribed positive constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature. The largest dimension for compactness is $24$ for $N=1$ ([21]), $2N+20$ for $N=2,3$ ([11]), $2N+19$ for $N=4,5$, $2N+18$ for $N=6,7,8$, $2N+17$ for $9\le N\le17$, and $2N+16$ for all $N\ge18$. The constructions in [4,5,33,11] for $N=1,2,3$ and in the companion paper [12] for $N\ge4$ give noncompact examples in every dimension exceeding the corresponding compactness bound. We show that these $L^{\infty}$-unbounded examples can be chosen to satisfy the same operator and mass hypotheses, proving sharpness within this class. Our method relates the Pohozaev quadratic forms to the Hessian $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$, where $\mathscr{F}$ is the volume-normalized total $Q_{2N}$-curvature functional and $g_c$ is the standard round metric on $\mathbb{S}^n$. The ambient metric argument of [12] supplies an explicit formula for $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$ on transverse-traceless tensors. The York decomposition projects metric perturbations onto this space. The scalar--vector--tensor decomposition represents the Pohozaev quadratic forms by explicit finite-dimensional matrices. We prove that these matrices are positive definite throughout the stated dimension range, a crucial step in establishing compactness.

papers.title: Constrained Mean Variance Portfolio Selection under Reflected Factor Dynamics: Stochastic Riccati Equations, Neumann Problems,and a Deep Solver
papers.abstract: We study extended stochastic Riccati equations (ESREs) arising in constrained continuous time mean variance portfolio selection with random market coefficients. Reflected Markovian diffusions are introduced to model factor dynamics in a bounded state space, naturally leading to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. A logarithmic transformation converts the extended stochastic Riccati equations into quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) driven by the reflected factors. We establish their probabilistic representation through semilinear parabolic Neumann problems and prove existence and uniqueness of bounded continuous viscosity solutions. Existence is obtained through stability and comparison arguments for quadratic BSDEs, whereas uniqueness is established by combining a Kobylanski-type transformation with a viscosity comparison principle adapted to the Neumann boundary setting. We further develop a Deep BSDE method combining reflected-path simulation, geometry-aware boundary treatment, and efficient evaluation of the constrained Hamiltonian. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, providing a mesh-free framework for high-dimensional constrained portfolio problems with Neumann boundary.

papers.title: Positive coexistence solutions for systems of multi-kernel Hammerstein type equations
papers.abstract: We investigate positive solutions with both components nontrivial for systems of Hammerstein integral equations associated with a general $2\times2$ matrix of Green's kernels, thereby extending the decoupled (diagonal) case to systems with cross-coupling. Such systems arise from boundary value problems in which the unknowns may be coupled both in the differential equations and in the boundary conditions, a setting that has received considerably less attention than the decoupled case. Using a component-wise Krasnosel'skiĭ compression--expansion fixed point theorem in product cones, we derive existence and non-existence criteria. A multiplicity result guaranteeing at least two positive solutions is also obtained, by means of the fixed point index in cones. As an application, we consider radially symmetric solutions for an elliptic system on an annulus with coupled Robin boundary conditions.

papers.title: Rigidity of Ricci solitons for $\varphi$-related metallic semi-Riemannian structures on para-Kenmotsu manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate Ricci solitons in the para-Kenmotsu setting with respect to a $\varphi$-related metallic semi-Riemannian metric arising from the underlying almost paracontact metric structure, under the assumption that the potential vector field is pointwise collinear with the Reeb vector field. We first establish the relation $\tS=S+2nβ\bigl(g-η\otimesη\bigr)$ between the Ricci tensors of the original metric $g$ and the $\varphi$-related metallic metric $\tg$. We then show that the Ricci soliton equation implies that the original metric $g$ is of $η$-Einstein type. By combining this condition with the contracted Bianchi identity, we obtain a rigidity result implying $f=0$, $λ=\frac{2n}{C}$, $S=-2ng$, and consequently $\tS=-\frac{2n}{C}\tg$. Thus, every Ricci soliton in this setting whose potential vector field is pointwise collinear with the Reeb vector field is necessarily trivial, and both $g$ and $\tg$ are Einstein. Finally, we provide two five-dimensional para-Kenmotsu examples: one realizing the resulting trivial Einstein Ricci soliton and another showing that failure of the required Einstein condition prevents the existence of such a soliton.

papers.title: Real alternative Daugavet property without Daugavet property in a separable complex Banach space
papers.abstract: We construct a separable complex Banach space whose underlying real space has the alternative Daugavet property, although the complex space fails the Daugavet property, thereby answering an open question posed by Kadets, Martin, and Paya in 2006.

papers.title: The group of strong automorphisms of the differential field of transseries
papers.abstract: We describe the group of strongly additive automorphisms of the differential field $\mathbb T$ of transseries as a non-trivial semidirect product. We show that this group is torsion-free and has trivial center, and that many naturally arising differential subfields of $\mathbb T$ are definably closed in $\mathbb T$.

papers.title: Small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation with the full velocity alignment source term, which serves as the mean-field equation for the stochastic Cucker--Smale model. Inspired by the idea of Hottovy et al. \cite{Hottovy2015} to rearrange SDEs via integration by parts, we repeatedly perform integration by parts on independent copies of our equation. Then we define a global position correction and a quadratic remainder, both with uniformly bounded tails. Applying the Aldous criterion, we obtain tightness of the position correction, which in turn yields tightness of the position process. Subsequently, using the averaging method on the fast time scale, the quadratic functional can be decomposed into the equilibrium average, local quadratic fluctuations, and exponential transients. Then, the Poisson--Lyapunov equation is employed to prove the convergence of the time integral. Finally, under various suitable assumptions, we obtain the weak convergence of the laws of the approximating processes to the law of the solution of the small-inertia limit equation, along with the identification of the limiting process, and also the convergence rate of strong $L^1$-convergence. The extra noise-induced drift term can be expressed as the solution of a contraction-type Fredholm equation. This paper is complementary to the deterministic particle limit work of \cite{Carrillo2021,Choi2021} .

papers.title: Uniform localization and boundary corrections for two-node quiver Coulomb branches
papers.abstract: We construct simple coherent classes and compute their normalized difference operators for the two-node quiver Coulomb branch with gauge group $GL_1\times GL_2$ and $m-1$ framing columns at the second node. The first magnetic charge is fixed at zero. For every $m\geq1$, every support $(n,-1)$ with $n\geq1$, and every integral electric twist, we prove that termwise saturation of the matter Koszul complex gives the simple intermediate extension. A graded normalization formula expresses its localization on every stratum as a finite binomial shuffle sum. The resulting operators satisfy bar symmetry, positive bubbling order, paired root-residue cancellation, and integral Laurent polynomial action. For $m=4$, we construct the derived boundary correction on $(2,-2)$, retaining the nonsemisimple odd-electric boundary object, and compute all electric twists. Finally, matter Euler divisibility proves triangular uniqueness on arbitrary fixed rank-two magnetic supports inside the actual integral Coulomb image. A pole-free counterexample shows why residue conditions alone do not give this uniqueness. Existence on general deeper mixed-sign supports remains open.

papers.title: Property F and weak integrality of braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: We prove that a braided fusion category with property F is weakly integral, provided it admits a pivotal structure whose left categorical dimensions are positive on the intersection of its Müger center and its adjoint subcategory. In particular, the converse implication in the property F conjecture holds for modular fusion categories and pseudounitary braided fusion categories. We also show that the positivity condition holds for every pivotal braided fusion category if and only if every braided fusion category over $\mathbb C$ admits a pivotal structure.

papers.title: A Variational Quantum Algorithm for Multi-Skill Project Scheduling
papers.abstract: Job scheduling is an NP-hard optimization problem with clear industrial relevance. In practice, distributing work across a team is not only about meeting deadlines or improving productivity; it also affects fatigue, stress, and employee well-being. Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) provide a promising way to address these problems through QUBO formulations, although their scalability on near-term NISQ hardware is still limited by Hilbert-space growth and barren plateaus. In this work, we simulate a VQA for a realistic Multi-Skill Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (MS-RCPSP), including worker capacities, skill matrices, task priorities, deadlines, and calendar stability during rescheduling. To keep the problem within a near-term circuit size, we use a temporal batch decomposition that solves one day at a time, propagates the remaining workload, and combines it with a logarithmic binary encoding that keeps every batch at or below 30 qubits. Because the ground state of a QUBO Hamiltonian is a computational basis state, entanglement is not required to represent the solution, raising the question of whether it helps or hinders ansatz training. We address this question by comparing the linear and brick-wall entangling topologies of a hardware-efficient ansatz with an entanglement-free reference that has the same number of parameters and by training every configuration with COBYLA and with Adam using SPSA gradient estimation. For the instance and initialization studied, the entanglement-free reference produced feasible schedules under both optimizers. With COBYLA, it produced the feasible schedule closest to the required workload at a fraction of the simulation cost of the entangled topologies, indicating that entanglement did not improve the solutions found by the VQA.

papers.title: Constrained defined-contribution pension management: A reparameterized neural network approach
papers.abstract: This paper studies constrained defined contribution (DC) pension management under a two-factor financial market model. The pension participant is allowed to invest in cash, two nominal bonds, an inflation-linked bond, and a stock index. Moreover, they can also purchase term life insurance to manage pre-retirement death risk. Unlike traditional literature, we consider a pension member restricted to a general non-empty, closed, and convex trading constraint set that includes no short-selling, no borrowing, and portfolio-mix constraints as special cases. Such restrictions reflect common limits on pension-account trading. To solve the problem, we construct a family of unconstrained artificial markets, in which the original trading constraints are satisfied by adjusting the drift terms of the risky assets. Using a duality transformation, we derive the Lagrangian dual problem and propose a reparameterized neural network method to compute lower and upper bounds on the primal value function. We calibrate our model with U.S. data using a Kalman filter method, and find that our method produces a smaller duality gap than the benchmark methods. We also compare the constrained results with the unconstrained explicit solution and find that trading constraints substantially change wealth accumulation, portfolio strategies, and insurance demand. This highlights that unconstrained solutions may provide misleading guidance for pension management in practice.

papers.title: A $2.81^n$ upper bound on the number of stable matchings
papers.abstract: We study the maximum number ${\rm SM}(n)$ of stable matchings in an instance with $n$ men and $n$ women. Karlin, Oveis Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018) proved the first single-exponential upper bound; their argument gives ${\rm SM}(n)\le 2^{17n}$ for sufficiently large $n$. Palmer and Pálvölgyi (FOCS 2021) improved this bound to $3.55^n+O(1)$. We prove that ${\rm SM}(n)<2.81^n$. This brings the exponential base closer to $2.28$, the base of the best known lower bound. More precisely, we bound the number of stable matchings in each instance in terms of each person's number of stable partners, where a stable partner is someone matched to that person in at least one stable matching. Our proof assigns each person a weight determined by this number and uses these weights to bound the number of stable matchings by induction.

papers.title: Largest-Angle Bisection and Statistical Regularization of Triangle Shapes
papers.abstract: Largest-angle bisection (LAB) repeatedly divides a triangle by bisecting its largest angle. Although this procedure is known to preserve nondegenerate triangle shapes, less is known about the distribution of shapes across the resulting refinement tree. We show that its long-term behavior is governed by a distinction between pure and mixed branches. A branch that eventually selects only one of the two children may approach an exceptional family of shapes. By contrast, every branch that changes children infinitely often converges in shape to a right-isosceles triangle. This follows from a projective Lyapunov function that is non-increasing at every refinement and decreases strictly whenever the selected child changes. Consequently, a random branch converges to the right-isosceles shape with probability one, and the proportion of triangles near that shape tends to one across complete refinement levels. Largest-angle bisection therefore produces statistical regularization even though exceptional branches remain present.

papers.title: How many sorted projections determine n points in k dimensions?
papers.abstract: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.78^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.

papers.title: Cycles in Regular Multipartite Tournaments
papers.abstract: We study balanced cycles in regular multipartite tournaments. A cycle in a $c$-partite tournament is $k$-balanced if it contains exactly $k$ vertices from each partite class. We prove that there exists an absolute integer $r_0$ such that every regular $c$-partite tournament with each partite class size of $r\ge r_0$ contains a $k$-balanced cycle for every $1\le k\le r$ when $c=3$ or $c\ge5$, and for every $2\le k\le r$ when $c=4$. In particular, our result confirms three conjectures of Volkmann and Winzen for large regular multipartite tournaments. We also confirm Yeo's conjecture on the existence of $(p,q)$-cycle factors for large regular $c$-partite tournaments $G$ with $c\ge4$, where a $(p,q)$-cycle factor is a pair of vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $p$ and $q$ spanning $G$.

papers.title: Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks with Uncertain and State-Dependent Couplings
papers.abstract: Phase locking in oscillator networks depends critically on the interaction strengths between coupled units. In many applications, however, these couplings are uncertain, state dependent, or time varying. We derive rigorous conditions for phase locking in Kuramoto-type networks when each coupling strength is known only within prescribed bounds. Building on a convex formulation of the nonlinear fixed-point equations, we obtain edge-wise error bounds for arbitrary feasible approximations that hold uniformly over all admissible couplings. These bounds yield sufficient conditions for the existence of phase-locked states with prescribed phase-difference limits. We illustrate the framework for AC power grids with uncertain voltage magnitudes and adaptive oscillator networks with state-dependent couplings. For the latter, the bounds can be further tightened by exploiting the state dependence of the couplings.

papers.title: Planar Central Configurations of Four Equal Masses: Classification and Morse Indices
papers.abstract: We study the planar central configurations of four equal positive masses under homogeneous interactions with force exponent $A>2$. For $2<A\le 3$, we prove that there are exactly four types of configurations up to similarity and relabeling: the square, the centered equilateral triangle, a unique nontrivial concave kite, and a unique collinear configuration. Combined with known results for $A>3$, this completes the classification for all $A>2$ and gives an affirmative answer to Problem 11 of Albouy, Cabral, and Santos. We also establish the nondegeneracy modulo rotation of these configurations and determine their Morse indices, confirming Hampton's Conjecture 2. Our proofs are based on analytic arguments and exact algebraic calculations.

papers.title: A general technique for explicit quantile representations
papers.abstract: This work proves existence of contours independent of probability level for exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities. Explicit constructions cover five broad distribution families and yield a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility using forward functions.

papers.title: Beyond the Gap: What Imaginary-Time Evolution Reveals About the Edge of the Continuum
papers.abstract: The spectral gap, the energy separating the ground state from the first excitation, governs many quantum phenomena, yet it is far harder to compute than the ground state. We propose a mathematically rigorous method for extracting the gap from imaginary-time evolution in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonians, where the first excitation typically marks the edge of a continuous spectrum. We show that a gap is not automatically detected: detection depends on how the initial state and observable couple the ground state to excitations at the bottom of the continuum. When this coupling follows a power law, the gap is recovered together with a logarithmic correction whose coefficient yields the exponent of the spectral density near the edge of the continuum, which reflects the physics of the excitations. We confirm both predictions numerically for an exactly solvable model. Our results offer a new numerical approach to many-body quantum physics, in which both the gap and the threshold exponent are obtained merely at the cost of a ground-state calculation.

papers.title: Szegő quasiforms: a Schottky-scheme construction for vertex operator superalgebras
papers.abstract: We study the half weight ($N=\half$) analogue of the Bers quasiform on a Schottky group $Γ$ of genus $g$: the Poincaré series $S_\eps(x,y)=\sum_{\gt\in\Gt}j(\gt,x)/(γx-y)\,(dx\,dy)^{1/2}$ over a lift $\Gt\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)$ of $Γ$. The $\Ng:=2^{g}$ lifts give $\Ng$ trivial $α$-holonomy even spin structures $\Lg$. The remaining $2^{2g}-\Ng$ spin structures are not treated in this paper. We prove, on an open set (H) of Schottky parameters and more generally whenever the critical exponent of $Γ$ is below $\half$ (any genus $g\ge 1$) the following: absolute and locally uniform convergence on $Ω_0\timesΩ_0$, where $Ω_0$ is the full region of discontinuity including the point $\infty$ (treated in homogeneous coordinates); invariance without Eichler-type defect; skew-symmetry; a simple pole on the diagonal as the only singularity; $H^0(\Sg,\Lg)=0$; and hence identification of $S_\eps$ with the Szegő kernel of $\Lg$. At genus one the kernel is computed explicitly and the relations between lifts and theta characteristics are determined. We further prove that the diagonal coefficient defines a projective connection that differs from the Bergman projective connection by a quadratic differential constructed from $θ[δ](0)$, a residue-reconstruction formula for half-differentials with poles of any order, an expansion in the Schottky multipliers, and a formula for the free fermion stress tensor.

papers.title: On isotropic points and contact invariants of curves
papers.abstract: Let $(C_{f},0) \subset (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$ be a germ of an irreducible holomorphic curve, given implicity by $f(x)=0$ if $n=2$ and by $f(x)=g(x)=0$ if $n=3$, and parametrised by $γ:(\mathbb{C},0) \rightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$. We define the contact invariants $\operatorname{Iso}_{f}$ and $\operatorname{Iso}_γ$ for $f$ and $γ$, respectively, which count the number of isotropic points that appear after a generic deformation of the curve. We first consider the case where the curve is regular and establish a relation between those invariants and the number of vertices, inflection points and the zero-torsion points (for $n=3)$ that emerge from the deformation of the curve. Furthermore, we consider a germ of a singular curve with an isolated singularity and relate the number of isotropic points with the Milnor number of $f$

papers.title: Escaping and generics over ideals
papers.abstract: We study the relation between the existence of escaping (or hyperimmune) functions and weak 1-genericity using computability over ideals. We prove in particular the existence of an $\mathcal{I}$-escaping function which does not $\mathcal{I}$-compute any weakly $\mathcal{I}$-generic set whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is a countable Turing ideal closed under the existence of diagonally non-computable functions.

papers.title: Private key sieves for improved attacks on RSA
papers.abstract: The RSA cryptosystem has been studied extensively and its insecurity in specific scenarios is well known. For instance, a sufficiently small private key allows to factorize the modulus $N$ and break the system. Attacks like this are often based on lattice reduction for finding small roots of polynomials, but high lattice dimensions can make it difficult to achieve the theoretically proved bounds in practice. In this paper, we adapt a sieve technique originally developed for deterministic integer factorization and apply it to RSA parameters. The sieve allows for an asymptotically significant reduction of the private key search space, and can be used to decrease the bounds for the polynomial roots. We also provide a square-root speed-up of the best currently known runtime bound for factoring semiprime $N=pq$ with small prime difference $q-p$.

papers.title: An equivalence principle for martingales
papers.abstract: We show that any discrete-time filtration can be embedded into a dyadic filtration, realized via a non-classical measure-preserving map. This embedding makes it possible to reduce certain problems involving vector-valued martingales to the case of Haar martingales. Some applications of this result will also be discussed.

papers.title: Quasinilpotency of commutators under a weakened Kleinecke--Shirokov condition
papers.abstract: Kramar and Kramar Fijavž proved that a commutator $Y=AB-BA$ of two complex square matrices is nilpotent whenever $Y$ commutes with an iterated commutator $δ_Y^{k}(A)$, where $δ_Y(T)=YT-TY$, and asked whether this result can be generalized to bounded operators on infinite-dimensional spaces. We show that for $k\geq 2$ such a commutator need not be quasinilpotent. On the other hand, for every $k$ it is quasinilpotent whenever it is compact, or more generally whenever it is a Riesz operator or $AY-YA$ is compact. Moreover, its Riesz projection at any non-zero isolated point of its spectrum always has infinite rank.

papers.title: Scopes arrangements and product formulas
papers.abstract: We develop normalized abacus combinatorics for affine type \(C\). We also give explicit product formulas for the number of Scopes classes at every level and every positive depth in affine types \(A\) and \(C\).

papers.title: On Partitions with Constant-Sum Gap Sequences
papers.abstract: We introduce and study \emph{constant-sum gap partitions}: for a fixed nonnegative integer $C$, these are partitions $λ=(λ_1,\ldots,λ_k)$ whose successive differences $d_i=λ_{i+1}-λ_i$ satisfy $d_i+d_{k-i}=C$ for all valid $i$. We derive the generating function for this family, treating partitions of odd and even length separately, and compute it explicitly for $C=0, 1,2,3,4$. We then construct explicit bijections between constant-sum gap partitions with $2m+1$, respectively $2m$, parts and partitions into odd, respectively even, parts in which parts below the largest part have bounded multiplicity, together with an exact weight relation between a partition and its image. Finally, we give a geometric characterization of constant-sum gap partitions in terms of their Ferrers diagrams: removing a prescribed, linearly growing number of cells from each row renders the diagram symmetric about its middle row, for both the odd- and even-length cases.

papers.title: Macroscopic return-time spectra and Hausdorff dimension transitions
papers.abstract: Can the complete macroscopic spectrum of return times determine the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding set of initial points? We classify all common lower and upper macroscopic intermediate-dimension spectra of zero-density integer sets and realize every admissible spectrum on a full-dimensional family of zero-frequency orbits under logarithmic-power bounds on inverse-branch contraction. For first-return branches with stretched-exponential contraction $e^{-n^δ}$, $0<δ<1$, complete spectrum levels exhibit a sharp zero/full dimension transition at the counting endpoint $δ$. At the critical exponent, exact laws $N_y(t)\sim c_0t^δ(\log t)^β$ yield zero dimension for $β\le0$ and full dimension for $β>0$, even with the complete spectrum fixed. An explicit two-branch intermittent interval map realizes this transition through genuine first returns. Above the critical exponent, imposing an exact counting law and a complete spectrum does not reduce the dimension of an intrinsic mean-energy level in an affine return tower. For nonlinear branches, we obtain quantitative bounds and an exact conditional-pressure formula under thermodynamic regularity assumptions, verified for an explicit non-affine family.

papers.title: Definably isometric cuboids over Hensel minimal fields
papers.abstract: We show that, over a valued field $K$ with $1$-h-minimal theory $\operatorname{Th}(K)$, two Cartesian products of balls must be equal up to translation and coordinate permutation in order for there to exist a definable surjective isometry between them. For this purpose, we introduce a notion of relative dimension for cuboids in $K^n$ that is computed combinatorially and relates to the notion of dimension for definable sets in Hensel minimal theories when $K$ has infinite residue field.

papers.title: A volume-conserving ALE continuous Galerkin method with residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann fluxes for nonlinear free-surface waves
papers.abstract: We develop an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian continuous Galerkin finite element method for two-dimensional fully nonlinear free-surface potential flow. An isoparametric finite element method computes the interior potential on the current fluid domain, while a residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann flux drives the surface evolution. The residual-based flux satisfies a global discrete balance inherited from the interior variational formulation. When combined with compatible mesh motion, surface projection, and quadrature, this balance yields conservation of the discrete fluid volume at the semi-discrete level. An optional volume-conserving sixth-order surface dissipation controls high-frequency oscillations, and the surface equations are advanced with fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration, updating the mesh and interior solution at every stage. Numerical experiments confirm the expected spatial convergence for linear free-surface waves and demonstrate reduced mesh sensitivity for nonlinear waves over flat and curved bottoms. A rotating-wavemaker example further illustrates the treatment of moving solid boundaries.

papers.title: Alexandrov's theorem in the anti-Gaussian space: A Reilly-formula approach
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Alexandrov's theorem about constant weighted mean curvature hypersurfaces in the anti-Gaussian space, due to the authors and Johne-Silini independently, via a Reilly-type formula approach. Moreover, we establish a sharp Heintze-Karcher-type inequality for hypersurfaces in manifolds with a generalized substatic condition, together with its rigidity in Euclidean space with density.

papers.title: Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: We study commutators $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ involving fractional Laplacians on quantum Euclidean spaces associated with arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices $θ$. For $d\geq2$ and $-\frac d2<ε\neq 0<1$, we characterize critical weak Schatten class membership of $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ for any $x$ as a tempered distribution by Sobolev spaces, with equivalent corresponding norms. We also establish precise asymptotics of singular values for $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$. For this purpose, we extend the Cwikel estimates and the required asymptotics of singular values to arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices, and we also establish a systematic approximation theory of tempered distributions on quantum Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: The optimal barrier parameter of the three-dimensional power cone
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier parameter for the three-dimensional power cone. Although several self-concordant barriers for this cone have been constructed, its optimal barrier parameter had remained unknown. For a power cone with exponent $c\in(0,1)$, we prove that the optimal parameter is $\frac{3}{1+\min\{c,1-c\}}$. Except at $c=1/2$, this value is strictly smaller than the parameter $3-2\min\{c,1-c\}$ of Chares' conjectured barrier. At $c=1/2$, the optimal parameter equals $2$, in agreement with the optimal barrier parameter of the second-order cone. The proof combines a sharp lower bound for arbitrary logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barriers with an explicit barrier attaining the bound.

papers.title: Twofold Control: Simultaneous Optimization of Initial Conditions and Control Inputs
papers.abstract: The paper introduces a novel control notion, twofold controllability, which consists of the joint optimisation of the initial state and the distributed control input in a controlled dynamical system, with the aim of reaching a prescribed target state within a given time interval. We show that the resulting problem is well-posed, derive the corresponding optimality conditions, and provide an explicit formulation of its solution. The proposed approach ensures the reachability of any target state independently of the Kalman rank condition. We show that incorporating the additional control component enlarges the set of states reachable with a fixed control cost. At the same time, the average energy required to reach target vectors on the unit sphere decreases. Furthermore, we analyse the asymptotic behaviour as the cost of controlling the system through the initial state tends to infinity. Particular attention is paid to the case in which the controllability Gramian is singular and the classical notion of controllability does not hold. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical examples, including ones arising from the semi-discretisation of the heat and wave equations with boundary control.

papers.title: On the proof of multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: In this article, we use Wu's method to prove Budur's multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for completeness.

papers.title: High-Degree Restricted Cohomology for $K(3;1)^{(1)}$ in Characteristics Five and Seven
papers.abstract: We determine the high-degree restricted first cohomology of the positive subalgebra of the rank-one contact algebra in characteristics five and seven, with parabolically induced coefficients. In degrees from twice the characteristic through four times the characteristic minus three, each characteristic has six nonzero homogeneous components, of total dimension thirteen. The constituents include Frobenius twists of the natural horizontal module, represented by Cartier cocycles. PBW duality converts the calculation into bounded-degree homology, where the coefficient action couples the natural and cubic relation coordinates. The resulting modules determine the high-degree part of the coefficient cohomology used in the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre term $E_2^{0,1}$ for extensions of induced contact modules. In particular, extensions from the Steinberg induced modules vanish in these degrees.

papers.title: The Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators in divergence form
papers.abstract:
We establish the Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators $L = -\operatorname{div}^α(μ
abla^α\cdot)$ of order $2α\in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $μ$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{α,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^αu\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $α$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(μ
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $α	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $α$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^α$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

papers.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
papers.abstract: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $γ$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when $γ=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

papers.title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
papers.abstract: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.

papers.title: Exponential Deviations and Hölder Continuity for Moving-Law Mixed Cocycles
papers.abstract: We study mixed random-quasiperiodic cocycles whose one-step laws evolve along an ergodic environment. Under mixed-base ergodicity, bounded logarithmic growth, and stationary-value uniqueness, which we characterize by relative quasi-irreducibility, we prove exponential quenched deviations for finite-time directional growth. A renewal example shows that, in general ergodic environments, annealed exponential deviations can fail despite quenched exponential concentration. This obstruction motivates us to consider a fixed finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov environment, where we establish annealed exponential deviation estimates uniform over a relative neighborhood of a reference sampling kernel in the bounded mixed-base-ergodic class at each fixed tolerance. These estimates yield local Hölder continuity of the maximal Lyapunov exponent near a stationary-value-unique kernel with a simple top exponent. Under common matrix and inverse bounds, the continuity applies to synchronized Wasserstein perturbations with fixed translation marginals and continuous matrix fields, or to ordinary Wasserstein perturbations with uniform Hölder regularity in the phase. As an application, suitable frequency-support and noise-nondegeneracy conditions yield Hölder energy dependence for moving-law Schrödinger cocycles with continuous potentials.

papers.title: Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence
papers.abstract: We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.

papers.title: Inference for Realized Quadratic Covariation of $R$ and $R^2$ as a Measure of Return Asymmetry
papers.abstract: We propose a nonparametric test of return asymmetry based on the realized quadratic covariation between a cumulative return path and its square using high-frequency data. Our null hypothesis is that the volatility path is independent of the Brownian motion driving returns. Under this null and a martingale condition, the infill limit of the statistic is conditionally Gaussian given the volatility path, with a conditional variance determined by integrated variance. Studentization by a feasible variance estimator yields an asymptotically standard normal statistic without specifying a parametric model for volatility. Simulations under Heston and Bates dynamics show near-nominal per-window size, quantify power gains from independent-window aggregation, and assess sensitivity to jump removal and volatility-dependent drift. An application to 165 U.S. stocks over 1998--2025 finds that rejections concentrate in negative asymmetry, consistent with the leverage effect.

papers.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
papers.abstract: We provide an algorithm for enumerating ordinary K3 surfaces over a fixed finite field based on Taelman's theorem. We use this algorithm to prove that there exist no K3 surfaces without rational points over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 13$. For elliptic K3 surfaces, we give a geometric proof of this non-existence without computer assistance. On the other hand, we also provide explicit pointless K3 surfaces over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\leq 11$.

papers.title: Four-colour counterexamples for monochromatic path partitions
papers.abstract: In 1989, Gyárfás conjectured that the vertex set of every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be partitioned into at most $r$ monochromatic paths. The case $r=2$ follows from a theorem of Gerencsér and Gyárfás, and Pokrovskiy proved the conjecture for $r=3$. Recently, Li and Wang disproved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $r$, leaving open the smallest number of colours for which it fails. We show that this number is four. For every integer $n\geq118$, we construct a four-edge-colouring of $K_n$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least five paths. We also construct, for every integer $n\geq60$, a four-edge-colouring of $K_{n,n}$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least eight paths, disproving Pokrovskiy's conjectured bound $2r-1$ for balanced complete bipartite graphs when $r=4$.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic limits of the asymmetric Brownian energy process and its dynamic generalization
papers.abstract: We prove that the hydrodynamic limit of the asymmetric Brownian energy process (ABEP) is the viscous Burgers equation. We also prove the hydrodynamic limit of the dynamic ABEP which leads to a nonlinear equation for the macroscopic tail-energy potential. Both processes are related to the Brownian energy process (BEP) through invertible, non-local transformations involving discrete tail energies, which can be thought of as the microscopic equivalent of a transformation of Cole-Hopf type. Our main tool is a general micro-to-macro result showing that, under suitable conditions, such microscopic tail transformations induce corresponding transformations of the limiting density profiles. Combining this result with the fact that the hydrodynamic limit of BEP is the heat equation, we obtain the limiting profiles of ABEP and dynamic ABEP as explicit nonlinear transformations of solutions of the heat equation.

papers.title: On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
papers.abstract: We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.

papers.title: A general Lê--Siersma formula
papers.abstract: We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. We give a formula that generalizes those of Lê and Siersma, expressing the difference of their Euler characteristics as a sum of local contributions associated with the critical points of the restriction of $s$. We provide an algebraic formula in the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is {smooth of pure dimension outside $f^{-1}(0)$}, and show some applications and examples.

papers.title: One-dimensional nodal solutions of the Lane--Emden problem in cylinders: asymptotic behaviour and energy stability
papers.abstract: We consider the Lane-Emden problem $-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$, $p>1$, in bounded domains of a half-cylinder $ω\times(0,+\infty)$, with Dirichlet conditions on the relative boundary and Neumann conditions on the boundary of the cylinder. In flat cylinders $ω\times(0,L)$ this problem admits, for every $p>1$, one-dimensional solutions with any prescribed number $m$ of nodal regions. We study the stability of these domains, as critical points of a related energy functional, with respect to volume-preserving deformations of the domain. We prove that, for $p$ large, the flat cylinders are stable as soon as their height exceeds a threshold growing linearly in $p$, while, for $p$ close to $1$, both stability and instability occur, with explicit thresholds depending on $m$ and on the first nontrivial Neumann eigenvalue of $ω$. These results rely on a detailed analysis of the one-dimensional profiles: we describe their asymptotic behaviour, and that of the first eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator, as $p\to1^+$ and $p\to+\infty$, we obtain expansions of the amplitude with explicit constants, and we prove global comparison results with respect to $p$, some of which are new also for positive solutions.

papers.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$. We prove that for every infinite cardinal $κ$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=κ$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. The extended functor commutes with direct sums and filtered colimits and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by Göbel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.

papers.title: Second critical exponent for a quasilinear Hardy--Hénon equation
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the parabolic Hardy--Hénon equation $\partial_tu=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p$ with slow diffusion $m>1$ and a potential which is singular at the origin, $-2<σ<0$, in dimension $N\ge3$. Above the Fujita exponent, global and blowing-up solutions coexist, and we show that the spatial decay of the initial data decides between them. The second critical exponent turns out to be the decay rate of an explicit singular steady state. Data decaying more slowly blow up in finite time, whatever their size, while faster decaying data which are small in a weighted supremum norm give rise to global solutions. At the critical decay, and in the range where the singular steady state exists, we construct bounded stationary barriers with exactly critical tail by gluing the singular steady state to regular steady states. We deduce that the critical amplitude separating global existence from blow-up lies between the amplitude of the singular steady state and an explicit constant. We also show that data lying below a proper fraction of the singular steady state produce global bounded solutions, and that the singular amplitude itself is attained by global solutions whenever a Joseph--Lundgren type condition fails. Conjectures and open problems complete the picture.

papers.title: Generalized principal eigenvalues for nonlocal operators with drift
papers.abstract: Nonlocal diffusion operators with a drift term naturally arise in models such as moving coordinate systems induced by climate change. This paper systematically studies several concepts of generalized principal eigenvalues (GPEs) for such operators. We allow the dispersal kernel to be heterogeneous and non-symmetric, and remove the standard global upper bound on the kernel (thereby covering the case of heavy-tailed dispersal kernels). To overcome the analytical difficulties brought by this more general setting, we establish a new Harnack-type inequality for non-compactly supported kernels, and apply homogenization and cut-off approximation techniques to derive two-sided bounds for the domain approximation limit of GPEs. Furthermore, under the almost periodic setting, we prove that the GPEs defined through different admissible test function spaces (e.g., \(C^1\) spaces with bounded derivatives and uniformly continuous function spaces in the viscosity sense) are completely coincident. This characterization reveals a fundamental unification: the limit result of principal eigenvalues under domain approximation by Coville and Hamel coincides exactly with the explicit variational formula by Du, Fang, and Ni, thereby bridging two previously independent theoretical results.

papers.title: Exact certification for conic optimization over quadratic modules: partitions of unity and recession directions
papers.abstract: We consider linear conic problems whose cone is a product of truncated quadratic modules, the sum-of-squares (SOS) side of the moment-SOS hierarchy. A floating-point solution is turned into an exact rational certificate in three steps: rounding, repair of each block residual by a constant, and absorption of the constants along a recession direction of the problem. The repair relies on strict partitions of unity in the quadratic modules. We characterize their existence, relate the canonical one to the analytic center of the dual pseudo-moment cone, Christoffel-Darboux polynomials and Pell equations, and we derive closed-form rational partitions for balls and boxes. The loss incurred by the certification is the optimal value of a recession problem, equal to a support function of the masses of the dual feasible pseudomoments. The method is illustrated on polynomial optimization, volume computation and positivity of polynomials along D-finite trajectories.

papers.title: Dolgopyat estimate for partially hyperbolic systems: limit theorems and exponential mixing
papers.abstract: We prove a Dolgopyat-type estimate for the twisted transfer operators of a class of two-dimensional partially hyperbolic endomorphisms of the torus, not necessarily skew-products. The twist satisfies a quantitative transversality condition on the cotangent dynamics of the associated three-dimensional extension which, in the skew-product case, is related to Tsujii's notions of transversality and partial captivity conditions. We use the main estimate to prove higher order expansions in the central and mixing local limit theorems for the two-dimensional base, including the case of several ergodic absolutely continuous invariant measures, and we prove exponential decay of correlations for the associated three-dimensional circle extensions, with a partially hyperbolic base.

papers.title: Normal form smoothing and spatial analyticity for the dispersion-generalized periodic KdV equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the persistence of spatial analyticity for solutions to the dispersion-generalized periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation $$\partial_tu-\partial_x|D_x|^αu+u\partial_xu=0,\qquadα\ge2.$$ For real-valued initial data $u_0\in G^{σ_0,s}(\mathbb T)$, with $σ_0>0$ and $s\ge-α/4$, we prove that the corresponding global solution satisfies $$u\in C([-T,T];G^{σ(T),s}(\mathbb T)),\qquadσ(T)=\min\left\{σ_0,\frac cT\right\},$$ for every $T>0$. As a consequence, our result improves the lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity established by Himonas, Kalisch, and Selberg (2017) for $2\leα<4$, including the classical periodic KdV equation, and establishes a unified $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the analyticity radius for every $α\ge2$. The main novelties are twofold. First, we introduce a normal form reduction at the level of the Gevrey energy, which reveals an additional cancellation in the cubic Gevrey commutator and separates it into a non-accumulating boundary correction and a quartic remainder. Second, we establish a global-in-time periodic $L_{t,x}^4$ estimate for the non-polynomial phase $k|k|^α$, valid for every real $α\ge2$. Together, these ingredients yield a refined almost conservation law and the $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity.

papers.title: A weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set under $\frak{p} = \frak{c}$
papers.abstract: Under $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$, Cantor space contains a weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set. This answers the consistency question of de Oliveira Rodrigues, dos Santos Ronchim, and Szeptycki. The hypothesis $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$ is compatible with the failure of the continuum hypothesis. The construction combines the finite-unions form of Hindman's theorem with Bell's characterization of $\mathfrak p$ in terms of $σ$-centered forcing. The increasing enumerations of the infinite members of the constructed space form an unbounded family under eventual domination. This makes the countable set of finite subsets of $ω$ a witness to the failure of the $λ$-property.

papers.title: Hamiltonicity and cycle factors in k-quasi-transitive digraphs of large diameter
papers.abstract: A digraph is $k$-quasi-transitive if the endpoints of every directed path of length $k$ are adjacent. In this paper, we prove that every strong non-bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian when $k\ge7$ is odd. Moreover, combined with the known even case, for $k\ge6$, we also prove that a strong bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it has a cycle factor. These answer two problems posed by Alva-Samos and Hernández-Cruz affirmatively [Journal of Graph Theory \textbf{96} (2021) 310--325].

papers.title: Identities of Representation of Lie subalgebras of the first Weyl algebra
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field. We study weak polynomial identities for pairs $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the first Weyl algebra over $F$ and $V$ is either a Lie subalgebra (under the usual Lie bracket) of $A$, or simply a vector subspace of $A$. Sometimes the weak identities of $(A,V)$, when $V$ is a Lie algebra, are called identities of representations of Lie algebras. Our starting point is the description of finite dimensional Lie algebras $L$ that can be embedded into the first Weyl algebra; this description was given by Rausch de Traubenberg, Slupinski and Tanasă in 2006. First we assume that $F$ is algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and describe a finite basis of the weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$ where $L=\mathfrak{sl}_2$. In order to obtain such a basis we invoke theorems by Razmyslov and by Trishin concerning the identities of infinite dimensional irreducible representations of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. Afterwards we consider $L$ as a filiform Lie algebra together with its concrete realisation inside the first Weyl algebra. We produce a finite basis of weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$, assuming $F$ to be infinite. Finally we study the weakest form of identities for $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the $n$-th Weyl algebra and $V$ is just a vector space - its canonical generating vector subspace. We deduce a basis of the weak identities in this case as well, once again assuming $F$ to be an infinite field, with no restriction on its characteristic. The same result was recently obtained by Dotsenko and Lopatin in characteristic $0$ by different methods. Our methods are combinatorial, we also use the theory developed by Razmyslov, and the representations of the symmetric and the general linear groups and their duality. We employ the characteristic-free description of the invariants of the symplectic group given by De Concini and Procesi.

papers.title: An Engineering Reading of the Bounded Halting Problem and Observable Properties of a Universal Machine
papers.abstract: The halting problem asks whether a program eventually halts, with unrestricted resources. Engineering systems instead certify bounded halting: given a program, an input, and a step budget T, decide whether the program halts within T steps. This paper studies two of its uses. First, it defines an exact finite-budget problem, placing the simulated program and the checker on the same unit-cost timescale, so the checker can be embedded in an adversarial program. A diagonal argument with explicit additive overhead shows that no fixed deterministic checker decides every instance within any fixed fraction of T below one, for large T. In the nondeterministic case, T bounds the branch depth allowed for a stable observable decision. Second, bounded-halting instances give adversarial tests for finitary universality, since a universal model must support arbitrary finite computations as T grows. The tests check resource growth with T, the absence of a fixed deliberation bound, and later access to intermediate data. They separate a fixed model with extendable external resources, a model family that grows with T, and a larger system built around a fixed component. For machine-learning systems, this identifies the resource growth a universality claim assumes and whether it fails for deployed models.

papers.title: Multiple $q$-zeta values as polynomials in partition multiplicities
papers.abstract: Writing multiple $q$-zeta values as sums over partitions, a conjecture of Bachmann, proved by Hirose, Maesaka and Watanabe by means of a recursion, says that polynomials in the parts and multiplicities can be replaced by polynomials in the multiplicities alone. We make this replacement explicit, derive from it bounds on weight and depth that make Bachmann's conjecture effective, and provide a closed formula for the Drop1 operator of Hirose, Maesaka, Seki and Watanabe.

papers.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
papers.abstract: We extend the method of Van Woerden \cite{woerden} to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\GLo-$equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\GLo$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\rint)$ obtained by Soulé \cite{soule_hermitian_bounds} and Houriet \cite{Juliet_PHD}. We emphasise the improvement of the general bound for $F=\mathbb Q$, unchanged since Soulé's work, and the independence of the discriminant exponent from the field degree for totally real and CM fields.

papers.title: Critical one-arm probabilities for metric-graph loop soups in dimensions $d\ge3$
papers.abstract: We study the critical Brownian loop soup on the metric graph $\widetilde{\mathbb Z}^d$. Using a new unified approach, we determine the one-arm probability up to multiplicative constants in all dimensions $d\ge3$. In particular, at the upper critical dimension $d_c=6$, we show that the one-arm probability is comparable to $r^{-2}(\log r)^{\frac12}$, and moreover, with high probability a box of radius $r$ contains on the order of $\log r$ macroscopic clusters, each with volume of order $r^4(\log r)^{-\frac12}$. For $d\ne6$, we recover the one-arm estimates of Cai and Ding, $r^{-(d-2)/2}$ for $d=3,4,5$ and $r^{-2}$ for $d>6$ (arXiv:2406.02397; Probab. Theory Relat.
