We show that this regulatory restriction is sufficient to guarantee finite-time convergence of best response dynamics to a pure Nash equilibrium under partial cooperation. In addition, we identify a sufficient condition under which an overload-free solution corresponds to a global minimizer of the potential function. Numerical experiments using one month of European flight data demonstrate that the proposed algorithm substantially reduces overload even with only minimal cooperation, achieving performance close to a centralized global mixed-integer optimizer and exceeding a centralized first-come-first-served baseline while requiring substantially less computation than centralized optimization. We further evaluate departure delay and fairness to quantify the operational cost of overload mitigation.

papers.title: Observable Dynamics and the Generic Coincidence of Milnor, Statistical, and Physical Attractors
papers.abstract: We study observable dynamics of generic continuous interval maps. We prove that, for a residual subset of $C([0,1])$, the global Milnor, statistical, and physical attractors coincide with the non-wandering set. Thus, for a typical interval map, the asymptotic dynamics detected by Lebesgue-almost every initial condition recovers all recurrent dynamics. The common attractor is a robust Cantor set of zero Hausdorff dimension. Moreover, every invariant probability measure has a basin of zero Lebesgue measure. We also present examples showing that, outside the generic setting, positive topological entropy may occur outside the global Milnor attractor, and the three attractors need not coincide.

papers.title: Quantifying discontinuity
papers.abstract: Given a compact space $X$ that does not admit an embedding (an injective continuous function) into $\mathbb{R}^d$, we study the discontinuity that any injective function $X \to \mathbb{R}^d$ must have. To this end, we define a scale invariant modulus of discontinuity and obtain general lower bounds, thus obtaining quantified nonembeddability results of Haefliger--Weber type. Moreover, we establish analogous lower bounds for simplicial complexes that do not admit an almost $r$-embedding in $\mathbb{R}^d$, thus obtaining a quantified version of the topological Tverberg theorem.

papers.title: Bilevel Learning via Strategically Inexact Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization is a central tool in computational imaging for high-dimensional hyperparameter tuning; prominent applications include learning data-adaptive regularizers and optimizing forward operators in variational regularization. However, due to the nested nature of the problem, exact gradients with respect to the parameters (so-called hypergradients) are not available: the precision of the hypergradient is linearly related to the computational cost, thus requiring algorithms which can solve the problem without unnecessary precision. In learned-regularizer pipelines, the inner reconstruction solver is typically run for a fixed number of iterations, leaving the hypergradient accuracy uncontrolled and existing convergence theory inapplicable. In this work, we analyze the schedules that practitioners actually run: we prove convergence of inexact stochastic bilevel optimization and establish rates under both decaying accuracy and step size schedules, showing that, with optimal configurations, convergence occurs at an $O(k^{-1/4})$ rate in expectation. This is the optimal rate of nonconvex stochastic gradient descent and matches single-loop stochastic bilevel methods; with warm-started inner solves, total costs also agree up to constants. Experiments on image denoising and inpainting with convex ridge regularizers and input-convex neural networks confirm our analysis: decreasing step sizes improve stability, accuracy scheduling is more critical than step size strategy, and adaptive preconditioning (e.g., Adam) further boosts performance, particularly for input-convex neural networks. In a budget-matched comparison with four state-of-the-art single-loop methods, accuracy-scheduled stochastic gradient descent and its Adam variant attain the highest test peak signal-to-noise ratio.

papers.title: Boscia.jl: A review and tutorial
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer nonlinear optimization (MINLP) comprises a large class of problems that are challenging to solve and exhibit a wide range of structures. The Boscia framework (Hendrych et al., 2025b) focuses on convex MINLP where the nonlinearity appears in the objective only. This paper provides an overview of the framework, showcases extensions post-publication and practical examples to illustrate its use and customizability. One key aspect is the integration and exploitation of Frank-Wolfe methods as continuous solvers within a branch-and-bound framework, enabling inexact node processing, warm-starting and explicit use of combinatorial structure among others. Three examples illustrate its flexibility, the user control over the optimization process and the benefit of oracle-based access to the objective and its gradient. Additionally, ablation studies are performed on the three examples to investigate the performance impact of the different features and customizations. The aim of this tutorial is to provide readers with an understanding of the main principles of the framework.

papers.title: Stochastic Derivative Estimation for Discontinuous Sample Performances: A Leibniz Integration Perspective
papers.abstract: Based on the multidimensional Leibniz integral rule, we propose a novel unbiased stochastic derivative estimation framework for sample performance functions that are discontinuous in the parameter of interest. In this framework, for general discontinuities, a change of variables followed by the Leibniz integral rule generally yields a multi-run estimator, whereas for indicator-type discontinuities, a suitable transformation of the sample performance leads directly to a single-run estimator. The new framework includes existing likelihood ratio (LR)-based approaches as special cases and applies more broadly. In particular, it encompasses generalized LR (GLR) methods and the new formulation permits us to obtain much milder and simpler sufficient regularity conditions for these estimators to be unbiased, compared with the conditions given in previous papers. We also provide guidance on how to construct efficient single-run estimators in settings where existing methods may require the simulation of multiple sample paths or may be inapplicable. We validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework through an inventory-price control problem.

papers.title: Strongly Regular Graphs of Rank Four
papers.abstract: Strongly regular graphs are regular graphs with a constant number of common neighbours between adjacent vertices, and a constant number of common neighbours between non-adjacent vertices. These graphs have been of great interest over the last few decades and often give rise to interesting groups of automorphisms. In this paper we take a reverse approach, and leverage strong classification results on rank four permutation groups to classify the strongly regular graphs which yield such groups as a group of automorphisms.

papers.title: Model-Adaptive Simulation of Hierarchical Shallow Water Moment Equations in One Dimension
papers.abstract: Shallow free surface flows are often characterized by both subdomains that require high modeling complexity and subdomains that can be sufficiently accurately modeled with low modeling complexity. Moreover, these subdomains may change in time as the water flows through the domain. This motivates the need for space and time adaptivity in the simulation of shallow free surface flows. In this paper, we develop the first adaptive simulations using the recently developed Shallow Water Moment Equations, which are an extension of the standard Shallow Water Equations that allow for vertically changing velocity profiles by including additional variables and equations. The model-specific modeling complexity of a shallow water moment model is determined by its order. The higher the order of the model, the more variables and equations are included in the model. Shallow water moment models are ideally suited for adaptivity because they are hierarchical such that low-order models and high-order models share the same structure. To enable adaptive simulations, we propose two approaches for the coupling of the varying-order shallow water moment equations at their boundary interfaces. The first approach dynamically updates padded state variables but cannot be written in conservative form, while the second approach uses fixed padded state variable values of zero and reduces to conservative form for conservative moment equations. The switching procedure between high-order models and low-order models is based on a new set of model error estimators, originating from a decomposition of the high-order models. Numerical results of a dam break and of the collision of a dam-break wave with a smooth wave for different friction parameter values yield accurate results, while achieving speedups up to 40 percent compared to a non-adaptive model with fixed modeling complexity.

papers.title: Derived isogenies between abelian varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a derived Torelli Theorem for twisted abelian varieties. Starting from this, we explore the relation between derived isogenies and classical isogenies. We show that two abelian varieties of dimension $\geq 2$ are derived isogenous if and only if they are principally isogenous over fields of characteristic zero. This generalized the result for abelian surfaces and completely solves the question raised in [arXiv:2108.08710].

papers.title: Efficient and Robust Carathéodory-Steinitz Pruning of Positive Discrete Measures
papers.abstract: In many applications, one seeks to approximate integration against a positive measure of interest by a positive discrete measure: a numerical quadrature rule with positive weights. One common desired discretization property is moment preservation over a finite dimensional function space, e.g., bounded-degree polynomials. Carathéodory's theorem asserts that if there is any finitely supported quadrature rule with more nodes than the dimension of the given function space, one can form a smaller (and hence more efficient) positive, nested, quadrature rule that preserves the moments of the original rule. We describe an efficient streaming procedure for Carathéodory-Steinitz pruning, a numerical procedure that implements Carathéodory's theorem for this measure compression. The new algorithm makes use of Givens rotations and on-demand storage of arrays to successfully prune very large rules whose storage complexity only depends on the dimension of the function space. This approach improves on a naive implementation of Carathéodory-Steinitz pruning whose runtime and storage complexity are quadratic and linear, respectively, in the size of the original measure. We additionally prove mathematical stability properties of our method with respect to a set of admissible, total-variation perturbations of the original measure. Our method is compared to two alternative approaches with larger storage requirements: non-negative least squares and linear programming, and we demonstrate comparable runtimes, with improved stability and storage robustness. Finally, we demonstrate practical usage of this algorithm to generate quadrature for discontinuous Galerkin finite element simulations on cut-cell meshes.

papers.title: Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,u}(t)$ via a Rank-Zero Elliptic Curve
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the even monic degree-8 cuboid polynomial $P_{a,u}(t)$ introduced by R. A. Sharipov in the first-cuboid specialization of his cuboid equations. For nonzero integers $a,u$ with $u^2\neq a^2$ we prove that $P_{a,u}(t)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[t]$ (equivalently, in $\mathbb{Q}[t]$), thus confirming Sharipov's irreducibility conjecture in this two-parameter case. Over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$ we have a factorization $P_{a,u}(t)=H_-(t)H_+(t)$ into two conjugate quartics. We show that reducibility of either $H_\pm$ would force the discriminant of a certain quadratic in $S=t^2$ to be a square in $K$, which in turn implies (via $τ=(au/Δ)^2$, where $Δ=u^2-a^2$) the existence of a rational point $(y,v)\in\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the genus-one quartic $\mathcal{C}: v^2=16y^4+136y^2+1$ with $y^2=τ$. We give an explicit isomorphism $\overline{\mathcal{C}}\simeq E$ with the elliptic curve $E: Y^2=X(X-8)(X-9)$, which has conductor $48$ and Mordell-Weil rank $0$. Enumerating $E(\mathbb{Q})$ and tracing back to $\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{Q})$ rules out the only possible values $τ\in\{0,1/4\}$, and hence excludes any further factorization of $H_\pm$ in $K[t]$. A quadratic Galois descent then yields the irreducibility of $P_{a,u}(t)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Infinite-Time Mean Field FBSDEs and the Associated Elliptic Master Equations
papers.abstract: We study discounted infinite-time mean field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) and the associated elliptic master equations, which were introduced in [20] as mathematical tools for solving discounted infinite-time mean field games. We first establish stability and flow properties, identify the backward decoupling field with the spatial derivative of the equilibrium value function, and prove that the value function is a viscosity solution of the master equation. Under additional smoothness and quantitative stability assumptions, we construct its Lions-derivative and the required higher-order derivatives using variational results from a companion paper [21]. These results show that the value function is a classical solution of the elliptic master equation. We also prove that the value function is the unique displacement-monotone regular solution.

papers.title: Observability estimates for the Schrödinger equation on the equilateral triangle
papers.abstract: We prove observability estimates for the Schrödinger equation posed on the equilateral triangle in the plane, under both Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions. No geometric control condition is required on the rough localization functions that we consider. This is the first result of this kind on a non-toric domain in the compact setting. Our strategy is to exploit Pinsky's tiling argument to deduce this result from observability estimates on rational twisted tori. These are obtained via propagation of singularities, adapting arguments from Burq and Zworski. The later require Strichartz estimates on such twisted rational tori, that we derive from Zygmund inequalities in the same geometric setting, also providing the sharp constant. Strichartz estimates on the equilateral triangle are also derived from this analysis.

papers.title: Holomorphicity of parabolic stable minimal surfaces of high codimension
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Micallef says that if $F \colon (Σ, g) \to \mathbb{R}^4$ is a stable minimal immersion of an oriented $2$-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold (that is parabolic) into $\mathbb{R}^4$, it is necessarily holomorphic with respect to some parallel orthogonal complex structure on $\mathbb{R}^4$. We generalize this theorem by replacing $\mathbb{R}^4$ with $\mathbb{R}^{2 + 2k}$ for any codimension $2k$, under the additional hypothesis that the normal bundle $N Σ$ is equipped with a complex structure that is compatible with the induced metric and parallel with respect to the induced connection. This is a necessary assumption for such a theorem to hold (as it is a consequence of the conclusion), and it is automatically satisfied in the classical case $k=1$. We also briefly discuss possible further generalizations of such a result to other calibrations and to Smith maps.

papers.title: Heavy repulsion of clusters in Bernoulli percolation
papers.abstract: We consider Bernoulli$(p)$ percolation on (non)unimodular quasi-transitive graphs and prove that, almost surely, for any two clusters $C$ and $C'$, the set of vertices in $C$ within distance one of $C'$ is light, i.e.\ it has finite total modular weight. This is a significant step towards resolving a longstanding question of Häggström, Peres, and Schonmann, and a generalization of a theorem of Timár, who proved the same result in the unimodular setting. We present two proofs. The first one is a hyperfiniteness argument that is specific to Bernoulli$(p)$ percolation and is new even in the unimodular case; the second is more general and follows Timár's approach, but requires the development of weighted analogues of several classical unimodular results. The new insight in both proofs is nonhyperfiniteness, which we obtain from the recently developed theory of measure class preserving equivalence relations and graphs. In particular, along the way we establish a generalization of a theorem of Benjamini, Lyons, and Schramm on the existence of an invariant random subgraph with positive weighted Cheeger constant, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: Stability and asymptotic behaviour of one-dimensional solutions in cylinders
papers.abstract: We consider positive one-dimensional solutions of a Lane-Emden relative Dirichlet problem in a cylinder and study their stability/instability properties as the energy varies with respect to domain perturbations. This depends on the exponent $p >1$ of the nonlinearity and we obtain results for $p$ close to 1 and for $p$ large. This is achieved by a careful asymptotic analysis of the one-dimensional solution as $p \to 1$ or $p \to \infty$, which is of independent interest. It allows to detect the limit profile and other qualitative properties of these solutions.

papers.title: Optimal expansion in unitary groups I: Golden adelic groups and cutoff
papers.abstract: In this paper and its companion [DEP2] we construct and study special generating sets for $p$-arithmetic unitary Lie groups, extending the seminal works of Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak to higher dimensions. The real embeddings of our sets form optimal topological generators for compact unitary Lie groups, and their $p$-adic embeddings give rise to Cayley graphs and complexes over finite unitary groups, which exhibit the cutoff phenomenon. In the current paper we prove two main results: First, we construct $p$-arithmetic lattices in $PU_4$ and $PU_8$ which act transitively on their corresponding Bruhat-Tits buildings. These groups are used to construct Golden Gate sets on two and three qubits, which have optimal circuit length and efficient compiling algorithms. Second, we study the cutoff phenomenon for quotients of the Bruhat-Tits building of a general semisimple $p$-adic group. We show that cutoff occurs for quotients which satisfy either the Ramanujan property or the weaker Sarnak-Xue Density Hypothesis (SXDH). For this purpose we bound the operator norms of a large class of Hecke operators in terms of the rate of decay of unitary representations. In the companion paper [DEP2], we prove such a SXDH result for unitary groups.

papers.title: A strong finiteness condition for smashing localisations
papers.abstract: We define a class of smashing localisations which we call compactly central and classify compactly central localisations of the category of spectra and of the category of $p$-local spectra. In both cases the compactly central localisations are those finite localisations which correspond to closed subsets of the Balmer spectrum with quasicompact complement. In particular, the finite chromatic localisation $L_n^f$ is compactly central. We generalise our results to the category $D(X)$ for $X$ a quasicompact quasiseparated scheme with an ample family of line bundles. Analogously to spectra, we show that compactly central localisations of $D(X)$ correspond to closed subsets of $X$ with quasicompact complement. This includes any scheme which is quasiprojective over an affine base.

papers.title: Combinatorics behind discriminants of polynomial systems
papers.abstract: Polymatroids provide a suitable combinatorial framework for enumerating components of discriminants of polynomial systems, a generalization of classical discriminants introduced by Gelfand, Kapranov, and Zelevinsky for multivariate polynomials. We explore the relations among polymatroids, their induced matroids, and principal partitions, following works of Fujishige and Narayanan. We obtain a sufficient condition for a polymatroid contraction to commute with taking the induced matroid. We establish a correspondence between different classes of polymatroids and critical values of their principal partitions. Three new conjectures about discriminants of polynomial systems are formulated.

papers.title: Entropy stable finite difference methods via entropy correction artificial viscosity and knapsack limiting
papers.abstract: Entropy stable methods have become increasingly popular in the field of computational fluid dynamics. They often work by satisfying some form of a discrete entropy inequality: a discrete form of the 2nd law of thermodynamics. Schemes which satisfy a (semi-)discrete entropy inequality typically behave much more robustly, and do so in a way that is hyperparameter free. Recently, a new strategy was introduced to construct entropy stable discontinuous Galerkin methods: knapsack limiting, which blends together a low order, positivity preserving, and entropy stable scheme with a high order accurate scheme, in order to produce a high order accurate, entropy stable, and positivity preserving scheme. Another recent strategy introduces an entropy correction artificial viscosity into a high order scheme, aiming to satisfy a cell entropy inequality. In this work, we introduce the techniques of knapsack limiting and artificial viscosity for finite difference discretizations. The proposed schemes preserve high order accuracy in sufficiently smooth conditions, are entropy stable, and are hyperparameter free. Moreover, the proposed knapsack limiting scheme provably preserves positivity for the compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. Both schemes achieve this goal without significant performance tradeoffs compared to state of the art stabilized schemes.

papers.title: Orthomesy and promotion on self-dual posets
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of orthomesy, which is related to homomesy, a central phenomenon in dynamical algebraic combinatorics. An orbit is said to be orthomesic with respect to a statistic if the orbit's average statistic value is equal to the global average. We particularly focus on the action of promotion on increasing labelings of certain fence posets called zig-zag posets, and two statistics, the antipodal sum statistic and the total sum statistic. We classify all of the orthomesic promotion orbits for the zig-zag poset with four elements. Along the way, we investigate how homomesy of one action can be used to find orthomesic orbits for another action, for the same fixed statistic. We prove several general results which can be used to find infinite families of orthomesic orbits for any self-dual poset that has an order-reversing involution.

papers.title: Minimax Analysis of Estimation Problems in Coherent Imaging
papers.abstract: Unlike conventional imaging modalities, such as magnetic resonance imaging, which are often well described by a linear regression framework, coherent imaging systems follow a significantly more complex model. In these systems, the task is to estimate the unknown image ${\boldsymbol x}_o \in \mathbb{R}^n$ from observations ${\boldsymbol y}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol y}_L \in \mathbb{R}^m$ of the form $ {\boldsymbol y}_l = A_l X_o {\boldsymbol w}_l + {\boldsymbol z}_l, l = 1, \ldots, L,$ where $X_o = \mathrm{diag}({\boldsymbol x}_o)$ is an $n \times n$ diagonal matrix, ${\boldsymbol w}_1,\ldots, {\boldsymbol w}_L \stackrel{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,I_n)$ represent speckle noise, and ${\boldsymbol z}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol z}_L \stackrel{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,σ_z^2 I_m)$ denote additive noise. The matrices $A_1, \ldots, A_L \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ are known forward operators determined by the imaging system. Here, $m$ can be less than $n$, which makes the linear model ill conditioned, and we collect $L$ measurements of the whole setup and try to quantify the loss. The fundamental limits of conventional imaging systems have been extensively studied through sparse linear regression models. However, the limits of coherent imaging systems remain largely unexplored. The goal of this paper is to close this gap by showing, for the first time in the literature, that the minimax risk of estimating ${\boldsymbol x}_o$ scales as $\frac{\max\{σ_z^4,\, m^2,\, n^2\}\, k \log n}{m^2 n L},$ where the parameter $k$ quantifies the effective complexity of the image class.

papers.title: Curve semistable Higgs bundles and smooth projective varieties whose canonical bundle is ample
papers.abstract: Considering the so-called Simpson system on smooth projective varieties, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, whose canonical bundle is ample, we provide a new proof of the stability of this Higgs bundle, which in turn yields another proof of the Miyaoka-Yau inequality. When equality holds, we prove that the discriminant class of the Simpson system is numerically trivial and that this Higgs bundle is curve semistable. This result follows from a study of the relations between weak ampleness, numerically effectiveness for Higgs bundles that ``feel'' the Higgs field and (semi)stability. Moreover, we obtain another proof of the algebraic hyperbolicity of these varieties which provides a lower bound on a positive real constant related to this property; to best of our knowledge, this is the first and only result of this type. We conjecture that a similar lower bound holds for smooth projective varieties whose canonical bundle is ample.

papers.title: Weighted eigenvalues of Dirac operators: complete continuity and comparison
papers.abstract: We give a min-max characterization of all of the weighted Dirac eigenvalues, and show that the weighted eigenvalues and eigenspaces of Dirac operators are continuous with respect to weak $L^p$ convergence of the weight, for any $p>n$. Moreover, we establish a comparison result for such weighted eigenvalue problems including the case of nontrivial harmonic spinors.

papers.title: Birational geometry of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the biregular and birational geometry of degree 6 del Pezzo surfaces with Picard number 1, defined over an arbitrary perfect field. Using Galois cohomology techniques, we obtain an explicit description of cocycles for such surfaces and describe the Severi-Brauer varieties associated with them, recovering the biregular classification of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. We then compute the automorphism groups of such surfaces, describe their closed points in general position and investigate the structure of Sarkisov links at such points and the corresponding birational models, answering a question of M. Rost. Using this description, we show that degree 6 del Pezzo surfaces are the only solid surfaces that admit infinite pliability. We also find a system of generators and relations for the groups of birational transformations of such surfaces and use it to construct nontrivial quotients of these groups, including free groups on uncountable sets.

papers.title: Noncommutative marked surfaces II: tagged triangulations, clusters, and their symmetries
papers.abstract: The aim of the paper is to define noncommutative cluster structure on several algebras ${\mathcal A}$ related to marked surfaces possibly with orbifold points of various orders, which includes noncommutative clusters, i.e., embeddings of a given group $G$ into the multiplicative monoid ${\mathcal A}^\times$ and an action of a certain braid-like group $Br_{\mathcal A}$ by automorphisms of each cluster group in a compatible way. For punctured surfaces we construct new symmetries, noncommutative tagged clusters and establish a noncommutative Laurent Phenomenon.

papers.title: Entropy Stable Nodal Discontinuous Galerkin Methods via Quadratic Knapsack Limiting
papers.abstract: Lin, Chan (High order entropy stable discontinuous Galerkin spectral element methods through subcell limiting, 2024) enforces a cell entropy inequality for nodal discontinuous Galerkin methods by combining flux corrected transport (FCT)-type limiting and a knapsack solver, which determines optimal limiting coefficients that result in a semi-discrete cell entropy inequality while preserving nodal bounds. In this work, we provide a slight modification of this approach, where we utilize a quadratic knapsack problem instead of a standard linear knapsack problem. We prove that this quadratic knapsack problem can be reduced to efficient scalar root-finding. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed quadratic knapsack limiting strategy is efficient and results in a semi-discretization with improved regularity in time compared with linear knapsack limiting, while resulting in fewer adaptive timesteps in shock-type problems.

papers.title: Polyhedral divisors and algebraic torus actions over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract: We provide a algebro-geometric combinatorial description of normal affine varieties endowed with an effective action of an algebraic torus over arbitrary fields. This description is achieved in terms of proper polyhedral divisors endowed with a Galois semilinear action.

papers.title: Prime order torsion on elliptic curves over number fields. Part I: Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotics of the set $S(d)$ of possible prime orders of $K$-rational points on elliptic curves over number fields $K$ of degree $d$ as $d$ tends to infinity. Assuming some conjectures on the sparsity of newforms of weight $2$ and prime level with unexpectedly high analytic rank, we show that $\max S(d) \le 3d + 1$ for sufficiently large even $d$ and $\max S(d) = o(d)$ for odd $d$. This gives a significant (but conjectural) improvement on the currently best known upper bound $\max S(d) \le (3^{d/2} + 1)^2$ due to Oesterlé.

papers.title: Asymptotic exponential moments of two-dimensional additive functionals above subcriticality
papers.abstract: We introduce new asymptotic formulas for the exponential moments of rescaled additive functionals of two-dimensional Brownian motion, extending the analysis to parameter regimes that go beyond the subcritical case underlying distributional limits. As an application, we develop a probabilistic-analytic approximation for the two-dimensional Laplacian with a singular perturbation at the origin. This method describes the perturbed Laplacian by combining analytic characteristics of the Kallianpur-Robbins and Kasahara-Kotani laws.

papers.title: Semimartingale characteristics of the two-dimensional stochastic heat equation at criticality
papers.abstract: We characterize the sample-path structure of the two-dimensional stochastic heat equation at criticality. The main theorems provide a complete, pathwise description of its semimartingale characteristics and establish explicit, exact formulas for the covariation measure. The proof derives an asymptotic expansion for the covariation measures of regularized approximate solutions by integrating techniques from quantum-solvable operators into stochastic integration theory.

papers.title: The Spear and the Ring: Emergent Structures in Magnetic Colloidal Suspensions
papers.abstract: We study from a mathematical point of view the nanoparticle model of a magnetic colloid, presented by G. Klughertz. Our objective is to obtain properties of stable stationary structures that arise in the long-time limit for the magnetic nanoparticles dynamics following this model. In this article, we present a detailed study of two specific structures using techniques from the calculus of variations. The first, called the spear, consists of a chain of aligned particles interacting via a Lennard-Jones potential. We establish existence and uniqueness results, derive bounds on the distances between neighboring particles, and provide a sharp asymptotic description as the number of particles tends to infinity. The second structure, the ring, features particles uniformly distributed along a circle. We prove its existence and uniqueness and derive an explicit formula for its radius.

papers.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $ψ$-Fueter operator
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.

papers.title: Stochastic Optimal Control with Measurable Coefficients and Applications
papers.abstract: We consider fully non-linear stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients and (local) uniformly elliptic diffusion. Using the theory of $L^p$-viscosity solutions, we show existence of an $L^p$-viscosity solution $v\in W_{\rm loc}^{2,p}$ of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, which, in turn, is also a strong solution (i.e. it satisfies the HJB equation pointwise a.e.). We are then led to prove verification theorems, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality. These results allow us to construct optimal feedback controls and to characterize the value function as the unique $L^p$-viscosity solution of the HJB equation. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results for fully non-linear stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients. We use the theory developed to solve a stochastic optimal control problem arising in economics within the context of optimal advertising.

papers.title: From multitype branching to multitype coalescents and back: Genealogies, duality and examples
papers.abstract: We establish new connections between multitype $Λ$-coalescents and multitype continuous state branching processes (CSBPs) through duality with a $Λ-$Wright-Fisher frequency process, and a homeomorphism between the spaces of the two classes of processes. The approach relies on a sequential sampling procedure for the frequency process of multitype CSBPs and provides an interpretation of multitype $Λ-$coalescents as the local genealogies of multitype CSBPs which gives further insight into different approaches to generalise $Λ-$coalescents to the multitype setup. As an application of the homeomorphism, we introduce and discuss multitype Beta-coalescents as the local genealogy of multitype $α$-stable branching processes.

papers.title: Reliably Learn to Trim Multiparametric Quadratic Programs via Constraint Removal
papers.abstract: In a wide range of applications, we are required to rapidly solve a sequence of convex multiparametric quadratic programs (mp-QPs) on resource-limited hardwares. This is a nontrivial task and has been an active topic for decades in control and optimization communities. Observe that the main computational cost of existing solution algorithms lies in addressing many linear inequality constraints, though their majority are redundant and removing them will not change the optimal solution. This work learns from the results of previously solved mp-QP(s), based on which we propose novel methods to reliably trim (unsolved) mp-QPs via constraint removal, and the trimmed mp-QPs can be much cheaper to solve. Then, we extend to trim mp-QPs of model predictive control (MPC) whose parameter vectors are sampled from linear systems. Importantly, both online and offline solved mp-QPs can be utilized to adaptively trim mp-QPs in the closed-loop system. We show that the number of linear inequalities in the trimmed mp-QP of MPC decreases to zero in a finite timestep, which also can be reduced by increasing offline computation. Finally, simulations are performed to demonstrate the efficiency of our trimming method in removing redundant constraints.

papers.title: Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction
papers.abstract: It is well-known that conditioning a supercritical (multi-type) branching process on the event that it eventually becomes extinct yields a subcritical branching process. We study the corresponding inverse problem: given a subcritical branching process, does there exist a supercritical branching process with the property that when we condition it on extinction, we get back the original subcritical branching process? We show that such a supercritical branching process (which we call a conjugate branching process) exists under mild hypotheses on the original subcritical branching process. We also show by example that if there are at least two types, then the conjugate branching process is not necessarily unique. Our results are relevant to the problem of constructing natural random planar maps whose scaling limit is given by supercritical Liouville quantum gravity. Moreover, conjugate branching processes can also be used to give alternative evolutionary hypotheses in cancer modeling.

papers.title: Community detection with the Bethe-Hessian
papers.abstract: The Bethe-Hessian matrix, introduced by Saade, Krzakala, and Zdeborová (2014), is a Hermitian matrix designed for applying spectral clustering algorithms to sparse networks. Rather than employing a non-symmetric and high-dimensional non-backtracking operator, a spectral method based on the Bethe-Hessian matrix is conjectured to also reach the Kesten-Stigum detection threshold in the sparse stochastic block model (SBM). We provide the first rigorous analysis of the Bethe-Hessian spectral method in the SBM under both the bounded expected degree and the growing degree regimes. Specifically, we demonstrate that: (i) When the expected degree $d\geq 2$, the number of negative outliers of the Bethe-Hessian matrix can consistently estimate the number of blocks above the Kesten-Stigum threshold, thus confirming a conjecture from Saade, Krzakala, and Zdeborová (2014) for $d\geq 2$. (ii) For sufficiently large $d$, its eigenvectors can be used to achieve weak recovery. (iii) As $d\to\infty$, we establish the concentration of the locations of its negative outlier eigenvalues, and weak consistency can be achieved via a spectral method based on the Bethe-Hessian matrix.

papers.title: An exact column generation algorithm for load balancing in capacity sharing networks
papers.abstract: Capacity sharing networks are typical heterogeneous communication networks widely applied in information and communications technology (ICT) field. In such networks, resources like bandwidth, spectrum, computation and storage are shared among various communication services. Meanwhile, the issue of network congestion is always a prominent challenge. To handle network congestion essentially needs to solve the load balancing of networks. In this paper, for capacity sharing networks, we formulate their load balancing problem as a maximum multi-commodity flow problem. For such a problem, always a large-scale linear programming, the column generation algorithm is a commonly used and crucial method to solve it. In each iteration, this algorithm involves solving a linear programming subproblem and determining whether to terminate or generate a new column for inclusion in the subproblem. This iterative procedure of solving and checking continues throughout the algorithm. Nevertheless, since the checking subproblem is NP-hard, its solution significantly impacts the overall efficiency of the algorithm. In this paper, we innovatively convert the checking subproblem into a single-constrained shortest path (SCSP) subproblem. By exactly solving the SCSP subproblem, we can obtain the optimal solution to the checking subproblem with same or less computing time. Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves computational efficiency comparable to heuristic algorithms while outperforming other state-of-the-art algorithms by at least an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
papers.abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel--Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point $ξ$, with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at $ξ$ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel--Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at $ξ$ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher--Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.

papers.title: Submersion constructions for geometries with parallel skew torsion
papers.abstract: In the absence of a de Rham decomposition theorem for geometries with torsion, we develop and unify ways to view a geometry with parallel skew torsion as the total space of a locally defined, not necessarily unique Riemannian submersion with totally geodesic fibers. We complete and extend the Cleyton-Swann classification of irreducible such geometries and characterize the cases where the stabilizer of the torsion is larger than the holonomy. As a byproduct, we obtain structure results on Gray manifolds, nearly parallel G$_2$-manifolds and Sasaki manifolds with reducible holonomy.

papers.title: Foundations on k-contact geometry
papers.abstract: $k$-Contact geometry is a generalisation of contact geometry to analyse field theories. As a main goal, we develop an approach to $k$-contact geometry based on distributions that are distributionally maximally non-integrable and admit, locally, $k$ commuting supplementary Lie symmetries: the $k$-contact distributions. More specifically, we investigate the existence of Reeb vector fields for $k$-contact distributions, $k$-contact Lie groups are defined and studied, and, after analysing compact manifolds, a Weinstein conjecture for a product of $k$ compact contact manifolds is discussed. Polarisations for $k$-contact distributions are introduced and it is shown that a polarised $k$-contact distribution is locally diffeomorphic to the Cartan distribution of the first-order jet bundle over a fibre bundle of rank $k$. We relate $k$-contact manifolds to presymplectic and $k$-symplectic manifolds on fibre bundles of larger dimension and define types of submanifolds in $k$-contact geometry. We study Hamilton--De Donder--Weyl equations on $k$-contact Lie groups. A theory of $k$-contact Hamiltonian vector fields is developed, and we describe characteristics of Lie symmetries for first-order partial differential equations in a $k$-contact Hamiltonian manner. We use our techniques to analyse Hamilton--Jacobi and Dirac equations, types of Engel and Goursat distributions, physical problems, and control systems. The work also presents introductory results so as to make it more self-contained.

papers.title: Valuation Model of Chinese Convertible Bonds Based on Monte Carlo Simulation
papers.abstract: We tackle the problem of pricing Chinese convertible bonds(CCBs) using Monte Carlo simulation and dynamic programming. At each exercise time, we use the state variables of the underlying stock to regress the continuation value, and apply standard backward induction to get the coefficients from the current time to time zero. This process ultimately determines the CCB price. We then apply this pricing method in simulations and evaluate an underpriced strategy: taking long positions in the 10 most undervalued CCBs and rebalancing daily. The results show that this strategy significantly outperforms the benchmark double-low strategy. In practice, CCB issuers often use a downward adjustment clause to prevent financial distress when a put provision is triggered. Therefore, we model the downward adjustment clause as a probabilistic event that triggers the put provision, thereby integrating it with the put provision in a straightforward manner.

papers.title: $SLE_6$ and 2-d critical bond percolation on the square lattice
papers.abstract: Through the rotational invariance of the 2-d critical bond percolation exploration path on the square lattice we express Smirnov's edge parafermionic observable as a sum of two new edge observables. With the help of these two new edge observables we can apply the discrete harmonic analysis and conformal mapping theory to prove the convergence of the 2-d critical bond percolation exploration path on the square lattice to the trace of $SLE_6$ as the mesh size of the lattice tends to zero.

papers.title: A Bregman-Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Maximum Weight Independent Set Problem
papers.abstract: We propose a scalable approximate algorithm for the NP-hard maximum-weight independent set problem, based on dual coordinate descent applied to a smoothed clique-cover LP relaxation. Our method, a variant of the Bregman/Sinkhorn algorithm, employs entropy smoothing with a novel duality-gap-based smoothing scheduling strategy that empirically outperforms standard feasibility scheduling for the relaxed problem. Our new projection to the primal feasible set enables accurate duality gap estimation. Combined with a basic primal heuristic leveraging reduced costs, our approach yields high-quality integer solutions. On real-world datasets, it efficiently finds high-quality approximate solutions for graphs with up to 882,000 nodes and 344 million edges within seconds.

papers.title: On the Existence, Smoothness, and Order-Two Entire Extension of the Navier-Stokes Equations in Critical Fourier-Besov Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish global existence, smoothness, and physical energy bounds for solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) under a scaling-critical smallness condition in the homogeneous Fourier-Besov spaces $\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined as the weak space $F \dot{B}^{\frac{d}{p'}-1}_{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$ and $F \dot{B}^{-1}_{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at the endpoint $p = 1$. By combining the nonassociative algebra of Riesz convolutions and spaces of functions dominated by Fourier-Caloric flows $\mathscr{V}(λ)$ with a Littlewood-Paley dyadic atomic decomposition, we prove that the Catalan Picard series converges globally whenever $\|\widehat{u^0}\|_{\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)} < Cν$. This threshold reaches the sharp boundary of well-posedness prior to norm inflation, strictly improves upon the classical Fujita-Kato $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ condition, and admits explicit multiscale Schwartz initial data with arbitrarily large $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $H^k(\mathbb{R}^d)$ norms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for positive times, the velocity and pressure fields admit an analytic extension to the complex domain $\mathbb{C}^d$, forming a smooth curve of entire vector fields of order two. Finally, for arbitrary initial data outside the critical ball, we employ fractional Riesz convolutions $*_α$ ($0 < α< 1$) to derive an explicit lower bound $T_{\max}(u^0) > 0$ on the lifespan of smooth, order-two entire solutions, establishing a sharp dichotomy between global continuation via viscous re-entry into the critical ball and a scaling-invariant lower blow-up rate.

papers.title: The extension of traces for Sobolev mappings between manifolds
papers.abstract: The compact Riemannian manifolds $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ for which the trace operator from the first-order Sobolev space of mappings $\smash{\dot{W}}^{1, p} (\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ to the fractional Sobolev-Slobodeckiĭ space $\smash{\smash{\dot{W}}^{1 - 1/p, p}} (\partial \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ is surjective when $1 < p < \dim \mathcal{M}$ are characterised. The traces are extended using a new construction which can be carried out assuming the absence of the known topological and analytical obstructions. When $p \ge \dim \mathcal{M}$ the same construction provides a Sobolev extension with linear estimates for maps that have a continuous extension, provided that the known analytical obstructions to such a control are not present.

papers.title: Unique continuation estimates for Baouendi--Grushin equations on cylinders
papers.abstract: We prove time-pointwise quantitative unique continuation estimates for the evolution operators associated to (fractional powers of) the Baouendi--Grushin operators on the cylinder $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^d$. Spectral inequalities are deduced, relating for functions from spectral subspaces associated to finite energy intervals their $L^2$-norm on the whole cylinder $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb T^d$ to the $L^2$-norm on so-called thick subsets of $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb T^d$. As a byproduct, we also obtain results on exact and approximate null-controllabilty for the corresponding evolution systems. This extends and complements results obtained recently by the authors and by Jaming and Wang.

papers.title: Time-Averages along Partial Orbits for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate the convergence of time-averages of continuous functions along partial orbits for continuous dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Unlike the classical focus of ergodic theory on convergence almost everywhere, our study emphasizes convergence at every point, motivated by problems in number theory. To this end, we consider a sequence having a uniform behavior property in the natural numbers. We also define and study two structural properties of dynamical systems along such partial orbits: minimal mean Lyapunov stability and minimal mean attractability. Our main result shows that if a continuous dynamical system is both minimally mean Lyapunov stable and minimally mean attractable along a given uniformly behaved sequence, and is minimally uniquely ergodic, then the time-average of any continuous function along the corresponding partial orbit converges to the space average at every point.

papers.title: On a metric view of the polynomial shift locus
papers.abstract: We introduce a path metric $ρ_D$ on the shift locus $\mathcal{S}_D$ of degree $D\geq2$ complex polynomials by connecting complex dynamics to geometric group theory. We encode the escape and deformation data of polynomial basins by metric graphs and use the thermodynamic geometry of the resulting metric graph space. We prove that $(\mathcal{S}_D,ρ_D)$ is complete if and only if $D=2$. For $D\geq3$, we show that the positive-height part of the metric boundary is naturally homeomorphic to the projectivized DeMarco--Pilgrim space $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{S}\mathcal{T}_D^*$. Our result provides a new way of understanding this space which encodes the topology of the shift locus and is defined abstractly as a monotone-light quotient.

papers.title: Torsion Vanishing for Some Shimura Varieties
papers.abstract: We generalize the torsion vanishing results of Caraiani-Scholze and Koshikawa. Our results apply to the cohomology of general Shimura varieties $(\mathbf{G},X)$ of PEL type $A$ or $C$, localized at a suitable maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ in the spherical Hecke algebra at primes $p$ such that $\mathbf{G}_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}$ is a group for which we know the Fargues-Scholze local Langlands correspondence is the semi-simplification of a suitably nice local Langlands correspondence. This is accomplished by combining Koshikawa's technique, the theory of geometric Eisenstein series over the Fargues-Fontaine curve, the work of Santos describing the structure of the fibers of the minimally and toroidally compactified Hodge-Tate period morphism for general PEL type Shimura varieties of type $A$ or $C$, and ideas developed by Zhang on comparing Hecke correspondences on the moduli stack of $G$-bundles with the cohomology of Shimura varieties. In the process, we also establish a description of the generic part of the cohomology that bears resemblance to the work of Xiao-Zhu. Moreover, we also construct a filtration on the compactly supported cohomology that differs from Manotovan's filtration in the case that the Shimura variety is non-compact, allowing us to circumvent some of the circumlocutions taken by Cariani-Scholze. Our method showcases a very general strategy for proving such torsion vanishing results, and should bear even more fruit once the inputs are generalized. Motivated by this, we formulate an even more general torsion vanishing conjecture.

papers.title: Ergodicity of a surgered flow on unit tangent bundle of hyperbolic surface
papers.abstract: Starting with a trivial periodic flow on $\mathbb{S}M$, the unit tangent bundle of a genus two surface, we perform a Dehn-type surgery on the manifold around a tubular neighborhood of a curve on $\mathbb{S}M$ that projects to a self-intersecting closed geodesic on $M$, to get a surgered flow which restricted to the surgery region is ergodic with respect to the volume measure. The surgered flow projects to a map on the surgery track that can be taken to be a linked twist map with oppositely oriented shears which generates the ergodic behavior for sufficiently strong shears in the surgery.

papers.title: Quartic Gauss sums over primes and metaplectic theta functions
papers.abstract: We improve 1987 estimates of Patterson for sums of quartic Gauss sums over primes. Our Type-I and Type-II estimates feature new ideas, including use of the quadratic large sieve over $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and Suzuki's evaluation of the Fourier-Whittaker coefficients of quartic theta functions at squares. We also conjecture asymptotics for certain moments of quartic Gauss sums over primes.

papers.title: Upper metric mean dimensions with potential of $ε$-stable sets
papers.abstract: For infinite-entropy systems, we investigate chaotic behavior occurring in stable sets and use upper metric mean dimensions to characterize the ``size" of $ε$-stable sets and stable sets. The main results of this paper are as follows: (1) We establish precise relations between the upper metric mean dimensions (with potential) of $ε$-stable sets and those of the whole phase space. As an application, we show that the corresponding upper metric mean dimensions defined by topological conditional entropy, preimage neighborhood entropy, and topological entropy coincide. (2) We prove that for every ergodic measure with positive upper mean Katok entropy, weakly mixing sets occur in the closures of stable sets for almost every point and have positive upper capacity metric mean dimension. Furthermore, the upper metric mean dimension of the whole phase space equals the divergence rate, as the scale tends to zero, of the supremum of the $ε$-topological entropies of its stable sets.

papers.title: Sharp estimates for the Opdam-Cherednik $W$-invariant heat kernel for the root system $A_1$
papers.abstract: In this version of the paper, we note important gaps in the previous version.

papers.title: Local structure of homogeneous $ANR$-spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate to what extend finite-dimensional homogeneous locally compact $ANR$-spaces have common properties with Euclidean manifolds. Specially, the local structure of homogeneous $ANR$-spaces is described. Using that description, we provide a positive solution of the problem whether every finite-dimensional homogeneous metric $ANR$-compactum $X$ is dimensionally full-valued, i.e. $\dim X\times Y=\dim X+\dim Y$ for any metric compactum $Y$.

papers.title: Forcing with Symmetric Systems of Models of Two Types
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a general method for forcing on $ω_2$ and $ω_3$ with finite conditions, while preserving all cardinals and some fragments of $\mathrm{GCH}$. This method is based on the technique of forcing with finite symmetric systems of elementary submodels, and improves earlier versions of this forcing by including models of two types. We will present several applications of the pure side condition forcing and variants thereof, by adding a Kurepa tree on $ω_2$, a club subset of $ω_2$ that avoids infinite sets from the ground model, a function bounding every canonical function below $ω_3$ on a club, and a simplified $(ω_2,1)$-morass.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this article, it is proved that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function must lie on the critical line, known as the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Metric mean dimension of flows
papers.abstract: We introduce metric mean dimension to characterize the complexity of continuous flows with infinite topological entropy and derive some of their elementary properties. The main results of this paper are as follows: $(1)$ We prove that different types of measure-theoretic $ε$-entropies of ergodic measures have the same divergent rate, and establish analogous variational principles for metric mean dimension in terms of the measure-theoretic $ε$-entropies of continuous flows. $(2)$ We introduce the measure-theoretic metric mean dimension of invariant measures and link it to metric mean dimension via a classical-type variational principle. $(3)$ Using the Carathéodory-Pesin structure, we introduce Bowen metric mean dimension on subsets and establish the variational principle for Bowen metric mean dimension of any non-empty compact subset. Furthermore, we show that the Bowen metric mean dimension of the set of generic points of an ergodic measure is bounded by the divergent rate of the upper and lower Brin-Katok $ε$-entropies.

papers.title: Loewner evolution driven by complex Brownian motion (with simulations by Minjae Park)
papers.abstract: We study the Loewner evolution whose driving function is $W_t = B_t^1 + i B_t^2$, where $(B^1,B^2)$ is a pair of Brownian motions with a given covariance matrix. This model can be thought of as a generalization of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) with complex parameter values. We show that our Loewner evolutions behave very differently from ordinary SLE. For example, if neither $B^1$ nor $B^2$ is identically equal to zero, then the set of points disconnected from $\infty$ by the Loewner hull has non-empty interior at each time. We also show that our model exhibits three phases analogous to the phases of SLE: a phase where the hulls have zero Lebesgue measure, a phase where points are swallowed but not hit by the hulls, and a phase where the hulls are space-filling. The phase boundaries are expressed in terms of the signs of explicit integrals. These boundaries have a simple closed form when the correlation of the two Brownian motions is zero.

papers.title: Borel Summability for Nonlinear Differential Systems on Characteristic Domains
papers.abstract: We investigate singularly perturbed nonlinear complex differential systems of the form $\hbar \partial_x f = F (x, \hbar, f)$, where $\hbar$ is a small complex perturbation parameter. We give geometric and analytic conditions under which the formal perturbative solution associated with a fixed regular leading-order branch is locally uniformly Borel summable. This leads to an existence and uniqueness theorem of holomorphic solutions with prescribed perturbative expansion. We give an explicit triangular example and a self-contained application to the singularly perturbed Painlevé I equation.

papers.title: Functional relations for higher-order free cumulants
papers.abstract: We establish the functional relations between generating series of higher-order free cumulants and moments in higher-order free probability, solving an open problem posed fifteen years ago by Collins, Mingo, Śniady and Speicher. We propose an extension of free probability theory, which governs the all-order topological expansion in unitarily invariant matrix ensembles, with a corresponding notion of free cumulants and give as well their relation to moments via functional relations. Our approach is based on the study of a master transformation involving double monotone Hurwitz numbers via semi-infinite wedge techniques, building on the recent advances of the last-named author with Bychkov, Dunin-Barkowski and Kazarian. We illustrate our formulas by computing the first few decaying terms of the correlation functions of an ensemble of spiked GUE matrices, going beyond the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem.

papers.title: On the Curved Patterns Seen in the Graph of PPTs
papers.abstract: Dr. Ron Knott constructed a graph of all Primitive Pythagorean Triples (PPTs) with legs up to length 10,000, using Mathematica. The patterns are very interesting, suggesting conic sections. We show that they indeed are parabolic curves which follow in a natural way from the mathematics of the subject matter.

papers.title: Algebraicity of the image of period map
papers.abstract: We prove that the image of period map is algebraic, as conjectured by Griffiths.

papers.title: Graded-Edge Rakotch Contractions in Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings on a generalized metric space with a weighted graph. We prove that the successive iterate of every starting point converge uniformly to a common limit, which is the unique fixed point. We derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound and, under a relaxed triangle inequality, a geometric rate whose constant is the graph invariant. Finally, we illustrate the theory on an explicit real graded contraction that realizes the interior optimum, on a quadratic integral equation, and on finite weighted digraphs.

papers.title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
papers.abstract: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, we characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and identify the geometric regions that govern stability loss and escape from retrieved memories. We further derive reduced slow dynamics and explicit criteria for transition onset, self-sustained retrieval, and collapse, expressed through escape times, gain thresholds, and fixed points. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing feedback-driven sequential retrieval in Hopfield networks.

papers.title: Pósa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $γ>0$, there exists $C=C(k,γ)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying \[ g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+γ\right) \binom{n-1}{k-1}p \qquad(1\le i<n/2) \] contains a Hamilton Berge cycle. The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic Pósa-type theorem. Our result gives a hypergraph analogue of the random-graph theorem of Condon et al. and strengthens the sharp Dirac-type resilience theorem of Chen and Zhang at the same logarithmic probability order. The deletion-resilience formulation has optimal probability order up to constant factors. The coefficient $1$ of $(i/n)^{k-1}$ cannot be replaced by a smaller constant. The proof controls adaptive rotations and representative-edge incidences uniformly. It also gives an endpoint-growth estimate under nonuniform deletion bounds.

papers.title: How to Look Inside the Black Box: A Survey of Yu. E. Nesterov's Contributions (On the Award of the 2026 Gauss Prize)
papers.abstract: On July 23, 2026, at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, the International Mathematical Union announced the award of the Gauss Prize to Yurii Evgenievich Nesterov -- an award for mathematical work with significant applications outside mathematics. This article explains the mathematical content of the recognized work of Yu. E. Nesterov and traces its influence on modern computational practice. The exposition is based on a concept that Yu. E. Nesterov himself regards as one of his main results: the classical complexity theory of convex optimization is oriented toward a black-box oracle, but its pessimistic bounds can be overcome by using a priori information about the internal structure of the objective function. We trace Yu. E. Nesterov's scientific career, then introduce the language of oracle complexity together with a classification of objective function models (geometric, algebraic, and structural), and subsequently discuss his main results in chronological order: the fast gradient method, fast automatic differentiation, the theory of self-concordant barriers and polynomial-time interior-point methods, the $π/2$ theorem, the stable dynamics model of traffic flows, the smoothing technique, primal-dual methods, cubic regularization of Newton's method, the modified Gauss--Newton scheme, coordinate descent methods and methods for huge-scale problems, gradient-free methods, universal gradient methods, implementable tensor methods, and "superfast" methods. Each topic is accompanied by historical background, precise statements specifying the problem class, oracle, and type of guarantee, examples, and a discussion of the current state of the art.

papers.title: On blow-up dynamics for the nonlinear wave equation and the harmonic map heat flow
papers.abstract: This Ph.D. thesis concerns the blow-up analysis, and more precisely, the asymptotic decomposition into profiles of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. In Chapter 1, we present a unifying framework for finding profile decompositions in Hilbert spaces using the notion of dislocation spaces. The next chapters are then devoted to my publications. In the second chapter, we construct solutions to the focusing, energy-critical, nonlinear wave equation in dimension 4 and 5, exhibiting finite-time Type II blow-up precisely at the origin with a single profile and a prescribed polynomial blow-up rate of order $-1-ν$, where $ν> 1$ in 4D and $ν> 3$ in 5D. The major difference between dimension 4 and 5 consists in the renormalization procedure. In 4D, we essentially follow the Krieger-Schlag-Tataru scheme developed for the 3-dimensional equation, where the polynomial structure of the nonlinearity permits the use of simple algebraic manipulations to control error terms. By contrast, the 5D case requires a modified setup due to the lower regularity of the nonlinearity, which complicates the treatment of nonlinear error terms. In Chapter 3, we provide a modern presentation of classical Lp and Schauder estimates for parabolic equations. Then, in Chapter 4, we consider finite-time and $k$-equivariant solutions to the harmonic map heat flow from a disk to a sphere. Under general time-dependent, $k$-equivariant and smooth boundary data, we prove that the profile decomposition at the singular time contains only one bubble. The method relies on the maximum and comparison principle. We also prove a global existence criterion and exhibit solutions blowing up in infinite time for any degree of equivariance. Finally, the appendix presents the profile decomposition for the harmonic map heat flow proved by Struwe and Qing using energy arguments and the Palais-Smale condition.

papers.title: Certified folding-free deformable image registration: A whole-cell Jacobian certificate and a sequential variational solver
papers.abstract: Registration maps propagate labels, measure local volume change, and map results back through their inverses; requiring invertibility. Voxelwise checks can miss folds between grid points. We study the canonical continuous extension of a nodal displacement field by trilinear interpolation and give a test that proves its Jacobian determinant positive in every grid cell or rejects the map. The test is rigorous under IEEE 754 binary64 arithmetic (correct rounding, no contraction). With a fixed boundary, certification implies a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of the image domain. We introduce SeqVP, built around this certificate. A proximal Jacobian-determinant-curl formulation yields inner problems whose penalties on changes in the map, Jacobian determinant, and curl vanish to first order at the current iterate. The method decreases a fixed outer energy up to a floating-point resolution guard and certifies every committed iterate. After certified initialization, stopping at any time returns a folding-free map. A Poisson-preconditioned gradient method with Jacobian-aware step prediction and affine-scaling damping, initialized by certified handoff from an uncertified binary32 pre-optimizer, handles a 1 mm brain MRI with about 2e7 unknowns in 90 s on one GPU. On 49 held-out OASIS pairs, SeqVP achieves mean Dice 0.821 over 35 structures and 0.889 over 4 tissue classes, with certified zero folding. Gains are 0.022 and 0.025 over ANTs SyN, and 0.022 and 0.023 over uniGradICON with instance optimization at equal time (paired, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), but maps are rougher. SeqVP is level with ANTs on LPBA40, behind it on IBSR18, and ahead of all label-free baselines on 20 large-deformation pairs. On fields from nine methods, the certificate finds non-positive-Jacobian cells in every ANTs SyN map (median 10, missed by voxelwise checks) and in maps from NiftyReg, ConvexAdam, uniGradICON, and TransMorph.

papers.title: Boundary Projection Acceleration for 2D One-cell Inversions in the Scattering Limit
papers.abstract: Efficient radiation transport on modern high-performance computers requires algorithms that expose spatial parallelism while maintaining robust convergence. One-cell inversion (OCI) replaces the spatially sequential transport sweep of source iteration with a cell-local solve, making discrete ordinates transport space-parallel, but its spectral radius approaches unity in diffusive problems, and existing accelerators such as transport synthetic acceleration reintroduce sweeps. Here we show that projecting the OCI residual onto a low-order angular space on cell boundaries accelerates convergence in scattering-dominated problems without a transport sweep. We implement the projection in a two-dimensional simple-corner-balance discretization with two angular bases: a linear ($P_1$) basis and one augmented with a quadrant moment ($P_1Q$). Fourier analysis of an infinite homogeneous medium shows that both corrections reduce the spectral radius in optically thick, highly scattering regimes, with $P_{1}Q$ being most effective. Across several test problems, including a modified version of the void-duct streaming benchmark, the method accelerates diffusive and scattering cases but does not uniformly improve convergence in streaming dominated problems. We also find that $P_{1}Q$ is a more robust accelerator than $P_1$ in situations where the flux has strong angular variation. Boundary projection substantially improves OCI convergence in diffusive regimes, and these results delimit the regimes that require additional stabilization or richer projection spaces.

papers.title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
papers.abstract: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $Σ_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$. For the degree pairs $(3,3)$ and $(2,4)$, we specify surface diffeomorphisms inducing the maps on first homology prescribed in~\cite{AY} and recover the integral first homology groups $(\Z/3)^2\oplus\Z/(3m)$ and $(\Z/2)^2\oplus\Z/(4m)$, respectively, for $m\geq1$. For the symmetric $m=1$ sum, we also give a simultaneous surface diagram of the relative product attachments and identify their product framings with the surface framings. The resulting symplectic sums are aspherical and symplectically minimal, and have the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.

papers.title: A toric approach to social choice theory
papers.abstract: This paper initiates a systematic study of objects in convex geometry and toric algebraic geometry arising from status quo systems in social choice theory. Our main application is to classify all cones arising from a large class of status quo systems that are smooth or simplicial.

papers.title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
papers.abstract: This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

papers.title: Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Formulations for the Euclidean Bottleneck Steiner Tree Problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: Given a set of terminals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and an integer $k\ge0$, the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem (EBSTP) asks for a tree spanning the terminals with at most $k$ Steiner points that minimizes its longest edge. Although the planar case has been widely studied, exact optimization methods for arbitrary dimension remain scarce. We develop two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) formulations for the EBSTP: a single-commodity flow formulation and a formulation with connectivity cuts. Both formulations share a geometric core based on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and are strengthened by problem-specific preprocessing, edge-dependent big-$M$ constants, symmetry-breaking constraints, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds on the optimal value. We establish the correctness of the formulations and prove the validity of all strengthening techniques. Computational experiments on 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions $d\in\{2,3,4\}$, with up to $50$ terminals and $9$ Steiner points, show that the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the formulation with connectivity cuts, with an advantage { in solved instances} that grows with dimension. The proposed global lower bounds substantially strengthen the root relaxation, while the single-commodity flow formulation provides the most robust exact solution method across all test sets. These results establish the single-commodity flow formulation as an effective exact approach for the EBSTP in arbitrary fixed dimension.

papers.title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
papers.abstract: We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. The construction extends to the G-equivariant setting for an algebraic group G, yielding in the elliptic case a theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology on algebraic varieties with G-action that takes values in sheaves on the stack of G-bundles. Over the complex numbers, and for G connected reductive, this lifts Grojnowski's theory from the moduli space of G-bundles to the stack. The key player is the category of perfect complexes on A with 0-dimensional support, equipped with the convolution product induced by the group law of A. It plays the role of a categorified circle and is used to define a loop space $L_A^G(X)$, whose structure sheaf gives rise to $H_A^G(X)$ after periodization. Sheaves on $L_A^G(X)$ equivariant under loop rotation provide a category of coefficients for $H_A^G(-)$ in the same way that D-modules provide coefficients for de Rham cohomology. At the point X = *, the theory also gives rise to an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum (or sheaf thereof) $K_A$, which recovers complex K-theory for $A = \mathbf{G}_m$, and the sheaf $\mathcal{O}^{top}$ of topological modular forms for the universal elliptic curve.

papers.title: Discrete Poincaré and Bogovskii operators for higher order finite element de Rham complexes
papers.abstract: We present discrete Poincaré and Bogovskii operators for the common finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex of arbitrary polynomial order. We first discuss how such operators arise from a decomposition of the finite element spaces into a lowest order component and a remainder. This results in a fast algorithm for computing grad, curl, and div potentials. We then introduce a nonlocal Poincaré operator on contractible domains, which generalizes existing constructions based on cone operators to arbitrary order by integrating over cones against extended test forms. This requires developing commuting extension operators, which turn out to be related to rational forms. We also show how the nonlocal construction is modified to obtain a discrete Bogovskii operator preserving homogeneous boundary conditions. We further discuss how the ideas of the construction fit into the theory of finite element systems.

papers.title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
