To establish such a framework, we dualize the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras developed by Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile, obtaining the theory of rooted Hopf algebras. An object in this category is a graded connected Hopf algebra equipped with a group-like element, called a root, in its completion. These roots dualize the character theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras and provide a natural way to extend Bernstein and raising operators to other rooted Hopf algebras. The resulting constructions extend Schur, Hall--Littlewood, and Macdonald functions to rooted Hopf algebras. As an application, we develop these constructions for symmetric functions in noncommuting variables.

papers.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: For a one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operator with bounded nonconstant iid potential, we prove a unit-intensity Poisson limit for local eigenvalues unfolded by the integrated density of states. The limit holds at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. In particular, it holds for Bernoulli potentials at every fixed nonzero coupling. The proof uses auxiliary phase functions built from inverse stationary measures to obtain an exact IDS drift. Projective contraction then yields exponential crossing times, and a spatial subdivision argument gives independent Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows. At energies where the IDS has a finite positive derivative, the usual linear rescaling gives the same limit.

papers.title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $Γ_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. We show that if $\text{length}(Γ) \le λ\, \text{length}(Γ_b)$, then the universal cover of $Γ$ contains a vertex around which, at every radius $R\ge 0$, the ball is at least as long as the ball of radius $R$ in the trivalent tree whose edges all have length $3λ$. In particular, for $λ\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3λ)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, and only for $λ\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. Finally, we conjecture the sharp, all-scale version of the minimal volume entropy inequality of Kapovich-Nagnibeda and Lim, and show that it would be optimal.

papers.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$. We apply the regularity lemma to obtain a short proof of the robust Borell inequality of Mossel and Neeman.

papers.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
papers.abstract: We answer, in the trace metric, a question of Kowalski and Untrau on Wasserstein distances of all orders between the distribution $μ_q$ of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and the Sato-Tate law $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$: we prove bounds for every order $s$ and show that their exponents are optimal for Katz-type moment bounds. In the trace metric we prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll_s q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s<3$, $W_3\ll q^{-1/3}(\log q)^{1/3}$, $W_s\ll_s q^{-1/4-1/(4s)}$ for $3<s<\infty$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/4}$. In the angle metric we obtain bounds of every order, including $W_2\le 7q^{-1/3}$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/6}$. These estimates follow from a general theorem for probability measures satisfying Katz-type Chebyshev moment bounds. Its proof combines an edge-sensitive discrepancy estimate with a new level-set bound for the distribution function and a quantile-displacement argument. We construct measures showing that the resulting exponents cannot in general be improved using moment bounds of this type alone, in the trace metric and in the angle metric for $s\le 2$ and $s\ge 6$ (up to logarithms); these constructions do not assert optimality for the Kloosterman measures themselves. A sharp comparison between Wasserstein distances and the Kolmogorov distance for the Sato-Tate law exhibits the same transition at $s=3$. Finally, using the exact third moment, we prove $W_1(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})>q^{-1/2}/10$ when $3\nmid q$.

papers.title: Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
papers.abstract: We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $α$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leqα<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $Γ$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $α=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $πc_{n-1,n}\max_Γ\sqrt{ab}$.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
papers.abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe equations of the form $i\partial_tu+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. Under the additional assumption $e\neq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. Unlike the previous $H^1$ global theory based on Takaoka's periodic well-posedness estimates (2000), our result does not require any non-resonance condition on the coefficients. Our approach relies on the construction of modified higher-order energies, following the strategy developed for the generalized KdV equation by Planchon, Tzvetkov and Visciglia (2023) and for the generalized DNLS equation by Hayashi, Ozawa and Visciglia (2025). Motivated by higher-order modulation theory, we exploit the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow to establish Sobolev bounds uniform in the modulation parameter $\varepsilon$ on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$. This corresponds to physical times of order $\varepsilon^{-3}$, which is the natural time scale anticipated for the NLS-Dysthe approximation.

papers.title: Variance Bounds for Minimum Perfect Matching Problem by Random Walk on Multinomial Distribution
papers.abstract: We establish variance upper bounds for the minimum perfect matching problem in general metric spaces under a geometric partition condition. As a principal application, let $H_n$ be the minimum perfect matching cost of $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, where $n$ is even and $d\ge2$. We prove $$\operatorname{Var}(H_n)\le C d n^{1-2/d},$$ where $C$ is independent of $n$ and $d$. This removes the logarithmic losses in earlier upper bounds in every dimension (Talagrand, 1995); in particular, the variance remains bounded in dimension two, answering an open question (Rhee, 1994). The proof relies on constructing a rapidly mixing Markov process with a multinomial stationary distribution.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
papers.abstract: This is the second paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. For an observable of two independently prepared systems, Alice's and Bob's, we study its idealized responses: the expectation values of Alice's limiting preparations, as functions of Bob's preparations, which serve as probes, with Bob's system idealized first. We show that the observable is NIP, that is, no sequence of Alice's preparations lets Bob's probes realize every finite pattern of high and low values at a fixed positive gap, exactly when all idealized responses are of the first Baire class, pointwise limits of sequences of continuous functions; they then form a separable Rosenthal compactum. Because Alice can mix preparations, this compactum is convex, and hereditary separability forces it to be metrizable, so that NIP observables occupy three of the four topological classes defined by metrizability and Todorčević's trichotomy. Comparisons of photon numbers, of positions and of events in spacetime realize these three classes, and trees of preparations realize the seven minimal families of the Argyros--Dodos--Kanellopoulos heptachotomy. For the ferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model at positive temperature, the finite-volume magnetizations with offset longitudinal fields form a stable family when the spontaneous magnetization vanishes, and a family whose closure is first countable but not hereditarily separable when it does not.

papers.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
papers.abstract: We study whether global asymptotic stability (GAS) of the origin is decidable for homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients. Our main technical contribution is showing that, for such vector fields of odd degree $d \geq 3$ in every sufficiently large dimension $n$, the problem of deciding GAS of the origin is many-one complete for the class of recursively enumerable sets (and hence undecidable). Using the tools we have built up, we also improve on some recent work by proving a similar result for Lyapunov stability instead of GAS. The proof of our main contribution splits naturally into two parts: - In the first part we give, for every fixed dimension $n$ and odd degree $2k+1$, a computable map which sends a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree $2k+1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ to a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree three on $\mathbb{R}^m$, where $m=\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, and preserves both GAS and Lyapunov stability. As a consequence, the problems of deciding whether the origin is GAS or Lyapunov stable for rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields of any degree, of any fixed odd degree $d \geq 3$, and of degree three are pairwise many-one equivalent. - In the second part we prove that there is a fixed dimension $n_*$ and a fixed odd degree $d_*$ such that the set of rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^{n_*}$ of degree $d_*$ whose origin is GAS is many-one complete. This is done by "transferring" many-one completeness between several different problems, starting from the solvability of a Diophantine equation and eventually arriving at our desired GAS decision problem.

papers.title: CutIGA with Least Squares Stabilized Nitsche Boundary Conditions: The Biharmonic Problem
papers.abstract: We propose a symmetric Nitsche method for the biharmonic Dirichlet problem on a smooth domain whose boundary may cut arbitrarily through the computational mesh. Bulk least-squares stabilization in a boundary strip and tangential boundary penalties control the consistency terms through an explicit lifting of the two Dirichlet traces. This gives coercivity on $H^4(Ω)$ without inverse inequalities and permits a fixed penalty independent of the cut configuration for sufficiently thin strips. Under suitable regularity assumptions, splines of degree $p\geq4$ give energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{p-1}$ and $h^{p+1}$. We also analyze a face-stabilized extension to $C^1$ splines of degree $p=2$ and $C^2$ splines of degree $p=3$. Exact-ellipse experiments examine convergence, cut stability, and parameter sensitivity.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
papers.abstract: This is the first of three papers that read the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables, through their expectation functions on product states. Here we study stability: the independence of the expectation from the order in which the preparations of the two systems are idealized. We show that stability is characterized by weak compactness, by factorization through a reflexive Banach space, and by the uniform simulation of idealized preparations by finite mixtures of actual ones. A uniform version of stability, which bounds at every margin the finite staircases of responses, governs adaptive discrimination and the online prediction of thresholded expectations; for the swap test, Hong--Ou--Mandel coincidences and discrete equality tests, it yields bounds independent of dimension.

papers.title: Sparse domination modulo polynomials
papers.abstract: We develop a sparse domination theory that captures both local polynomial approximation and cancellation of the input below the scale of each sparse cube. Its coefficients are percentiles of localized smooth maximal functions of the input minus its local polynomial approximation, combining features of mean-oscillation sparse bounds and of the cancellative sparse bounds of Conde-Alonso, Lorist and Rey. Using wavelet representations, we characterize the Calderón-Zygmund operators whose derivatives admit these bounds by explicit polynomial testing conditions. In the homogeneous setting, the same conditions characterize weighted Hardy-Sobolev inequalities with linear dependence on the $A_\infty$ characteristic. This quantitative dependence detects the transition from BMO to $L^\infty$ testing conditions that Lerner found for pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials, a distinction that qualitative weighted estimates cannot recover. In the inhomogeneous setting, we prove corresponding weighted inequalities and show that they are strictly weaker than pointwise sparse domination from the second derivative order onward. Consequences include Hardy-Sobolev estimates below the Banach range, sharp weighted Sobolev inequalities, and pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials.

papers.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
papers.abstract: We prove that the probability that Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting on $n \times n$ Gaussian random matrices has growth $ρ$ is at least inverse quasi-polynomial: $Ω\left(\exp\left(-c \log^2 \left(\fracρ{\sqrt{n}}\right)\log(n)\right)\right)$ for some constant $c > 0$. In particular, the probability of growth $ρ\ge n^{1/2 + ε}$ is at least $\exp(- O (ε^2 \log^3 (n) ))$. This lower bound breaks standard conjectures in the smoothed and average-case analysis of Gaussian elimination. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first non-trivial lower bound on the probability of large growth for Gaussian random matrices.

papers.title: When Hilbert functions determine generic initial ideals
papers.abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we characterize the Hilbert functions that determine the degree reverse lexicographic generic initial ideal among Artinian quotients of embedding dimension $n\ge2$ with the $(n-2)$-strong Lefschetz property. The criterion is a finite arithmetic test on successive positive differences of the Hilbert function. It uses recursively defined integer vectors and requires no construction of a monomial ideal. When uniqueness holds, the same vectors recover the common generic initial ideal degree by degree. The proof reduces uniqueness successively to uniqueness of lower sets of specified cardinalities in Borel orders. In four variables, the test simplifies to avoidance of explicitly computed integer intervals. We recover the quasi-symmetry criterion of Harima and Wachi and give infinite families beyond that criterion in every number of variables at least four.

papers.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
papers.abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) for approximately counting and uniformly sampling common bases of two matroids given by their independence oracles. Moreover, our algorithms generalize far beyond this to Hadamard products of two probability measures on the Boolean cube satisfying a simple nonnegative curvature condition. These algorithmic primitives have myriad applications in statistical physics, polyhedral combinatorics, the theory of quantum many-body systems, and beyond. The central difficulty is that the hard constraints imposed by the two input matroids (or the two input measures, more generally) obstruct traditional approaches based on local Markov chains. Relaxing these constraints can restore rapid mixing, but configurations that satisfy the original hard constraints may become exponentially rare if this is done naïvely. Our main contribution is a novel approach for approximate counting that marries Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with convex programming to overcome these obstacles: - We relax the intersection by imposing an overlap penalty on the product measure formed by the two input measures. We prove, via an integrated Bochner-type method, that this "soft intersection" satisfies a Poincaré Inequality uniformly over all external fields. - We use samples from the relaxed distribution to solve a dual maximum entropy convex program inspired by the Gurvits capacity. This program reweights the soft intersection measure using external fields to boost the aggregate probability of configurations satisfying the hard intersection constraint, without changing their relative weights. We bound the success probability directly using the uniform Poincaré Inequality and smallness of the gradient norm. AI Disclosure: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra and GPT-6 Astra Ultra were heavily used to develop the ideas in this paper.

papers.title: Finite Stick Breaking Sequences
papers.abstract: In 1949, De Bruijn and Erdős considered infinite stick-breaking sequences. In this work, we consider finite sequences and prove that an infinite sequence that is due to De Bruijn, Erdős, and Toulmin is in some sense unique.

papers.title: Sharp Riesz capacity inequalities and the Pólya--Szegő conjecture
papers.abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $p\in(n-2,n)$, we prove that closed balls maximize the ratio of Riesz $p$-capacity to Newtonian capacity among all compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. This resolves the classical Pólya--Szegő capacity ratio conjecture and its higher-dimensional extensions. For $n\geq4$, a sharp inequality for the ratio of Newtonian capacity to logarithmic capacity is established. All equality cases are characterized.

papers.title: Infinitesimal Hilbertianity for manifolds with Sobolev regular Riemannian metrics through uniform lower capacity bounds
papers.abstract: We prove that metric measure spaces arising from $2$-manifolds equipped with Riemannian metrics $g$ such that $g, g^{-1} \in L^\infty_{\rm loc} \cap W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ are infinitesimally Hilbertian. Along the way, we establish uniform lower $1$-capacity bounds of several $1$-dimensional subsets of $\R^2$.

papers.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
papers.abstract: Understanding nonlinear dynamics is central to many fields of study, yet most nonlinear systems are beyond the reach of closed-form solutions. Numerical simulation is then used to reveal dynamical structures before their existence can be established. This alone, however, leaves the validity of the computed solution unanswered. Rigorous numerical methods address this gap by combining computation with explicit analytic estimates. Among them, the radii polynomial approach, a Newton--Kantorovich type argument, turns a numerical approximation into a proof of existence and uniqueness of a true solution near that approximation. In previous practice, the verification of these inequalities relies on interval-arithmetic libraries and hand-derived algebraic bounds. In this paper, we present a framework for the radii polynomial method in the Lean~4, which turns numerical certificates into fully type-checked theorems about the true solution. A central challenge in this process is to manage the complexity of the formalization. Our approach begins with a family of problems and their common structure. The spaces in which the analysis takes place are developed through universal properties in suitable categories, with extension properties that characterize maps by their action on generators. These properties guide the design of a reusable interface such that problem-specific arguments concentrate on the numerical data and the algebraic bounds that distinguish one equation from another. We formalize a general radii polynomial theorem, develop weighted coefficient algebras and reusable operator estimates, connect finite computational checks to the hypotheses of the theorem, and establish the realization theorems that transport certified coefficient space zeros to analytic solutions of the original equations.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(π_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.

papers.title: Universal Formulas for de Jonquières Loci and Equivariant Contact Problems
papers.abstract: Given a family of genus $g$ curves $f:Ψ\to S$ and a relative degree $d$ line bundle $L$ on $Ψ$ such that $f_*L$ is a vector bundle, the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ is stratified by relative de Jonquières loci, which parameterize sections of $L$ with prescribed vanishing orders. We give universal formulas for the classes of these loci in terms of the relative $O(1)$ on $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ and tautological classes pulled back from the universal Picard stack $\mathrm{Pic}_g^d$. When $f$ is the family of lines in $\mathbb{P}^r$, we use the universal polynomials to compute $\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}$-equivariant classes of loci of hypersurfaces and complete intersections admitting lines with prescribed contact orders.

papers.title: Critical semilinear damped wave equations beyond moduli of continuity
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear classical damped wave equations with general nonnegative nondecreasing nonlinearities, without imposing a modulus-of-continuity structure or convexity. A Dini-type integral condition expressed directly in terms of the nonlinearity gives small data global in-time existence and extends the nonlinear framework of Ebert--Girardi--Reissig [Math. Ann. 378 (2020), 1311--1326]. When this Dini-type integral diverges and the effective total mass of the initial data is positive, convergence of the Keller--Osserman tail integral is necessary and sufficient for finite-time blow-up of the maximal mild Sobolev solution, particularly, divergence of the tail integral gives global grow-up. The resulting integral criteria distinguish the contributions of the nonlinearity near zero and at infinity in governing small data global in-time existence with diffusion decay, global grow-up, and finite-time blow-up.

papers.title: Metric foundations of geometry
papers.abstract: A metric space is called all-set-homogeneous if every isometry between two of its subsets extends to an isometry of the whole space. We classify all-set-homogeneous length spaces: besides the classical examples, they include the universal metric trees of finite valence.

papers.title: Word Length and Diameter in Permutation Groups
papers.abstract: In the binary diameter problem, the input consists of explicitly given permutations generating a finite group $G$ and a binary-encoded number $k$, and the question is whether every element of $G$ is a product of at most $k$ of the given generators. In the binary length problem, the input additionally contains a permutation $g \in G$, and the question is whether $g$ is such a product. We show that the binary diameter problem is PSPACE-complete, thereby confirming a conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski (2023). Moreover, we show that PSPACE-hardness already holds for solvable groups of derived length at most 3, whereas the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups. For the binary length problem, we establish a sharp complexity threshold: the problem is NP-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups, which extends a result of Lohrey and Rosowski for abelian groups, and PSPACE-complete for groups that are simultaneously 3-step nilpotent and metabelian, which strengthens the main result of Jerrum (1985). Finally, we show that the unary diameter problem, where $k$ is encoded in unary, is $Π_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for generating sets of the full symmetric group, confirming another conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski.

papers.title: Descent along flat composed with radicalization
papers.abstract: We study the following general situation. Let $R\to S$ be a finite flat morphism of regular rings of zero (resp. prime) mixed or (equi)-characteristic. For $P\in Spec R$, put $A=R/P, C=S/PS,$ and $B=S/\sqrt{PS}=C_{\mathrm{red}}.$ The basic question is whether a property of $B$ forces the same property of $A$. The main point is that ordinary finite-flat descent applies naturally to $A\to C$, whereas the passage $C\to C_{\mathrm{red}}$ may (not) destroy nilpotent information.

papers.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: The Komlós problem asks for signs $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^n$ with $\|A\varepsilon\|_\infty$ bounded by an absolute constant whenever the columns of $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ have Euclidean norm at most $1$. We give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem in the unit-cost real-RAM model. Our deterministic algorithm achieves discrepancy at most $8272$. As a consequence, we obtain a deterministic $O(\sqrt t)$-discrepancy algorithm for the Beck-Fiala problem on set systems in which each element belongs to at most $t$ sets. Our algorithm rounds a fractional coloring while keeping the row sums bounded. Its key idea is to keep the number of nearly tight row constraints small relative to the number of active coordinates. We achieve this through a spectral bound based on a weighted Gram matrix of squared row entries. We maintain the bound using a cubic spectral potential and negative-curvature updates that satisfy the required linear constraints.

papers.title: Isogeometric analysis for the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: The transmission eigenvalue problem plays an increasingly important role in inverse scattering theory. Although significant progress has been made in developing efficient numerical methods for the problem over the last two decades, its numerical treatment for curved domains in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2,3$) remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce and analyze a geometrically flexible and $H^2$-conforming isogeometric method for solving a fourth-order, quadratic and non-self-adjoint eigenvalue problem arising from the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem. Using the spectral approximation theory for compact non-self-adjoint operators, we derive optimal error estimates for the discrete eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. Numerical results for the two- and three-dimensional benchmark problems, including those defined in curved domains, are presented to verify our theoretical results, and to demonstrate the advantages of the method over existing numerical methods in terms of both accuracy and geometric flexibility.

papers.title: Stable Movement for Nondual Lipschitz Convex Optimization: Efficiency and Nearly Optimal Oracle Rates
papers.abstract: We study efficient algorithms for realizing the first-order oracle complexity of optimization of $G$-Lipschitz convex functions with respect to the $\ell_q$-norm over an $\ell_p$-ball of radius $R$, where $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$. For $p<q$, we obtain error $\widetilde{O}_{p,q}(GR/T^{1/p-(1/q-1/2)_{+}})$ after $T$ oracle queries, attaining the lower bounds in a COLT 2015 open problem (Guz15b) with efficient algorithms. In particular, the rate is $\widetilde{O}(GR/T)$ for Euclidean Lipschitzness with an $\ell_1$-ball domain of radius $R$ ($p=1,q=2$). Our solution consists of reducing convex Lipschitz optimization to the chasing nested convex sets problem (BBE+20) in sublevel sets of an evolving maximum of affine lower bounds, that is, the bundle (LNN95): at each query we either find a point with low function value or we produce a deep cut in the current sublevel of the bundle that we chase. The dichotomy between stability of selectors and forced movement by deep cuts bounds the number of iterations of the algorithm nearly optimally. For nested convex subsets of the $\ell_p$ ball $R B_p^d$, we introduce novel stable selectors whose movement is nearly optimal in high dimensions. A Monte Carlo average of the proposed selector achieves near-optimal rates with high probability and can be implemented for our optimization algorithm in polynomial time in the real-arithmetic model.

papers.title: The First-Order Oracle Complexity of Lipschitz Convex Optimization in Nondual Settings
papers.abstract: We study first-order black-box convex optimization over an $\ell_p$-ball for objectives Lipschitz in the $\ell_q$-norm, solving in the affirmative the nonsmooth version of the COLT open question (Guz15b) on whether the geometry of a smaller feasible set ($p < q$) can improve convergence rates in convex optimization, and matching prior lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. Our rates include $\widetilde{O}(1/T)$ for convex Euclidean-Lipschitz optimization over the $\ell_1$-ball, improving on the $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ classical rate under general assumptions. The key technical device is a new online learning game, where the comparator is evaluated using the maximum of affine losses observed so far. We bound the value of this game above and below in terms of a combinatorial online learning quantity: the sequential fat-shattering dimension, which we characterize for the $\ell_p / \ell_q$ case. Our results generally apply when the feasible set $\mathcal{X}$ and the set of possible subgradients $\mathcal{H}$ admit a type of minimax theorem, advancing on a fundamental question by Sridharan (Sri12, Section 10.1.2, Q3). As a geometric consequence of our analysis, of independent interest, we obtain estimates for the expected distance of a convex hull of samples to their mean in several Banach geometries, a version of the celebrated Wendel's theorem (Wen62), but quantitative and for bounded general distributions as opposed to centrally symmetric ones.

papers.title: Physical and emergent nonpairwise interactions in oscillator networks: from higher-order phase reduction to coupling design
papers.abstract: Phase reduction is a powerful technique to obtain phase models from high dimensional oscillatory systems. Starting from pairwise interactions, a first order approximation yields Kuramoto and Winfree phase models, while nonpairwise interactions emerge at the second order. Recently, phase models have been extended to account for nonpairwise interactions, notably, the higher-order Kuramoto model. Is there an intrinsic difference between physical and emergent nonpairwise interactions? And can we make use of the former to even out the effects of the latter? In this work, we exploit a recently developed parametrization method to compute the phase reduction and answer these questions. After a comparison of the new method with the classic Kuramoto-style phase reduction, we derive the network motifs of the emergent nonpairwise interactions and compare them with the physical once. Lastly, we exploit the motifs to adopt a coupling design approach. Our framework paves the way for further exploitations of physical nonpairwise interactions for applications in synchronization engineering.

papers.title: Monge's transport problem in synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of solutions to the Lorentzian Monge problem on synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes that satisfy the forward timelike measure contraction property $TMCP^+(K,N)$. The cost for this problem is the time separation function $\ell(x,y)$ (the Lorentz distance), which represents the maximum amount a particle can age when traveling from $x$ to $y$. The solution is based on the needle decomposition technique, and amounts to a reduction of the full problem to its one-dimensional counterparts. As an application of needle decomposition, we introduce the blended $TMCP$ condition, and obtain a quantitative refinement of the synthetic Hawking singularity theorem. We additionally prove a timelike nonbranching reversibility theorem for $TCD_p(K,N)$ spacetimes, showing that forward $p$-essentially nonbranching spacetimes are backward $p$-essentially nonbranching.

papers.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given rational Hermitian matrices $H_1,\dots,H_N$ of rank at most one, finds signs $s\in\{\pm1\}^N$ with $\|\sum_i s_i H_i\|\le 13\|\sum_i H_i^2\|^{1/2}$. As a corollary, for vectors $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=I$ and $\|v_i\|^2\leδ$, the signs yield a partition $[N] = S_1 \cup S_2$ such that each part satisfies $\|\sum_{i \in S_j} v_i v_i^* - \frac{I}{2}\| \leq \frac{13}{2}\sqrtδ$ for $j = 1,2$. This gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Kadison--Singer problem, in Weaver's equivalent discrepancy-theoretic $\mathsf{KS}_2$ formulation, with a universal constant.

papers.title: The Aldous chain on cladograms mixes in order $n^2$ steps
papers.abstract: Cladograms of size $n$ are unrooted binary trees whose leaves are labelled from 1 to $n$. Aldous introduced in 2000 a Markov chain on cladograms, a step of which consists of removing a leaf uniformly at random and reinserting it on a uniformly chosen edge. We introduce a coupling for this walk, which follows multiple colored subtrees in parallel. We go around the lack of independence of the colored components by finding a relevant statistic, namely the sum of the squares of the sizes of all colored components, which we prove has a drift. We deduce that the mixing time of the walk is of order $n^2$, solving a conjecture of Aldous.

papers.title: A Cheeger Inequality for Hypergraphs and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Hypergraphs provide a natural framework for modeling higher-order relationships, but the development of spectral techniques with provable guarantees for general non-uniform hypergraphs remains challenging. Building on Banerjee's normalized adjacency matrix and Spiro's averaging-based diffusion framework, we develop a spectral framework for non-uniform hypergraphs and establish Cheeger's inequality for their conductance. A fundamental result in the spectral theory of hypergraphs asserts that, for every non-covering hypergraph, the second-smallest eigenvalue of its normalized Laplacian is at most one. This spectral characterization yields an improved Cheeger's inequality for non-covering hypergraphs, and we show that the resulting inequality is tight on both sides using cycle and cube hypergraphs. Our framework further yields higher-order Cheeger inequalities and provides theoretical guarantees for Fiedler's spectral partitioning algorithm, all in the setting of hypergraphs. Finally and most notably, we construct a new family of optimal hypergraph expanders that is tight for the Alon-Boppana bound.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Fixed Points for Set-Valued Contractions
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of finding fixed points of set-valued contractions. We first formulate a computational problem for Nadler's fixed-point theorem, PROJECTED-NADLER, and prove that it is CLS-complete by showing its equivalence to CONTINUOUS-LOCALOPT. We then establish a stronger converse to Nadler's theorem, which can be applied as a tool to analyze the convergence rate of the set-valued basic iteration procedure. Finally, we reduce the large-margin triplet stationarity problem to PROJECTED-NADLER. Combining the argument for CLS-hardness of exact triplet stationarity problem [Yan et al. 2025] with the CLS-hardness of approximate KKT points of quadratic programs [Fearnley et al. 2025], we obtain CLS-completeness of large-margin triplet stationarity at any prescribed accuracy.

papers.title: Polynomial-time Tensor Decomposition under the Kruskal Condition and the Lovitz--Petrov Generalization
papers.abstract: An identifiability criterion is a condition on a tensor decomposition that certifies uniqueness when the condition holds. Kruskal's classical condition is one of the best-known deterministic criteria for identifiability. However, no polynomial-time decomposition algorithm is known under the Kruskal condition; verifying the condition itself is NP-hard. Lovitz and Petrov introduced a strictly more general identifiability condition which, in contrast, is polynomial-time verifiable, but no polynomial-time decomposition algorithm was known under this condition either. In this paper we give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, in the algebraic model over $\mathbb R$, for tensor decomposition under the Lovitz--Petrov condition, and therefore also under the stricter Kruskal condition. Moreover, combining our algorithm with polynomial-time verification of the Lovitz--Petrov condition yields an efficient end-to-end certification procedure: after computing a decomposition, one can deterministically certify in polynomial time that it is unique and therefore of minimum rank.

papers.title: Long-Time Dispersion and Threshold Resonances for the Landau Hamiltonian on the Hyperbolic Plane
papers.abstract: A uniform magnetic field completely suppresses long-time dispersion for the Euclidean Landau Hamiltonian. We show that negative curvature fundamentally changes this behavior. For the Landau Hamiltonian with arbitrary field strength $B\in\mathbb R$ on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb H$, we establish sharp dispersive estimates for the Schrödinger evolution on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace. The decay is $|t|^{-1}$ at short times and, strikingly, improves to $|t|^{-3/2}$ at large times whenever $B\notin\frac12+\mathbb Z$. At half-integer fields, we identify a threshold resonance and isolate its leading contribution, which yields the slower but sharp rate $|t|^{-1/2}$. Thus the long-time dynamics exhibit a resonance-driven dichotomy with no analogue in the flat constant-field problem. Our analysis is based on an explicit representation of the magnetic Schrödinger kernel together with a precise separation of the Landau levels and threshold profile. As a further consequence, for every nonthreshold field we obtain global-in-time Strichartz estimates on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace throughout the full hyperbolic admissible region.

papers.title: Free-Probabilistic State Evolution and Random Matrix Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Let $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be independent $d \times d$ real symmetric Gaussian random matrices, and consider the linear operator $A(x) = n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i$, $x\in \mathbb R^n$. We construct an iterative algorithm in the Approximate Message Passing family which iterates over $A$ and its adjoint $A^*$, and establish a state evolution result which characterizes its behavior in the limit $d\to \infty, 2n/d^2 \to α$ in terms of a correlated Gaussian-semicircular process in a free probability space, in the sense of strong convergence of operators. We then apply this iteration to the random matrix discrepancy problem which asks for a binary vector $x \in \{-1,+1\}^n$ such that $A(x)$ has a small operator norm. Our algorithm achieves an operator norm $2σ(α)$, for a standard deviation $σ(α)<1$ for all $α>0$, and $σ(α) = O(1/\sqrt{α\log α})$ for large $α$. This resolves the algorithmic question of Kunisky-Zhang (2023) and Maillard (2025).

papers.title: Max Independent Set Remains NP-hard when Excluding a Planar Induced Minor (and More)
papers.abstract: We show that Max Independent Set (MIS) remains NP-hard in graphs excluding the $5 \times 5$ grid as an induced minor. This negatively answers a question of Dallard--Milanič--Štorgel that has attracted sustained attention, and refutes a conjecture by Gartland and Lokshtanov. Unless $N$-variable 3-SAT can be solved in time $2^{\mathcal O(N^{1-\varepsilon})}$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, MIS requires $2^{Ω(n^{1/2-o(1)})}$ time on $n$-vertex graphs in this class. This complements a $2^{\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})}$-time algorithm on any $H$-induced-minor-free class by Korhonen and Lokshtanov. Exploiting a connection between low twin-width or reduced parameters on one hand and planar-induced-minor-freeness on the other, we further show that 3-Coloring, Feedback Vertex Set and Dominating Set are NP-complete on weakly sparse graphs of reduced component max-leaf (hence twin-width) at most 3, even when a witnessing contraction sequence is given. Classes of bounded reduced component max-leaf (by any constant) and of twin-width at most 3 are known to exclude a fixed planar graph as an induced minor. The 3-Coloring and Feedback Vertex Set results refute more cases of the Gartland--Lokshtanov conjecture, even when the inputs are weakly sparse. The complexity of MIS in weakly sparse graphs excluding a planar induced minor remains open.

papers.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality on quantum euclidean spaces. Our result implies the sharp Hausdorff--Young constants for the Weyl transform. The key ingredients are a sharp Hessian comparison inequality and a novel flow related to the mixed- norm of noncommutative Gabor transform; the Hessian comparison leads to the monotonicity of the flow. We also apply the same flow technique to prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities on Heisenberg groups and the affine group.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the four-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system and for Vlasov--Riesz equations
papers.abstract: We establish global classical well-posedness for the four-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system, for every nonnegative \(f_0\in C_c^1(\mathbb{R}^8)\). We also prove global well-posedness for Vlasov equations with power-law interactions for \(d\ge4\). For every \(0<α<3\), we treat both attractive and repulsive interactions with arbitrary nonnegative, compactly supported bounded initial data. Neither result requires a smallness assumption on the initial data. For attractive interactions, a virial argument yields finite-time breakdown for negative-energy solutions when \(3\leα<d+1\). The global existence proofs combine estimates along characteristics, analysis in Lagrangian coordinates, and Serre's compensated integrability.

papers.title: Recovery Theory for Projected Power Iterations in Permutation Synchronization
papers.abstract: We study the projected power method for permutation synchronization: recovering $n$ unknown permutations of $m$ objects from pairwise relative permutations, observed independently with probability $p$ and independently corrupted by uniform permutations with probability $1-π_0$. Our main theorem establishes uniform one-step contraction for all estimates with optimally aligned block-error fraction at most $1/2-ε$, for fixed $ε>0$, including measurement-dependent estimates. When $np\ge C_0\log(n)$ and $m=o(npπ_0^2)$, one update contracts the error by a factor $O(m/(npπ_0^2))$, up to a floor of $O(e^{-c\min\{m\,npπ_0^2,\,npπ_0\}} + \log(n) / n)$. Thus, every initialization in this majority basin achieves $o(1)$ error after one update and maintains it uniformly over subsequent iterations. A reference-block spectral initializer enters the basin with probability $1-o(1)$, yielding end-to-end almost-exact recovery. If additionally $\min\{m\,npπ_0^2,\,npπ_0\} \ge C\log(n)$ for sufficiently large $C$, the method achieves exact recovery in finitely many iterations. We also establish prescribed-block recovery under weaker conditions for measurement-independent estimates and extend the guarantees to independent permutation-valued corruptions with uniform mean and to partial permutations with common visible support.

papers.title: On the Brill--Noether Theory of Sheaves on Regular Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Brill--Noether theory of higher rank sheaves on surfaces $X$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X) = 0$ and its interactions with the classical Brill--Noether theory of line bundles on curves lying on $X$. Denoting by $\mathrm{Spl}(v)$ the moduli space of simple sheaves on $X$ with Chern character $v = (r,c_1,\mathrm{ch}_2)$, we introduce the Brill--Noether loci $BN^k(v)^\circ \subseteq \mathrm{Spl}(v)$ of \emph{generically $k$-generated} sheaves and show, under assumptions on $c_1$ and $K_X$, certain well-behavedness results. In particular, if $c_1$ is \emph{indecomposable} and $X$ is a K3 surface, we generalize a Brill--Noether theorem for sheaves on K3s due to Yoshioka. This is achieved by employing He's deformation theory of the moduli space of coherent systems and a globalization of the Lazarsfeld--Mukai construction, providing a correspondence between the Brill--Noether theories of generically $r$-generated sheaves on $X$ and that of line bundles on curves $C \in |c_1|$. The same techniques yield upper bounds on the dimension of $\mathcal{W}^{r,\mathrm{bpf}}_d(|c_1|) \setminus \mathcal{W}^{r+1}_d(|c_1|)$ consisting of basepoint-free line bundles in terms of the number of endomorphisms of associated Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, for arbitrary $c_1$. This generalizes a result of Aprodu and Farkas in the context of Green's conjecture beyond K3 surfaces. In the case $r = 1$ of pencils, we obtain smoothness and expected-dimension results under an effectivity condition on $-K_X|_C$ for $C \in |c_1|$. As an application, we prove Green's conjecture for the general curve on a rational surface with a nef and effective anticanonical divisor.

papers.title: Sparse Koopman Autoencoders Identify Local Dynamical Regimes in Multibasin Systems
papers.abstract: Koopman autoencoders (KAEs) seek a higher-dimensional latent representation in which nonlinear dynamics evolve linearly. However, many interesting systems have multiple basins of attraction, and both theoretical and empirical work has shown these multibasin systems cannot generally admit a single finite-dimensional global Koopman embedding under standard assumptions. We posit that encoders with a sparsity-inducing objective encouraging few active latent coefficients will provide latent supports as an inspectable basin-modeling principle for Koopman autoencoders. We use these encoders producing sparse latents in training Sparse Koopman Autoencoders (SKAEs) without basin labels or other regime annotations, and treat the learned latent supports as model-produced regime variables after training. Across a range of procedurally generated multibasin systems and chaotic flows, we show that SKAEs have superior forecasting performance compared to dense-latent KAEs. We also perform a mechanistic study that shows latent supports produced by SKAEs are both essential for the quality of the representation and useful for identifying basins on basin-interior states, whereas dense-latent KAEs collapse to an uninformative single support family. These results identify sparse latents and their corresponding supports as label-free, interpretable regime variables for Koopman learning in nonlinear systems with multiple local dynamical laws.

papers.title: Quadratic Complexity of Voronoi Diagrams in $\mathbb{R}^3$ for Lines in a Single Ruling of a Regulus
papers.abstract: We study nearest and farthest Voronoi diagrams of lines in three-dimensional Euclidean space, which partition space according to the closest and farthest input lines, respectively. For arbitrary lines, a gap remains between the known quadratic lower bound and near-cubic upper bounds for the complexity of the nearest diagram. We consider input lines chosen from one of two continuous families of straight lines on a smooth surface defined by a quadratic equation, with one line from each family passing through every point of the surface. Under the geometric assumptions stated in the paper, we prove quadratic upper bounds on the total number of vertices, edges, faces, and connected three-dimensional regions in both diagrams. We also construct quadratically many nearest vertices using lines from a single family on one fixed surface, establishing a tight quadratic worst-case bound. The farthest diagram has quadratic total complexity for every input satisfying our assumptions. Our proof uses a parametrization that arranges the input lines in a cyclic order and expresses tangency to a sphere by a polynomial equation of degree four. At a Voronoi vertex, the four tangent input lines give four distinct roots. The sign changes between these roots, together with the nearest or farthest condition, force two intervening parameter intervals to contain no other input parameters. Thus, only quadratically many choices of four lines can define a vertex, and each choice yields at most eight isolated candidate centers.

papers.title: The Cesàro Operator, Rhaly operators, and the Toeplitz Algebra
papers.abstract: Barría and Halmos [\emph{Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.} (1982), (10) Example] asked whether the Cesàro operator belongs to the Toeplitz algebra. We answer this question affirmatively and prove that the Cesàro operator is the product of a Toeplitz operator and a continuous function of a self-adjoint Toeplitz operator. Rhaly operators are a natural generalization of the Cesàro operator. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for a Rhaly operator to belong to the Toeplitz algebra or the Hankel algebra. The main approach is to use the Fejér kernels to get localized estimates for operators. This yields a necessary condition for an operator to belong to the Hankel algebra. As an application, we find a class of Rhaly operators that are asymptotic Toeplitz operators and essentially commute with the unilateral shift, but are not in the Hankel algebra. This answers (17) Question in the same paper.

papers.title: A Spectral Local-to-Global Principle for Spin Systems on Graphs with Girth At Least Five
papers.abstract: It is proved that, for every $δ\in (0,1)$, the Glauber dynamics for the uniform distribution on proper $q$-colorings is rapidly mixing when $q \geq (1+δ)Δ$ and the underlying graph has girth at least $5$ and maximum degree $Δ= Ω_δ(1)$. This result also extends to general multi-spin systems satisfying a $\textit{local spectral contraction}$ condition, including the anti-ferromagnetic Potts model with $q\geq (1+δ)(1-β)Δ$. These results are achieved by a new spectral local-to-global principle on graphs with girth at least five for general multi-spin systems, and a novel Fourier analysis for Glauber dynamics on a star. The main ideas behind all the proofs were developed through several rounds of interaction with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

papers.title: The Wave Kinetic Theory for Quasilinear MMT Equation
papers.abstract:
We study the one-dimensional quasilinear Majda--McLaughlin--Tabak (MMT) equation on a large torus $[0,L]$:  egin{align*} i \partial_t u +2π|
abla|^σu +λ^{2}|
abla|^β\left[ \left||
abla|^βuight|^{2} |
abla|^βuight]=0, \end{align*} with $σ\in(0,1)\cup (1,2]$ and $0<β<σ/4$. We consider Gaussian random initial data and work in the joint limit $L	o\infty$ with $α=λ^2L^{-1}	o0$. The quasilinear structure leads to unavoidable derivative loss, which prevents the direct construction of solutions via iteration of the Duhamel formula. For $σ\in(1,2]$, we prove that, with high probability, solutions exist up to time scales ${T} \simα^{-{ rac43}+} \wedge α^{- rac1{σ/2-β}+}$, and that only trivial four-wave resonances occur, leading to a degenerate wave kinetic equation. For $σ\in(0,1)$, we prove the existence up to time scales $T\sim α^{- rac43+}$, and show that the second-order statistics are well approximated by the wave kinetic equation. In both cases, the solutions remain smooth while exhibiting smallness in suitable $L^\infty$-based norms. The proof combines propagation of randomness for a truncated equation with deterministic energy estimates and a bootstrap argument. The main technical difficulties arise in the regime $σ\in(0,1)$. At low frequencies, the counting argument requires simultaneous control of the frequency gap and the associated resonant phase gap. In the energy estimate, nontrivial resonances generate quartic terms that prevent the energy estimates from closing the bootstrap on $[0,T]$. To overcome this obstruction, we develop a new normal-form $L^2$ energy estimates, using distinct frequency truncations for the initial data and the nonlinearity.

papers.title: A Note on Topological Hochschild Homology Relative to $\Sphere_{W(k)}[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
papers.abstract: We explain the relation between the relative topological Hochschild homology $\THH(R/\Sphere_{W(k)}[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$ and the Nygaard-completed Frobenius-twisted relative prismatic cohomology $\widehat{\Prism}^{(1)}_{R/W(k)[x_0,\ldots,x_n]^\wedge}$, where $W(k)[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n]\rightarrow R$ is relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid. As an application, for $R=\Z_p[x]/(px)$, we compute $π_*\THH(R)^\wedge_p$ by descent along $\THH(R)^\wedge_p\rightarrow \THH(R/\Sphere_p[z,x])$, where $R$ is regarded as an $\Einfty$-$\Sphere_p[z,x]$-algebra via $\Sphere_p[z,x]\xrightarrow{z\mapsto p,x\mapsto x}\Z_p[x]/(px)$.

papers.title: Borelness of Moduli Spaces of Metrics Implies Separability
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metrizable space, and let $\mathrm{Met}(X)$ denote the space of metrics compatible with the topology of $X$, regarded as a subspace of the space of continuous pseudometrics with the topology induced by the supremum metric. We first prove that if $Z$ is a discrete space whose cardinality is the first uncountable cardinal, then $\mathrm{Met}(Z)$ is not Borel. As a consequence, if $\mathrm{Met}(X)$ is Borel, then $X$ is separable. Combined with a theorem of Koshino, our result yields that the space of bounded compatible metrics on a metrizable space $X$ is completely metrizable if and only if $X$ is $σ$-compact. We also establish non-Archimedean analogues for spaces of ultrametrics. We further prove componentwise versions of these results, where two metrics belong to the same component if their distance is finite.

papers.title: Witt groups of smooth real curves and surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathbf{I}^*$-cohomology of a smooth real algebraic curve in terms of its real locus and its geometric genus. We notably extend results of Knebusch and Monnier to the twisted case. We further describe how to compute twisted Witt groups of surfaces, generalising work of Sujatha, and apply our results to the computation of the shifted and twisted Witt groups of the smooth real anisotropic quadric surface. Finally, we extend Monnier's investigation of the image of the global signature homomorphism for surfaces.

papers.title: Indefinite integrals of Bessel and Struve functions with half-integer indices, and incomplete gamma functions with integer indices, all multiplied by $Exp(-ax^{2})$ and divided by powers
papers.abstract: Indefinite integrals are found for 63 half-integer Bessel and Struve functions, and incomplete gamma functions with integer indices, each multiplied by $Exp(-ax^{2})$ and divided by powers. A series solution is given for the individual terms (of any inverse power) in such functions, split into even and odd portions. Eight integrals are given involving these series. Three infinite sets of auxiliary integrals are also given.

papers.title: Intersective Polynomials and Universal Separation of Divosor Profiles
papers.abstract: We classify universal divisor-profile separation for coprime polynomial pairs of arbitrary degree and for all pairs of degree at most two. For \(A\subset\N\) and \(m\in\Z\), let \(d_A(m)\) count the members of \(A\) dividing \(m\). For coprime nonzero \(F,G\in\Z[x]\), universally unbounded separation between \(d_A(F(n))\) and \(d_A(G(n))\) occurs if and only if one of \(F,G\) is intersective, that is, has a root modulo every positive integer. More generally, an intersective factor separated from finitely many polynomial opponents yields simultaneous one-sided dominance against all of them. For pairs with common irreducible factors, let \(U,V\) be the products of the factors occurring only on the two respective sides. Universal separation forces \(UV\) to have a root modulo almost every prime; equivalently, its Galois action has no derangement. We resolve the remaining finite \(p\)-adic boundary for all pairs of degree at most two: separation holds exactly when \(UV\) and at least one of \(F,G\) are intersective, and the criterion is unchanged by contents or factor multiplicities. The same criterion holds, in arbitrary degree, for three linear support factors with arbitrary positive multiplicities. The proofs combine uniform almost-prime values on root progressions with an adaptive local-routing argument.

papers.title: The $β=2$ partition function of Dirichlet $L$-functions and typical maxima
papers.abstract: We study the $β=2$ partition function $\int_{|h| \leq \log ^θ q/2}|L(1/2+ih,χ)|^2dh$ for typical Dirichlet characters modulo a large prime $q$ and $θ\in (-1/3,0]$ motivated by a $q$-analogue of the Saksman--Webb conjectures. When $θ<0$, we use an extension of Harper's randomisation argument with different localisations to recover moment upper bounds consistent with the critical normalisation predicted there. As an application, we prove that for $q(1-o(1))$ Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ with $U(q) \to \infty$, $$\max_{|h| \leq 1/2}|L(1/2+ih,χ)|\ll \frac{e^{U(q)}\log q\log_3 q(\log_4 q)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 q)^{3/4}},$$ establishing an upper bound matching the predictions of the $q$-analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating conjectures up to second order. Our proofs adapt Harper's argument in \cite{harper2019partition}.

papers.title: Monoidal and symmetrized parametrized topological complexity
papers.abstract: We introduce and study monoidal and symmetrized versions of parametrized topological complexity. First, we develop parametrized analogues of the monoidal topological complexity theories of Iwase--Sakai, Aguilar-Guzmán--González (based on the Fadell--Husseini approach), and Dranishnikov. We investigate the parametrized Iwase--Sakai conjecture and provide sufficient conditions under which it holds. We then introduce symmetrized parametrized topological complexity and combine it with the monoidal perspective to define monoidal symmetrized parametrized topological complexity, showing that the resulting notions agree. Finally, we compute these invariants for Fadell--Neuwirth fibrations.

papers.title: A Torelli-type theorem for hyperkähler quotients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the moduli space of algebraic asymptotic hyperkähler structures on hyperkähler quotients arising from a quaternionic vector space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We consider the period map on this moduli space, and prove a Torelli-type theorem (i.e., the bijectivity of the period map) under mild assumptions including the surjectivity of the Kirwan map. This work provides an algebro-geometric generalization of the Torelli-type theorem for ALE gravitational instantons by Kronheimer (1989). In particular, this theorem applies to toric hyperkähler varieties and Nakajima quiver varieties.

papers.title: Rigorous Low-Degree Implications for Planted Subgraph Detection: Noise and Treewidth
papers.abstract: The low-degree method predicts computational thresholds by asking whether low-degree polynomials can distinguish a planted distribution from a null one. Recent counterexamples by Buhai, Hsieh, Jain, and Kothari (FOCS 2025) and Mao (2026) show that low-degree indistinguishability does not, in general, rule out efficient algorithms, even on noisy inputs. Hsieh, Kane, Kothari, Li, Mohanty, and Tiegel (STOC 2026) asked what it does imply, and showed that for permutation-invariant distributions on $\{0,1\}^n$, low-degree indistinguishability from the uniform distribution implies statistical indistinguishability after noise. In this work, we study the same question for planted subgraphs in sparse random graphs. Let $Q_n=G(n,c/n)$, and let $P_n$ be obtained by planting a uniformly random copy of a deterministic graph $Γ_n$ into an independent sample from $Q_n$. In the supercritical regime $c>1$, we show that if $P_n$ is degree-$D_n$ indistinguishable from $Q_n$ and the treewidth of $Γ_n$ is $o(D_n/\log n)$, then a noisy version of $P_n$ is asymptotically indistinguishable from $Q_n$. In the critical and subcritical regimes $0<c\le 1$, we obtain the same conclusion without any treewidth assumption, provided $D_n=ω(\log n)$. Our proof has two main ingredients. First, we identify the subgraph-count and automorphism factors in the Fourier expansion with counts of isomorphism triples. Second, we cut a tree decomposition of $Γ_n$ into subtrees, which splits each large Fourier support into low-degree pieces that meet at only a few interface vertices, and we use noise to absorb the cost of reassembling them. At and below criticality, we use the low-degree assumption to rule out short cycles and noise to destroy the remaining long ones.

papers.title: Topological Computational Paths: Presentation Invariance and Observable Quotients
papers.abstract: A computational path records the steps used to establish an equality. Topologies on computational equality witnesses can depend on the chosen generators and execution schedule, even when their algebraic and homotopical meanings agree. We study continuous presentations of finite computational paths whose declared rewrites are realized by endpoint-fixed homotopies. We compare a topology retaining the full signed trace with an observable topology recording endpoints, length, and exact path realization. Continuous finite-word interpretations that are inverse up to scoped rewriting preserve trace-sensitive quotient arrows and their final composable-pair spaces. Observable quotients behave differently. Over a point with a nonempty primitive alphabet, we classify their topology: it records length parity when all named relations preserve parity, and is otherwise indiscrete. Adjoining a conservative abbreviation can therefore turn a discrete two-element quotient into an indiscrete space, even though ordinary multiplication remains continuous. A circle presentation also gives nonhomeomorphic quotients under binary and equal-slot timing. Geometric completeness alone does not identify the trace-sensitive and observable topologies. Multiplication is continuous on the quotient of composable representatives. We characterize when this topology agrees with the ordinary pullback topology and give an open-projection criterion. Universal presentations recover classical fundamental-groupoid topology. Normal forms, primitive interchange, and a Cayley covering prove completeness for circle, torus, product, and rose presentations. A literal-word correspondence relates the semantics to the reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity fragment of equality derivations. Selected results are formalized in Lean, with the realization models and proof coverage stated explicitly.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

papers.title: Many Antipodal Pairs Force Many Neighboring Pairs
papers.abstract: Let $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points of diameter at most $1$. It is natural to expect that if many pairs $(x_i,x_j)$ lie at distance close to $1$ from each other, then some clustering phenomenon must occur, implying that a significant number of these pairs are also very close to each other. %For $0<\varepsilon<1$, we call a pair $(x_i,x_j)$ $\varepsilon$-antipodal if $\|x_i-x_j\|\ge 1-\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon$-neighboring if $\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon$. We prove that there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon<1$, whenever $n$ is large enough, we have: \[ \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon\}\big| \geq c\cdot \varepsilon^{1/2}\cdot \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\geq 1-\varepsilon\}\big|. \] This confirms a recent conjecture of Steinerberger, who asked whether the $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ ratio is the best possible. We also study a two-parameter version of Steinerberger's question by considering the number of pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon_1$ and at distance at least $1-\varepsilon_2$. We show that in this case the optimal ratio is $\varepsilon_1^2\cdot\varepsilon_2^{-3/2}$ when $\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2$, and $\varepsilon_1^{1/2}$ otherwise. The proof proceeds by introducing an auxiliary graph associated with the set $X$ and reducing the problem to bounding the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. Our main result is the outcome of human--AI interactions using ChatGPT 5.4.

papers.title: $0/1$-Polytopes with Exponentially Small Edge Expansion
papers.abstract: We present a simple construction of a family of $0/1$-polytopes whose edge expansion decreases exponentially with the dimension, which disproves the Mihail-Vazirani conjecture that the graph of every $0/1$-polytope has edge expansion at least one.

papers.title: Limit theorems for differential systems with multipoint boundary conditions in Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: The most general class of multipoint inhomogeneous boundary-value problems for systems of linear ordinary differential equations of arbitrary order $r\geq 1$ is investigated, whose solutions belong to a given Sobolev space $W_p^{n+r}$, where $n\geq 0$ and $1\leq p\leq \infty$. The boundary conditions in these problems contain Caputo derivatives of fractional or integer orders, which may exceed the order of the differential system equations. Constructive sufficient conditions are established under which the solutions of these problems are continuous with respect to a parameter from an abstract metric space in the Sobolev space $W_p^{n+r}$.

papers.title: An infinitesimal deformation of the post-Lie and post-Hopf algebra correspondence
papers.abstract: We describe infinitesimal deformations of post-Lie algebras and post-Hopf algebras and prove that the universal enveloping algebra and primitive elements adjunction is compatible with the infinitesimal structure. In characteristic zero, this restricts to an equivalence for connected cocommutative infinitesimal post-Hopf algebras, extending the Cartier--Milnor--Moore theorem. We parametrize all infinitesimal post-Lie structures on $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ and exhibit a second-order obstruction. From a geometric point of view, infinitesimal post-Lie algebras emerge from flat connections with covariantly constant torsion and an additional compatible symmetric $(1,2)$-tensor. This leads to explicit examples of infinitesimal post-Lie structures based on Heisenberg Lie algebras. On the Hopf side, we classify infinitesimal structures above the trivial action, prove rigidity for group algebras, and describe the structures on Sweedler's Hopf algebra. The subadjacent construction induces a Hopf algebra deformation with fixed coproduct. Finally, we prove that the quadratic operad of infinitesimal post-Lie algebras is Koszul, using a filtered distributive law between the operads of Lie algebras and bi-magmas.

papers.title: Automated Numerical Stability Analysis of Deep Learning Operators
papers.abstract: Finite-precision arithmetic unavoidably introduces numerical approximation errors. Numerical computations may use insufficient precision or an improper formulation, which leads to numerical instability. In this paper, we introduce a unified software tool for stochastic numerical validation of deep-learning operators. The tool follows CESTAC on supported exposed operations and uses an operator-level data-perturbation approximation for GEMM-like kernels. Our developed software not only enables numerical validation with a single computation pass but also detects the sources of numerical instability and provides numerical stability monitoring during deep learning training and inference. We verified its effectiveness on the detection of polluted operators with injected numerical instabilities across various tasks. We believe that our developed method and tools provide valuable insights into developing numerically stable computing kernels, which are particularly critical for numerically stable and efficient deep learning training and inference.

papers.title: Optimizing the Preconditioner: A Black-box Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Static Regret Minimization Oracles
papers.abstract: Stochastic nonconvex optimization is central to training deep networks and LLMs in modern machine learning. We give a black-box reduction from stochastic nonconvex optimization to ordinary static regret minimization in online convex optimization (OCO), addressing the open problem posed by Chen and Hazan (2024). Our reduction maintains a predictable gradient tracker, while a black-box online learner $\mathcal A$ selects a preconditioner that transforms this tracker into the update direction. Given a $β$-smooth function with initial gap at most $M$ and an unbiased gradient oracle with variance bounded by $σ^2$, we bound the expected average squared gradient norm by $O(σ\sqrt{Mβ/T}+\sqrt{Mβ}\mathrm{Reg}_T(\mathcal A)/T+\frac{Mβ}{T})$, where $\mathrm{Reg}_T(\mathcal A)$ is the static regret of $\mathcal A$ against the identity preconditioner. Thus, any OCO oracle with $O(\sqrt T)$ regret recovers the classical $O(T^{-1/2})$ convergence rate. We also prove that the additive variance term cannot be removed: every conversion making a constant number of stochastic-oracle queries per round, whose guarantee is stated through static regret against a comparator that the online learner can play, must contain an additive term of order $σ\sqrt{Mβ/T}$ for sufficiently large $T$. Moreover, for every online learner, our conversion bound is tight up to universal constants. We also extend the framework to nonsmooth nonconvex optimization, still relying only on ordinary static regret, and attain the optimal convergence rate for Goldstein-type stationarity. Finally, we conduct numerical experiments on nonconvex objectives to illustrate how the reduction exploits online-selected preconditioners while using the same stochastic-oracle budget as stochastic gradient descent.

papers.title: A Minimax Analysis of the Last Iterate of the SubGradient Method in Finite Dimension
papers.abstract: We study the last iterate of the projected subGradient Method with a constant stepsize for convex $L$-Lipschitz objectives in $\mathbb{R}^d$, minimized over closed convex sets. Assuming that the initial iterate $x_1$ has distance at most $R$ from a minimizer, we establish matching upper and lower bounds on the minimax optimization error at $x_n$, where the infimum is taken over constant stepsizes. Specifically, this error is of order $L\cdot R\cdot\sqrt{\min\{d,\log n\}/n}$. Notably, when the dimension is fixed, the minimax error decays as $1/\sqrt{n}$, without the extra logarithmic factor intrinsic to dimension-free analyses. Our analysis exploits a combinatorial argument based on linear algebra and novel geometric constructions.

papers.title: Online Beck--Fiala Down to Logarithmic Sparsity
papers.abstract: The celebrated (offline) Beck--Fiala conjecture asserts that every matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times T}$ with at most $d$ nonzero entries in each column has discrepancy $O(\sqrt d)$. In this note, we consider the {\it online} version of the conjecture. For every fixed $η>0$, we give a randomized online algorithm that achieves $O_η(\sqrt d)$ prefix discrepancy for every fixed sequence of $d$-sparse vectors $a_t\in[-1,1]^n$, except with probability at most \[ C_ηT\exp\left[-\frac{c_ηd}{\log^{2+η}(ed)}\right]. \] In particular, this gives an optimal $O(\sqrt d)$ discrepancy upper bound for $d\geq C_η(\log T)(\log\log T)^{2+η}$. This range of sparsity is optimal up to $\log\log T$ factors. The result also resolves in strong form the {\it online Spencer problem}, corresponding to the case $d = n$. The algorithm is based on a compactly supported Metropolis walk, constructed by combining ideas from several recent works on online vector balancing. The proof was generated in conversation with ChatGPT 5.6 Pro; the authors provided high-level guidance in several rounds of prompting, followed by manual checking and rewriting of the proof.

papers.title: Flag Varieties of General Quiver Representations: Characteristic Classes and Semi-Invariants
papers.abstract: We study flags of subrepresentations of a general representation of a finite quiver. For each representation, its flag scheme is the zero scheme of a section of a quotient bundle on a product of partial flag varieties. We obtain the generic dimension and cycle class and equivariant localization formulas for Euler characteristics and parabolic Schubert coefficients. We further express these coefficients as finite signed sums of semi-invariant dimensions for auxiliary star quivers with inward and outward flag arms. In the acyclic one-step case, this is compatible with the result of Derksen--Schofield--Weyman, and the zero-dimensional case recovers their semi-invariant counting theorem. Examples treat matrix pencils and generalized Kronecker quivers.

papers.title: LQG solution for POMDP without estimating states: A minimum variance approach
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the control of discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) systems subject to incomplete and corrupted measurements. Specifically, we focus on designing a Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller without relying on explicit state estimation. By leveraging minimum variance duality, our approach allows the current control input to be represented as a linear function of available measurements and previously applied inputs, successfully reducing the task to a tractable deterministic optimization problem. We provide theoretical justification for this framework and demonstrate its practical effectiveness through numerical experiments.

papers.title: Optimal Sparsifiers for Abelian Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that for every Cayley graph $\mathcal{G}$ over any finite abelian group $G$, there is a weighted Cayley graph with $O(\log |G|)$ generators that is a spectral sparsifier for $\mathcal{G}$. This bound is optimal. Applying our bound to the group $G = \mathbb{F}_2^n$, yields, as a corollary, $O(n/\varepsilon^2)$-sized code sparsifiers for $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear codes, improving on the work of Khanna, Putterman and Sudan (SODA'24) who obtained a similar result with an additional $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ loss. Our proof is strongly inspired by a recent work of Reis and Rothvoss for the construction of $\ell_1$-sparsifiers. Following their work, the abelian Cayley sparsification problem can be reduced to establishing a lower bound for the volume of a certain natural convex body. This volume bound follows from a short, elementary argument that relies on character symmetry.

papers.title: A note on prismatic sites for p-quasisyntomic rings
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a fixed prime number and let $R$ be a $p$-quasisyntomic ring. We provide conditions for objects in the absolute prismatic site $R_\Prism$ to cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and to admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$. More precisely, we introduce in $R_\Prism$ the so-called transversal objects, so that the coproduct of any object in $R_\Prism$ with a transversal object exists in $R_\Prism$. As an immediate generalization, we introduce the so-called relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid covers of $R$, whose prismatic cohomology (of $δ$-pairs, in the sense of Antieau-Krause-Nikolaus) produces objects in $R_\Prism$ that cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$.

papers.title: Steady Euler flows with contact discontinuities in infinitely long nozzles
papers.abstract: We investigate two-dimensional steady subsonic Euler flows with a contact discontinuity in infinitely long nozzles.
